The seed hypothesis is still right for the rest: the (W1.083O3)x(Nb2.1O5)1-x mixtures at x = 0.31 and 0.48 work out to W:Nb near 0.23 and 0.48, far on the Nb-rich side of the 47 series, which is the Wadsley-Roth block-structure region. So the host holds both and splits on the W:Nb ratio.
taxonomy_feedback: The same 47-oxygen series sits in two entries: block_shear_niobate names Nb8W9O47 in its notes while tungsten_bronze lists Nb5W12O47 and Nb4W13O47 in representative_materials. They are tetragonal tungsten bronzes and belong in tungsten_bronze; block_shear_niobate should keep Nb12O29, Nb12WO33 and the Nb-rich Wadsley-Roth phases. Worth fixing before v4, since this host is the only place both entries are cited.
reference_disagreement: MP has Nb12WO33 C2 mp-1198790 (1 ICSD reference, hull 0.041) and NbWO7 Ima2 at hull 0.376 -- a block phase and a computed one. Neither is a 47-oxygen bronze, so no mp_id is recorded for either prototype here, and the TTB symmetry variant is left unresolved rather than guessed.
note: The delta in Nb8-xW9+xO47-delta is oxygen deficiency from the reduced single-step synthesis of the first paper, i.e. the carrier-concentration variable. No element in this host falls below the 5 at.% split, so there are no dopant_roles.

basis: The host is the Ag2Te-Ag2S pseudobinary: Ag4TeS is Ag2Te plus Ag2S in equal parts, and Ag2Te0.8S0.2 and Ag2Te0.6S0.4 are S-substituted silver telluride. The low-temperature structure is the monoclinic P2_1/c hessite/acanthite type rather than the orthorhombic naumannite the entry is named for -- the taxonomy notes that difference and keeps them in one shard -- and the 297-723 K window crosses the superionic transition of both end members, above which the cation sublattice is disordered on a bcc/fcc anion frame. The seed is refined for a second reason as well: the two papers describe Ag4TeS as a ductile amorphous/crystalline composite and as a semiconductor glass, so for 13 of the 18 samples a crystalline prototype describes only part of the material.

solid_solution_axis.note: S/(S+Te) spans 0.20-0.50 over 12 compositions, i.e. the whole Ag2Te-Ag2S join up to the 1:1 Ag4TeS point. The transition temperature moves along it -- Ag2Te transforms near 418 K and Ag2S near 452 K -- so the single value recorded in phases cannot cover the host and is flagged as approximate.
solid_solution_axis.axis_check: S and Te are the same group on the same anion sublattice.

reference_disagreement: The taxonomy gives 406 K for this transition, which is the Ag2Se value; this host contains no Ag2Se, so 418 K (Ag2Te) is used instead and the basis is recorded as llm_materials_knowledge rather than taxonomy_default. MP offers only Ag2TeS3 Cc mp-29163, a thio-tellurite of different stoichiometry, so mp_id is null throughout.

basis: LaAl2 and its dilute-Ce variants are 12 of the 18 samples: the cubic C15 Laves phase, MP LaAl2 Fd-3m mp-2694 with 15 ICSD references at hull 0.000, and the first paper is titled Thermoelectric power of RAl2. The (La,Ce)Al3 compositions are a different structure -- MP puts LaAl3 at P6_3/mmc mp-959 with 4 ICSD references, the hexagonal Ni3Sn D0_19 type -- and the taxonomy has only the cubic L1_2 entry for AB3, so ni3sn_d019 is proposed before use and the host splits on the Al:La ratio.

dopant_roles.basis: (La1-xCex)Al2 at x = 0.006-0.015 and Ce0.01-0.1La0.9-0.99Al3. Dilute Ce is the single-ion Kondo impurity whose giant thermopower these three papers measure -- the second is titled Giant thermoelectric power of (La,Ce)Al2 -- so it is a magnetic impurity on the rare-earth site, not a carrier dopant.

basis: RuAl2 with Fe, Si, Mn or a rare earth substituted into it is the whole host, and RuAl2 is the semiconducting TiSi2 (C54) intermetallic: MP Al2Ru Fddd (70) mp-10910 at hull 0.000 with 2 ICSD references, the same orthorhombic C54 structure proposed as tisi2_c54 for RuGa2 in chunk 005. The second paper is titled for binary semiconducting intermetallic compounds, which is what this narrow-gap Fddd aluminide is. Al13Ru4 and Al3Ru2 exist in the chemistry but no composition here is near their stoichiometries.

dopant_roles.basis: Ru0.85Fe0.15Al2 and (Ru0.85Fe0.15)0.95-0.98Mn0.02-0.05Al2: 15% of the Ru site is an alloying level, not dilute doping, and it is the base composition the Mn and Si series are built on.
Ru0.85Fe0.15Al1.95Si0.05; the first paper is on silicon- and manganese-doped RuAl2, so Si is the main-group substituent on the Al site.
The other dopant of that paper, on the transition-metal site.

Rare-earth additions to RuAl2 appear in three compositions, but nothing in the composition strings says whether they substitute on a lattice site or form a rare-earth aluminide second phase, and the rare earths are far too large for either site. Left unknown rather than assumed.
Same as Ce: addition of unresolved role.
Same as Ce: addition of unresolved role.

basis: PrBaCo2O5+delta -- Pr0.94BaCo2O5, Pr0.94BaCo2O6, PrBaCo2O5 and the Ca-substituted variants -- is the A-site-ordered 112 double perovskite of the two fuel-cell cathode papers, so the seed holds for those compositions. Pr0.5Ba0.5CoO3 and Pr0.7Ba0.3CoO3 are the disordered simple perovskite of the R1-xAxCoO3 transport paper: the same cations without the layer ordering. As in the La analogue, the cation ratio cannot tell them apart -- the oxygen content and the A-site ordering do -- so the host is mixed and the split rule has to use oxygen.

dopant_roles.basis: PrBa0.42Sr0.5Co2O5 and relatives: isovalent alkaline earth on the ordered A site, used to tune the tolerance factor. At half the Ba site it is alloying rather than doping.
Pr0.9Ca0.1BaCo2O5 -- the third paper is titled for A-site calcium-doped Pr1-xCaxBaCo2O5+delta, so Ca sits on the rare-earth half of the ordered A site.

basis: (Sr,Ba)PbO3 across Ba/(Ba+Sr) = 0.3-0.5 is an ABO3 perovskite with tetravalent Pb on the B site -- the papers are titled for perovskite-type Sr1-xBaxPbO3 ceramics and for A-site doped (Sr0.6Ba0.4)1-xMx perovskites. Ba0.4Sr0.6Pb1.1-1.2O3.2-3.4 is the same phase prepared with excess PbO, which is a processing surplus rather than a second structure.

solid_solution_axis.note: Ba/(Ba+Sr) spans 0.30-0.50 over 17 compositions. Both end members are ABO3 perovskites so the prototype is constant; the substitution moves the tolerance factor and hence the octahedral tilt, which is why the space group is given as the orthorhombic tilt system with medium confidence rather than cubic.
solid_solution_axis.axis_check: Ba and Sr are the same group on the same 12-coordinate site.

reference_disagreement: MP offers only BaSr(PbO3)2 Pmc2_1 mp-1227843, a computed 1:1 A-site ordering at hull 0.007. These samples scan x continuously and are a disordered solid solution, so the ordered cell is not their structure and mp_id is left null.

dopant_roles.basis: Bi goes on the B site in this family -- BaPb1-xBixO3 is the classic bismuthate line -- not on the A site with Ba and Sr, which is the natural but wrong reading of an A-site doping paper title.
Trivalent donor on the A site; the third paper is on A-site doped (Sr0.6Ba0.4)1-xMxPbO3.

basis: Every composition is Bi2Te3 with a carbon addition (Bi2Te3Cx at x = 0.3-3) and the curator details name graphene/Bi2Te3, CNT/Bi2Te3 and vol% additions of 2 to 20. That is a matrix plus a second phase, not a carbide and not a solid solution: carbon takes no lattice site in Bi2Te3. The matrix itself is tetradymite, recorded as the alternative so stage 2 resolves the Bi2Te3 structure rather than treating the host as structureless.
note: Carbon is above the 5 at.% split in every composition here -- Bi2Te3C3 is a third carbon by atom count -- so it appears as a host element and carries no dopant_roles entry, even though it is physically a dispersed second phase. The Bi2(Se,Te)3 composite of the third paper adds Se to the matrix, but no Se composition is visible in the shown subset.

basis: YbCd2-xZnxSb2 across the whole Cd/(Cd+Zn) range is the CaAl2Si2-type trigonal Zintl phase: Yb between [M2Sb2] slabs of edge-sharing MSb4 tetrahedra, P-3m1. The first paper is titled for the Zintl phase YbCd2-xZnxSb2 and the second surveys AM2Sb2 (A = Ca, Sr, Ba, Eu, Yb; M = Zn, Cd) as one structural family, so both end members are the same prototype and the solid solution never leaves it.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: tetrahedral M site of the [M2Sb2] slab
solid_solution_axis.note: Cd/(Cd+Zn) spans 0.20-0.85 over 15 compositions, which is the whole YbZn2Sb2-YbCd2Sb2 join. Isostructural end members, so the prototype is constant and the mixing acts on mass contrast and band width.
solid_solution_axis.axis_check: Cd and Zn are the same group on the same tetrahedral site.

reference_disagreement: No reference line is offered for this four-element host. mp_id is left null; stage 2 should resolve YbCd2Sb2 and YbZn2Sb2 separately.

basis: NaCo2-xFexO4 from x = 0.4 to 1.4 is the gamma-NaxCoO2 layered cobaltite written in its historic NaCo2O4 form: edge-sharing (Co,Fe)O2 sheets with Na between them at Na:(Co+Fe) = 1:2, which is Na0.5MO2. Two of the four papers are titled for NaCo2-xFexOy. Confidence is medium rather than high because the Fe-rich end (NaCo0.6Fe1.4O4) is past the point where the gamma stacking is usually retained, and the third paper is on Na0.7CoO2, so the Na content itself varies between papers more than the strings suggest.
reference_disagreement: No reference line is offered for this chemistry, so mp_id is null and the P6_3/mmc space group is the family archetype rather than a measured one.
note: Fe is above the 5 at.% split in every composition and so carries no dopant_roles entry, but its role is clear from the stoichiometry: it substitutes for Co inside the MO2 sheet across the whole series. alpha-NaFeO2 (the ordered-rocksalt 1:1 phase, alpha_nafeo2_layered) is the neighbouring structure in this chemistry, but no composition here reaches Na:M = 1:1.

basis: Nickel with 5 to 31 at.% chromium is the nichrome fcc substitutional solid solution -- Cr is soluble in fcc Ni to roughly 35 at.% and no composition here exceeds that, Ni68.6Cr31.4 being the extreme. The papers are on metallic thermocouple alloys and on hydrogen dissolved in nickel-chromium alloys, which is the interstitial-H version of the same fcc lattice rather than a different phase.
reference_disagreement: Every MP entry for this chemistry is an ordered compound -- Cr3Ni Pm-3m at hull 0.148, CrNi3 I4/mmm, Cr2Ni and CrNi2 Fd-3m at hulls of 0.21-0.27 -- each with a single ICSD reference, and MP flags CrNi3 ambiguous. None of them is the disordered fcc alloy these samples are, so mp_id is left null rather than taking the nearest formula. This is the standard failure mode of matching a random solid solution against a database of line compounds.

basis: Cu2GeSe3 with In or Sb on the Ge site, plus slightly Cu- and Se-deficient variants, is all 16 compositions. MP Cu2GeSe3 Imm2 mp-4728 (2 ICSD references, hull 0.000) is the orthorhombic ordered-zincblende structure this entry names, and the third paper calls the family ternary diamondlike semiconductors.

other_polymorphs.note: Cc at hull 0.002 with one ICSD reference, and a further Fdd2 entry mp-1225866 at hull 0.004. These are cation-ordering variants of the same diamond-like net at essentially the same energy; the first paper is titled for crystallographic control at the nanoscale, so which ordering forms is synthesis-dependent rather than reached by heating.

dopant_roles.basis: Cu2Ge1-xInxSe3 at x = 0.05-0.15, the subject of the second paper: a trivalent cation on the tetravalent Ge site, so it is an acceptor.
Same cation site; single composition.

note: Cu2.00Ge0.96Se2.82 and Cu2.00Ge0.93Se2.79 are cation and anion off-stoichiometry rather than doping. Cu, Ge and Se are all above the 5% split so they carry no dopant_roles entries, but stage 3 should treat those deficiencies as non-stoichiometry.

basis: The visible compositions are Cux(TiO2)1-x at x = 18-46 at.%, which is Cu powder added to reduced TiO2-x -- a metal/oxide composite, the first paper being on the effect of Cu powder addition to Cu/TiO2-x. That confirms the seed for those. But the dopant-candidate list (Ru 7, Y 5, Ca 4, Cr 4, Mn 4 and six single rare earths) cannot come from a Cu/TiO2 composite: it is the signature of CaCu3Ti4O12, where Ca is exactly 5 at.% of the 20-atom formula and Ru, Cr and Mn substitute on the Ti site while rare earths go on the Ca site. The second paper, on complex transition-metal oxides, fits that reading. So the host mixes a Cu/TiO2 composite with the CCTO family and needs a per-composition split. Only 6 of its 18 compositions are shown in the chunk file, so the proportion between the two cannot be settled here.
reference_disagreement: The MP entries offered are Ti3Cu3O and Ti4Cu2O Fd-3m suboxides and two rare-earth cuprotitanates; none is either a Cu/TiO2 composite or CaCu3Ti4O12, so mp_id is null. The rare-earth Ti-Cu-O entries do at least corroborate that rare earths and Ti-Cu-O coexist in real structures.

dopant_roles.basis: If the unseen compositions are CaCu3Ti4O12, Ca is the A-site cation of that structure -- a host constituent, listed as a candidate only because 1 atom in 20 is exactly at the 5% cut -- not a dopant. Recorded as unknown because the composition strings that would settle it are not shown.
Ru appears in 7 compositions, which in this chemistry is the CaCu3Ti4-xRuxO12 series; Ru would sit on the octahedral Ti site.
Same octahedral B site; the third paper is on a YCr0.5Mn0.5O3-type oxide, so Cr and Mn arrive together.
Same octahedral B site as Cr.
Trivalent rare earth on the large A site of the CCTO-type compositions; 5 compositions.
One of six single-composition rare-earth substitutions on the A site.
As Nd.
As Nd.
As Nd.
As Nd.
As Nd.

basis: Gd1-xSrxMnO3 at x = 0.3-0.7 is all five compositions, and two of the three papers are titled for Gd-Sr manganites and for Gd1-xSrxMnO3. Gd is a small A cation so the tolerance factor is low and the GdFeO3-type octahedral tilt large, but nothing leaves the ABO3 line, so one prototype covers the host.
reference_disagreement: No reference line is offered for this chemistry at all, so the space group is the manganite archetype rather than a measured one and mp_id is null. The third paper reports structural distortion as the variable behind the thermoelectric behaviour, which is exactly what a reference would be needed to pin down.
note: Sr runs from 0.3 to 0.7 of the A site, so it is an alloying component of the host string rather than a dopant, and no element here falls below the 5 at.% split.

basis: Ge0.5Sn0.25Pb0.25Te is 7 of the 18 samples and is a GeTe-rich pseudoternary rocksalt alloy: at half GeTe the rhombohedral R3m distortion survives at room temperature and relaxes to cubic Fm-3m on heating, which is what the first and third papers are about (phase morphology in Pb0.25Sn0.25Ge0.5Te, and band inversion giving multiple valleys). Sn0.8Ge0.1Pb0.1Te is the opposite end of the same join and is cubic rocksalt throughout, so the host holds both prototypes and splits on the Ge fraction.

solid_solution_axis.note: Ge/(Ge+Sn) spans 0.11-0.86 over 12 compositions, but Pb occupies the same cation site as well, so the real axis is a three-way cation mixture. The rhombohedral-to-cubic boundary moves along it, which is why the transition temperature is recorded as composition-dependent rather than as a host constant.
solid_solution_axis.axis_check: Ge, Sn and Pb are all group 14 on the same cation site.

note: The chunk file shows no MEASUREMENT CROSSES A TRANSITION line for this host because no single prototype was hypothesised for it, so the transition is added here from the chemistry: pure GeTe transforms near 700 K and alloying with 50% PbTe plus SnTe lowers it substantially. 600 K is an estimate for the dominant composition and needs a paper to confirm, which is why transition_basis is llm_materials_knowledge and both phases are medium confidence.

dopant_roles.basis: Sn0.47Cd0.03Ge0.25Pb0.25Te: divalent cation on the cation site, used in this family to widen the gap and suppress the rhombohedral distortion.
Ge0.5Sn0.25Pb0.25TeAg0.003, a monovalent acceptor on the cation site.
Ge0.5Sn0.25Pb0.25Te1.0009Bi0.0006, a trivalent donor on the cation site.

basis: Every composition is MPt4Ge12 with M = Pr, Ce, La, Eu or Th: the germanide filled skutterudite, a Pt4Ge12 framework of Ge12 cages in Im-3 with the guest inside. That is the RyM4X12 archetype of this entry with X = Ge rather than Sb or P, and all three papers are on PrPt4Ge12 and its La/Ce/Eu/Th-substituted relatives. The framework never changes across the 18 compositions; only the guest does.
reference_disagreement: assigned sg [204], ICSD-backed references for this host report [140, 58, 62, 189]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

dopant_roles.basis: The guest in the Ge12 cage of PrPt4Ge12. The fillers fall below 5 at.% only because one guest serves sixteen framework atoms, and mixing two guests halves each fraction again -- they are the compound, not impurities in it.
Pr1-xCexPt4Ge12: Ce substitutes for Pr on the cage site, which is what the first paper probes.
La1-xMxPt4Ge12 of the third paper; same cage site.
Pr0.5Eu0.5Pt4Ge12; same cage site.
Tetravalent actinide guest in the same cage, used to change the electron count without a 4f moment.

basis: LaS1.33-1.50 is the gamma-La3-xS4 phase: a cubic I-43d Th3P4 framework whose La vacancies run continuously from metallic La3S4 to semiconducting La2S3, which is exactly the carrier-concentration knob this entry describes. The second paper is titled for the preparation of gamma-LaSy at 1.33 < y < 1.50, so the composition range is the phase field itself, and MP La3S4 I-43d mp-567 carries 7 ICSD references.

other_polymorphs.note: alpha-La2S3, the orthorhombic Pnma sesquisulfide that TEDesignLab gives for this chemistry. It is a genuine polymorph of the y = 1.5 end but is a different preparation rather than a step in a thermal sequence from gamma, and the taxonomy has no entry for it, so it is parked here rather than given a prototype.

reference_disagreement: TEDesignLab, which the project ranks above MP, offers only La2S3 Pnma and LaS2 Pnma -- the orthorhombic sesquisulfide and the disulfide. Neither is what these samples are. The papers name the gamma Th3P4 phase explicitly, so the reference is describing other polymorphs of the chemistry rather than the one made here, and the assignment follows the papers and MP La3S4 instead of the preferred reference.

dopant_roles.basis: La2Ti0.075S2.67, from the paper on lanthanum sesquisulfide with Ti additive. Ti is added as a sintering and grain-control additive; nothing says it enters the La site, and it is too small for it.
Divalent cation on the La site, which fills vacancies and lowers the carrier count.
Divalent rare earth on the La site of the Th3P4 framework.
As Eu.
As Eu.

note: The La deficiency itself (LaS1.48 is La3-xS4 with x near 0.03) is the carrier-concentration variable, not doping; La and S are both above the 5% split so this is recorded here rather than as a dopant role.

basis: SrMoO3 with Mg, Fe, Co or Al on the Mo site is the whole host: the reduced Mo4+ cubic perovskite, MP SrMoO3 Pm-3m mp-18747 with 5 ICSD references. The first paper is titled for perovskite-type strontium molybdate and the rest are SOFC anode papers on SrMo1-xMxO3-delta, which is the same phase.
reference_disagreement: MP ranks SrMoO4 I4_1/a first for this chemistry on 13 ICSD references. That is scheelite, the fully oxidised Mo6+ molybdate: a different compound, not a polymorph of these samples. It also explains why the perovskite sits at hull 0.071 in the 2019 dump -- the oxidised phase is what is stable in air -- and that hull value should not be read as SrMoO3 being metastable as synthesised under reducing conditions.

dopant_roles.basis: SrMg0.1Mo0.9O3, the composition of the second paper title: a divalent cation on the octahedral B site, which brings oxygen vacancies with it.
SrMo0.9Fe0.1O3 and SrMo0.8Fe0.2O3, B-site substitution at alloying levels.
SrMo0.9Co0.1O3-delta is the third paper title exactly.
Trivalent cation on the same B site.
Rare earth on the A site; appears in 5 compositions, in the SOFC anode series.

basis: Nb4SiTe4 with Ti, Mo or Sb substituted at the fraction-of-a-percent level is the bulk of the host, and it is the quasi-one-dimensional M4SiTe4 needle crystal proposed as ta4site4_chain in chunk 007 -- the first paper is titled for hole-doped M4SiTe4 (M = Ta, Nb) and MP gives Nb4SiTe4 Pbam mp-1232409 at hull 0.000, isostructural with Ta4SiTe4. Nb3SiTe6 (3 samples, its own paper) is a different compound: a van der Waals layered ternary telluride rather than a chain, with no taxonomy entry, so nb3site6_layered is proposed and the host splits on the Te:Si ratio of 4:1 against 6:1.
reference_disagreement: assigned sg [55], ICSD-backed references for this host report [14]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

dopant_roles.basis: Mo has one more d electron than Nb, so on the metal-chain site it is the electron-doping variable; it appears in 7 compositions.
(Nb1-xTix)4SiTe4 at x = 0.002-0.05 -- one d electron fewer, so this is the hole doping of the first paper title.
Pnictogen on the chalcogen sheath site; single composition.

basis: SrVO3 with Nb, Ti, La or Y substitution is all 13 compositions: the correlated-metal cubic perovskite, MP SrVO3 Pm-3m mp-18717 with 3 ICSD references. The papers are on the Mott transition in SrVO3, on SrTi1-xVxO3, and on epitaxial SrVO3 as a transparent conductor -- all the ABO3 line.
reference_disagreement: MP ranks SrV6O11, Sr2VO4 and a chloride Sr5V3ClO12 above SrVO3 on ICSD count, but those are different compounds of the Sr-V-O chemistry rather than polymorphs of these samples; SrVO3 itself is present at hull 0.036 and is what is recorded. Sr2VO4 would be the n=1 Ruddlesden-Popper member, and no composition here has the 2:1 A:B ratio it needs, so the disagreement is one of chemistry coverage, not of structure.

dopant_roles.basis: SrV1-xNbxO3 at x = 0.03-0.2: a pentavalent 4d cation on the B site. At x = 0.2 it is an alloying level, not dilute doping.
La0.2Sr0.8VO3: trivalent donor on the A site, which is how this family is driven across the Mott transition.
Same trivalent A-site role, smaller cation.
SrTi0.17V0.83O3 sits on the SrTiO3-SrVO3 join, which is the band-filling axis of the second paper, so Ti is an end member below the cut rather than an impurity.

basis: PbSnTeSe in equal parts is the four-component rocksalt solid solution the papers call a high-entropy alloy: Pb and Sn share the cation site, Te and Se the anion site, and every end member of the join is Fm-3m rocksalt. The structure prototype is therefore rocksalt, with high_entropy_alloy recorded alongside as the disorder descriptor rather than as the structure -- the papers are titled for PbSnTeSe high-entropy alloys and for Na-doped nanocrystalline PbSnTeSe.

solid_solution_axis.note: Pb/(Pb+Sn) spans 0.20-0.89 over 17 compositions, and Te/Se mix independently on the anion site, so this host is disordered on both sublattices at once. That is what the high-entropy label is describing; the prototype does not change along either axis.
solid_solution_axis.axis_check: Pb and Sn are the same group on the cation site; Te and Se likewise on the anion site.

reference_disagreement: MP offers SnTePbSe R3m mp-1218892 (hull 0.024) and P4/mmm mp-1218887, both computed orderings of the four species. The samples are a disordered solid solution, not an ordered cell, so mp_id is left null. A computed low-symmetry ordering is the standard artefact for a high-entropy composition in a database of ordered structures.

dopant_roles.basis: Pb1-xSnTeSeLax at x = 0.02-0.1: a trivalent donor on the cation site.
The third paper is on Na doping of nanocrystalline PbSnTeSe; monovalent Na on the cation site is the p-type acceptor, as in PbTe.

basis: Both halves of the seed are present and a third thing besides. Te95Se5 and the (Bi2Se3)x(Te3)y compositions are trigonal Te with Se substituting on the helical chains -- Se and Te form a continuous trigonal solid solution -- and the first paper is on the effect of selenium on the thermoelectric properties of tellurium. (Te85Se15)45As35Cu25 is the Te-As-Cu chalcogenide glass of the second paper, which is the amorphous half. The rest are that glass with 10-50% Bi0.5Sb1.5Te3 added, i.e. tetradymite crystallites in a glass matrix, which is a composite and is recorded as one rather than being forced into either half.

solid_solution_axis.note: Se/(Se+Te) spans 0.05-0.29 with a median of 0.09, so this is Te with a little Se rather than a balanced alloy. Trigonal Se and Te are isostructural, so the prototype holds across the axis -- but the axis is only meaningful for the crystalline compositions; in the glass compositions Se is a network component with no site at all.
solid_solution_axis.axis_check: Se and Te are the same group and both form the same helical chain structure.

reference_disagreement: MP offers only Te3Se P6_3/mmc mp-1187404 at hull 0.200, a computed ordering that is not the trigonal chain structure of either element. mp_id is null.

dopant_roles.basis: As is 35 at.% of the (Te85Se15)45As35Cu25 glass, i.e. a network former of the chalcogenide glass, not a dopant. It falls under the 5% cut only after dilution by the Bi0.5Sb1.5Te3 additions.
Cu is 25 at.% of the same glass; as for As, it is a glass constituent.
A further glass-former constituent in the Te-based glass-ceramic compositions.
Sb arrives entirely as the Bi0.5Sb1.5Te3 crystallites added to the glass, so it belongs to a second phase rather than substituting in trigonal Te.
As Sb: from the added Bi0.5Sb1.5Te3 and from Bi2Se3 in the third paper, both second phases in a Te matrix.

basis: AgInSe2 with Zn on either cation site is the chalcopyrite the seed names -- TEDesignLab gives InAgSe2 I-42d mp-20554 with 13 ICSD references at hull 0.000, the best-attested entry in the chemistry. But the single largest composition is AgIn5Se8 (5 samples), and that is not chalcopyrite: it is the In-rich ordered-vacancy compound, which TEDesignLab itself lists at space group 111 rather than 122. The two are different prototypes, so defect_chalcopyrite_ovc is proposed before use and the host splits on the In:Ag ratio.
reference_disagreement: The two references disagree about AgIn5Se8: TEDesignLab gives space group 111 while MP gives In5AgSe8 C2 (5) mp-1224092 at hull 0.003. Following the project precedence the ICSD-backed TEDesignLab symmetry is preferred, but neither is confirmed here and the ordered-vacancy compounds of this family are known to take several closely related tetragonal orderings. MP also lists three further AgInSe2 polymorphs (R-3m, R3m, I4_1/amd) at hulls of 0.07-0.11, none of them the ambient chalcopyrite.

dopant_roles.basis: The second paper is titled for the site occupations of Zn in AgInSe2-based chalcopyrites, and the composition strings show the answer is not single-valued: Ag0.95InZn0.05Se2 puts Zn on the Ag site while Ag0.975In0.975Zn0.05Se2 splits it between both cation sites. The site is composition-dependent and stage 2 should keep both.
Divalent cation on the cation sublattice, as for Zn.

basis: In0.53Ga0.47As and In0.52Al0.48As lattice-matched to InP, grown as films, superlattices, devices and modules -- all zincblende III-V. Er is not a dopant here: ErAs is a semimetallic rocksalt second phase deliberately embedded as nanoparticles, and the curator details say so directly (0.6 vol% ErAs, 0.6 at.% ErAs, ErAs nanoparticles inside In0.53Ga0.27Al0.20As), which is what all three papers are built on.

solid_solution_axis.note: Al/(Al+Ga) spans 0.20-0.51 over 10 compositions, but In sits on the same site and is the majority cation, so the detected axis is only the Al/Ga part of a three-way III-site mixture held at the InP lattice constant. The composition is set by lattice matching, not by a doping series.
solid_solution_axis.axis_check: Al, Ga and In are all group 13 on the same cation site.

reference_disagreement: No reference line is offered for this four-element host, so mp_id is null. Stage 2 should resolve InAs, GaAs and AlAs separately rather than looking for one entry for the quaternary.

dopant_roles.basis: ErAs nanoparticles embedded in the InGaAlAs matrix at 0.3-0.6%: a rocksalt semimetal second phase used for electron filtering and phonon scattering, not a substitutional rare earth. Deliberate rather than a contaminant, but it is not in the zincblende lattice.

basis: Ca12Al14O33 and the identical formula written as (CaO)12(Al2O3)7 are 14 of 17 samples: mayenite, the I-43d cage framework Ca12Al14O32 plus one extra oxygen distributed over the cages. Replacing that cage oxygen with electrons is what makes the C12A7 electride, which is exactly what the electride and superconducting-transition papers measure, and the prototype is the same framework either way. The (Ca12Al14O33)x(CB)y entries are the same host milled with carbon black.
reference_disagreement: Neither reference ranks mayenite first: TEDesignLab gives CaAl4O7 and Ca4Al6O13 as primaries and MP gives the Ca3Al2O12 garnet at hull 0.407 on 10 ICSD references. The entry that is actually mayenite is MP Ca6Al7O16 I-43d (220) mp-721592 at hull 0.000, which is Ca12Al14O32 -- the framework without the extra cage oxygen -- so it is recorded with medium confidence and stage 2 should check the oxygen content rather than assume a stoichiometric cage.

dopant_roles.basis: The CB in (Ca12Al14O33)34.73(CB)65.27 is carbon black, a deliberate second phase in the mayenite cement composite of the second paper, not carbon in the lattice.
There is no boron in this host. B appears only because the composition string writes carbon black as CB, which the parser read as the elements C and B.

basis: CeAl3 with its La-substituted variants is 11 of 17 samples and is the archetypal heavy-fermion trialuminide; the light rare-earth RAl3 compounds take the hexagonal Ni3Sn D0_19 ordering rather than the cubic L1_2 one, which is why that entry was proposed for LaAl3 in chunk 008 and names CeAl3 explicitly. CeAl2 (5 samples) is the C15 Laves phase MP gives as mp-2088 with 23 ICSD references, and Ce3Al is the L1_2 AB3 ordering at mp-2413, so the host holds three prototypes and splits cleanly on the Ce:Al ratio.
reference_disagreement: MP does not offer CeAl3 at all -- the ranked list runs CeAl2, Ce3Al, CeAl4, CeAl, Ce3Al11 -- so the dominant composition of the host has no mp_id and the D0_19 assignment rests on the structure literature. mp-2088 covers the CeAl2 compositions and mp-2413 the Ce3Al one.

dopant_roles.basis: Ce0.9La0.1Al3 and Ce0.99La0.01Al3: non-magnetic La dilutes the Kondo lattice, which is how the single-ion and coherence contributions to the thermopower are separated. It is not a carrier dopant.

basis: Every composition is CeFeAsO with F on the oxygen site and Co on the iron site: the 1111 oxypnictide, alternating Ce2O2 and Fe2As2 layers in P4/nmm, which MP gives as CeFeAsO mp-1079570 with 5 ICSD references. The first paper measures thermopower across the whole RFeAsO series and the other two are on carrier doping in the reservoir and conduction layers, which is what the F and Co substitutions do.

dopant_roles.basis: CeO0.9F0.1FeAs: F-for-O in the charge reservoir is the electron-doping variable of the 1111 family, exactly as the taxonomy notes for LaFeAsO1-xFx, not an impurity.
CeO0.9F0.1Fe1-xCoxAs at x = 0.05-0.15: Co dopes directly into the conducting FeAs layer, which is the simultaneous doping of both layers that the third paper is about.

basis: Eu(Fe0.925Co0.075)2As2 is 16 of 17 samples: the 122 iron arsenide, body-centred tetragonal I4/mmm, which MP gives as Eu(FeAs)2 mp-20890 at hull 0.000 with 10 ICSD references. The single remaining sample is EuFe4As12, a filled skutterudite of the same three elements and an entirely different structure -- the first paper is titled for it -- so the host splits on the Fe:As ratio, 1:1 for the 122 and 1:3 for the skutterudite.

dopant_roles.basis: Eu(Fe0.925Co0.075)2As2: Co-for-Fe is the electron-doping variable that suppresses the spin-density-wave order in the 122 arsenides, the same role K-for-Ba plays on the other sublattice. At 7.5% it is a deliberate doping level, not a trace.

basis: Pr0.67Ba0.33MnO3 and Pr0.5Ba0.5MnO3 are hole-doped manganite perovskites, and Pr2BaMn3O9 is the same ABO3 stoichiometry written per three B sites. The complication is ordering rather than chemistry: at the 1:1 A-site ratio the compound can be the A-site layered ordered double perovskite that MP lists as BaPrMn2O6 P4/mmm mp-19274, and whether a given sample is ordered or disordered depends on the synthesis, not on the formula. The (Pr0.67Ba0.33MnO3)x(PdO)y entries are PdO composites of the same manganite.
reference_disagreement: The spacegroup is left null deliberately. Mixed-valence manganites of this A-site size run from orthorhombic Pnma through rhombohedral R-3c to cubic with composition and temperature, and the measured window reaches 1074 K, so naming one tilt variant for the host would assert more than the composition supports.

dopant_roles.basis: (Pr0.67Ba0.33MnO3)0.9(PdO)0.1: PdO is added as a separate oxide phase in a composite, not dissolved on the B site.
Pr2(Ba0.9Cs0.1)Mn3O9 is the Pr2/3(Ba1-xCsx)1/3MnO3 series of the first paper: a large monovalent cation on the A site, which is a hole-doping variable.

basis: Mg3Bi2 and the Mg-excess Mg3.2Bi2 are the alpha phase: the trigonal CaAl2Si2-type Zintl structure P-3m1 that Mg3Sb2 shares, with Mg on both the octahedral interlayer site and the tetrahedral site of the [Mg2Bi2] slab. The first paper is titled for Zintl Mg3Bi2-xPnx and the third is the Science paper on n-type Mg3Bi2, so the whole host is one prototype; Mg3Bi0.33 is a film composition parsed as strongly Mg-rich rather than a second structure.
reference_disagreement: assigned sg [164], ICSD-backed references for this host report [206]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

dopant_roles.basis: Mg3.2Bi1.998Te0.002 and Mg3.2Bi1.996Te0.004: Te on the pnictide site is the standard n-type donor for Mg3Sb2 and Mg3Bi2, and the levels here are genuinely dilute.
Mg3.2Bi1.898Sb0.1Te0.002 sits on the Mg3Sb2-Mg3Bi2 join, which is one continuous solid solution of the same prototype; Sb tunes the band gap rather than the carrier count.

basis: CdSb with dilute Ag, Cu, Au and Te is 15 of 17 samples, nearly all single crystals, and TEDesignLab gives CdSb Pbca (61) mp-1321 at hull 0.000 with 4 ICSD references -- the orthorhombic CdSb the seed names, whose anisotropic multicentre bonding is the subject of the first paper. Cd12.7Sb10 is not that structure: it is the Cd13-xSb10 phase of the third paper, the cadmium analogue of beta-Zn4Sb3 with disordered interstitials, which is why MP offers Cd6Sb5 R-3c mp-669510 for this chemistry.

dopant_roles.basis: Cd0.99Ag0.01Sb, and the curator details give CdSb + 0.01% Ag + 0.01% Te directly: monovalent Ag on the Cd site is the acceptor half of the donor-acceptor compensation study the second paper reports.
Ag0.0001CdSbTe0.0001 and the same curator details: Te on the Sb site is the donor half of that pair.
CdSb + 0.01% Cu + 0.01% Te in the curator details: another monovalent acceptor on the cation site.
CdSb + 0.1% Au + 0.001% Te: as Ag and Cu, a coinage-metal acceptor on the Cd site.

basis: CePd2Si2 with its Ni-, Cu- and La-substituted variants is 11 of 17 samples: the ThCr2Si2 122, MP Ce(SiPd)2 I4/mmm mp-3826 at hull 0.000 with 13 ICSD references, and the second paper is on heavy-fermion behaviour in Ce(NixPd1-x)2Si2. The host is not single-structured, though: Ce2PdSi3 (2 samples) is the AlB2-derived 2-1-3 in which Pd and Si share a honeycomb layer, and Ce3Pd5Si (3 samples) is a third stoichiometry that neither reference resolves -- MP offers Ce3(Si3Pd10)2, Ce2(Si2Pd7)3 and CeSiPd2 but nothing at 3-5-1.

dopant_roles.basis: Ce(Ni0.1Pd0.9)2Si2: Ni-for-Pd applies chemical pressure and tunes the Kondo lattice towards the quantum critical point, which is the axis of the second paper. At 10% it is an alloying level.
Ce(Pd0.95Cu0.05)2Si2, the series of the third paper: a transition-metal substitution on the same site, changing the electron count as well as the cell volume.
Ce0.8La0.2Pd2Si2: non-magnetic dilution of the Ce sublattice, the standard single-ion reference measurement.

basis: CeRhSi3 is the largest composition, 8 of 17 samples, and it is not a 122: it is the BaNiSn3-type RTX3, the non-centrosymmetric I4mm relative of ThCr2Si2, and the second paper is on thermoelectric power in single-crystalline CeRhSi3. The taxonomy had no entry for it, so banisn3_i4mm is proposed before use. CeRh2Si2 and CeRh2-xNixSi2 (3 samples) are the centrosymmetric 122 that MP gives as Ce(SiRh)2 I4/mmm mp-4090 with 10 ICSD references, and Ce3RhSi3 (5 samples) is a third phase the references do not cover -- they offer Ce3(SiRh)2 and Ce2Si5Rh3 but nothing at 3-1-3.
reference_disagreement: No reference entry is offered for CeRhSi3 itself, so the dominant composition of the host has no mp_id and its space group comes from the structure literature rather than from the refs. MP also flags Ce2Si3Rh P6/mmm mp-31163 AMBIGUOUS, so the minority phases of this chemistry are not cleanly resolved either.

dopant_roles.basis: CeRh2-xNixSi2 at x = 0.1-0.2, the alloy series of the third paper: an isostructural substitution on the transition-metal site of the 122 compositions, not of CeRhSi3.
Ce(Rh0.90Ru0.10)2Si2: the same transition-metal site, one electron fewer, which is how the magnetic ordering of the 122 is tuned.

basis: The host is the TiCoSb-TiNiSn join: TiCo1-xNixSn1-xSbx runs between two 18-electron half-Heuslers, keeping the valence-electron count fixed, and Ti2NiCoSnSb is the midpoint that the second paper calls a half-Heusler-type high-entropy alloy. (TiCoSb)0.8(TiNi2Sn)0.2 is a different thing: TiNi2Sn is the full Heusler, so those samples are a half-Heusler matrix with full-Heusler inclusions, which is the phase-stability question the third paper asks.
reference_disagreement: No reference line is offered for this five-element host, so mp_id is null. Stage 2 should resolve TiCoSb and TiNiSn separately and treat the quaternary as a join between them rather than looking for one entry.

dopant_roles.basis: The curator details spell the series out as Ti2-x-yAlxTayNiCoSn0.5Sb1.5, so Al sits on the Ti site of the half-Heusler.
Same curator formula: Ta is the second substituent on the Ti site, a heavier isoelectronic-with-Nb cation used for mass contrast.
Ti2-x-y-qAlxTayZrqNiCoSn0.5Sb1.5 in the curator details: Zr is isoelectronic with Ti on the same site and is the usual alloy-scattering addition.

basis: Sr0.7Y0.3CoO3 and Sr3YCo4O10.5 are the same material written two ways: the oxygen-deficient cobaltite Sr3YCo4O10.5+delta, in which Sr and Y order on the A site and the oxygen vacancies order in alternating layers, giving a 2ap x 2ap x 4ap superstructure of the ABO3 cell. The prototype is the perovskite; the ordering is a superstructure of it, and the first paper is explicitly about the effect of structural disorder in this compound.
reference_disagreement: MP offers Sr2YCoO6 Fm-3m mp-1080434, a rock-salt-ordered double perovskite at 1:1 Co:Y, plus two computed layered entries. None is at the 3:1:4 Sr:Y:Co stoichiometry of these samples, and the vacancy-ordered superstructure is not represented at all, so mp_id is null. The oxygen content is the variable here and cannot be read from the references.

dopant_roles.basis: Sr2.2Ca0.8YCo4O10.5 and Sr2.6Ca0.4YCo4O10.5: Ca on the A site is the chemical-pressure axis named in the third paper.
Sr3YCo3.8Ga0.2O10.5: a non-magnetic trivalent cation on the B site, which dilutes the cobalt network and changes the vacancy order.

basis: Two sulfide families with different anion counts. CuxFe4Sn12S32 at x = 4 to 7.5 normalises to Cu1-2FeSn3S8 -- 32 S is the content of a spinel cell and Sn:Fe is 3 -- so these are the Cu-deficient thiospinels of the chalcogenide-spinel paper, the rhodostannite-type family. Cu2FeSnS4 is stannite instead, Sn:Fe of 1, the I-42m quaternary TEDesignLab gives as FeCu2SnS4 mp-22648, and the first paper runs the stannite-kuramite Cu2+xFe1-xSnS4 solid solution. The split is the Sn:Fe ratio, and which family carries more of the 17 samples cannot be settled from the listed counts, hence medium confidence.
reference_disagreement: MP offers FeCu2Sn3S8 only as a computed R-3m ordering mp-1225180 at hull 0.015, not as the cubic thiospinel, and its other Cu-Fe-Sn-S entries are P-4m2 orderings at 1 ICSD reference each. The well-attested entry in the chemistry is the stannite, which is the minority family here, so mp_id is left null for the spinel series and stage 2 should expect the tetragonal I4_1/a rhodostannite variant as well as Fd-3m.

basis: Three structures, and the seed names only two of them. Cu26V2Ge6S32 and Cu24Zn2V2Ge6S32 are colusite, the P-43n sulfosalt of the first paper. Cu7.2-7.76GeS6 is the one the seed misses: Cu8-xGeS6 is an argyrodite, which TEDesignLab gives as Cu8GeS6 Pmn2_1 mp-5546, and the copper deficiency there is the carrier-concentration knob rather than a dopant. Cu2GeS3 Cc mp-15252 is the cu2gese3 half of the seed. The host splits on the Cu:Ge ratio -- about 4.3 for colusite, 7 to 8 for the argyrodite, 2 for Cu2GeS3.
reference_disagreement: Neither reference carries colusite itself: TEDesignLab covers Cu8GeS6 and Cu2GeS3 and MP adds Cu2GeS4 and two further Cu2GeS3 orderings. The colusite compositions therefore have no mp_id, which is expected -- these are large-cell sulfosalts underrepresented in the 2019 snapshot.

dopant_roles.basis: V is a structural constituent of colusite Cu26V2Ge6S32, occupying the tetrahedral V site of the sulfosalt framework. It reads as 3 at.% only because the colusite cell is large, so the 5% cut misfiles it as a dopant candidate.
Nb and Ta replace V on the same framework site in the Cu26A2Ge6S32 colusite series of the second paper, which is how the electron count of the framework is set.
As Nb: the same framework site of the colusite, not a dilute impurity.
Cu24Zn2V2Ge6S32: divalent Zn on the copper sublattice of the colusite, which reduces the hole count.
Cr appears in the same Cu26A2Ge6S32 series as an alternative to V on the framework site.

basis: Cu2ZnGeSe4 is 6 of 16 samples and the rest are the off-stoichiometric Cu2+xZn1-xGeSe4 series around it; TEDesignLab gives ZnCu2GeSe4 I-42m (121) mp-10824 at hull 0.002 with 5 ICSD references, which is the stannite ordering of the quaternary adamantine framework. The Cu-rich, Zn-poor compositions are cation antisite series on that lattice rather than a second structure. The one curator detail reading Bi2-xSbxTe3-y belongs to a different chemistry and is ignored.

other_polymorphs.note: The first paper is on wurtzite Cu2ZnGeSe4 nanocrystals: the hexagonal adamantine polytype is reachable in solution-grown nanocrystals but is not produced by heating the bulk tetragonal phase, so it is recorded here rather than in phases.

dopant_roles.basis: Trivalent In on the tetravalent Ge site of the adamantine framework is an acceptor, the standard carrier-tuning substitution for this quaternary.
The second paper is on magnetic ions in wide-band-gap semiconductor nanocrystals, and divalent Fe takes the divalent Zn site.

basis: Fe2VGa and its Ti- and Ge-substituted variants are the whole host: the L2_1 full Heusler, MP VGaFe2 Fm-3m mp-21883 at hull 0.000 with 3 ICSD references. All three papers are about the pseudogap at the Fermi level of Fe2VGa, which is a property of exactly that ordered cubic structure, and the off-stoichiometry the third paper studies is antisite disorder on it rather than a different prototype.

dopant_roles.basis: Fe2V1-xTixGa at x = 0.05-0.15: one electron fewer on the V site, which moves the Fermi level across the pseudogap. At these levels it is a doping series.
Fe2VGa1-xGex, the substitution of the second paper: one electron more on the main-group site, the n-type counterpart to Ti.

basis: Every composition is (Nd,Sr)FeO3 with Cu, Zn, Co or Mo on the iron site -- Nd0.5Sr0.5Fe0.8Cu0.2O3 is the largest -- which is the simple ABO3 orthoferrite perovskite with a mixed rare-earth/alkaline-earth A site. The papers are on cobalt-free oxide electrodes and on (Ln0.5M0.5)FeO3-delta, i.e. oxygen-deficient perovskites, and the oxygen deficiency is a vacancy concentration on that lattice, not a different structure.
reference_disagreement: MP offers only computed Sr-Nd-Fe-O orderings -- Sr2Nd(FeO3)3 C2/c mp-1218798, Sr3Nd(FeO4)2, SrNd2Fe2O7, SrNdFeO4 -- none with an ICSD reference and none the simple perovskite these samples are. The last three are Ruddlesden-Popper stoichiometries, which need an A:B ratio above 1 that no composition here has, so mp_id is null and the Pnma spacegroup is the usual orthoferrite tilt system rather than a database match.

dopant_roles.basis: Nd0.5Sr0.5Fe0.8Cu0.2O3: Cu on the B site at 20% is an alloying-level substitution that creates oxygen vacancies, which is the point of the cobalt-free electrode papers.
The same B-site role as Cu, divalent and non-magnetic.
Co and Fe form a continuous B-site solid solution in these perovskites; here Co is the minority component.
La0.2Nd0.3Sr0.26Ca0.24FeO3: Ca is a second alkaline earth on the A site, an alloying component of a four-cation A sublattice rather than a dopant.
Same composition: La is a second rare earth on the A site.
A high-valence donor on the B site, used to compensate the acceptor doping.

basis: Pr1-xSrxFeO3 is 9 of 17 samples and MP gives PrFeO3 Pnma mp-24995 at hull 0.000 with 6 ICSD references: the orthoferrite perovskite. The Ni-, Cu-, Ti- and Co-substituted members sit on the same B site. The second paper reports a perovskite/brownmillerite nanocomposite, so the vacancy-ordered brownmillerite ABO2.5 is genuinely present in part of the host rather than being a possibility raised by the stoichiometry alone.

dopant_roles.basis: Pr0.9Sr0.1FeO3 and Pr0.8Sr0.2FeO3: divalent Sr on the A site is the hole-doping variable of the orthoferrites and the axis of the first paper.
Pr0.8Ca0.2Fe0.8Ni0.2O3: the same A-site acceptor role as Sr, smaller cation.
Sr0.1Ba0.1Pr0.8Cu0.1Ti0.1Fe0.8O3, the (SrBa)1-xPrx series of the third paper: a third alkaline earth on the A site.
PrFe0.8Ni0.2O3: Ni on the B site at 20% is an alloying-level substitution that raises the conductivity.
Same B site, from the (SrBa)(CuTi)0.2Fe0.8O3 series.
Paired with Cu on the B site in the same series; tetravalent Ti compensates the monovalent-to-divalent Cu.
Another 3d cation on the B site of the same perovskite.
As Mn: B-site substitution, continuous with the ferrite-cobaltite join.

basis: FeS2 and its Co- and Se-substituted variants are 12 of 17 samples, and the first paper is on nanoscale FeS2 pyrite; TEDesignLab gives FeS2 Pa-3 (205) mp-226 at hull 0.007 with 18 ICSD references. The third paper is on spark-plasma-sintered Fe7-xCoxS8, which is pyrrhotite -- a vacancy-ordered NiAs-derived monosulfide, not a disulfide -- so the host splits on the S:Fe ratio, 2 for pyrite against 8:7 for pyrrhotite.

other_polymorphs.note: MP puts marcasite FeS2 Pnnm at hull 0.000 against 0.007 for pyrite, but pyrite carries 18 ICSD references to marcasite 8 and is what these papers synthesise. Marcasite is the low-temperature metastable polymorph and converts irreversibly to pyrite on heating, so it is not a thermal phase of this measurement.

reference_disagreement: Both references rank a monosulfide first for this chemistry -- TEDesignLab FeS P-62c troilite with 22 ICSD references, MP the thiospinel Fe3S4 greigite (flagged AMBIGUOUS) -- because they describe the whole Fe-S system, in which the monosulfides are the most-studied phases. The samples here are overwhelmingly the disulfide, so the ranking is followed only after filtering to FeS2.

dopant_roles.basis: Fe1-xCoxS2 at x = 0.01-0.04: Co on the Fe site is the n-type donor of pyrite. The same element also appears at much higher levels in the Fe7-xCoxS8 pyrrhotite samples, where it is an alloying component instead.
FeS1.99Se0.01: Se on the anion site of the disulfide, isoelectronic and dilute.

basis: The host is one composition, GaN, across 17 samples of free-standing material, films and single crystals. TEDesignLab gives GaN P6_3mc (186) mp-804 at hull 0.000 with 22 ICSD references -- the wurtzite polytype that essentially all GaN growth produces.

other_polymorphs.note: Cubic GaN, 10 ICSD references at hull 0.005, is grown only on cubic substrates; heating wurtzite GaN does not produce it. Film samples are present in this host, which is why it is recorded rather than dropped.
The rocksalt phase at hull 0.478 forms above roughly 50 GPa.

basis: GeSe is the orthorhombic Pnma GeS-type layered structure, MP mp-700 at hull 0.000 with 9 ICSD references, and the first two papers are on exactly that orthorhombic IV-VI. GeAg0.05Sb0.05Se1.1 is the exception and is not a dopant series: co-alloying with AgSbSe2 is what stabilises cubic rocksalt GeSe, which is the crystalline cubic germanium selenide of the third paper, so those samples are a different prototype reached by alloying rather than by heating.

other_polymorphs.note: 1 ICSD reference against 9 for Pnma. It is reached by AgSbSe2-type alloying or epitaxy, not by heating pure GeSe -- GeSe does have a Pnma to Cmcm transition, but near 900 K, above the 755 K top of the robust measured range.

dopant_roles.basis: Ge1-xAgxSe at x = 0.002-0.03: monovalent Ag on the Ge site is the p-type acceptor. In the GeAg0.05Sb0.05Se1.1 samples Ag is instead half of the AgSbSe2 alloying pair.
Trivalent Sb on the Ge site is a donor, and paired with Ag in equal amounts it is charge-balanced AgSbSe2 alloying rather than doping.
A single composition carries Te on the anion site; GeSe and GeTe are a continuous join, so this is isoelectronic alloying.

basis: Every composition is RIr2Zn20 for R = Yb, Pr, Ce or Sm: the CeCr2Al20 cage structure in Fd-3m, with the rare earth inside a Zn16 Frank-Kasper cage. MP confirms the type in this chemistry at Ce(Zn10Ir)2 Fd-3m mp-1199912, hull 0.000, and the first two papers are on the YbT2Zn20 heavy-fermion series. All 14 compositions are single crystals of the 1-2-20 stoichiometry.

dopant_roles.basis: YbIr2Zn20 is the parent compound of 4 of the samples. The rare earth is 1 of 23 atoms, so at 4.3 at.% the whole-formula 5% cut pushes the cage-centre species of the prototype below the line; it is a host species, not a dopant.
PrIr2Zn20 is likewise its own parent compound, the quadrupolar-ordering member of the third paper, not Pr-doped YbIr2Zn20.
Yb0.6Ce0.4Ir2Zn20: here Ce genuinely shares the cage site with Yb, an alloy on the rare-earth sublattice.
Yb0.87Ce0.08Sm0.05Ir2Zn20: a third rare earth on the same cage site.
Non-magnetic Y on the cage site is the standard dilution reference for these heavy-fermion cages.

PrIr2Zn19.5Ga0.5 and PrIr2Zn19Ga: Ga replaces Zn in the cage framework and changes its electron count, which is how the third paper tunes the crystal-field ground state. This is framework substitution, not cage filling.

basis: AgInTe2 and the Ag-deficient Ag1-xInTe2 series are 10 of 16 samples, and TEDesignLab gives InAgTe2 I-42d (122) mp-22386 at hull 0.000 with 9 ICSD references: the I-III-VI2 chalcopyrite of the pseudocubic-materials paper. AgIn5Te8 is the In-rich ordered-vacancy compound of the same family, which TEDesignLab itself lists at space group 111 rather than 122, and Ag0.4Cd0.2In2.4Te4 is another In-rich member -- the same split made for Ag-In-Se in chunk 008, so defect_chalcopyrite_ovc is reused rather than re-proposed.
reference_disagreement: MP ranks In5AgTe8 C2 (5) mp-1224268 first for this chemistry and offers four AgInTe2 polymorphs (P-4m2, R-3m, P4/mmm, P3m1) at hulls of 0.013 to 0.269, none of them the ambient chalcopyrite that TEDesignLab backs with 9 ICSD references. Following project precedence the ICSD-backed symmetry is taken, and the two references disagree about the ordered-vacancy compound exactly as they did for AgIn5Se8.

dopant_roles.basis: Ag0.4Cd0.2In2.4Te4: divalent Cd on the monovalent cation site, which is the solid solution with CdTe that the third paper is about rather than dilute doping.

basis: Three compositions, Pd0.86Ag0.14 through Pd0.61Ag0.39, from one paper on the influence of hydrogen on electron transport in Pd-Ag. Pd and Ag are completely miscible in the fcc A1 structure across the whole range, so this is a disordered substitutional alloy with no ordered superstructure, which is what the seed names.

solid_solution_axis.note: Ag/(Ag+Pd) spans 0.14-0.39 over the three compositions. This axis is NOT isoelectronic: Ag is group 11 and Pd group 10, so each Ag adds an electron and progressively fills the Pd 4d band, which is the whole point of the alloy series. The automatic detector does not flag it for that reason, but the prototype is unchanged along it.
solid_solution_axis.axis_check: Different groups, same fcc site -- valence-changing alloying rather than isoelectronic substitution.

reference_disagreement: MP offers only ordered Ag3Pd I4/mmm mp-985296 and AgPd R-3m mp-1229012, both flagged AMBIGUOUS and both computed orderings of a system that is disordered at these temperatures, so mp_id is null. The hydrogen the paper studies is not in the composition strings and therefore not in this record.

basis: Ag2Se1-xTex at x = 0.2-0.5, with Ag2Se0.5Te0.5 carrying 13 of 16 samples: the orthorhombic beta-Ag2Se naumannite structure with Te on the chalcogen site, which the second paper presents as a near-room-temperature thermoelectric. The measured window runs from 296 to 622 K and Ag2Se turns superionic near 400 K, so both the ordered low-temperature phase and the bcc superionic phase are inside it.

solid_solution_axis.note: Se/(Se+Te) spans 0.50-0.80 with a median of 0.70. At the Te-rich end the parent is Ag2Te, which is monoclinic rather than naumannite and has no taxonomy entry, so the prototype recorded here is only safe for the Se-rich half; and the superionic transition temperature moves with x, so the 400 K value cannot cover the whole host.
solid_solution_axis.axis_check: Se and Te are the same group on the same anion site.

reference_disagreement: No reference line is offered for this host at all, so both phases carry a null mp_id and the transition temperature comes from materials knowledge rather than from the papers or the references. This host belongs in the review queue.

basis: AlxCoCrFeNi at x = 0.25 to 2 across 15 compositions, and the first paper is titled for high-entropy alloys as high-temperature thermoelectric materials. The structure is deliberately not a single space group along that series -- low Al is the fcc A1 solid solution, high Al the bcc/B2 ordered one, with a two-phase field between -- which is exactly what the high_entropy_alloy entry exists to carry rather than forcing one prototype.
reference_disagreement: No reference line is offered for this five-element host, so mp_id is null. A database of ordered structures cannot represent a five-component random solid solution directly, and stage 2 should record fcc or bcc per composition instead of looking for an entry.

dopant_roles.basis: The second paper is titled for the effect of scandium ternary intergrain precipitates, so Sc is a deliberate grain-boundary phase rather than a solute in the matrix.

basis: Mn2VAl is 13 of 16 samples and MP gives Mn2AlV Fm-3m mp-10895 at hull 0.000 with 2 ICSD references: the L2_1 full Heusler, and the second paper is titled for a half-metallic full-Heusler. The curator details record antisite-defect fractions of 14-50%, which is disorder on that same L2_1 lattice -- the first paper is about the impact of order degree on the power factor -- and disorder of this kind changes the space group of a real sample without changing the prototype, so it is noted rather than assigned.

dopant_roles.basis: Mn2V(Al1-xSix) at x = 0.02-0.06: one electron more on the main-group site, which shifts the Fermi level in the half-metallic gap. A genuine dilute doping series.

basis: Every composition is Al-doped ZnO at x up to 0.12 -- Zn(Al)O, Al0.1Zn0.9O, (Zn0.876Al0.124)O -- grown mostly as highly oriented epitaxial films and powders. The transport being measured is that of the wurtzite ZnO matrix with Al as a shallow donor, which the papers on crystal-orientation-dependent properties and on Al- and Sn-doped ZnO nanoparticles are about.
reference_disagreement: assigned sg [186], ICSD-backed references for this host report [227]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: Every composition is BayFe4-xMxSb12: the Ba-filled skutterudite, MP Ba(FeSb3)4 Im-3 mp-1189647 at hull 0.000. The filling is not optional here -- the FeSb3 framework does not exist without a guest, unlike CoSb3 -- so the unfilled skutterudite entry never applies, and the Ba0.87 and Ba0.99 compositions are filling-fraction variation on the host site rather than doping. The papers are on BayFe4-xCoxSb12 and on rattling in filled skutterudites.

dopant_roles.basis: BaIn0.5Fe3.7Co0.3Sb12: In is a second guest species in the icosahedral void alongside Ba, the double-filling strategy for scattering a wider phonon band, not a substituent on a framework site.

BayFe4-xCoxSb12, the series of the third paper: Co on the framework transition-metal site sets the electron count and hence the filling fraction y, which the curator note records as falling from 0.99 at x=0 to 0.60 at x=3.
BaFe4-xPtxSb12 at x = 0.1-0.2: the same framework site, a heavier substituent.

basis: Every composition is Ba8Ga16(Si,Ge)30 to within the refinement scatter: the type I clathrate, with Ba8 guests in the dodecahedral and tetrakaidecahedral cages of a group-14 framework and Ga16 setting the framework electron count. All three papers are on Si-Ge type I clathrates, and the framework composition varies only in the Si:Ge ratio.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: the group-14 framework site of the type I cage
solid_solution_axis.note: Ge/(Ge+Si) spans 0.55-0.89 over 12 compositions. Both end members form the same type I clathrate with Ba and Ga, so the prototype holds across the axis; what changes is the cage size and the mass contrast, which is what all three papers are measuring.
solid_solution_axis.axis_check: Si and Ge are the same group and share the framework site.

reference_disagreement: No reference line is offered for this four-element host, so mp_id is null. Stage 2 should resolve Ba8Ga16Ge30 and Ba8Ga16Si30 separately and interpolate rather than seek one quaternary entry.

basis: Bi2Ir2O7 is 8 of 16 samples and the substituted members are Y0.4Bi1.6Ir2O7 and Bi2-xSrxIr2O7: the A2B2O7 pyrochlore, and two of the papers name the structure directly -- the Bi2-xSrxIr2O7 pyrochlore solid solution and the pyrochlore iridates of the third. The A-site substitutions keep the 2:2:7 stoichiometry throughout.
reference_disagreement: assigned sg [227], ICSD-backed references for this host report [62]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

dopant_roles.basis: Bi2-xSrxIr2O7 at x = 0.1-0.4: divalent Sr on the trivalent A site is the hole-doping variable of the solid solution the second paper reports.
Y0.4Bi1.6Ir2O7 sits on the Y2Ir2O7-Bi2Ir2O7 join of the first paper, so Y is an alloying end member on the A site rather than a dilute dopant.
Another rare earth on the same A site of the pyrochlore.

basis: Every composition is CaxFe4Sb12 at x = 0.91 to 1, plus one CaFe3.5Co0.5Sb12: the Ca-filled skutterudite, MP Ca(FeSb3)4 Im-3 mp-13464 at hull 0.000 with 2 ICSD references. The seed offers both skutterudite and filled_skutterudite, but there is no unfilled composition in this host and there cannot be one -- binary FeSb3 is not stable without a guest -- so the hypothesis is refined to the filled entry alone and the x below 1 is filling-fraction variation, which the third paper studies as the mechanism for low thermal conductivity.

dopant_roles.basis: CaFe3.5Co0.5Sb12: Co on the framework transition-metal site adds electrons and reduces the filling fraction the framework requires. At 12.5% of the site it is an alloying level rather than dilute doping.

basis: CeInCu2 is the largest composition and MP gives CeInCu2 Fm-3m mp-19834 at hull 0.000 with 5 ICSD references -- the L2_1 Heusler ordering of the MnCu2Al type, the heavy-fermion compound of the first and third papers. The host is not one structure, though: CeCu5In and (Ce,La)Cu5In are Cu-rich AB5-derived phases, and CeCu4In is the cubic MgCu4Sn type, which the taxonomy does not carry. MP also lists CeInCu P-62m mp-20665, the ZrNiAl type proposed in this chunk for La-Rh-Sn, showing how many stoichiometries this chemistry supports.
reference_disagreement: No reference entry is offered at the CeCu5In or CeCu4In stoichiometries that make up most of the compositions, so those are recorded as alternatives without an mp_id. Calling CeCu4In the MgCu4Sn type comes from the structure literature, not from the refs, and the taxonomy has no entry for it -- worth adding if the family recurs.

dopant_roles.basis: (Ce1-xLax)Cu5In at x = 0.15-0.3: non-magnetic dilution of the Kondo lattice, the standard reference measurement rather than carrier doping.
The third paper is on CeInCu2-yAgy, so Ag shares the transition-metal site of the Heusler with Cu.

basis: CeRu2Si2 with its La- and Rh-substituted variants is 15 of 16 samples: the ThCr2Si2 122, MP Ce(SiRu)2 I4/mmm mp-3566 at hull 0.000 with 10 ICSD references. This is the archetypal metamagnetic heavy fermion and all three papers are about that compound. The single CeRuSi2 sample is a different stoichiometry, which MP places at CeSi2Ru P2_1/m mp-1025521.

dopant_roles.basis: Ce0.87La0.13Ru2Si2 and Ce0.95La0.05Ru2Si2: non-magnetic dilution of the Ce sublattice, used to separate single-ion from coherent Kondo behaviour.
Ce(Ru0.92Rh0.08)2Si2: an extra electron on the transition-metal site, which is how the metamagnetic transition field of CeRu2Si2 is tuned.

basis: La0.6Sr0.4Co1-xFexO3 -- LSCF, 8 of 16 samples -- is the disordered ABO3 perovskite with Co and Fe sharing the B site. LaSrCoFeO6 and SrLaFeCoO6 are the same elements at 1:1 written as a double perovskite, and the first paper is titled for enhancing the power factor by inducing octahedral order, so B-site ordering is the experimental variable and ordered and disordered samples coexist at the same composition in this host.
reference_disagreement: MP offers only computed Sr-La-Fe-Co-O supercells (Sr2La2FeCoO8 Amm2, four R3m/R-3m 15-oxygen orderings), none with an ICSD reference and none the rhombohedral LSCF these samples are, so mp_id is null. R-3c is recorded as the spacegroup because that is the usual tilt system for LSCF at x = 0.4, not because a reference supports it.

basis: TiFexCoySb across 10 compositions: Fe-doped TiCoSb, the 18-electron half-Heusler F-43m that MP carries as TiFeCoSb mp-998973, and the first paper is on p-type Fe-doped TiCoSb half-Heuslers. The Fe and Co totals run both above and below 1 (TiFe0.29Co0.78Sb, TiFe0.665Co0.5Sb), which is the off-stoichiometry the third paper builds its Ti1+xFe1.33-xSb-TiCoSb series from -- excess transition metal partially fills the vacant fourth site of the half-Heusler cell, moving towards the full Heusler without leaving the family.
reference_disagreement: MP places TiFeCoSb at hull 0.198, i.e. formally well above stability, though the compound is routinely synthesised and is the subject of three papers in this host. As with TaFeSb in the same chunk, e_above_hull is not usable as a filter for half-Heuslers.

dopant_roles.basis: TiFe0.4256Co0.68Sb0.875Sn0.125: one electron fewer on the main-group site, the p-type doping variable, and at 12.5% of the site an alloying level.

basis: LaCo1-xMnxO3 with Sr, Pb or Ca on the A site is the disordered ABO3 perovskite, and La0.95Sr0.05Co1-xMnxO3 at x = 0.33, 0.5 and 0.67 is a straightforward B-site solid solution. La2CoMnO6 is the B-site ordered double perovskite instead, and (LaCoO3)0.5(La0.7Sr0.3MnO3)0.5 is a two-phase composite by construction -- the first paper is on exactly that composite -- so three different things share this host.
reference_disagreement: The reference cannot separate the two orderings of La2MnCoO6: MP gives P2_1/c mp-19208 as PRIMARY with 5 ICSD references but flags it AMBIGUOUS, while the C2/m ordering mp-1105414 carries 6 at hull 0.007. That is a real ambiguity in the literature about the degree of Mn/Co order, not a ranking artefact, so neither mp_id is taken.

dopant_roles.basis: La0.95Sr0.05Co1-xMnxO3 and the La0.7Sr0.3MnO3 half of the composite: divalent Sr on the A site is the hole-doping variable of both manganites and cobaltites.
La0.98Pb0.02Mn0.74Co0.25O3, the single crystal of the third paper: divalent Pb on the A site, the same acceptor role as Sr.
Divalent non-magnetic Mg most plausibly occupies the B site alongside Co and Mn, but no composition string carrying it is shown, so the site is inferred from the chemistry alone.
A further 3d cation on the B site, continuous with the manganite-ferrite join.

basis: All five compositions are LaCo1-xRhxO3 at x = 0.3 to 0.7, from the single paper on the LaCo1-xRhxO3 solid solution. Co and Rh are both trivalent group-9 cations on the perovskite B site, so the series is one continuous ABO3 phase; the lattice crossover and mixed valency the paper reports are changes in spin state and bond length within that structure, not a change of prototype.

solid_solution_axis.note: Co/(Co+Rh) spans 0.30-0.70 with a median of exactly 0.50, so every composition in this host is a genuine alloy rather than a doped end member. Both end members LaCoO3 and LaRhO3 are the same prototype, so no parent compound needs to be chosen per composition here -- unusually for a detected axis.
solid_solution_axis.axis_check: Co and Rh are both group 9 and trivalent on the same octahedral site.

reference_disagreement: No reference line is offered for this host, so mp_id is null. R-3c is recorded as the spacegroup from LaCoO3, but the Rh-rich end is orthorhombic Pnma like LaRhO3, so the tilt system changes along the axis even though the prototype does not.

basis: CuInSe2 is the largest composition and TEDesignLab gives InCuSe2 I-42d (122) mp-22811 at hull 0.000 with 41 ICSD references -- the best-attested entry anywhere in this chunk -- and the second and third papers are on p-type CuInSe2 chalcopyrites. The CuIn3Se5-type compositions (CuIn3Se4.9Te0.1 and its neighbours) are not chalcopyrite: they are the In-rich ordered-vacancy compounds of the same family, so the host splits on the In:Cu ratio, 1 for chalcopyrite and 3 for the OVC.
reference_disagreement: MP ranks In9(CuSe4)4 P-43m mp-21827 first and offers In2CuSe4, In3CuSe5, In11Cu9Se20 and In8Cu7Se16, several in P1 -- computed orderings of the In-rich vacancy compounds rather than the ambient chalcopyrite. TEDesignLab is followed for the main phase; for the OVC compositions the symmetry is unresolved, as it was for Ag-In-Se in chunk 008.

dopant_roles.basis: Isovalent-pair doping with Zn is the enhancement the second paper reports; divalent Zn on the monovalent Cu site is a donor, and it may also sit on In, which stage 2 should resolve.
CuIn1-xMnxSe2 at x = 0.05-0.1: a magnetic cation on the trivalent site.
CuIn3Se5-xTex at x = 0.05-0.2: Te on the anion site of the ordered-vacancy compositions, isoelectronic and dilute on that sublattice.

basis: (Ru0.5Cu0.5)(Sr,Nd)2(Nd,Ce)2Cu2O10 accounts for 5 of the 16 compositions listed and is the Ru-1222 ruthenocuprate: the RuSr2RCu2O8 stacking with a fluorite (Nd,Ce)2O2 block inserted, which the first paper studies with Ba substitution. Nd1.38Ce0.22Sr0.4CuO4 is a different structure entirely -- the T* 214 cuprate of the second paper, a K2NiF4-derived single layer with mixed T and T-prime oxygen coordination -- so the host splits on the Ru content.
reference_disagreement: MP offers only SrNd2(CuO3)2 in I4/mmm and I4mm and a lead-bearing Sr5CeNd3Cu4PbO18, none with an ICSD reference and none at the 1222 stoichiometry, so mp_id is null. The ruthenocuprate entry itself is named in the taxonomy for the Gd member; the Nd/Ce variant here has a fluorite block the 1212 parent does not, which stage 2 must not flatten.

dopant_roles.basis: Ce is a constituent of the (Nd1.34Ce0.66)2O2 fluorite block of the 1222 and, in the 214 sample, the electron-doping variable of Nd2-xCexCuO4. Either way it is a structural component at 66% of a site, not a dilute impurity; it reads as a dopant candidate only because the formula unit is large.
Ru is half of the (Ru0.5Cu0.5) charge-reservoir layer, which is what makes these compounds ruthenocuprates at all.
The first paper is on Ba doping of (Ru,Cu)(Sr,Nd)2(Nd,Ce)2Cu2O10, with Ba replacing Sr in the rock-salt block at up to 0.5 of the site.

basis: Every composition is Sm2-xCexCuO4 at x = 0 to 0.15: the electron-doped T-prime 214 cuprate, MP Sm2CuO4 I4/mmm mp-4210 with 5 ICSD references, and the third paper is on the anomalous thermopower of Sm2-xCexCuO4. T-prime differs from La2CuO4 T by having no apical oxygen, but both are n=1 K2NiF4-derived layers, and the taxonomy already files Nd2CuO4 -- the Cu-Nd-O host -- under ruddlesden_popper, so this follows that precedent rather than inventing a parallel entry.
reference_disagreement: A taxonomy caveat rather than a reference one: ruddlesden_popper is exemplified by La2CuO4, which is the T structure with apical oxygen, while these samples are T-prime. The structure to resolve in stage 2 is Nd2CuO4-type, not La2CuO4-type -- the two have the same I4/mmm symmetry and different anion arrangements, so a lookup by space group alone would not catch the difference.

dopant_roles.basis: Sm2-xCexCuO4: tetravalent Ce on the rare-earth site is the electron-doping variable of the T-prime cuprates, and at x up to 0.15 the upper end is an alloying level rather than dilute doping.

basis: One composition, LiF, across 16 samples in three papers on phonon thermal conductivity and isotope scattering. MP gives LiF Fm-3m mp-1138 at hull 0.000 with 8 ICSD references: the rocksalt halide, and nothing in the measured range perturbs it.

other_polymorphs.note: The CsCl-type phase at hull 0.273 with 1 ICSD reference is the high-pressure form of LiF; heating at ambient pressure does not reach it.
No ICSD reference; a computed hypothetical polymorph at hull 0.008.

basis: (La0.3Sr0.7)1-yTi0.3Fe0.7O3-delta and La0.5Sr0.5Fe0.5Ti0.5O3: a simple ABO3 perovskite with two cations on each site, in which the A-site deficiency (y = 0 to 0.09) and the matching oxygen deficiency are the experimental variables -- the second paper is a neutron structural characterisation of exactly these oxygen-deficient perovskites. Both are defect concentrations on the perovskite lattice, not different prototypes.
reference_disagreement: MP offers only two computed SrLaTiFeO6 orderings, F-43m mp-1218147 at hull 0.034 and Fmm2 mp-1218316, i.e. B-site ordered double perovskites with no ICSD backing. These samples are B-site disordered and A-site deficient, so mp_id is null; a database entry at the ordered 1:1 composition would be the wrong structure for them.

dopant_roles.basis: The third paper is on Co- and Ti-substituted SrFeO3, so Co takes the B site alongside Fe and Ti.

basis: TaFeSb with Ti on the Ta site is the whole host, 8 of 16 samples being the undoped compound: the 18-electron half-Heusler F-43m, and the second paper is titled for the discovery of TaFeSb-based half-Heuslers with high thermoelectric performance. The Ti1-x series is a clean single-site doping study on that structure.
reference_disagreement: MP places TaFeSb mp-631267 at hull 0.777 with no ICSD reference, which as a stability filter would reject the compound outright. It is nonetheless synthesised, high-pressure-sintered and measured in three papers here. This is the clearest case in the chunk of e_above_hull being unusable, and the mp_id is taken for the structure only, not as evidence that the phase is stable.

dopant_roles.basis: Ta1-xTixFeSb at x = 0.02-0.12: one electron fewer on the Ta site, the p-type doping variable that sets the carrier concentration in this family.

basis: The dominant series is (GaSb)1-x(Ga2Te3)x -- written as (GaSb)2.25(Ga2Te3)0.25 and (GaSb)2.7(Ga2Te3)0.1, and as Ga7Sb2Te10 and Ga12Sb2Te15 -- which is zincblende GaSb alloyed with Ga2Te3. Ga2Te3 is itself a defect zincblende with one third of the cation sites vacant, so the whole join is one tetrahedral framework carrying a rising concentration of ordered cation vacancies, and the third paper is on (GaSb)3(1-x)(Ga2Te3)x. GaSb5Te9 is Sb- and Te-rich enough to be a tetradymite-based phase instead, and nothing in the chunk resolves it.
reference_disagreement: No reference line is offered for this host at all, so mp_id is null throughout and the assignment rests on the pseudo-binary the papers name. Stage 2 should resolve GaSb and Ga2Te3 separately; the vacancy-ordered superstructures of the Ga2Te3-rich end are their own problem and may need more than one entry.

dopant_roles.basis: Ga2Cu0.05Sb0.3Te2.65 carries Cu at a dilute level on the cation sublattice of a Te-rich composition.

basis: Ge1-xMnxTe with Bi, Sb or Na is the whole host: rhombohedral GeTe with Mn on the cation site. The transition line is the point of the host rather than an incidental crossing -- the first paper is on suppressing the transition temperature to achieve cubic GeTe and the third on rhombohedral-to-cubic conversion of GeTe via MnTe alloying -- so Mn drives the R3m to Fm-3m transition down through the measured 299-827 K window, and at GeMnTe2 the material is already cubic at room temperature. Both phases are therefore present across the host at different compositions as well as at different temperatures.
reference_disagreement: The 700 K transition temperature is the taxonomy default and is known to be wrong for most of this host: the papers report it falling steeply with Mn content, to below room temperature at high x. It is recorded as a default rather than adjusted because no paper has been read, and this host should be high in the review queue. MP offers only computed MnGeTe2 orderings (P4/mmm mp-1221610 at hull 0.070, R-3m mp-1221803 at 0.451), neither an ICSD-backed GeTe polymorph, so both phases carry a null mp_id.

dopant_roles.basis: Ge0.86Mn0.1Bi0.04Te through Ge0.66Mn0.3Bi0.04Te: trivalent Bi on the Ge site is the n-type donor that compensates the intrinsic Ge-vacancy holes. In Ge0.7Na0.15Bi0.15MnTe2 it is instead half of a NaBiTe2 alloying pair.
Paired with Bi in equal amounts in the GeMnTe2-NaBiTe2 alloys of the second paper, so charge-balanced alloying rather than acceptor doping.
The same donor role as Bi on the cation site, a lighter homologue.

basis: GeTe1-xSex with a median Se share of 0.20: mostly rhombohedral GeTe with Se on the anion site, and the second paper is on the influence of Se substitution in GeTe. At the Se-rich end the structure becomes orthorhombic Pnma GeSe -- (GeSe)0.95(Sb2Te3)0.05 is on that side -- and the third paper is once more the AgSbSe2-stabilised cubic rocksalt germanium selenide, so all three IV-VI structures appear along one composition axis. GeTe also converts to rocksalt near 700 K, inside the measured 295-796 K window.

solid_solution_axis.note: Se/(Se+Te) spans 0.10-0.86 over 15 compositions with a median of 0.20. Unlike most detected axes this one crosses a prototype boundary: the Te-rich end is rhombohedral GeTe and the Se-rich end orthorhombic GeSe, so the parent must be chosen per composition. The transition temperature also moves along the axis -- Se substitution raises it -- which is why the 700 K value is only a default.
solid_solution_axis.axis_check: Se and Te are the same group on the same anion site.

dopant_roles.basis: A donor on the Ge site, the standard compensation for Ge vacancies in GeTe.
The same donor role; in (GeSe)0.95(Sb2Te3)0.05 Sb arrives as part of an Sb2Te3 alloying addition instead.
Monovalent Ag on the cation site is an acceptor, and paired with Sb it is the AgSbSe2 alloying that stabilises the cubic phase.
Another monovalent acceptor on the cation site, at a dilute level.

basis: La1-xSrxVO3 at x = 0 to 0.18 is every composition: the orthorhombic Pnma perovskite vanadate, MP LaVO3 mp-19350 at hull 0.000 with 8 ICSD references, and the second paper is on thermoelectric response near the Mott transition, which is what Sr doping of LaVO3 drives.
reference_disagreement: TEDesignLab covers only LaVO4, the orthovanadate, in monoclinic P2_1/c and tetragonal I4_1/amd. That is a different compound from the LaVO3 perovskite these samples are -- V5+ isolated tetrahedra against V3+ corner-shared octahedra -- so the ICSD-backed reference simply does not cover the phase, and MP is used instead. This is also the pair the README cites as having band gaps of 3.50 and 3.15 eV for the two LaVO4 polymorphs, neither relevant here.

dopant_roles.basis: La1-xSrxVO3 at x = 0.1-0.18: divalent Sr on the A site is the band-filling variable that drives the Mott transition, not an impurity. At these levels it is a heavy doping series.

basis: Ca0.2La2.8Rh4Sn13 is 13 of 16 samples: the R3T4Sn13 Remeika phase, cubic Pm-3n, which MP gives as La3Sn13Rh4 mp-30513 at hull 0.000 with 5 ICSD references -- a caged stannide whose rattling Sn cages are why the second paper studies atomic-scale disorder and superconductivity in it. The taxonomy had no 3-4-13 entry, so it is proposed before use. LaRhSn (3 samples) is the equiatomic ZrNiAl-type hexagonal phase instead, also proposed here, so the host holds two prototypes and splits on the Rh:Sn ratio.

dopant_roles.basis: Ca0.2La2.8Rh4Sn13: Ca on the rare-earth site at 7% of it is the disorder and hole-doping variable of the second paper, which is about increasing atomic-scale disorder by doping. It falls below the 5 at.% cut only because the formula unit has 20 atoms.

basis: (Mg1-xZnx)3Sb2 across the whole host, with Zn reaching 55% of the cation site: the CaAl2Si2-type trigonal Zintl structure of Mg3Sb2, with Zn taking the tetrahedral Mg site of the [Mg2Sb2] slab. The first paper is titled for isostructural (Mg1-xZnx)3Sb2 and the second for the structural properties of Mg3-xZnxSb2 up to x = 1.34, so the series is isostructural by construction.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: the tetrahedral cation site of the CaAl2Si2-type slab
solid_solution_axis.note: Zn/(Mg+Zn) spans 0.10-0.55 over the listed compositions. The automatic detector did not flag this host because Mg is group 2 and Zn group 12, but both are divalent on the same site and the papers treat it as one continuous isostructural series, so it is recorded as an axis anyway.
solid_solution_axis.axis_check: Different groups, same site and same valence -- chemically isoelectronic even though the group test fails.

reference_disagreement: MP offers Mg(ZnSb)2 P-3m1 mp-1210585 at hull 0.021 and several Mg-rich binaries, none with an ICSD reference. The P-3m1 entry is the right structure type but at the 1:2 composition rather than the 3:2 of these samples, so mp_id is left null and stage 2 should resolve Mg3Sb2 and interpolate along the Zn axis.
