dopant_roles.basis: Monovalent Na on the octahedral Mg site is the standard p-type acceptor for Mg3Sb2 and is what the third paper uses to reach high p-type performance.
Divalent Yb on the octahedral cation site, isovalent and used for mass contrast rather than doping.

basis: Two silicates, both measured as environmental barrier coatings. Y2Si2O7 is 11 of 16 samples: the rare-earth disilicate built from corner-shared Si2O7 dimers, whose beta polymorph is the thortveitite C2/m structure TEDesignLab gives as mp-5652. Y2SiO5 is the other 5: the X2 monosilicate of isolated SiO4 tetrahedra, MP C2/c mp-3520 with 4 ICSD references. They are different structures and the taxonomy carried neither, so both are proposed and the host splits on the Si:Y ratio.
reference_disagreement: TEDesignLab marks Y2Si2O7 C2/m mp-5652 AMBIGUOUS, at 2 ICSD references against 2 for P2_1/c mp-7999, and it is right to: Y2Si2O7 has at least five polymorphs whose stability fields lie inside the plasma-spray and sintering range these coatings are made in, so which one a given sample is cannot be settled from composition. The mp_id is recorded for the beta polymorph with medium confidence and stage 2 needs the paper.

basis: Pb1-xSnxSe, and the two end members are different structures, so the host cannot have one prototype. The median Pb share is 0.16, i.e. most compositions are Sn0.85Pb0.15Se and sit on the SnSe side, which is orthorhombic Pnma GeS-type; Pb0.854Sn0.15Se0.998Cl0.002 is on the PbSe side and is rocksalt. The first paper is titled for the Pb1-xSnxSe solid solution and the other two for polycrystalline SnSe alloyed with Pb, so both ends are deliberately sampled. The SnSe-side compositions also cross the Pnma to Cmcm transition inside the measured 296-925 K window.

solid_solution_axis.note: Pb/(Pb+Sn) spans 0.10-0.85 with a median of 0.16 over 16 compositions. This axis crosses a prototype boundary rather than staying within one: PbSe is cubic rocksalt and SnSe orthorhombic Pnma, so the parent must be chosen per composition. Pb alloying also lowers the SnSe Pnma-to-Cmcm transition temperature, so the 800 K default cannot hold along the whole axis.
solid_solution_axis.axis_check: Pb and Sn are the same group on the same cation site.

reference_disagreement: The three MP entries offered (Sn2PbSe3 P-3m1 mp-1219016, SnPb4Se5 R-3m mp-1218958, SnPbSe2 R-3m mp-1218938) are all computed ternary orderings with no ICSD backing, and none is rocksalt or Pnma. They describe hypothetical ordered ternaries, not the disordered pseudobinary these samples are, so mp_id is left null and stage 2 should resolve PbSe and SnSe separately.

dopant_roles.basis: Pb0.854Sn0.15Se0.998Cl0.002: a halide on the anion site is the standard n-type donor for the IV-VI rocksalts.
Sn0.88Pb0.12Na0.01Se: monovalent Na on the cation site is the standard p-type acceptor for SnSe and PbSe alike.
The same anion-site donor role as Cl.

basis: Elemental palladium with dilute transition-metal solutes at or below 3 at.%: face-centred cubic Pd, MP mp-2 at hull 0.000 with 20 ICSD references, measured from 10 to 297 K. Fe0.001Pd and Fe0.0004Pd are the giant-moment dilute alloys of the millikelvin thermopower paper and Pd0.97Ce0.03 a Kondo alloy; none of them changes the fcc host lattice.
note: Pd0.97Ce0.03H0.05 is the hydrogenated sample of the first paper, and the curator detail records the alpha-plus-beta two-phase hydride field. Beta-PdH is the interstitial_hydride entry, whose exemplar is already PdH0.66 and whose example host is H-Pd; it keeps the fcc Pd sublattice and only fills octahedral voids, so the host is not marked mixed, but that one composition is the reason interstitial_hydride is listed as an alternative.

dopant_roles.basis: Fe0.001Pd and Fe0.0002Pd: dilute Fe on the Pd site carries the giant induced moment that the millikelvin thermopower paper is about.
Pd-Ru is a substitutional solid solution and the third paper measures it from 50 mK.
Neighbouring transition metal, fully substitutional on the fcc site.
Pd0.97Ce0.03: a dilute Kondo impurity on the Pd site; Ce is much larger than Pd so the solubility limit is nearby.
Pd0.97Ce0.03H0.05: hydrogen dissolves into octahedral voids of the fcc lattice rather than replacing Pd, which is what the hydrogenated-palladium paper measures.

basis: SmSx over x = 0.8 to 1.5, which is not one structure. Stoichiometric SmS is 7 of 16 samples and is rocksalt, MP mp-1269 at hull 0.000 with 21 ICSD references. The sulphur-rich compositions SmS1.333, SmS1.355, SmS1.375, SmS1.414 and SmS1.501 lie on the Sm3-xS4 line between Sm3S4 and Sm2S3, which is the Th3P4 defect series with ordered cation vacancies -- exactly the La3-xTe4 case the th3p4 entry names, MP Sm3S4 I-43d mp-2038 with 7 ICSD references. So the host splits on the S:Sm ratio at about x = 1.33.
note: SmS also has the famous black-to-gold valence transition, but it is isostructural -- rocksalt on both sides, only the lattice parameter and the Sm valence change -- so it is not a prototype change and is not recorded in phases. It is pressure-driven in stoichiometric SmS and so is not crossed by the 11-999 K measurements here.
reference_disagreement: MP also offers Sm2S3 Pnma mp-1403 with 4 ICSD references. The orthorhombic alpha form is the low-temperature Sm2S3 polymorph, but the samples at x near 1.5 come from a continuous SmSx series prepared in one run, which points at the vacancy-ordered cubic gamma (Th3P4) form rather than at alpha. Composition cannot separate them, so th3p4 is recorded with the caveat rather than Pnma.

basis: Every composition is Ca1-xCexAg1-ySb with x near 0.16 and y from 0 to 0.15, which is exactly the series the JACS paper is titled for. The equiatomic CaAgSb parent takes the hexagonal ZrBeSi type -- an ordered AlB2 derivative with an Ag-Sb honeycomb and Ca between the layers -- the structure of the isostructural CaAgAs and CaAgP. The taxonomy has the binary AlB2 parent only, so the ordered ternary is proposed before use. Ce substitutes for Ca on the interlayer site and the Ag vacancies are the carrier knob, which is what the Chem. Mater. paper on defect chemistry addresses.
reference_disagreement: This host carries no reference line at all -- neither TEDesignLab nor Materials Project offers an entry -- so nothing here is backed by ICSD and mp_id stays null. Confidence is medium for that reason and not because the compositions are unclear. The second paper is titled for phase transitions in this system, so a second structure may well appear once the paper is read.

basis: AgGaTe2 and its Ag-deficient variants are 7 of 15 samples and are chalcopyrite, TEDesignLab GaAgTe2 I-42d mp-4899 at hull 0.000 with 7 ICSD references, and two of the three papers name the chalcopyrite structure in their titles. Ag9GaTe6 is the other phase present: an argyrodite, not a diamond-like ternary, so the host holds two prototypes and splits on the Ag:Ga ratio.
reference_disagreement: The MP primary for this chemistry is Ga12Ag2Te19 P1 mp-675033 at hull 0.055, a computed triclinic entry with no ICSD backing, and the second MP entry puts GaAgTe2 in P-4m2 rather than I-42d. TEDesignLab is preferred here, per the project precedence: it is ICSD-backed and gives the I-42d chalcopyrite the papers name.

dopant_roles.basis: AgGa0.95Cu0.05Te2, and the second paper is titled for the effect of Cu doping into the Ga site. Cu is monovalent against trivalent Ga, so it is an acceptor.
Divalent on the trivalent group-III site, an acceptor in the same way as Cu.
Same divalent-for-trivalent acceptor role as Zn.
Divalent on the group-III site.
One composition only, and neither site nor valence can be judged from the formula; Nb is an unusual substituent in a I-III-VI2 chalcopyrite and may be a processing addition.

basis: Al1-xInxN across the full range, grown as films and one single crystal, and all three papers are titled for Al1-xInxN or lattice-matched InAlN. AlN and InN are both wurtzite and mix continuously on the cation site, so the whole axis is one structure; the lattice-matched InAlN of the third paper is the x near 0.82 composition grown on GaN, still wurtzite.

other_polymorphs.note: Zincblende AlN and InN can be stabilised epitaxially on cubic substrates, and 8 of the 15 samples are films, so the chunk file flags the possibility. The papers grow on GaN or on semi-insulating substrates that select the wurtzite polytype, so it is not put in the thermal sequence.

solid_solution_axis.note: Al/(Al+In) spans 0.12-0.83 with a median of 0.55 over 12 compositions. Unlike most axes in this set this one does not cross a prototype boundary -- both end members are wurtzite -- so the structure is constant and only the band gap and lattice parameter move along it. There is a wide miscibility gap in AlInN, so mid-range films are metastable and may be phase-separated.
solid_solution_axis.axis_check: Al and In are the same group on the same cation site.

reference_disagreement: No reference line is offered for this host at all, so the assignment rests on the compositions and the nitride literature; mp_id stays null.

basis: Elemental gold and dilute solutes at or below 4 at.%, written in at.% form: Au96.99Pd3.01, Au98.99Pt1.01, Au96.5Mn3.5. Face-centred cubic Au, MP mp-81 at hull 0.000 with 15 ICSD references, and the third paper uses thin gold wires as the reference standard for thermopower measurement, which only works because the host is plain fcc Au.

dopant_roles.basis: Au-Pd is a continuous fcc solid solution; at 3-4 at.% it is dilute substitutional.
Same fcc substitutional role, at 1-2 at.%.
Au96.5Mn3.5, and the first paper is titled for dilute alloys of Mn in noble metals: a local-moment Kondo impurity on the Au site.

basis: Not a ternary compound at all: the curator records SiC-70wt.%B4C, 30wt%B4C and simply mixture, and all three papers are titled for SiC-B4C composites. Each sample is two separate crystalline phases, silicon carbide and boron carbide, so the host is a mechanical mixture and neither single prototype describes a sample. The Al2O3 in two compositions is a sintering aid, a third phase.
note: The detected C/(C+Si) axis spanning 0.50-0.74 is an artefact of writing a two-phase mixture as one formula: C and Si do not share a site here, they belong to different phases, and moving along that ratio changes the SiC:B4C phase fraction rather than a site occupancy. It is recorded as null rather than as an isoelectronic series for that reason.

dopant_roles.basis: (Al2O3)0.02Si0.75B0.92C: alumina added at 5wt% as a sintering aid, per the curator detail, so it is a separate oxide phase and not a substituent in either carbide.
Arrives only as the oxygen of that Al2O3 addition.

basis: Every composition is Ba8Ga16ZnxGe30-x with x near 3, the classic type I germanium clathrate: 8 Ba guests in the cages of a 46-atom Ga-Zn-Ge framework, and all three papers are titled for Ba8Ga16ZnxGe30-x or Zn-substituted germanium clathrates. Ba8Zn6Ga4Ge36 is the same framework with the Zn:Ga ratio shifted, not a different structure.
note: Zn sits above the 5 at.% cut so it is a host element and gets no dopant_roles entry, but its role is framework substitution: Zn and Ga both replace Ge in the covalent cage and together set the electron count that makes these samples p-type, which is what the Ga content paper varies. No reference line is offered for this host, so mp_id stays null.

basis: Every composition is an AxNb2O6 niobate of the tetragonal tungsten bronze family: Sr0.25Ba0.75Nb2O6 is SBN, the exemplar the taxonomy entry already names, ((Nd)(Ca,Ba))Nb2O6 is the same filled-bronze framework with Nd and Ca on the A sites, and the third paper is titled for the tungsten bronze Ba6Ti2Nb8O30, which is the A6B10O30 formula unit of the TTB cell written out. The framework is corner-sharing NbO6 octahedra enclosing pentagonal, square and trigonal channels; the A cations fill the two larger ones.
reference_disagreement: TEDesignLab makes BaNb2O6 P2_1/c mp-28150 primary, but on a single ICSD reference, and the monoclinic form is not the bronze these samples are. The MP list is more informative sideways than head-on: Ba2NaNb5O15 P4bm mp-15983 is a tetragonal tungsten bronze in this chemistry, which supports the structure type even though that specific compound contains Na and is not in this host. mp_id is left null: the right entry is an SBN-type bronze at the measured A-site occupancy, and none is offered.

dopant_roles.basis: In Ba6Ti2Nb8O30 Ti occupies octahedral B sites of the bronze framework alongside Nb and sets the Nb4+/Nb5+ balance that makes the material conduct. In BaNb2O6(TiC)0.25 the Ti instead arrives as a TiC addition and is a second phase, so the element has two different roles across this host.
Sr0.25Ba0.75Nb2O6: Sr and Ba share the A channels of the bronze and the second paper scans that ratio; isovalent, so it tunes the structure rather than the carrier count.
Same divalent A-channel site as Sr, in the (Ca,Ba)Nb2O6 composition.
Trivalent Nd on a divalent A site is a donor and the carrier-generating dopant of that composition.
Appears only in BaNb2O6(TiC)0.05 and (TiC)0.25, where TiC is a deliberate conductive second-phase addition and not part of the oxide lattice.

basis: BiTeI and its additions are 10 of 15 samples: the polar layered structure with a I-Bi-Te stacking that lacks inversion symmetry, MP P3m1 mp-22965 at hull 0.000 with 4 ICSD references, and the first paper measures BiTeBr and BiTeI single crystals side by side. The BiI3, CuI and excess-Bi additions of the second paper are second phases in that host, not new structures. Bi2(Se0.07Te0.93)3I0.4 is different: that is tetradymite Bi2Te3 with a little Se and a TeI4 donor addition, per the curator detail, so the host holds two prototypes.

dopant_roles.basis: Bi2(Se0.07Te0.93)3I0.4: Se on the Te anion site of the tetradymite composition, 7 percent of that sublattice, tuning the band structure rather than adding carriers.

(BiTeI)97.62(CuI)2.38: CuI is added as a whole compound, and the paper title lists it alongside BiI3 and excess Bi as additions rather than as site substitution. Whether some Cu enters the lattice needs the paper.
BiTeBr is the isostructural bromide end member of the same polar family, so Br on the halide layer keeps the structure and shifts the Rashba splitting.

basis: Ten of the twelve compositions are Sr4-xCaxFe6O13 with x from 1.6 to 2.8, and the one paper of this host is titled for the synthesis and crystal chemistry of the intergrowth. A4Fe6O13 is not a perovskite, not brownmillerite and not Ruddlesden-Popper: it stacks perovskite blocks with a distinct five-coordinate iron-oxide sheet, so a new prototype is proposed before use. Sr0.4Ca0.6FeO3 is the one simple perovskite composition, so the host splits on the A:Fe ratio.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: the A sites of the perovskite blocks
solid_solution_axis.note: Ca/(Ca+Sr) spans 0.40-0.70 over 12 compositions. Both are divalent on the same A sites, so the axis does not change the structure type, but it does change the tolerance factor and hence the modulation of the intergrowth, which is what the crystal-chemistry paper follows.
solid_solution_axis.axis_check: Ca and Sr are the same group on the same A site.

reference_disagreement: Every MP entry offered for this chemistry is a computed ordering with no ICSD reference -- Sr3Ca(Fe2O5)2 in P1, Sr3Ca(FeO3)4 in Pm marked AMBIGUOUS, Sr4Ca(FeO2)5 in Cmmm -- and none is at the A4Fe6O13 stoichiometry of these samples. They are enumerated cation orderings rather than observed phases, so mp_id is left null.

dopant_roles.basis: Sr2.4Ca1.6Fe5.4Co0.6O13: Co on the iron sites of the intergrowth, used to change the transition-metal valence and the oxygen content.
Same B-site substitution as Co.
Same B-site substitution as Co.
Same B-site substitution; Cu prefers the square-pyramidal sites of the intergrowth sheet, which stage 2 should check once the structure is resolved.

basis: CeCu2Ge2 is 13 of 15 samples and one more is its Co-substituted variant: the body-centred tetragonal ThCr2Si2 structure, MP Ce(CuGe)2 I4/mmm mp-20173 at hull 0.000 with 3 ICSD references, and the heavy-fermion and quantum-criticality papers of this host are all about that compound. Ce2CuGe6 is the one exception and is a different structure entirely.
note: Ce2CuGe6 (1 sample) is the orthorhombic Ce2CuGe6 type, MP Amm2 mp-5684 with 1 ICSD reference, and is the R2MGe6 family the first paper is titled for. The taxonomy has no R2MGe6 entry and one sample does not justify proposing one, so it is parked in unresolved_crystalline rather than folded into the 122 -- the same treatment the README records for bornite.

dopant_roles.basis: Ce(Cu0.9Co0.1)2Ge2: Co on the transition-metal site of the 122, which changes the cell volume and hence the Kondo coupling -- chemical pressure rather than carrier doping.

basis: GdCoO3 and its Ca- and Ni-substituted variants are all four compositions: an ABO3 rare-earth cobaltite, and the first paper is titled for the high-temperature thermoelectric properties of Ln(Co,Ni)O3 across the lanthanide series while the third is about the influence of rare-earth ionic size on those properties. That series is the GdFeO3-type orthorhombic distortion of the perovskite, and Gd sits well inside the distorted regime.
reference_disagreement: assigned sg [62], ICSD-backed references for this host report [221]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

dopant_roles.basis: Gd0.9Ca0.1CoO3 and Gd0.8Ca0.2CoO3: divalent Ca on the trivalent A site is the hole-doping variable of these cobaltites, and at 10-20 percent of that site it is a heavy doping series rather than a dilute impurity.
GdCo0.95Ni0.05O3: Ni on the octahedral B site, which is what the Ln(Co,Ni)O3 paper varies.

basis: Every composition is Ti0.5Zr0.25Hf0.25CoSb with substitutions, and the third paper is titled for (Ti,Zr,Hf)(Co,Pd)Sb half-Heusler alloys: the cubic MgAgAs ordering, an 18-electron semiconductor with Ti/Zr/Hf sharing one site, Co the second and Sb the third. The heavy triple substitution on the M site is the standard mass-disorder route to low lattice thermal conductivity in this family and does not change the prototype.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: the M site of the half-Heusler, shared with Hf
solid_solution_axis.note: Ti/(Ti+Zr) spans 0.31-0.67 with a median of 0.67 over 14 compositions, but the real axis is ternary: Hf occupies the same site at a fixed 0.25 in most compositions. All three are group 4 and isovalent, so the structure is constant along it and the effect is on phonon scattering, not on carrier count.
solid_solution_axis.axis_check: Ti, Zr and Hf are the same group on the same M site.

reference_disagreement: No reference line is offered for this five-element host, so mp_id stays null; stage 2 should resolve TiCoSb and ZrCoSb and interpolate.

dopant_roles.basis: Co0.95Ni0.05: Ni has one more electron than Co, so on the Co site it is the n-type donor that the second paper scans as Co1-xNix.
One fewer valence electron than Sb on the main-group site, the standard p-type counterpart to Ni doping in the CoSb half-Heuslers.

In appears only paired one-to-one with excess Sb -- In0.03...Sb1.03, In0.07...Sb1.07 -- which is the InSb nanoinclusion route rather than site substitution, and the first paper is about optimising the electronic and thermal properties independently, which is what a nanoinclusion does. Whether any In also enters the lattice needs the paper.
The third paper is titled for (Ti,Zr,Hf)(Co,Pd)Sb, so Pd shares the Co site; isoelectronic with Ni it acts as a donor there too.

basis: Ho0.33Sr0.67CoO3-d at three oxygen contents is 12 of 15 samples, and the first paper is titled for the structural, transport and magnetic properties of the cation-ordered cobaltite while the second reports a room-temperature magnetoresistive phase. That family is an A-site-ordered, oxygen-vacancy-ordered perovskite superstructure, which is the class the layered_double_perovskite entry names. It is a refinement of that entry rather than a clean fit: the ordering here is one Ho layer to two Sr layers over a three-layer repeat, not the one-to-one Ln:Ba ordering of the LnBaCo2O5+d exemplar.
note: Two compositions do not parse as perovskites at all: Sr1.65Ho0.35CoO3 and Sr1.6Ho0.4CoO3 put the A cations at twice the Co count, which is an A2BO3 formula that no perovskite has. Either the oxygen index is a transcription problem for the same Ho0.35Sr0.65CoO3 phase that appears two lines above it, or these are a K2NiF4 Ruddlesden-Popper cobaltite. Composition cannot settle it, so is_mixed is set and those two samples are flagged rather than forced. No reference line is offered for this host, so mp_id and space group both stay null.

basis: Every composition is Ti1-xZrxCoSb with Ni, Sn, Pd or Hf substitutions, and two of the three papers are titled for p-type half-Heusler Zr1-xTixCoSnySb1-y alloys. Cubic MgAgAs ordering with Ti and Zr sharing the M site, Co on the second and Sb on the third; the Ti/Zr mixing is mass disorder for phonon scattering and leaves the prototype alone.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: the M site of the half-Heusler
solid_solution_axis.note: Ti/(Ti+Zr) spans 0.30-0.80 with a median of 0.60 over 11 compositions. Both are group 4 and isovalent on the same site, so the structure is constant and the axis controls lattice thermal conductivity and band position rather than carrier count.
solid_solution_axis.axis_check: Ti and Zr are the same group on the same M site.

reference_disagreement: No reference line is offered for this host, so mp_id stays null.

dopant_roles.basis: Ti0.6Zr0.4Co0.93Ni0.07Sb: one extra electron on the Co site, the n-type donor of this family.
Zr0.5Ti0.5CoSn0.15Sb0.85: one fewer electron on the main-group site, which is the p-type route the first paper is titled for.
The third paper is titled for (Ti,Zr,Hf)(Co,Pd)Sb, so Pd shares the Co site.
Group 4 like Ti and Zr and on the same site; here it falls below the 5 at.% cut, but it is a third member of the alloying axis rather than a dopant.

basis: CrO2 is 13 of 15 samples counting the SnO2-added one: the ferromagnetic half-metal, rutile P4_2/mnm, MP mp-715486 at hull 0.000 with 33 ICSD references, and the third paper is titled for two-band magnetotransport in half-metallic chromium dioxide. Cr2O3 is the other 2 samples and is corundum with 55 ICSD references -- a different prototype -- so the host splits on the O:Cr ratio.
note: The Cr2O3 samples come from the specific-heat paper near the Neel temperature; the antiferromagnetic ordering there is magnetic, not structural, so it is not a phase in the crystallographic sense. The 1273 K outlier in the full span belongs to the plasma-sprayed Cr3C2-NiCr coating paper, whose measured material is a carbide coating rather than either oxide -- worth knowing before a sample-level pass.

dopant_roles.basis: (CrO2)0.9(SnO2)0.1: SnO2 is itself rutile and isostructural with CrO2, so Sn enters the same octahedral cation site and the addition is a solid solution rather than a second phase.

basis: Gamma-CuI with eight different 0.1 percent dopants is every composition: the zincblende form, TEDesignLab CuI F-43m mp-22895 with 12 ICSD references, and the third paper is titled for effective dopants for CuI single nanocrystals as a room-temperature p-type transparent conductor. The 5th-95th percentile window of 298-446 K sits entirely inside the gamma field.
note: The sequence is deliberately truncated. Above about 680 K CuI enters the alpha phase, in which the iodine sublattice stays close-packed and the copper becomes mobile; that is a cation-disordered fcc superionic phase and does NOT match bcc_superionic, whose exemplar is bcc alpha-AgI, so no prototype is recorded for it rather than the wrong one. The 1156 K end of the full span belongs to the first paper, which measures MOLTEN CuI and AgI, where no crystal prototype applies at all. Only a minority of curves leave the gamma field.
reference_disagreement: The MP list for this chemistry is dominated by computed Cu13I15, Cu14I19 and Cu16I19 entries in Cm with no ICSD backing, plus CuI2 and CuI4 far above the hull. TEDesignLab is preferred, per the project precedence, and gives the F-43m zincblende the papers use.

dopant_roles.basis: CuTb0.001I, the most-used of the eight dopants screened; all are written on the Cu site at 0.1 percent and the paper is a dopant screen for the Cu site.
CuCo0.001I, from the same dopant screen.
CuGa0.001I, from the same dopant screen.
CuSn0.001I, from the same dopant screen.
CuMn0.001I, from the same dopant screen.
From the same dopant screen.
From the same dopant screen; divalent on a monovalent site, so nominally a donor.
From the same dopant screen.

basis: LaNi1-xCuxO3 across x = 0.3 to 0.7 is 8 of 15 samples: the rhombohedral perovskite nickelate with Cu on the octahedral B site, and the first and third papers are titled for doped LaNiO3 perovskites. The remaining 7 samples are the (LaNiO3)(La2CuO4) heterostructure of the second paper, which is not a doped perovskite but a stack of a perovskite and a K2NiF4 Ruddlesden-Popper cuprate, so the host holds two prototypes.
note: The heterostructure composition cannot be resolved even per composition: both constituents are present in every sample of it by construction, so those 7 samples are a two-phase stack rather than one structure. Cu sits above the 5 at.% cut and is a host element, so it gets no dopant_roles entry, but its role in the LaNi1-xCuxO3 compositions is B-site substitution for Ni -- the doping variable the first paper scans.
reference_disagreement: The only MP entry offered is La4CuNiO8 C2/m mp-1223008 at hull 0.076 with no ICSD reference -- a computed ordered 1:1 Cu/Ni phase at an oxygen content matching neither the perovskite nor the cuprate here. mp_id is left null.

basis: EuO and Gd-doped Eu0.95Gd0.05O are the only two compositions: the ferromagnetic semiconductor in the rocksalt structure, MP mp-21394 at hull 0.000 with 5 ICSD references, and the third paper is titled for the magnetic and transport properties of degenerate ferromagnetic semiconductors, which is what Gd-doped EuO is. The 10-299 K window stays well inside the rocksalt field.
note: The second paper measures EuO films with a large excess of europium. That is metal-rich non-stoichiometry on the Eu sublattice, and the oxygen vacancies it creates are what make undoped EuO conduct; Eu is a host element so it raises no dopant_roles entry, but it is the reason two otherwise identical EuO samples can differ by orders of magnitude in resistivity.

dopant_roles.basis: Eu0.95Gd0.05O: trivalent Gd on the divalent Eu site donates one electron each and is the classic n-type dopant that drives EuO metallic below its Curie point. At 5 percent of the cation site this is a degenerate doping level, not a dilute impurity.

basis: LaFe4Sb12 is 14 of 15 samples and every paper of this host names filled skutterudites: the CoSb3 framework with Fe on the transition-metal site and La filling the icosahedral void, MP La(FeSb3)4 Im-3 mp-30073 at hull 0.000 with 2 ICSD references. Filling is not optional here -- FeSb3 is not stable unfilled, so the La is a structural constituent rather than a dopant, which is why it sits above the 5 at.% cut and appears in the host key.
note: La1.5Fe4Sb12 (1 sample) is a nominal loading rather than a real occupancy: the cage holds at most one filler per formula unit, so the excess La is either a second phase or simply the weighed-in composition. Stage 3 should treat the La content as a cage-filling fraction capped at 1, not as a linear variable.

basis: Gd2Zr2O7 and its Yb-substituted variants are every composition, and the first paper is titled for rare-earth A2Zr2O7 zirconates. But the curator settles what the ratio cannot: two samples are recorded as Phases present Fluorite and one as Pyrochlore plus Fluorite. Gd2Zr2O7 sits right on the pyrochlore/defect-fluorite stability boundary for its cation radius ratio, so which one a given sample is depends on how it was sintered, and both occur here. The seed hypothesis is refined rather than confirmed for that reason.
note: Pyrochlore is the cation- and vacancy-ORDERED superstructure of defect fluorite, so the two are the ordered and disordered forms of one arrangement rather than unrelated types. Disorder increases with temperature and the measurements run to 1473 K, but the order-disorder crossover in Gd2Zr2O7 is processing-history dependent rather than a sharp thermal transition, so it is not recorded in phases. (Gd2O3)48.5(ZrO2)51.5 is the same 1:1 cation ratio written as an oxide mixture.

dopant_roles.basis: (Gd1-xYbx)2Zr2O7 with x to 0.10, which the third paper is titled for. Yb is trivalent like Gd and sits on the same A site; because it is smaller it pushes the composition toward the disordered fluorite side, so the substitution changes the ordering as well as the phonon scattering.

basis: Three different IV-VI structures sit in this host. Ge0.90Sb0.10Te0.88Se0.12 (3 samples) is Sb- and Se-doped GeTe, which the third paper is titled for, and that is rhombohedral R3m below about 700 K. Ge2Sb2Te4.5Se0.5 and Ge2Sb2Te4Se are the Ge2Sb2Te5 homologue with Se on the anion site. The (GeSe)1-x(Sb2Te3)x series is the cubic germanium selenide of the first paper, whose title names glass-like transport in crystalline CUBIC germanium selenide -- Sb2Te3 alloying is what stabilises the rocksalt form against orthorhombic GeSe. So the host splits per composition and the measured 297-801 K window also crosses the GeTe rhombohedral-to-cubic transition.

solid_solution_axis.note: Se/(Se+Te) spans 0.10-0.79 with a median of 0.14 over 13 compositions, so most samples are Te-rich. The axis is not a clean one here: the Se-rich end is reached by alloying GeSe with Sb2Te3 rather than by substituting Se into GeTe, so Se arrives together with a change of cation chemistry. Se substitution also raises the GeTe rhombohedral-to-cubic transition temperature, so the 700 K default moves along the axis.
solid_solution_axis.axis_check: Se and Te are the same group on the same anion site.

reference_disagreement: No reference line is offered for this four-element host, so all mp_ids stay null.

basis: Every composition is NdOZnSb with Sr or Ag substitution, and both papers call it a layered compound: the ZrCuSiAs type, alternating [Nd2O2] and [Zn2Sb2] layers, MP NdZnSbO P4/nmm mp-12516 at hull 0.000 with 2 ICSD references. It is the pnictide analogue of the BiCuSeO the taxonomy entry is named for, with the same P4/nmm stacking.

other_polymorphs.note: Nd2ZnSb2O P4/mmm mp-1209925 sits 1.164 eV above the hull with no ICSD reference. At that hull distance it is a computed structure rather than a phase anyone has made, and it is a different stoichiometry from these samples.

dopant_roles.basis: Nd1-xSrxOZnSb with x to 0.08, which the first paper is titled for. Divalent Sr on the trivalent Nd site of the oxide layer is the hole-doping variable, the same mechanism as Sr or Ba doping in BiCuSeO.
The second paper is titled for the influence of Ag doping on this layered compound; monovalent Ag on the divalent Zn site of the conducting pnictide layer is an acceptor.

basis: Ni0.786Te is the single largest composition (4 samples) and the first paper is titled for single-crystal Ni0.786Te; together with NiTe it is the NiAs-type hexagonal telluride, MP NiTe P6_3/mmc mp-203 with 8 ICSD references. NiTe2 and Ni32Te67 are the CdI2 end of the same series, MP P-3m1 mp-2578 with 6 ICSD references. NiAs and CdI2 are the filled and half-emptied forms of one hexagonal metal sublattice, and Ni1-xTe moves continuously between them, so this host is a vacancy series rather than two unrelated compounds -- but the two ends are distinct prototypes in this taxonomy, so it is marked mixed and splits on the Ni:Te ratio.
note: Ni3Te2 (1 sample) is neither: MP puts it at P2_1/m mp-31103 with 1 ICSD reference, a monoclinic metal-rich telluride with no taxonomy entry, so it is parked in unresolved_crystalline rather than forced into the NiAs series. Ni2Te3 as written is the Ni0.67Te composition and belongs inside the vacancy series.

dopant_roles.basis: Sb appears in the samples from the two Bi2Te3 papers -- the contact study and the Ni-nanoparticle study -- where the nickel telluride forms against a Bi-Sb-Te matrix. The Sb is from that matrix rather than a deliberate substituent on either site, so it should not be treated as doping in stage 3. This needs the paper to be certain.

basis: Pb1-yLa0.1(Zr0.65Ti0.35)O3 at a range of nominal Pb loadings is 12 of 15 samples: PLZT, the lanthanum-modified lead zirconate titanate, and the first paper is titled for hot-pressed Pb0.85La0.1(Zr,Ti)O3. ABO3 perovskite with Pb and La on the A site and Zr and Ti sharing the octahedral B site; at Zr:Ti = 65:35 with 10 percent La the composition sits on the rhombohedral side of the morphotropic phase boundary.
note: The Pb index varies from 0.85 to 1.5 across the compositions. That is weighed-in PbO excess to compensate lead volatilisation during hot pressing, not a real A-site occupancy of 1.5; Pb is a host element so it takes no dopant_roles entry, but stage 3 must not read the excess as a stoichiometric variable. The measured window of 14-373 K sits below the ferroelectric Curie point of this composition, so no transition is crossed.
reference_disagreement: assigned sg [161], ICSD-backed references for this host report [99]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

dopant_roles.basis: Present in every composition at 10 percent of the A site. Trivalent La on the divalent Pb site is charge-compensated by A-site vacancies, and that vacancy concentration is what makes PLZT a relaxor rather than a normal ferroelectric. Not a dilute impurity despite falling under the 5 at.% whole-formula cut.
An acceptor on the octahedral B site, the usual hardening dopant in PZT. In the (PZT)(La0.65Ca0.35MnO3) composite of the second paper it is instead a constituent of the manganite layer.
Ca appears only through the La0.65Ca0.35MnO3 layer of the composite recorded in the curator detail, so it belongs to a second perovskite phase and not to the PZT lattice.
Divalent on the A site, isovalent with Pb; one composition only.

basis: Si30P16Te8 and its variants are every composition, and two of the three papers name type I clathrates in their titles -- one of them is titled for the new clathrates I Si30P16Te8. This is the inorganic type I clathrate with a group 14/15 framework: P substitutes into the 46-atom Si cage framework to balance the charge of the Te guests that fill the eight cages. Si132P40Te21.5 is the same 46:8 framework-to-guest ratio scaled.
note: This is the inverted case of the usual clathrate: the guest is an anion (Te) rather than a cation, and the framework carries the positive charge through P-for-Si substitution. Stage 3 must not treat P as a dilute dopant -- at 16 of 46 framework atoms it is the charge-balancing constituent, the same way Ga is in Ba8Ga16Ge30. The MP entry offered, Si60Te13P32Se3 Pmmm mp-1219353 at hull 0.027, has no ICSD reference and is a computed ordering of the disordered framework, so mp_id stays null.

dopant_roles.basis: Si30.3P15.6Te6.6Se1.46: Se replaces Te in the cages, which is the homovalent half of the homo- and heterovalent substitutions the second paper is titled for. Same group, same guest site, so it changes rattling and mass contrast without changing the electron count.

A halide guest in place of a chalcogen guest is heterovalent and therefore changes the framework charge the P content must balance -- the other half of the same paper. Recorded as a cage filler rather than a substituent because the guest site is what it occupies.

basis: URu2Si2 is 13 of 15 samples and two of the papers are titled for it directly: the body-centred tetragonal ThCr2Si2 structure, MP U(SiRu)2 I4/mmm mp-3388 at hull 0.000 with 12 ICSD references, the largest ICSD count in this chemistry. U2Ru3Si5 is the other 2 samples and is a different structure.
note: Two things this host does NOT need. The hidden-order transition of URu2Si2 at 17.5 K, inside the measured 10-1084 K window, is electronic rather than crystallographic -- the lattice stays I4/mmm -- so it is not recorded in phases, even though it is why the compound is measured so often. And U2Ru3Si5 (2 samples, the U2M3Si5 paper) is the U2Co3Si5 type, MP C2/c mp-1188211 with 1 ICSD reference; the taxonomy has no 2-3-5 entry and two samples do not justify proposing one, so it is parked in unresolved_crystalline.

basis: CeAgAs2 is the only composition, 14 samples, and both papers are titled for it. The CeTAs2 compounds are HfCuSi2-type: the ZrCuSiAs stacking with a planar As square net in place of the oxide layer, so [Ce2As2] slabs alternate with [AgAs] layers. The ambient structure is the orthorhombically distorted variant of that tetragonal parent, driven by the As net dimerising, which is what MP gives as the best-attested entry.
note: The prototype id is used at one remove and that should be visible. zrcusias_1111 is defined for the ABXO oxychalcogenide BiCuSeO in P4/nmm; CeAgAs2 is the same layer stacking with As in both anion roles and no oxygen, and its observed cell is the Pbcm distortion of it. MP ranks CeAgAs2 Pbcm mp-672195 first with 3 ICSD references against P4/nmm mp-20384 with 1, which supports the distorted form over the ideal tetragonal one; the space group recorded is therefore 57. If a HfCuSi2 entry is added to the taxonomy in v4 this record should move to it.

basis: (GeTe)1-x(AgBiSe2)x across x = 0.175 to 0.50, all from one paper titled for realizing both n- and p-type GeTe thermoelectrics. AgBiSe2 is a rocksalt-derived ordered ternary and alloying it into GeTe is precisely the route used to suppress the rhombohedral distortion, so the heavily alloyed compositions -- the median Se share is 0.57, i.e. most samples carry 35-50 percent AgBiSe2 -- are cubic rocksalt at room temperature. The Te-rich end at x = 0.175 is still rhombohedral GeTe, so the host splits along the alloying axis.

solid_solution_axis.note: Se/(Se+Te) spans 0.21-0.82 with a median of 0.57 over 14 compositions. The anion ratio is a proxy here rather than the real variable: Se and Te do share the anion site, but Se only ever arrives as part of an AgBiSe2 unit, so moving along this axis also puts Ag and Bi onto the cation site. The rhombohedral-to-cubic boundary sits somewhere inside the range, which is why the host is mixed rather than one prototype.
solid_solution_axis.axis_check: Se and Te are the same group on the same anion site, but the axis is not independent of the cation composition.

reference_disagreement: No reference line is offered for this five-element host, so mp_id stays null.

dopant_roles.basis: (GeTe)50(AgBiSe1.995Cl0.005)50: a halide on the anion site donates an electron and is what converts the alloy to n-type, which is the point of the paper.
The same anion-site donor role as Cl.
The same anion-site donor role as Cl.

basis: BiAgSeS with Cl substitution is every composition, and the first paper is titled for high thermoelectric performance in n-type BiAgSeS due to intrinsically low thermal conductivity. BiAgSeS is the silver sulphide analogue of BiCuSeO: alternating [Bi2Se2] and [Ag2S2] layers in the ZrCuSiAs stacking, with the two chalcogens in chemically distinct layers rather than mixed on one site.
note: The detected S/(S+Se) axis at a median of exactly 0.50 is almost certainly spurious and is recorded as null rather than as a series. This is the case the README warns about with O and Se in BiCuSeO: same group does not mean same site. In the 1111 stacking, Se sits in the [Bi2Se2] layer and S in the [Ag2S2] layer, so BiAgSeS at 1:1 is an ordered stoichiometric compound, not a half-way point on a solid solution. The 0.10-0.90 spread comes from the third paper, which works on AgBi3(Se,S)5 -- a different compound (Ag:Bi = 1:3) in the same element set, and one whose structure is NOT this one. Those samples would need their own prototype if any are in this host.
reference_disagreement: Both MP entries offered are computed with no ICSD backing: AgBiSeS P4/mmm mp-1229089 at hull 0.095 and Ag2Bi2SeS3 Imm2 mp-1229130 at hull 0.062. P4/mmm is not P4/nmm -- it is a different tetragonal cell that does not have the glide-related double layer of the 1111 type -- and at 0.095 eV above the hull it reads as an enumerated ordering rather than the observed structure. mp_id is left null for stage 2.

dopant_roles.basis: BiAgSeS1-xClx to x = 0.05: a halide on the sulphur site of the [Ag2S2] layer donates an electron and is the n-type doping variable of the first two papers.

basis: Every composition is Cu0.8Ag0.2(In1-xGax)Te2, a I-III-VI2 ternary with both cation sublattices alloyed, and the single paper is titled for ultralow thermal conductivity in diamondoid structures. CuInTe2, CuGaTe2 and AgInTe2 are all chalcopyrite (I-42d) and mix continuously, so the whole 14-composition set is one structure with mass and strain disorder on both sites.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: the group-III cation site of the chalcopyrite
solid_solution_axis.note: Ga/(Ga+In) spans 0.20-0.80 with a median of 0.80 over 14 compositions. There is a second, unflagged axis in parallel: Cu and Ag are fixed at 0.8:0.2 on the group-I site in every composition, so that one is a constant rather than a variable here. Both are isovalent, so the structure is constant and the axis is the disorder knob the paper uses to suppress lattice thermal conductivity.
solid_solution_axis.axis_check: Ga and In are the same group on the same cation site.

reference_disagreement: The one MP entry offered, InGaCuAgTe4 I-4 mp-1224000 at hull 0.012, has no ICSD reference. I-4 is a fully cation-ORDERED quaternary derivative of chalcopyrite, which is the structure a calculation must pick to model a 1:1:1:1 composition; the real samples are disordered on both cation sublattices and the diffraction cell is I-42d. mp_id is left null rather than recording an ordering the samples do not have.

basis: Every composition is Ag9GaSe6 with Te substitution, and two of the three papers say argyrodite outright -- one is titled for an argyrodite-type Ag9GaSe6 liquid-like material with ultralow thermal conductivity. A9BX6 with a rigid Ga-Se framework and a mobile silver sublattice, which MP gives as Ga(Ag3Se2)3 P2_13 mp-27163 at hull 0.000. The ordered-to-superionic transition sits just above room temperature, inside the measured window.
note: The prototype does not change across that transition -- both entries are argyrodite -- only the space group does, as the Ag sublattice disorders from the ordered P2_13 cell into the cubic F-43m one the taxonomy already lists as the high-temperature form. It is recorded as two phases anyway because the measurement starts at 296 K, essentially on the boundary, and the third paper is titled for entropy-optimised phase transitions in this material. The 320 K value is from the argyrodite literature, not from the papers, and Te substitution shifts it, which is part of what that paper is doing.
reference_disagreement: TEDesignLab makes GaAgSe2 I-42d mp-5518 primary with 15 ICSD references, and that is the best-attested phase in this chemistry -- but it is the chalcopyrite AgGaSe2, and NOT ONE of the 12 compositions in this host is AgGaSe2. Every one is Ag9GaSe6. This is the clearest example in the chunk of a reference describing a chemistry rather than the samples, so the ICSD-backed entry is set aside and the MP argyrodite entry used instead.

dopant_roles.basis: Ag9Ga(Se1-xTex)6 with x to 0.12, which the third paper scans. Te on the framework anion site is isovalent; it raises the mass contrast and shifts the order-disorder transition rather than doping.

basis: Elemental aluminium (12 samples) and one dilute Zr alloy written in at.% as Zr0.08Al99.92: face-centred cubic Al, MP mp-134 at hull 0.000 with 24 ICSD references, measured as a reference metal -- the papers are about measurement technique, commercial metals and welded joints rather than about a compound.

other_polymorphs.note: Im-3m Al at 0.095 eV above the hull with 1 ICSD reference, and a P6_3/mmc entry at 0.020. Aluminium is fcc from cryogenic temperatures to the melt at ambient pressure; the bcc and hcp entries are high-pressure or computed and are not reached on heating.

dopant_roles.basis: Zr0.08Al99.92: 0.08 at.% Zr, the standard grain-refining addition in commercial aluminium. At that level it is partly in solid solution and partly as Al3Zr precipitates, so the solid-solution reading is the nominal one.

basis: Nine of 14 samples are decagonal or approximant phases: Al75Co22Ni3 and Al76Co22Ni2 are the classic decagonal Al-Co-Ni quasicrystal composition (the curator records an initial melt composition of Al81.9Co14.5Ni3.6, so these are grown crystals), and Al13Co4 is the orthorhombic approximant the first paper names in its title, on anisotropic transport in Al13TM4 complex metallic alloys. The third paper is on icosahedral Al-Co alloys. Al5Co2 and its Fe-substituted variants are the remaining 3 samples and are a distinct hexagonal intermetallic, proposed here as co2al5_d811.
note: The README flags quasicrystal_approximant as needing special handling in stage 2, and this host is exactly why: a decagonal quasicrystal has no periodic cell at all, while Al13Co4 is a genuine large-cell approximant that MP gives at Pmn2_1 mp-1198336 with 1 ICSD reference and an AMBIGUOUS flag. The two are grouped here because both papers treat them as one family, but they should not be handed the same structure file.

dopant_roles.basis: Al75Co22Ni3: Ni shares the transition-metal site with Co, and in the decagonal phase it is not an impurity -- the Ni content is what stabilises the quasicrystalline order, so the ternary is the phase rather than a doped binary.
Al5(Co0.95Fe0.05)2: Fe on the Co site of the hexagonal phase, used to move the Fermi level within the pseudogap that the second paper is titled for.

basis: BaFe2As2 with Co on the Fe site or K on the Ba site is every composition, mostly single crystals, and the first paper is titled for the thermoelectric properties of electron- and hole-doped BaFe2As2. The body-centred tetragonal ThCr2Si2 structure, [Fe2As2] layers separated by Ba, which is the parent structure of the 122 iron pnictide superconductors. The measured 10-301 K window crosses the tetragonal-to-orthorhombic structural transition of the undoped parent.
note: The prototype is the same on both sides -- the low-temperature Fmmm cell is an orthorhombic distortion of the I4/mmm one, not a different structure type -- so this is a distortion crossing rather than a reconstructive transition, recorded the way the README describes the WO3 series. It matters here because the transition is the central variable of the host: it sits near 140 K in undoped BaFe2As2 and Co or K doping suppresses it toward zero, which is exactly what the samples scan, so the 140 K value applies only to the undoped compositions.
reference_disagreement: The only MP entry offered is Ba4Na(FeAs)10 I4/m mp-1228543, a computed Na-containing ordering with no ICSD reference and a composition that is not in this host. BaFe2As2 itself is absent from the 2019 snapshot for this host, so mp_id is left null rather than taking a neighbouring compound.

dopant_roles.basis: Ba(Fe0.9Co0.1)2As2: Co directly on the Fe site of the conducting layer, one extra electron each, and the electron-doping half of the first paper. At 10 percent of the Fe site this is a heavy doping series that suppresses the structural transition and induces superconductivity, not a dilute impurity.
Ba1-xKxFe2As2: monovalent K on the divalent Ba site is the hole-doping variable the README itself cites for this family, and the second paper is titled for Ba1-xMxFe2As2 with M = La and K.

basis: UAs1-xSe1+x with x scanned over about 7 percent of the anion content is the whole host, and all three papers are titled for UAsSe as a Kondo ferromagnet. UAsSe takes the tetragonal PbFCl type, MP P4/nmm mp-22595 at hull 0.000 with 4 ICSD references -- layers of U with square nets of As on one side and Se on the other. The taxonomy carries only the filled ZrCuSiAs derivative of that stacking, so the parent type is proposed before use.
note: No element falls below the 5 at.% cut, so dopant_roles is empty -- but the carrier-concentration variable is still there: the As:Se ratio moves from 0.926:1.074 to 1.021:0.979, which is non-stoichiometry between two host sites, and the third paper is titled for coherent electronic scattering in UAs1-xSe1+x. Stage 3 should read that off the parsed fractions of the two host elements rather than looking for a dopant.

basis: Every composition is written as (TiB2)n(SrTiO3)m or the Y-substituted equivalent, and the papers are titled for microstructural control and densification of thermoelectric SrTiO3. These are TiB2 particles dispersed in a SrTiO3 matrix -- a deliberate conductive-inclusion composite, two crystalline phases per sample -- so no single prototype describes a sample. Sr0.9Y0.1Ti1.25O3B0.5 is the same mixture with the boride written out into the formula.
note: The two constituents are both in the taxonomy and both are named as alternatives: the matrix is cubic perovskite SrTiO3 and the inclusion is TiB2, which is the AlB2 type the alb2 entry covers. Unlike a mixed host that splits per composition, this one cannot be split at all -- both phases are present in every sample by design -- which is what composite_multiphase is for. No reference line is offered for this host.

dopant_roles.basis: Sr0.9Y0.1TiO3: trivalent Y on the divalent A site of the perovskite is the n-type donor that makes SrTiO3 conduct, and it belongs to the matrix rather than to the boride. At 10 percent of the A site it is a heavy doping level despite falling below the whole-formula 5 at.% cut.

basis: SmB6 and its Sm-deficient variants Sm0.94B6, Sm0.8B6 and Sm0.75B6 are all four compositions: the cubic CaB6 structure, a simple-cubic Sm lattice interpenetrating a framework of B6 octahedra, MP Pm-3m mp-6996 at hull 0.000 with 30 ICSD references -- the best-attested entry in this chemistry by a wide margin. All the papers are about SmB6 as a Kondo or unconventional insulator.
note: The state transition and electron phase transition the first two paper titles refer to are the opening of the Kondo hybridisation gap below about 50 K and the low-temperature resistivity plateau. Both are electronic; the lattice stays Pm-3m throughout the 10-299 K window, so nothing goes in phases. The Sm deficiency down to Sm0.75B6 is vacancy non-stoichiometry on the metal site and is the valence and carrier-concentration knob, but Sm is a host element so it takes no dopant_roles entry.

basis: Every composition is BaCd2Sb2 with Na, Ag or Yb substitution, from one paper on heavily doped BaCd2Sb2. AM2Pn2 is the CaAl2Si2 formula archetype and the seed hypothesis takes it there, but I am not confident and the confidence is set low deliberately: Ba is at the top of the size range for that structure type, and the heavier AM2Pn2 barium compounds -- BaZn2Sb2 in particular -- are reported in the orthorhombic BaCu2S2 type instead, with puckered layers rather than the CaAl2Si2 slab. Composition cannot separate the two and the references do not either, so this needs the paper.
reference_disagreement: Neither reference settles it and both point somewhere else. TEDesignLab covers only Ba11(CdSb2)6, i.e. Ba11Cd6Sb12 -- a different Zintl phase entirely, the one the zintl_11_6_12 entry names -- and not BaCd2Sb2. The MP entry that matches the stoichiometry, Ba(CdSb)2 P-3m1 mp-8150 at hull 0.000, is the CaAl2Si2 type and would support the seed, but it carries no ICSD reference at all, so it is a calculation rather than an observation. mp_id is left null. bacu2s2_layered, proposed from chunk 007 for BaCu2Te2, is the specific alternative to test.

dopant_roles.basis: Ba0.99Na0.01Cd2Sb2: monovalent Na on the divalent A site is an acceptor and the main p-type knob of the paper.
BaCd1.98Ag0.02Sb2: monovalent Ag on the divalent Cd site of the polyanionic layer, an acceptor acting on the other sublattice, which is how the paper reaches multiband transport.

Ba0.7975Yb0.2Na0.0025Cd2Sb2: divalent Yb on the divalent A site at 20 percent of it, so alloying for mass contrast rather than doping -- and note it is well above a dilute level despite being under the whole-formula cut.

basis: SmBaMn2O6 is 10 of 14 samples and SmBaMn2O5 two more: the A-site ordered double perovskite, with Sm and Ba on alternating layers rather than mixed, which the second paper states in its title as the A-site ordered manganite. That ordering is exactly what the layered_double_perovskite entry describes, at Mn rather than Co. Sm0.5Ba0.5MnO3 is the A-site DISORDERED solid solution of the same composition and is a simple perovskite, so the host holds both the ordered and the disordered form.
note: The first paper is titled for anomalous thermal conductivity ACROSS the structural transition in SmBaMn2O6, so the crossing is established by the paper even though the temperature is not: the charge- and orbital-ordering transition of the half-doped ordered manganites sits near 380 K, and the measured window runs to 398 K in the robust range and to 1172 K in the full span. The prototype and the A-site ordering survive it -- only the cell symmetry changes -- so both phases carry the same id and the space groups are left null rather than guessed. SmBaMn2O5 is the oxygen-vacancy-ordered reduced form of the same ordered framework, kept under the same prototype.
reference_disagreement: assigned sg [47, 123], ICSD-backed references for this host report [87]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

dopant_roles.basis: Sm0.9La0.24Ba0.86Mn2O6: trivalent La on the trivalent Sm site is isovalent, so it changes the average A-site radius and hence the ordering temperature rather than the carrier count.

basis: BiCuOS with Pb, Ca or Se substitution is every composition, and the first paper is titled for the BiCuSeO-BiCuSO solid solution. It is the sulphur analogue of BiCuSeO itself, the exemplar of this taxonomy entry: alternating insulating [Bi2O2] and conducting [Cu2S2] layers in the P4/nmm ZrCuSiAs stacking.
reference_disagreement: The only MP entry offered is Cu2BiSO2 P4/mmm mp-1206303 at 0.773 eV above the hull with no ICSD reference. At that hull distance it is not a phase anyone has made, and the stoichiometry is not BiCuOS either, so it is ignored and mp_id left null. The absence is a gap in the 2019 snapshot rather than evidence against the assignment -- the README notes the same for Bi2Se3.

dopant_roles.basis: Bi1-xPbxCuOS to x = 0.05: divalent Pb on the trivalent Bi site of the oxide layer is the standard hole dopant of the BiCuChO family and is what the third paper means by band structure engineering.
Bi0.98Pb0.01Ca0.01CuSO: divalent Ca on the same trivalent Bi site, a second acceptor used alongside Pb.

BiCuSe0.1S0.9O sits on the BiCuSeO-BiCuSO solid solution of the first paper. Se and S share the chalcogen site of the conducting layer and are isovalent, so this is alloying rather than doping -- and note that oxygen, also group 16, does NOT share that site: it belongs to the [Bi2O2] layer.

basis: LaOBiS2 and its F-, Se- and oxygen-deficient variants are every composition, and the papers are titled for layered bismuth-sulphide thermoelectrics and for the anisotropy and high thermopower of LaOBiS2. This is the exemplar family of the bis2_layered entry, whose archetype is written REO1-xFxBiS2: [La2O2] blocks alternating with BiS2 bilayers in P4/nmm. MP LaBiS2O mp-1078397 at hull 0.005 agrees.
note: No seed hypothesis was offered even though the taxonomy entry names Bi-F-O-Pr-S as an example host, i.e. the same family one rare earth over. Worth folding this host into example_host_systems for v4.

dopant_roles.basis: LaO0.95F0.05BiS2: F on the oxygen site of the blocking layer donates one electron into the BiS2 layer and is the doping variable the whole family is defined by -- the taxonomy writes the archetype as REO1-xFxBiS2 for that reason. LaO0.9BiS2 and LaO0.93BiS2 achieve the same thing with oxygen vacancies instead.
LaOBiS1.8Se0.2, which the second paper is titled for: Se on the chalcogen site of the conducting bilayer, isovalent, used to apply chemical pressure in that layer.

basis: Ca2Fe2O5 and its Zn-substituted variants are the largest group and the second paper is titled for the structural behaviour and thermoelectric properties of the brownmillerite: the oxygen-deficient perovskite with alternating octahedral and tetrahedral iron layers, MP Pnma mp-25750 with 20 ICSD references. But the host holds at least two more structures: CaFeO3 is the fully oxidised cubic-derived perovskite with Fe4+ (mp-19115, 18 ICSD references), and the Ca1-xCoxFe2O4 compositions of the third paper are AB2O4 ferrites at an entirely different cation ratio.
note: The AB2O4 compositions are the loose end and spinel is recorded as an alternative with a caveat rather than as an answer. Ca0.9Co0.1Fe2O4 could be Co-substituted CaFe2O4, which is the orthorhombic post-spinel calcium-ferrite type -- MP Ca(FeO2)2 Pnma mp-25690 with 22 ICSD references, the single best-attested entry in this chemistry -- or Ca-substituted CoFe2O4, which is a cubic spinel. The paper title, on Ca-Co ferrites, does not distinguish them and the taxonomy has no CaFe2O4-type entry, so this is flagged for the paper rather than settled here. Brownmillerite and perovskite are also linked by oxygen content rather than being unrelated: Ca2Fe2O5 is CaFeO2.5, so the same sample can move between them on oxidation.

dopant_roles.basis: On the iron site in the ferrite compositions, where it is a major constituent (up to 30 percent of the A position) rather than a dopant.
Ca2Zn0.1Fe1.9O5: Zn on the tetrahedral iron layer of the brownmillerite, which is where a divalent d10 cation prefers to sit -- stage 2 should confirm the layer once the structure is resolved.
Divalent on the A site, isovalent, so it changes the tolerance factor and the octahedral tilt rather than the carrier count.
Trivalent on the divalent A site, so an electron donor that also reduces the average Fe valence.
B-site substitution alongside Co and Zn.
Trivalent A-site donor, same role as Pr.

basis: Two different Zn-Sb structures share this host. Zn0.2Cd0.8Sb is 6 of 14 samples and is the equiatomic CdSb-type orthorhombic phase, which the third paper is titled for as the ZnxCd1-xSb solid solution. The (Zn1-xCdx)13Sb10 compositions and (Zn0.9Cd0.1)4Sb3 are the other group: beta-Zn4Sb3, a disordered rhombohedral phase with interstitial Zn, whose modern formula is Zn13Sb10 -- the first paper is titled for single-phase (Zn1-xCdx)13Sb10. They are different prototypes and the host splits on the Sb:(Zn+Cd) ratio.

solid_solution_axis.note: Cd/(Cd+Zn) spans 0.10-0.80 with a median of 0.30 over 9 compositions. Both are group 12 and divalent on the same cation site, and ZnSb and CdSb are isostructural, so within the 1:1 compositions the axis does not change the prototype. It cuts across the 1:1 and 13:10 groups, though, so it must not be used on its own to choose the parent.
solid_solution_axis.axis_check: Zn and Cd are the same group on the same cation site.

reference_disagreement: The only MP entry offered is ZnCdSb2 P2_12_12_1 mp-1215678 at hull 0.035 with no ICSD reference, a computed ordered 1:1:2 cell. The real 1:1 phase is the disordered CdSb-type Pbca structure, so mp_id is left null and stage 2 should resolve ZnSb and CdSb separately. The 11-342 K window sits below the beta-Zn4Sb3 low-temperature transitions near 250 K reported for the pure binary, which Cd substitution suppresses; the chunk shows no transition line and none is recorded, but it is worth checking for the 13:10 samples.

basis: CeRu2Ge2 is the only composition, 14 samples, and both papers are titled for it: the body-centred tetragonal ThCr2Si2 structure, MP Ce(GeRu)2 I4/mmm mp-22343 at hull 0.000 with 5 ICSD references, the best-attested entry in this chemistry. It is a textbook Kondo-lattice 122 whose magnetic phase diagram is followed by thermopower under pressure, which is the subject of both papers.
note: The high-pressure work in both papers drives CeRu2Ge2 across a magnetic quantum critical point, not a structural transition, so the 10-300 K ambient-pressure measurements stay in one phase. The pressure axis is not represented in this schema at all, which is worth knowing before these curves are compared with ambient-pressure data.

basis: One composition, CeRh0.58Ir0.42In5, 14 samples, from a single paper on quantum criticality in it. CeRhIn5 and CeIrIn5 are both HoCoGa5-type 115 compounds -- alternating CeIn3 and TIn2 layers in P4/mmm -- and they form a continuous solid solution, so the mixed Rh/Ir composition is one structure. The taxonomy has no 115 entry despite this being one of the most-studied heavy-fermion families, so it is proposed before use.

solid_solution_axis.note: Rh and Ir share the T site at a fixed 0.58:0.42 in the single composition of this host, so there is no spread to report -- but the ratio is the tuning variable of the paper, chosen to sit at the point where conventional and unconventional quantum criticality meet. The automatic detector did not flag it because both elements fall below the 5 at.% cut of a formula with seven atoms, which is the sublattice-versus-formula mismatch the README describes.
solid_solution_axis.axis_check: Rh and Ir are the same group on the same transition-metal site.

reference_disagreement: No reference line is offered for this host at all, so the space group comes from the structure literature and mp_id stays null. Confidence on the phase entry is medium for that reason while the host-level call is high.

basis: CeRuSn3 and its off-stoichiometric variants CeRuSn2.91 to CeRuSn3.09 are 8 of 14 samples, and the third paper is titled for the RERuSn3 series. Those cubic RERuSn3 stannides are the disordered member of the R3T4Sn13 Remeika family -- MP gives CeSn3Ru Pm-3n mp-1198476 at hull 0.000 with 3 ICSD references and Ce3Sn13Ru4 in the same space group with 3 more -- so they take the 3-4-13 entry proposed from chunk 009. CeRu4Sn6 is the other 3 samples and is a different structure, the tetragonal Kondo insulator of the first paper, proposed here.
note: The confidence is medium rather than high because of how the 1-1-3 and 3-4-13 formulas relate. MP lists both CeSn3Ru and Ce3Sn13Ru4 in Pm-3n with equal ICSD support, and the RERuSn3 compounds are usually described as a substitutionally disordered variant of the 3-4-13 cell rather than as a separate type; whether the samples here are the ordered or the disordered form needs the paper. The Sn index scanned from 2.91 to 3.09 is site non-stoichiometry on a host element and should be read from the parsed fractions in stage 3.

basis: One composition, RuCl3, 14 samples and 12 of them single crystals, and both papers are titled for it as a Kitaev quantum magnet and a van der Waals magnet. Alpha-RuCl3 is a layered trihalide: sheets of edge-sharing RuCl6 octahedra in which one third of the octahedral metal sites is vacant, leaving a Ru honeycomb, with the sheets held together only by van der Waals contact. The taxonomy has no layered trihalide entry, so it is proposed before use.
note: The measured window of 10-91 K sits entirely below the stacking transition near 150 K, so no crossing is recorded: these samples are in the low-temperature rhombohedral R-3 stacking throughout, which is why space group 148 rather than the room-temperature C2/m is on the phase. The magnetic ordering near 7 K is not a structural transition. Beta-RuCl3, a chain polymorph, exists but is not reached by cooling single crystals of the alpha form.
reference_disagreement: assigned sg [148], ICSD-backed references for this host report [193]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: Every one of the 9 compositions is YbCu2Si2-xGex, from YbCu2Si1.75Ge0.25 to YbCu2Si0.25Ge1.75. YbCu2Si2 is the ThCr2Si2 body-centred tetragonal I4/mmm type, and Ge substitutes isoelectronically for Si on the tetrahedral main-group site without changing the structure type anywhere along the series. The second paper, on chemical expansion and Yb valence, is about exactly that: a lattice expanded at fixed structure.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: the 4e main-group site of the ThCr2Si2 cell
solid_solution_axis.note: Si and Ge are both group 14 and genuinely share one crystallographic site here, so this is a real isoelectronic series: YbCu2Si2 at one end, YbCu2Ge2 at the other, and no single parent for the host. The series exists to expand the lattice and drive the Yb valence, so x is a tuning variable rather than a doping level.

note: No reference line of any kind is offered for this host, so mp_id is left null. The first paper on the papers line is titled for rare-earth doping of SrTiO3, which has nothing to do with this chemistry; the DOI-to-title link looks wrong in the input and it was not used in this assignment.

basis: Every composition is Ti50Ni50-xCux with x from 5 to 30 at.%, i.e. the TiNi shape-memory alloy with Cu on the Ni site, and the single paper is titled for the Cu-substitution effect on the TiNi-based alloy. The measured 12-386 K window spans the martensitic transformation, so the host needs both the B2 austenite and its martensite. Cu selects which martensite: 4 of the 6 listed compositions carry 10 at.% Cu or more, where the product is orthorhombic B19 and the monoclinic shear is suppressed, so B19 is the low-temperature prototype for most of the host.
note: The transformation temperature is strongly composition-dependent and roughly 330 K is a mid-range value for this Cu series, not a measured one. The two low-Cu compositions, Ti50Ni45Cu5 and Ti50Ni42.5Cu7.5, transform to monoclinic B19-prime instead, which is why the record is mixed and stage 2 must split it on the Cu fraction rather than take one martensite for the host. I disagree with the Materials Project list offered here: all five entries are off-stoichiometry Ti-Cu-Ni ternaries (TiCuNi2 Pmmn, Ti8Cu3Ni, TiCuNi I4mm and so on), none of which is the pseudobinary TiNi phase these samples are, so no mp_id is taken from them.
reference_disagreement: assigned the B2 / B19 pseudobinary TiNi phase; the MP entries ranked for this host are all distinct ternary compounds and support none of it.

basis: LaNi itself is 6 of the 14 samples and is the CrB type, orthorhombic Cmcm, which Materials Project confirms at mp-1064719 with 5 ICSD references. But the host is a stoichiometry scan of the whole La-Ni binary line and four different structure types sit in it: LaNi5 is the hexagonal CaCu5 type, LaNi2 (as the Ce0.12La0.88 alloy) is a cubic C15 Laves phase, La7Ni3 is the hexagonal Th7Fe3 type, and La2Ni7 is the Ce2Ni7 intergrowth. One label cannot stand for that.
note: La2Ni7 (1 sample) is the Ce2Ni7 type, P6_3/mmc, which is an ordered intergrowth of CaCu5 slabs and MgZn2 Laves slabs rather than either one on its own. It has no taxonomy entry; it is not proposed here for a single sample, but stage 2 should not silently file it under cacu5. The papers are about Ce-based valence fluctuation, with La as the non-magnetic reference compound, which is why so many stoichiometries appear together.

dopant_roles.basis: La(Ni0.965Ga0.035)5: Ga sits on the transition-metal sublattice of the CaCu5 cell, the standard way of tuning LaNi5.
(Ce0.12La0.88)Ni2: Ce replaces La on the rare-earth site, and the whole point of the paper is the Kondo behaviour that brings.

basis: The compositions are La3Te4, La2Te3 and the Yb- and Ca-substituted La3-xTe4 in between; the second paper is titled for optimising La3-xTe4 via Yb substitution. La3Te4 and La2Te3 are the two ends of one continuous cubic Th3P4 phase, I-43d, in which La vacancies run from zero to one third and carry the carrier concentration. Materials Project gives La3Te4 I-43d mp-879 at hull 0.001 with 6 ICSD references.
note: The La vacancy content between La3Te4 and La2Te3 is the carrier-concentration knob for this material, not an impurity effect, and it is a host-element non-stoichiometry rather than a minor element, so it does not appear in dopant_roles. It is what stage 3 has to compute for this host.
reference_disagreement: Both references put LaTe2 first for this host -- TEDesignLab lists only LaTe2, and MP ranks LaTe2 P4/nmm mp-1329 PRIMARY on 8 ICSD references -- but not one of the 14 compositions is LaTe2. The references are describing which phases exist in the La-Te chemistry, and the papers here made a different one. I take Th3P4 over both.

dopant_roles.basis: Yb0.044La0.377Te0.579 and its siblings: Yb replaces La on the cation site of the Th3P4 cell and, being divalent rather than trivalent, changes the electron count -- which is how the paper tunes the carrier concentration without moving the vacancy content.
La2.8Ca0.2Te4: divalent Ca on the trivalent La site, the same acceptor trick as Yb.

Pb appears in 3 compositions that the chunk file does not print. The first paper is on segmented and cascaded thermoelectric legs, where La3-xTe4 is joined to a PbTe segment, so Pb here is more likely an interface or second-phase artefact than a dopant on the La site. Not resolvable without the composition strings.
Sb appears in 2 compositions not printed in the chunk file, again from the segmented-leg paper. Left unknown rather than guessed.

basis: Rb0.3MoO3 is 10 samples outright and the three W-substituted variants are 3 more, so 13 of 14: this is the molybdenum blue bronze, a monoclinic C2/m stack of ten-octahedron slabs with Rb between them, and the quasi-one-dimensional Peierls conductor that the W-doping and K-doping papers are about. The remaining composition, Rb1.5Mo8O16, is the hollandite named in the first paper title.
note: The seed hypothesis, tungsten_bronze, is refined rather than confirmed. That entry names the tetragonal tungsten bronze Sr0.5Ba0.5Nb2O6 and the cubic AxWO3 bronze; blue bronze shares the AxMO3 formula and the mixed-valence idea but not the framework, and calling it a tungsten bronze would put a one-dimensional layered molybdate into a three-dimensional niobate framework class. The charge-density-wave transition near 180 K sits inside the 18-290 K measured window but is electronic, with a superstructure rather than a new structure type, so no phase change is recorded. Materials Project offers nothing at A0.3MoO3 and every entry it ranks for the host is a molybdate on a single ICSD reference, so mp_id is null.

dopant_roles.basis: Rb0.3Mo0.999W0.001O3 up to Rb0.3Mo0.995W0.005O3: W goes onto the Mo site of the slab at the 0.1-0.5% level, which is the isoelectronic scattering-centre experiment of the third paper rather than a carrier doping.

basis: The host is ScN and its Mg- and Nb-substituted variants; 6 samples are plain ScN. ScN is the rocksalt transition-metal nitride, Fm-3m, and TEDesignLab confirms it directly at mp-2857, hull 0.000, 11 ICSD references. The papers are on epitaxial ScN films, which grow in exactly that structure.

other_polymorphs.note: TEDesignLab lists ScN Pm-3m at hull 1.033 with 5 ICSD references. A whole eV above the hull is not a phase anything is measured in; the ICSD references are most likely to a cubic cell indexed without the anion sublattice. Not reached by heating.

MP gives zincblende ScN at hull 0.304 with 2 ICSD references. Five of the samples are films, where a metastable polymorph can in principle be stabilised, but nothing in the paper titles suggests these are; recorded here so the possibility is not lost.

note: N vacancies are the usual carrier source in ScN films and are a host-element non-stoichiometry rather than a minor element, so they do not appear in dopant_roles.

dopant_roles.basis: Sc0.962Mg0.038N and Sc0.967Mg0.033N: divalent Mg on the trivalent Sc site is an acceptor, used to compensate the natural n-type character of ScN.
Sc0.96Nb0.04N and Sc0.93Nb0.07N: Nb on the Sc site adds electrons, the donor counterpart to the Mg series.

basis: PtSb2 dominates the host -- plain PtSb2, the Ir-substituted series Pt1-xIrxSb2 and the Te-substituted PtSb2-xTex -- and the first paper is titled for Ir doping of PtSb2 with the pyrite structure. Materials Project confirms Sb2Pt Pa-3 mp-562 at hull 0.000 with 4 ICSD references, which is the pyrite setting.
note: One composition of the twelve is PtSb rather than PtSb2, and equiatomic PtSb is the NiAs type, P6_3/mmc, which MP gives at mp-2845 with 4 ICSD references. That is a single sample, so the host is marked mixed only so stage 2 splits it on the Sb:Pt ratio rather than averaging a NiAs arsenide into the pyrite shard.

dopant_roles.basis: Pt0.99Ir0.01Sb2 through Pt0.9Ir0.1Sb2: Ir on the Pt cation site removes an electron per substitution and is the p-type dopant of the first paper.
PtSb1.998Te0.002: Te on the Sb site of the anion dimer is the n-type counterpart, and the third paper is titled for PtSb2-xTex.

basis: The host is elemental tungsten: 8 samples of plain W, one Ta-alloyed, and four W-TiC composites at well under 1% TiC. W is body-centred cubic A2 from room temperature to the melt, and Materials Project ranks W Im-3m mp-91 first at hull 0.000 with 14 ICSD references. There is no structural transition anywhere in the 10-1404 K measured window.

other_polymorphs.note: beta-W, the A15 Pm-3n form, is real but forms only in sputtered films and oxygen-stabilised deposits, never in the bulk rod and wire these samples are. The remaining MP entries for W at hull 0.48 to 1.2 are computed cells, not phases.

note: The curator composition details are revealing and are the reason two samples are not pure metal: one records 1-2 vol% ThO2 with trace Si, Nb, Fe, which is thoriated tungsten, a dispersion-strengthened lamp and electrode material, and another says unalloyed tungsten. Neither changes the matrix structure. A third detail is a note about thermocouple calibration and says nothing about composition. The papers line is also mismatched: the first is titled for niobium and the second for liquid Ga-Zn alloys.

dopant_roles.basis: (W)99.76(TiC)0.24 and siblings: Ti arrives only as TiC, a deliberately dispersed carbide particle, and does not enter the bcc W lattice.
The same TiC dispersion. Not milling residue here -- the TiC fraction is written into the composition on purpose.
W0.98Ta0.02: Ta and W form a continuous bcc solid solution, so Ta simply takes W sites.

basis: AgBi3S5 is 5 samples outright plus two off-stoichiometry variants, and the third paper is titled for it. It is the pavonite-homologue sulfosalt, monoclinic C2/m, which MP gives at mp-23474, hull 0.000, 2 ICSD references: a complex Bi-chalcogenide built from alternating rocksalt-like and Bi-Ag slabs rather than a simple binary type. That is what the bi_chalcogenide_complex entry is for.
note: One composition is AgBiS2, which is a different structure: a cation-disordered rocksalt at room temperature, ordering rhombohedrally on cooling (MP has both, R-3m mp-29678 and P-3m1 mp-1172905, within 0.001 eV of each other). The second paper, on cation disorder and bond anharmonicity, is about that compound and not about AgBi3S5, so the two must not be merged. Confidence is medium because the AgBi3S5 stoichiometry is written three ways across the samples -- AgBi3S5, AgBi3S5.00, AgBi3S5.04 -- which is a deliberate sulfur scan, and the pavonite series has several homologues at nearby compositions.

dopant_roles.basis: AgSb0.3Bi2.7S5: Sb for Bi is a same-group substitution on the same site, tuning the band structure and the lattice thermal conductivity rather than adding carriers. At 10% of the Bi site it is alloying, not doping.
AgBiS1.02Se0.08: Se on the S anion site, same group.
Cl appears in one composition not printed in the chunk file; a halide on a sulfide anion site is the standard n-type donor for this family.

basis: Most of the host is GeTe with Ag8GeTe6 added -- (GeTe)0.92(Ag8GeTe6)0.08 and its siblings, plus the TAGS-like (GeTe)5.5AgIn0.5Sb0.5Te2 -- and the second paper is titled for GeTe-Ag8GeTe6 eutectic composites. The matrix of those samples is rhombohedral GeTe, R3m, which is what the prototype names. Only 2 samples are Ag8GeTe6 on its own.
note: No MEASUREMENT CROSSES A TRANSITION line was printed for this host, because the taxonomy does not name it under gete_rhombohedral -- but the measured window is 81-798 K and the GeTe R3m to Fm-3m transition sits at about 700 K, so the phases are recorded anyway. The 700 K value is the taxonomy default for pure GeTe and shifts with Ag, In and Sb content, so it is approximate for every composition here. These are eutectic composites by design: the Ag8GeTe6 second phase is argyrodite and is present as a distinct phase rather than dissolved, which is why the record is mixed and composite_multiphase is listed. The only reference offered is Ag8GeTe6 P1 mp-685969, a computed triclinic cell with no ICSD backing, so no mp_id is taken.

dopant_roles.basis: (GeTe)5.5AgIn0.5Sb0.5Te2 is a TAGS-type composition: Ag and Sb together substitute for Ge in equal amounts, keeping the electron count while heavily disordering the cation site. Sb is a framework constituent of that alloy rather than a dilute dopant.
The same TAGS-related indium composition; the third paper is titled for TAGS-related indium compounds. In on the Ge site is a resonant-level dopant in this family.
Bi appears in one composition not printed here; on the Ge site of GeTe it is a donor and the usual partner of Sb in this literature.

basis: Ba8Al16Ge30 is 7 of the 13 samples, with Ba8Al14Ge32 and Ba8Al18Ge28 either side of it: that is the type I clathrate, cubic Pm-3n, with Ba filling both cage types of a Ge framework in which Al substitutes to satisfy the Zintl count. But Ba24Al12Ge88 and Ba24Al9Ge91 are 4 more samples and are the type III clathrate, and two of the three papers say so in their titles.
note: The seed hypothesis is refined rather than confirmed: clathrate_i is right for the 8-16-30 compositions but the 24-x-y compositions are a different framework topology, and the split is clean on the Ba:Ge ratio, so stage 2 can make it from composition alone. The first paper, on host structure engineering in thermoelectric clathrates, is about moving between these framework types deliberately. No reference entry offered is a clathrate at all -- MP ranks BaAlGe, Ba(AlGe)2, Ba10Al3Ge7 and Ba3(AlGe)2, all small-cell Zintl compounds of the same chemistry -- so mp_id is left null rather than taken from a compound that is not in the host.
reference_disagreement: assigned sg [223], ICSD-backed references for this host report [187, 71, 139, 193]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: CeCu4Al is 7 samples and its La-diluted form Ce0.8La0.2Cu4Al is 5 more, so 12 of 13 sit at the 1-4-1 stoichiometry. CeCu4Al is a CaCu5-derived hexagonal intermetallic, P6/mmm, with Al taking one of the two framework sites of the CaCu5 cell; the third paper calls it a Kondo lattice, which is the physics that hexagonal structure supports.
