CePd2Ga is 4 of 10 samples and MP gives CeGaPd2 Pnma (62) mp-639863 at hull 0.000 with 3 ICSD references, the best-attested entry here, which is the ordered cementite RT2X type and not the cubic full Heusler an AB2C formula would suggest. CePdGa is 2 samples and is an equiatomic Pnma RTX from a paper on ternary equiatomic compounds. The four CePdxGa4-x compositions with x = 0.4-0.8 are 1:4 and belong to the BaAl4-derived tetragonal family, which MP supports with Ce2Ga10Pd I4/mmm mp-12746. Confidence is low because no paper text was read and two of the three assignments rest on structure-type convention alone.

CePt4Ge12 and its Pr- and Sb-substituted variants are 6 of 10 samples. Pt4Ge12 is the skutterudite framework of tilted PtGe6 octahedra enclosing Ge12 rings, with Ce as the cage guest, and MP prints it as Ce(Ge3Pt)4 Im-3 (204) mp-1190040 at hull 0.000 -- Im-3 is the skutterudite space group. The rest of the host is different structures: CePtGe at 3 samples is an equiatomic Pnma RTX, and Ce3Pt4Ge6 is a third phase again, so the host is mixed and must be split per composition. Note that this filled skutterudite is a superconductor studied for correlated-electron physics rather than a CoSb3-type thermoelectric.

dopant_roles.basis: Pr0.125Ce0.875Pt4Ge12: Pr takes the guest site from Ce, and the paper is titled for probing PrPt4Ge12 superconductivity through Ce substitution. It is a guest-site swap, not framework doping.
CePt4Ge11.5Sb0.5: Sb enters the Ge12 ring of the covalent framework and changes its electron count, the same role Ga or Al play in a clathrate framework.

basis: CeO2 is 9 of 10 samples and MP gives CeO2 Fm-3m (225) mp-20194 at hull 0.000 with 49 ICSD references, the strongest evidence in this chunk. The doped members are written with the oxygen deficit explicit -- Ce0.9Sm0.1O1.95 -- which is fluorite vacancy chemistry on the anion sublattice and not a change of structure. The reduced phases MP also lists, Ce2O3 P-3m1 mp-2721 and Ce7O12 R-3 mp-2629, are not what a pellet sintered and measured in air is, so I do not follow them. Two of the three papers use CeO2 as a nuclear-fuel surrogate rather than as a thermoelectric.

dopant_roles.basis: Gd0.1Ce0.9O2 is gadolinium-doped ceria, the standard solid-electrolyte composition: trivalent Gd on the tetravalent cation site, charge-compensated by oxygen vacancies rather than by carriers.
Ce0.9Sm0.1O1.95, the same acceptor chemistry as Gd with the vacancy count written into the formula.
(Ce3Si2)3.86(CeO2)96.14 is a deliberate two-phase CeO2-Ce3Si2 composite, named as such in its paper title. Silicon is a separate silicide phase, not a substituent in the fluorite lattice.

basis: CePd0.6Rh0.4 is 7 of 10 samples. CePd1-xRhx is the orthorhombic FeB-type solid solution used for the ferromagnetic quantum-criticality work in these papers, a structure of trigonal-prismatic chains rather than either binary end type. The other three samples are Ce(Pd,Rh)3 with B or Ag added, which is the cubic Cu3Au-type CePd3 Kondo lattice at a different stoichiometry, so the host is mixed. Both MP entries for this chemistry, Ce2(PdRh)3 Pmmm mp-1226828 and CePdRh2 P4/mmm mp-1226507, are computed cells above the hull with no ICSD backing and match neither group. Confidence is medium because the FeB assignment rests on the structure-type literature for CePd1-xRhx and not on evidence in this dataset.

dopant_roles.basis: Ce(Pd0.85Rh0.15)3B0.05 and Ce(Pd0.91Rh0.09)3B0.05: in CePd3Bx boron occupies the empty octahedral interstice at the body centre of the Cu3Au cell. It expands the lattice and tunes the Kondo temperature without replacing anything.
Ce(Pd0.85Rh0.09Ag0.06)3: silver sits on the transition-metal site alongside Rh, which is what the substitution-and-doping paper title describes.

basis: CuCoO2 is 9 of 10 samples and two of the three papers name the delafossite explicitly, one for its ion-exchange preparation and one for hole-doped CuCoO2 -- linear O-Cu-O dumbbells linking edge-sharing CoO6 layers, the same CuMO2 family as CuCrO2 and CuAlO2. The remaining sample is Co1.6Cu0.4O4, which is Cu-substituted Co3O4 spinel and a genuinely different structure, so the host is mixed. MP prints no delafossite CuCoO2 for this chemistry at all -- every entry listed is a computed Cu-Co-O cell -- so the reference is silent here rather than contradicting me.

dopant_roles.basis: CuCo1-xMgxO2 at x = 0.0002 to 0.0016: divalent Mg on the trivalent Co site is an acceptor, and the paper is titled for the thermopower of hole-doped delafossite CuCoO2. The levels are extremely dilute, which is the point of the measurement.

basis: Every composition is Co2Ge3S3, that is CoGe1.5S1.5 -- the ternary skutterudite in which the Sb4 rings of CoSb3 are replaced by alternating Ge and S. Ordering the ring lowers the symmetry from cubic Im-3 to rhombohedral, which is exactly what both references report: TEDesignLab gives Co2(GeS)3 at 146 and MP gives R-3 (148) mp-2956 at hull 0.000 with 3 ICSD references. The two references differ on R3 versus R-3, which is a question of Ge/S ordering detail to settle in stage 2, not a different prototype. The cage site is empty here, so this is unfilled skutterudite.

dopant_roles.basis: Co2Ge3-xZnxS3 at x = 0.01 to 0.05, and the paper is titled for partial substitution of Ge. Zinc enters the Ge/S framework ring rather than a cage, so it acts on the electron count of the polyanion.
Co2Ge3-xCdxS3 at x = 0.01 to 0.05, the same site and the same role as Zn.

Listed as a dopant candidate in 3 compositions that the chunk file truncates, so the formula was not seen; by analogy with Zn and Cd in the same single-paper series it is a framework substituent on the Ge site.

reference_disagreement: assigned sg [204], ICSD-backed references for this host report [148, 146]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: Every composition is (Zr0.5Hf0.5)(Co,Ir)Sb with about 1 percent Sn on the Sb site -- the cubic F-43m MgAgAs half Heusler with both the group-4 site and the Co site alloyed, and the first paper is titled for Ir substitution in exactly that phase. Three samples are written as (half-Heusler)100-x(CoSb)x with x up to 4; the second paper is on spinodal decomposition in off-stoichiometric Zr0.5Hf0.5CoSb, so that CoSb is a deliberate second phase in a matrix which is still half-Heusler. Neither reference covers this five-element host.

dopant_roles.basis: Sb0.99Sn0.01 in every composition: tin is one electron short of antimony, so it is the standard acceptor on the main-group site of an XCoSb half-Heusler and the one carrier knob held fixed while Co/Ir is scanned.

solid_solution_axis.note: Co/(Co+Ir) runs 0.30-0.70 with median 0.52. Zr and Hf are alloyed 50:50 on the group-4 site as well, but that pair sits above the 5 percent cut so both are host elements and no axis was flagged for them.

basis: HfCoSb, counting the Sn- and Nb-substituted members, is 9 of 10 samples, and the papers are titled for TiCoSb-ZrCoSb-HfCoSb pseudo-ternaries and for short and long range order of half-Heusler phases in (Ti,Zr,Hf)CoSb -- the cubic F-43m MgAgAs structure with the fourth site vacant. The remaining sample is Hf6CoSb2, the hexagonal P-62m metal-rich 6-1-2 phase which MP lists as mp-1206239 at hull 0.000, so the host is mixed and separates on the Hf:Co ratio. MP has no HfCoSb F-43m entry at all and its only other line, HfCo2Sb Immm mp-1097490 at hull 2.825, is a computed artefact; the reference simply does not cover the phase that dominates this host.

dopant_roles.basis: HfCoSb0.85Sn0.15: tin on the main-group site is the standard acceptor for XCoSb half-Heuslers, and at 15 percent of that site it is heavy p-type doping rather than a trace.
Hf0.88Nb0.12CoSb: niobium has one more valence electron than hafnium, so on the group-4 site it is an n-type donor -- the opposite knob to Sn and on the opposite sublattice.

basis: Every composition is CoV1-xMnxSb for x = 0.25 to 0.8, and the single paper is titled for the galvanomagnetic properties of disordered Mn semi-Heusler phases -- semi-Heusler is half-Heusler, the cubic F-43m MgAgAs structure, here with V and Mn sharing the group-5 site. CoVSb and CoMnSb are both established members of that family, so the whole join is one prototype; the disorder the title reports is site mixing within the structure, not a different one. V and Mn are not isoelectronic, so no solid-solution axis was flagged even though they do share a site -- the electron count varies across the join and that is what the paper is scanning. Neither reference covers this host.

The host is a single composition, CoZr2, across all 10 samples, from a paper on the normal-state anisotropy of superconducting Co1-xZr2. MP gives Zr2Co I4/mcm (140) mp-628 at hull 0.000 with 5 ICSD references, which is the CuAl2 C16 structure the seed hypothesis names. MP ranks ZrCo2 Fd-3m first on 21 ICSD references, but that is the C15 Laves phase at the inverse stoichiometry and nothing here is near it, so the ranking does not bear on this host.

Every composition is ZrFe2-xCrx for x = 0.2 to 1.5, the full AB2 join between two Laves phases -- cubic C15 ZrFe2 and ZrCr2 -- with Fe and Cr sharing the B sublattice of the Frank-Kasper packing. The paper measures ZrFe2-xCrxHy, so these are hydrides and hydrogen occupies interstitial sites; it does not appear in the parsed compositions and does not change the metal framework. MP lists no Laves entry for the ternary: Zr2Cr3Fe, Zr2CrFe3 and ZrCrFe at Amm2 about 0.03 above the hull are computed orderings of this same solid solution, and ZrCrFe F-43m at hull 0.891 is an artefact. The assignment comes from the binary end members, not from those entries.

Every composition is La0.75Sr0.25Cr1-xMnxO3 for x = 0.4 to 0.7, the LSCM solid-oxide-cell electrode: a single ABO3 perovskite with La and Sr on the A site and Cr and Mn sharing the B site. The first paper is titled for the Cr doping effect at the B site of La0.75Sr0.25MnO3 and its phase stability, which is a substitution within one perovskite rather than the formation of a new phase. MP offers only computed ordered supercells with no ICSD backing -- Sr3LaMnCrO8 Amm2 mp-1218443 and the SrLa3Mn2Cr2O12 family in P2, R3, C2 and P1 -- and I do not read those as evidence for B-site ordering: at x near 0.5 in a sintered electrode the Cr/Mn distribution is disordered, so this stays perovskite and not double_perovskite.

The host is a single composition, Eu8Ga16Ge30, but that formula covers two different clathrates and the first paper is titled for the high-temperature thermoelectric properties of alpha- and beta-Eu8Ga16Ge30. Beta is the type I clathrate, Pm-3n, with Eu guests in the 20- and 24-atom cages of a Ga/Ge framework; alpha is the type VIII clathrate, I-43m, a single distorted dodecahedral cage per guest. They are different prototypes at one stoichiometry, so this host cannot be resolved by composition -- it needs the sample. I record type I as the primary because it is the more commonly synthesised and the more commonly measured form, with type VIII as the alternative. MP covers neither: Eu3(Ga2Ge3)2 C2/m mp-1193402 and EuGaGe P6_3/mmc mp-1101845 are unrelated Eu-Ga-Ge phases at other stoichiometries.

Every composition is Eu5In2Sb6 with Zn or Cd on part of the In site, and both papers name the Zintl phase Eu5In2Sb6 in their titles. The 5-2-6 structure is a pair of corner-linked InSb4 tetrahedral chains charge-balanced by divalent Eu, which is exactly the seed hypothesis. Neither reference covers this host, so the assignment rests on the composition and the papers.

dopant_roles.basis: Eu5In2-xZnxSb6 for x = 0.025 to 0.2: divalent Zn on the trivalent In site of the tetrahedral chain is an acceptor, and the paper is titled for Zn-doped Eu5In2Sb6. It substitutes into the polyanion, not into the Eu sublattice.
Eu5In1.98Cd0.02Sb6 and the paper title on Cd substitution in the Zintl phase Eu5In2Sb6: the same acceptor role as Zn on the same site.

basis: Every composition is LaFePO with F on the oxygen site or Sr on the La site. LaFePO is the phosphide member of the 1111 family -- La2O2 fluorite-like layers alternating with anti-PbO FeP layers, the ZrCuSiAs structure -- and the first paper measures LaFePO1-xFx and LaFeAsO1-xFx side by side, which only makes sense because they are isostructural. MP has nothing usable for this host: its single entry, La2FeP2O P4/mmm mp-1211330, sits 1.819 above the hull with no ICSD backing and is not this compound.

dopant_roles.basis: LaFePO1-xFx for x = 0.03 to 0.1. Fluorine on the oxygen site of the La2O2 layer is the doping variable of the whole 1111 family: it injects electrons into the FeP layer and is what drives superconductivity, not an impurity.
La0.9Sr0.1FePO: divalent Sr on the trivalent La site is the hole-doping counterpart to F, acting on the same charge-reservoir layer from the cation side.

Listed as a dopant candidate in 3 compositions that the chunk file truncates, so the formula was not seen. Ce is trivalent like La and the third paper is on Kondo and spin-glass behaviour in a La-based 1111, which is what a dilute rare-earth moment on the A site produces.

basis: Every composition is Fe3-xVxSi for x = 0.2 to 0.92, written either that way or as atomic fractions such as Fe0.7V0.05Si0.25. That join runs from DO3 Fe3Si to L2_1 Fe2VSi, which are the same Fm-3m framework differing only in whether V orders onto one of the two Fe sublattices, so one prototype covers it -- MP gives VFe2Si Fm-3m mp-4595 at hull 0.000 with 3 ICSD references and the first paper is titled for Fe-V-Si Heusler type compounds. The other MP entries, V2FeSi Ama2 mp-1216581 and V5Fe5Si6 Amm2 mp-1216470, are computed cells at stoichiometries none of these samples reach.

The host is URhGa5 and URh0.97Pd0.03Ga5, 10 samples from one paper on Pd-for-Rh substitution in the semimetal URhGa5. The 1-1-5 stoichiometry with a tetragonal P4/mmm cell is the HoCoGa5 structure -- UGa3 cubic blocks intergrown with RhGa2 layers -- and MP confirms it directly as UGa5Rh P4/mmm (123) mp-1078033 at hull 0.000 with an ICSD reference. The other MP entries, UGaRh P-62m mp-1078870 and U2(Ga3Rh)3 Cmcm mp-1208091, are different stoichiometries that no composition here approaches.

dopant_roles.basis: URh0.97Pd0.03Ga5 in 8 of the 10 samples: Pd takes the transition-metal site of the 115 structure and adds one electron per substitution, which is what the paper is measuring on the thermoelectric power of the semimetal.

basis: Every composition is NdGd1+xS3, a mixed rare-earth sesquisulfide (Nd,Gd)2S3 with deliberate cation excess for x = 0.01 to 0.08. The gamma form of a Ln2S3 is the Th3P4-type structure written Ln3-xS4, and the x that two of these papers scan is exactly the cation-vacancy knob that structure provides -- the same carrier-concentration variable as in La3-xTe4. Both thermoelectric papers make the material by sulfurising oxides with CS2, which is the standard route to the gamma phase. Neither reference covers this host at all, so this rests on the sesquisulfide structural chemistry; heavier rare-earth sesquisulfides can take the delta or epsilon forms instead and Gd is the borderline case, so confidence is medium.

The host is a single composition, Sr0.9La0.1(Zr0.25Sn0.25Ti0.25Hf0.25)O3, from one paper titled for a novel high-entropy perovskite ceramic. Four tetravalent cations share the B site in equal parts, which raises the configurational entropy and scatters phonons, but the framework is still corner-sharing BO6 octahedra with Sr on the A site -- a perovskite with a disordered B site, not a new prototype. It is deliberately not filed as high_entropy_alloy, which is a metallic prototype. Neither reference covers a six-element host.

dopant_roles.basis: Sr0.9La0.1: trivalent La on the divalent A site is an electron donor, the standard n-type route in SrTiO3-family titanates and the only carrier knob in this composition -- the B-site mixing is isovalent and adds none.

basis: Every composition is La2Zr2O7 with Y partly on the La site and, in two of them, a little Y on the Zr site with the matching oxygen deficit written out. TEDesignLab gives La2Zr2O7 Fd-3m (227) mp-4974 at hull 0.000 with 8 ICSD references, which confirms the seed pyrochlore and outranks every MP line here. MP PRIMARY entries La3NdZr4O14 and La4CeZr3O14 at R-3m are computed rare-earth-ordered cells for other chemistries, and La2Zr2O7 Pmma mp-674999 sits 0.272 above the hull. Two of the three papers are on thermal barrier coatings, so these curves are thermal conductivity rather than thermoelectric transport.

dopant_roles.basis: (La1-yYy)2Zr2O7 for y = 0.05 to 0.22. Y is trivalent like La so it adds no carriers; it shrinks the A cation and pushes the pyrochlore towards the disordered defect-fluorite limit, which is how these coatings are tuned. In (La0.82Y0.18)2(Zr0.98Y0.02)2O6.98 a small part of the Y sits on the Zr site instead, and the formula records the oxygen vacancy that requires.

basis: Every composition is Li1+xTi2-xO4 around LiTi2O4, and two of the three papers name the spinel superconductor LiTi2O4 in their titles. MP gives LiTi2O4 Fd-3m (227) mp-5670 at hull 0.000 with 6 ICSD references. The Li:Ti ratio moves from Li0.8Ti2.2O4 to Li1.2Ti1.8O4, which is cation redistribution between the tetrahedral and octahedral sites of one spinel -- the Li1+xTi2-xO4 series the first paper is titled for -- rather than a change of phase. The Li2TiO3 and Li2Ti3O7 entries MP also lists are different compounds at ratios no sample here reaches.

dopant_roles.basis: The second paper is titled for the V and Mn doping effects on the spinel superconductor LiTi2O4, so vanadium takes the octahedral Ti site and changes the d-electron count that sets the superconducting transition.

basis: NdMnO3, with Na on part of the Nd site in six of the compositions, is the whole host. MP gives NdMnO3 Pnma (62) mp-25051 at hull 0.000 with 4 ICSD references -- the orthorhombic GdFeO3-tilted, Jahn-Teller distorted manganite perovskite that the seed names. MP ranks NdMn2O5 Pbam mp-19393 first on 5 ICSD references, but that is the mullite-type 125 phase at a Mn:Nd ratio of 2 and nothing here is near it, so I do not follow the ranking. The oxygen content written as 2.97 to 3.09 in the Na-doped members is the usual non-stoichiometry of a sintered manganite. The measurement reaches 1073 K and the RMnO3 Jahn-Teller transition lies near the top of that window, but the chunk file flags no crossing and that transition changes the octahedral distortion within the same perovskite, so no phase sequence is recorded.

dopant_roles.basis: Nd1-xNaxMnO3 for x = 0.03 to 0.21, and the first paper is titled for Nd-Na-Mn-O manganites. Monovalent Na on the trivalent A site is strong hole doping -- each Na forces one extra Mn4+ -- which is the standard way to reach the mixed-valence ferromagnetic metallic state without an alkaline earth.

basis: Every composition is Nd0.7Pb0.3MnO3 with La partly replacing Nd. These are colossal-magnetoresistance manganite perovskites of the R0.7A0.3MnO3 family, with Nd, La and Pb sharing the A site and Mn alone on the B site, and both papers measure exactly that series -- eight of the ten samples are single crystals. MP offers only Nd5Mn8(PbO8)3 Pm-3m mp-1210163 at hull 0.103 with no ICSD backing, a computed cell whose stoichiometry matches nothing here, so the reference gives no support either way.

dopant_roles.basis: (La0.35Nd0.65)0.7Pb0.3MnO3 and La0.2Nd0.5Pb0.3MnO3: La is trivalent like Nd, so it adds no carriers and acts only on the average A-site radius, which is the variable the first paper scans as La1-xNdx. The hole count is set by Pb, which is a host element here.

basis: Tl2Mn2O7 with Sc on the Tl site or Ru on the Mn site is every composition, and MP gives Mn2Tl2O7 Fd-3m (227) mp-25554 at hull 0.000 with 3 ICSD references -- the A2B2O7 pyrochlore the seed names. Two papers call it the colossal-magnetoresistance pyrochlore in their titles; it matters that this is a metallic pyrochlore and not a mixed-valence perovskite manganite, because the magnetoresistance mechanism differs. The MnTlO3 entries MP also lists at P6_3cm, Pnma, P2_1/c and R-3 are computed ilmenite and perovskite alternatives at a 1:1 ratio no composition here approaches.

dopant_roles.basis: Tl2-xScxMn2O7 for x = 0.05 to 0.4. Sc is trivalent where Tl is nominally trivalent too, but it has no 6s states, so replacing Tl withdraws the Tl-6s contribution at the Fermi level -- the first paper is titled for the carrier density change it produces.
Tl2Mn1.95Ru0.05O7: Ru takes the octahedral B site alongside Mn, doping the magnetic sublattice directly rather than the A site.

basis: The host is one composition, NdN, 10 samples from one paper on polycrystalline NdN bulk with various porosities. MP gives NdN Fm-3m (225) mp-2599 at hull 0.000 with 21 ICSD references -- the rocksalt rare-earth mononitride, the strongest single piece of reference evidence in this host. The experimental variable in the paper is porosity, not chemistry, so every sample is the same phase.

other_polymorphs.note: NdN Pm-3m at hull 0.781 with a single ICSD reference. Rare-earth mononitrides convert B1 to B2 under compression, so this is the high-pressure form and is not reached anywhere in the 297-1473 K measurement.

basis: NbSb2 is 8 of 10 samples and MP gives NbSb2 C2/m (12) mp-1969 at hull 0.000 with 5 ICSD references, listing no Pnnm polymorph at all. NbSb2 and TaSb2 are OsGe2-type monoclinic semimetals, so the seed hypothesis marcasite is rejected outright rather than refined, and a new prototype osge2_monoclinic is proposed for the family. The other two samples are written (Zn0.005Nb0.995)4Sb3 and (Zn0.01Nb0.99)4Sb3, but their paper is titled for the effects of Nb doping on the thermoelectric properties of Zn4Sb3: the Zn and Nb fractions have been transposed in transcription, and those samples are really Nb-doped Zn4Sb3 belonging to the zn4sb3 prototype and to a Zn-Sb host. I record that rather than assigning them here quietly.

dopant_roles.basis: Zn appears only in the two (ZnxNb1-x)4Sb3 compositions, and only because the fractions were transposed -- the paper dopes Zn4Sb3 with a little Nb, not the reverse. Within the Nb-Sb host Zn is therefore an artefact of the formula string, not a dopant; stage 3 should not compute a level for it and the two samples should be rerouted.

basis: The host is a single composition, TmNiSb, across all 10 samples, and all three papers are titled for half-Heusler RENiSb phases and their solid solutions. MP gives TmNiSb F-43m (216) mp-4025 at hull 0.000 with 2 ICSD references, the cubic MgAgAs structure with the fourth tetrahedral site vacant. Tm5Ni2Sb I4/mcm mp-1207984, the other MP line, is a metal-rich phase no sample reaches. The third paper describes a composite based on the half-Heusler antimonide, so a minority second phase may be present in some samples without changing what the matrix is.

Sr2RhO4, counting the Ce-substituted members, is 6 of 10 samples: the n = 1 Ruddlesden-Popper K2NiF4 stack of single RhO2 sheets between SrO rock-salt layers. MP gives Sr2RhO4 I4_1/acd (142) mp-757102 at hull 0.000, and the I4_1/acd setting rather than I4/mmm reflects a rotation of the RhO6 octahedra within the same prototype. The host is not single-phase, though: SrRhO3 is a perovskite, and Sr5CoRh3O12 is what the first paper calls a quasi-one-dimensional oxide -- a hexagonal face-sharing-chain oxide of the Ca3Co2O6 family, not a layered rhodate. Three prototypes, so this must be split per composition.

dopant_roles.basis: Sr2-xCexRhO4 for x = 0.1 to 0.2. Ce enters the rock-salt SrO layer as a tetravalent ion on a divalent site, so it is strong electron doping of the RhO2 sheet -- the third paper is titled for a charge-doping driven metal-insulator transition, which is that knob.

Co appears only in Sr5CoRh3O12, where it shares the face-sharing octahedral chain with Rh. It is a constituent of that chain compound rather than a dopant in Sr2RhO4, so its role is tied to the composition it belongs to.

basis: Every composition is TiRu1+xSb for x = 0.1 to 1.0, from one paper titled for half-Heusler-like compounds with wide continuous compositions and tunable properties. TiRuSb at the bottom of the range is the cubic F-43m MgAgAs half-Heusler, which MP lists as TiSbRu mp-31458 with an ICSD reference, and TiRu2Sb at the top is the L2_1 full Heusler: the extra Ru fills the vacant tetrahedral site of the half-Heusler cell, so the series is a continuous filling between two prototypes rather than two unrelated phases. The host is marked mixed for that reason and splits on the Ru:Ti ratio. MP places TiSbRu 0.093 above the hull, which for a compound with an ICSD reference is a hull artefact rather than evidence against it.

Sb2Te3-ySey for y = 0.6 to 1.8 is 6 of the 8 compositions: the tetradymite quintuple layer with Se and Te sharing the chalcogen sites, and two of the papers scan exactly that join in Sb2Te3. MP supports it with Sb2Te2Se R-3m (166) mp-3525 carrying 2 ICSD references; its hull value of 0.660 is the layered-chalcogenide artefact of the 2019 dump that the chunk header warns about, so I do not read it as instability. The remaining two compositions, Te0.97(Sb2Se3)0.03 and Te0.90(Sb2Se3)0.10, are elemental tellurium with a few percent Sb2Se3 added -- a trigonal Te matrix, a different prototype -- so the host is mixed and those two split off on the Te fraction.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: chalcogen sites of the quintuple layer
solid_solution_axis.note: Se/(Se+Te) runs 0.08-0.60 with median 0.33. Within the tetradymite compositions this is genuine anion alloying, but the two Te-rich points at the bottom of the range are the elemental-Te samples rather than dilute Se in Sb2Te3, so the axis should not be read across the whole host.

basis: Every composition is Sb2Si2Te6 or a Te-rich variant of it, all from one paper titled for high-performance thermoelectrics from cellular nanostructured Sb2Si2Te6. The structure is the Cr2Si2Te6 type: a van der Waals stack in which one third of the octahedral sites between two Te sheets carries an Si-Si dimer standing perpendicular to the layer, with the trivalent cation sublattice partly vacant at this stoichiometry. Nothing in the taxonomy covered it and neither reference covers the host, so cr2si2te6_layered is proposed. Sb2Si2Te6.43, Sb2Si2Te6.93 and Sb2Si2Te7.5 are excess-Te variants of the same phase, not separate structures. Confidence is medium because the structure type comes from the literature on this one compound with no reference line to test it against.

Every composition is BaAgSb with the Ba content moved deliberately from 0.97 to 1.01, and one sample carrying Eu. MP gives BaAgSb P6_3/mmc (194) mp-1205316 at hull 0.000 with an ICSD reference: that hexagonal ABX setting is the ZrBeSi type, an ordered AlB2 derivative in which the honeycomb layer alternates Ag and Sb with Ba between the layers. That is precisely the quasi-2D structure the second paper title invokes, and the first paper is a point-defect study in the same Zintl phase, which is what the deliberate Ba off-stoichiometry is for. Ba2AgSb Fm-3m mp-984720 is a computed cell 0.023 above the hull at a stoichiometry no sample reaches.

dopant_roles.basis: Ba0.97Eu0.1AgSb: divalent Eu on the divalent Ba site adds no carriers, only a 4f moment and a smaller cation. The carrier count in this host is set by the Ba vacancy concentration instead, which is why the compositions scan Ba from 0.97 to 1.01.

basis: Seven of the nine samples are AgBiTe films, from a paper on thermoelectric generators from AgBiTe and AgSbTe thin films. AgBiTe2 is the cation-disordered rocksalt of the AgSbTe2 family -- Ag and Bi share one cation sublattice and order along a cube diagonal when they order at all, which is what MP records as AgBiTe2 R-3m (166) mp-29656 with 2 ICSD references at hull 0.018. The other two samples are different materials: Ag0.4Bi2Te3 is tetradymite Bi2Te3 with 5 vol percent Ag nanoparticles, which the curator states outright, and the third is an Ag2Te-Bi2Te3 nanowire composite. So the host is mixed. All the majority samples are films, and a film is exactly where a cation ordering that bulk synthesis would not give can be stabilised, so the R-3m and Fm-3m variants must not be treated as interchangeable in stage 2.

AlB12 is 5 of 9 samples, three are Y0.62AlyB14 for y = 1.24 to 1.86, and one is AlB2. The seed hypothesis boron_carbide is the rhombohedral B4C type with its inter-icosahedral C-B-C chain, which none of these is, so it is refined into two new icosahedral-boride prototypes rather than accepted: alb12_icosahedral for AlB12, which is a tetragonal framework of B12 and B19 units with Al in channels, and mgalb14_boride for the Y-Al-B14 series, which is orthorhombic with two partly occupied metal sites. The Y paper is titled for a rapid synthesis route to complex thermoelectric borides, and the fractional Al and Y occupancies in those formulae are structural rather than doping levels. The Al/(Al+B) axis the chunk file flags is not a shared sublattice: Al and B are both group 13, but Al never substitutes for B here -- it sits in framework channels in AlB12, in its own layer in AlB2 and on a metal site in YAlB14 -- so the 0.08 to 0.33 spread just reflects three different compounds and no solid-solution axis is recorded. MP prints only AlB2 P6/mmm mp-944 for this host and covers neither icosahedral phase.

dopant_roles.basis: Y falls just under the 5 at. percent cut in Y0.62Al1.24B14 but it is a structural constituent, not a dopant: the MgAlB14 framework has a second, larger metal site and the rare earth is what fills it. Without Y those three compositions would not be this compound at all, so stage 3 should not compute a doping level from the 0.62.

basis: Every composition is (Ce1-xNdx)3Al, from one paper on the physical and magnetic properties of that series. The light rare-earth R3Al trialuminides take the hexagonal Ni3Sn DO19 ordering of close-packed AB3, the prototype already proposed for CeAl3 and LaAl3, and the measurement stops at 295 K. Ce3Al is the awkward member: a cubic Cu3Au-type form also exists and which one is present depends on heat treatment, so that is recorded as a polymorph and confidence is medium. MP offers only CeNdAl4 F-43m mp-1226518 at hull 0.019 with no ICSD backing, a computed 1-1-4 cell matching no composition here. Note that the composition string (Ce0.7Nd3)3Al is a transcription error in the source; the other eight are consistent with x running 0.1 to 0.81.

other_polymorphs.note: Ce3Al is also reported in the cubic Cu3Au L1_2 ordering. Which form a sample holds depends on annealing rather than on temperature within the measured 10-295 K window, so it is kept out of the thermal sequence and flagged for the paper to settle.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: rare-earth site of the AB3 cell
solid_solution_axis.note: Ce/(Ce+Nd) runs 0.19-0.90 with median 0.50; both are trivalent rare earths on one site, so no end member is the parent and stage 3 should record the site fraction.

basis: Every composition is CeRu2Al10 with a little Y or La on the Ce site, and the papers are titled for the anisotropic transport of CeRu2Al10 and for the effects of Y- and La-doping on its ordering and Kondo behaviour. MP confirms the phase directly as Ce(Al5Ru)2 Cmcm (63) mp-31364 at hull 0.000 with 2 ICSD references -- the YbFe2Al10 type, an orthorhombic aluminium cage framework around the rare earth, which had no taxonomy entry, so ybfe2al10_cage is proposed. The other MP lines here, Ce2AlRu2 Cmce, Ce5Al2Ru3 R3, Ce3(Al3Ru)4 P6_3/mmc and CeAlRu Pnma, are all genuine Ce-Al-Ru compounds but at stoichiometries no composition in this host reaches.

dopant_roles.basis: Ce1-xYxRu2Al10 at x = 0.05 and 0.1. Y is trivalent but has no 4f electron, so it dilutes the Kondo lattice site by site -- the third paper is titled for exactly that effect on the magnetic ordering.
Ce1-xLaxRu2Al10 at x = 0.05 and 0.1: the same non-magnetic dilution as Y, with a larger cation, run in parallel in the same paper to separate size effects from 4f dilution.

basis: Every composition is (Fe1-xCox)2VAl for x = 0.12 to 0.5, and both papers are titled for that series. Fe2VAl is the archetypal L2_1 full Heusler pseudogap thermoelectric and Co substitutes on the Fe sublattice to move the Fermi level across the pseudogap. MP gives AlVFeCo F-43m (216) mp-1008530 with an ICSD reference at hull 0.027; F-43m rather than Fm-3m is what results when Fe and Co order onto the two distinct Fe sites, which at x = 0.5 would make FeCoVAl a quaternary Heusler rather than a disordered full Heusler. Only one sample sits at x = 0.5 and the papers treat the series as a solid solution, so I keep the full Heusler label and flag the ordering question for stage 2 rather than splitting the host on one sample.
reference_disagreement: assigned sg [225], ICSD-backed references for this host report [216]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: Every composition is Sr8AlxGa16-xSi30 for x = 7 to 12, and the single paper is titled for the synthesis and thermoelectric properties of silicon clathrates Sr8AlxGa16-xSi30. That is the type I clathrate: a Pm-3n sp3 silicon framework into which Al and Ga substitute, with Sr filling the 20- and 24-atom cages, and the 8:16:30 stoichiometry is what makes the framework electron-precise. The seed hypothesis is confirmed. Neither reference covers this four-element host.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: framework sites of the type I clathrate cage
solid_solution_axis.note: Al/(Al+Ga) runs 0.31-0.75 with median 0.56. Both are group 13 and both substitute into the same Si framework, so the total of 16 is fixed by electron counting while the Al:Ga split is the variable the paper scans -- it changes the framework bonding and the lattice thermal conductivity, not the carrier count.

basis: Every composition is K8Al8Si38 or its Ba-substituted form K8-xBaxAl8+xSi38-x, and all three papers are titled for type I clathrates in this system, one of them for tuning their thermoelectric properties along exactly that substitution line. The framework is the Pm-3n silicon network with Al substituting into it and K in the cages -- the same type I architecture as Ba8Ga16Ge30 but with a monovalent guest, which is why the framework Al count is 8 rather than 16. MP prints only KAlSi2 I4_1/acd mp-1180795 at hull 0.054 with one ICSD reference, a dense non-clathrate ternary that matches no composition here, so the reference does not reach the phase.

dopant_roles.basis: K8-xBaxAl8+xSi38-x for x = 1 to 2: Ba takes cage sites from K, and because it is divalent each swap is compensated by one more Al in the framework -- the third paper title carries that coupled formula. It is a guest-site substitution that sets the electron count jointly with the framework, not an independent dopant.

reference_disagreement: assigned sg [223], ICSD-backed references for this host report [142]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: Every composition is Al71Pd20(Re,Ru)9, one of them tagged _IQC in the source, and two of the papers are titled for Al-Pd-Re(-Ru) icosahedral quasicrystals. Al-Pd-Re is the canonical high-resistivity icosahedral quasicrystal and Ru substitutes for Re on the transition-metal site without destroying the quasiperiodic order, which is what the first paper measures. The seed hypothesis is confirmed. MP offers only Al2PdRu Fm-3m mp-862715, a computed cubic cell with no ICSD backing, which is not a quasicrystal at all -- consistent with the README note that this prototype has no periodic structure and that stage 2 must map it to a named approximant and say so.

dopant_roles.basis: The series runs continuously from Al71Pd20Re9 to Al71Pd20Ru9, so Re and Ru share the transition-metal site and the parsed minority element depends on which end a composition sits at. Re is the element the classic Al-Pd-Re quasicrystal is built on, and the first paper measures the effect of replacing it with Ru; the two are not isoelectronic, so the substitution changes the pseudogap filling.

basis: BAs is the dominant phase: two compositions written BAs plus six written B21As20I, which is BAs at a 21:20 ratio carrying iodine. Both Science papers here are the 2018 measurements of unusually high thermal conductivity in cubic boron arsenide crystals, which are grown by chemical vapour transport with iodine as the transport agent -- that is where the I comes from. TEDesignLab gives BAs F-43m (216) mp-10044 with 3 ICSD references, the zincblende structure, and that is what those papers measure. One sample is B12As2, the icosahedral boron subarsenide isostructural with B4C, a genuinely different structure, so the host is mixed. MP ranks B6As R-3m mp-624 PRIMARY on 3 ICSD references and puts BAs 0.080 above the hull, but B6As is another icosahedral boride at a ratio no sample here has; I follow TEDesignLab and the papers rather than that ranking.

dopant_roles.basis: Iodine appears only in the six B21As20I compositions, at about 2 at. percent. BAs single crystals are grown by chemical vapour transport with iodine, so this is residual transport agent rather than a lattice substituent -- there is no site in zincblende BAs for it, and the papers are about intrinsic thermal conductivity, which they would not be if it were doped.

basis: The host is a single composition, Ce0.6Y0.4FeAsO0.8F0.2, across all 9 samples, from one paper on the correlation between superconductivity and structure under pressure. This is the 1111 iron arsenide: (Ce,Y)2O2 fluorite-like layers alternating with anti-PbO FeAs layers, the ZrCuSiAs structure, with F on the oxygen site at the standard 20 percent electron-doping level and Y substituting for Ce on the rare-earth site as chemical pressure. F is not flagged as a dopant candidate because one fifth of the oxygen site puts it exactly at the 5 at. percent cut, so it counts into the host. The seed hypothesis is confirmed. Neither reference covers this six-element host, and the 10-149 K window confirms this is a superconductivity study rather than thermoelectric characterisation.

Every composition is NdFe1-xRuxAsO0.89F0.11 for x = 0.3 to 0.8, from one paper on the effects of Ru doping on transport and the superconducting transition. The structure is the same 1111 ZrCuSiAs type as LaFeAsO -- Nd2O2 layers alternating with (Fe,Ru)As layers -- with Ru isovalent on the Fe site and the electron doping supplied entirely by F on the oxygen site, which is held fixed at 0.11 across the series. Neither reference covers this host.

dopant_roles.basis: O0.89F0.11 in every composition: fluorine on the oxygen site of the Nd2O2 charge-reservoir layer is the doping variable of the 1111 family, injecting electrons into the (Fe,Ru)As layer. Held constant here so that Ru content is the only variable.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: transition-metal site of the pnictide layer
solid_solution_axis.note: Fe/(Fe+Ru) runs 0.20-0.70 with median 0.50. Fe and Ru are both group 8, so this is isovalent substitution within the conducting layer -- it dilutes the magnetism and applies chemical pressure without changing the carrier count, which F sets separately.

basis: CaB6 with Sr, Ba or Yb partly on the Ca site is every composition, and the papers are titled for the thermoelectric properties of alkaline-earth hexaborides and of metal hexaborides generally. MP gives CaB6 Pm-3m (221) mp-865 at hull 0.000 with 10 ICSD references -- the CsCl-like packing of Ca cations and covalently bonded B6 octahedra that the seed names. CaB4 P4/mbm mp-1213975 and CaB2 P6/mmm mp-1009695 are other Ca-B phases at boron ratios no composition here reaches. Note that Ca0.75B4.5Sr0.25B1.5 is a split-boron transcription of Ca0.75Sr0.25B6 and is the same material as the entry above it, not a fifth compound.

dopant_roles.basis: Ca0.75Sr0.25B6: Sr is divalent like Ca, so the B6 framework charge balance is unchanged and the substitution acts on the cation size and the phonon spectrum. The second paper is on high-pressure densified solid solutions of alkaline-earth hexaborides, which is this axis.
Ca0.75Ba0.25B6: the same divalent cation-site alloying as Sr, one row further down.

Ca0.95Yb0.05B6. Yb is nominally divalent in YbB6 and so nominally isovalent with Ca, but it is the one alkaline-earth-like substituent here that can be mixed-valent, which is why hexaboride doping studies single it out; I record it as substitutional rather than isoelectronic for that reason.

basis: The host is HfB2 with two off-stoichiometric points, HfB1.9 and HfB2.1. MP gives HfB2 P6/mmm (191) mp-1994 at hull 0.000 with 14 ICSD references -- the AlB2 structure of alternating Hf layers and flat boron honeycombs. All three papers are on ultra-high-temperature ceramics and report thermal conductivity and oxidation rather than thermoelectric transport, and the full span reaches 2173 K, which is refractory characterisation. HfB, HfB12 and HfB6 in the MP list are other Hf-B phases at ratios these samples do not approach.

Every composition is Bi1.6-1.8Ba2(Co,Rh)2O8, which the second paper writes out as [Bi2Ba2O4]p(Co,Rh)O2 in its title -- the misfit layered cobaltite: a rock-salt Bi-Ba-O block intergrown with a CdI2-type (Co,Rh)O2 sheet, the two subsystems incommensurate along one in-plane axis. That is the seed hypothesis and the paper states it. Neither reference covers the host, which is expected rather than a gap: an incommensurate composite has no single Materials Project entry, and the README flags this prototype for special handling in stage 2, where it needs one structure per subsystem.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: octahedral site of the CdI2-type (Co,Rh)O2 sheet
solid_solution_axis.note: Co/(Co+Rh) runs 0.40-0.60 with median 0.50, entirely within the conducting sheet; the rock-salt block is untouched. Both papers are titled for cobalt-rhodium oxides, so this join is the subject rather than a dopant series.

basis: Eight of the nine compositions are Ba1-xNaxCu2Se2 and the single paper is titled for BaCu2Se2 based compounds as promising thermoelectric materials. TEDesignLab gives both forms of that compound: Ba(CuSe)2 Pnma (62) mp-4473 at hull 0.004 with 2 ICSD references and Ba(CuSe)2 I4/mmm (139) mp-10437 at hull 0.036 with 1. These are the alpha form, the BaCu2S2 type with puckered CuSe layers, and the beta form, the ThCr2Si2 type. I take alpha as the primary on the ICSD count, and record beta as a polymorph rather than a thermal phase: which form is obtained is a synthesis outcome in this family and there is no evidence that the 21-771 K window crosses a conversion, so it does not belong in a phase sequence. The ninth composition, Ba1Cu2Se3, is a different compound again -- a BaCu2S3-type chain structure, for which the taxonomy has no entry -- so the host is mixed and stage 2 should propose one for it.

other_polymorphs.note: beta-BaCu2Se2, the I4/mmm ThCr2Si2-type form, 1 ICSD reference against 2 for the Pnma alpha form. Kept out of phases because nothing establishes it as reached on heating within the measured window; the paper should settle which form these samples are.

dopant_roles.basis: Ba1-xNaxCu2Se2 for x = 0.005 to 0.1: monovalent Na on the divalent Ba site is an acceptor, the hole-doping knob the paper scans across the whole series.

basis: Every composition is an ABO3 ferrite with the rare earth and the alkaline earth sharing the A site and Fe on the octahedral B site: Nd0.4Ba0.6Fe0.9Ni0.1O3, Nd0.5Ba0.5Fe0.9Co0.1O3, La0.04Nd0.46Sr0.24Ba0.26FeO3. All three papers are on Ln0.5M0.5FeO3-delta electrode materials, so oxygen non-stoichiometry is part of the chemistry. Confidence is medium rather than high because at Ln0.5Ba0.5FeO3-delta the large Ba and the small Nd frequently order into alternating A-site layers, giving the NdBaFe2O5+delta double perovskite -- and that is exactly what MP offers as its best-attested entry for this host, BaNdFe2O5 Pmc2_1 (26) mp-1182187 at hull 0.000 with 2 ICSD references. Whether these samples are A-site ordered cannot be decided from the composition, since the ordered and disordered forms share it, so the simple perovskite is recorded with the double perovskite as the alternative.

dopant_roles.basis: Nd0.4Ba0.6Fe0.9Ni0.1O3 and Nd0.6Ba0.4Fe0.9Ni0.1O3: Ni on the octahedral B site, the standard way this family is tuned.
Nd0.4Ba0.6Fe0.9Cu0.1O3, B-site substitution at the same level as Ni.
Nd0.5Ba0.5Fe0.9Co0.1O3, B-site substitution.
La0.04Nd0.46Sr0.24Ba0.26FeO3: Sr is a third A-site cation alongside Nd and Ba rather than a dopant, and falls below the cut only because the A site is shared four ways.
La0.04Nd0.46Sr0.24Ba0.26FeO3: a minor A-site rare earth, isovalent with Nd.

basis: The single composition Ba0.92Ni4Sb6.7Sn5.3 is the paper own subject, Ba-filled Ni-Sb-Sn based skutterudites. Sb plus Sn totals 12.0 per four Ni, which is the CoSb3 framework count exactly, so the structure is a Ni4(Sb,Sn)12 corner-linked pnictide framework with Ba in the icosahedral void. Sn-for-Sb on the framework is what compensates the electrons that filling with divalent Ba adds, which is why the ratio lands where it does. Ba sits at 5.4 at.% so the split carries it as a host element rather than a dopant candidate, but structurally it is the cage filler, and the anomalously low lattice thermal conductivity in the title is the rattling it produces. No reference entry is offered for this quaternary.

Every composition is BaZn2Sb2 with a trace of Ag, and the first paper calls it a Zintl compound in its title. MP gives Ba(ZnSb)2 Pnma (62) mp-14207 at hull 0.000 as the primary, which is the alpha-BaCu2S2 type: puckered edge-sharing ZnSb4 tetrahedral layers separated by Ba. Ba is far too large for the CaAl2Si2 trigonal form that the lighter AM2Pn2 Zintls take, which is consistent. I record a disagreement with ref 1: TEDesignLab covers Ba2ZnSb2 Ibam (72) mp-1079149, a 2-1-2 compound at a different stoichiometry from anything measured here, so despite being the preferred reference it does not bear on BaZn2Sb2. Confidence is medium because the Pnma primary rests on a single ICSD reference and the alpha/beta choice in this family is synthesis-dependent.

other_polymorphs.note: Ba(ZnSb)2 I4mm at hull 0.209 with no ICSD reference -- a computed polar variant, not a phase these samples pass through.

dopant_roles.basis: Ba(Zn1-xAgx)2Sb2 for x = 0.002 to 0.01, and the second paper is titled for Ag substitution at the Zn site. Monovalent Ag on divalent Zn is an acceptor, the hole-doping knob scanned across the series.

basis: All six compositions are Bi2Te3 carrying copper -- Bi0.38Te0.57Cu0.05 is the Bi2Te3 ratio with 5 at.% Cu, and Bi2.23Te3Cu0.97 the heavily loaded end -- and both papers say so, one on Cu-doped Bi2Te3 films and one on heavily Cu-doped Bi2Te3 nanoparticles. Copper in Bi2Te3 goes into the van der Waals gap between Te-Bi-Te-Bi-Te quintuple layers as an intercalant, and at low levels onto the Bi site; neither disturbs the R-3m tetradymite stacking, which is why CuxBi2Te3 is reported as single phase over this whole range. Cu exceeds 5 at.% in every composition so it is carried as a host element and does not appear as a dopant candidate. The chunk flags that films are present and a metastable polymorph could in principle be reachable, but nothing in these compositions or titles points to one. No reference entry is offered for the ternary.

The single composition PrO0.1F0.9BiS2 is a REO1-xFxBiS2 layered superconductor, and the paper is on BiS2-based superconductors. The seed taxonomy exemplar for this prototype is literally PrO0.5F0.5BiS2 and its listed example host is Bi-F-O-Pr-S, the same chemistry at a lower F level; no seed hypothesis line printed here only because O falls under 5 at.% at x = 0.9 and so drops out of the host key. Fluorite-like Pr(O,F) layers alternate with BiS2 bilayers in P4/nmm. No reference entry is offered.

dopant_roles.basis: This is the one host in the chunk where oxygen is not milling residue. The O/F site is the doping variable of the REO1-xFxBiS2 family, and PrO0.1F0.9BiS2 sits at the far F-rich end of that line, so O is the minority end member on a shared site rather than a dopant added to the lattice. It falls under the 5 at.% cut only because it is 0.1 of 4.1 atoms.

basis: The compositions are the BiFeO3-PbTiO3 solid solution written out explicitly, (Bi0.8La0.2FeO3)0.57(PbTiO3)0.43, and both papers are on BiFeO3-PbTiO3 piezoelectric ceramics near the morphotropic phase boundary. Both end members are ABO3 perovskites and the join is a single perovskite phase, tetragonal and rhombohedral variants coexisting at the boundary. The (Fe2O3)0.025 to (Fe2O3)0.25 terms are excess hematite added for insulation, a deliberate second phase rather than part of the perovskite, so they do not change the host label. I disagree with the reference: the five MP candidates are Cmm2, P1 and Imm2 quaternary Bi-Pb-Fe-Ti-O cells with no ICSD backing at all, computed orderings that do not describe a 57:43 solid solution, and the primary flags on them mean only that nothing better exists in the snapshot.

dopant_roles.basis: Bi0.8La0.2FeO3: La on the A site of the BiFeO3 end member, the usual way its leakage and volatility are controlled.
(BiFeO3)0.6(PbTiO3)0.27Ba0.13(Zr0.5Ti0.5)0.13O0.39: Ba enters the A site as part of a BaZr0.5Ti0.5O3 third end member.
Same composition: Zr on the octahedral B site alongside Ti, from the BaZr0.5Ti0.5O3 addition.

basis: All four compositions are LaOBiS2-xSex and all three papers name that compound, one of them in its title as LaOBiS2-xSex. This is the CeOBiS2 type in P4/nmm: fluorite-like La2O2 layers alternating with a BiCh2 bilayer, with Se substituting for S inside that bilayer. Here the F-for-O knob of the family is untouched and the tuning is on the chalcogen instead. No reference entry is offered.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: the chalcogen site of the BiCh2 bilayer
solid_solution_axis.note: S/(S+Se) runs 0.50 to 0.80 with median 0.70, so these span genuine alloy through to S-rich, and no single parent covers the host. Note that oxygen is also group 16 but is NOT on this axis: it sits in the La2O2 fluorite layer and never exchanges with the bilayer chalcogen, which is the BiCuSeO caution in the README applying directly here.

basis: Bi1.8Sr2Rh1.6O8 and Bi0.78Sr0.4RhO3 are two ways of writing the same misfit layered rhodium oxide, [Bi2Sr2O4][RhO2]x: a rock-salt Bi-Sr-O block intergrown with a CdI2-type RhO2 sheet, the two subsystems incommensurate along one in-plane axis, with the second formula normalised per RhO2 and the first per rock-salt block. Two of the papers are on layered or misfit-layered rhodium oxides and the third puts the compound in the misfit-layered-cobalt-oxide family in its own title. I assign misfit_cobaltite because it is the taxonomy entry for this structure and it already lists Ba-Bi-Co-O-Rh among its example hosts, but I disagree with its name rather than quietly matching it: there is no cobalt at all here, the conducting sheet is RhO2, and the prototype should be renamed metal-agnostic in v4. As the README notes for this prototype, an incommensurate composite has no single MP entry, so the absence of a reference line is expected and stage 2 needs one structure per subsystem.

dopant_roles.basis: (Bi0.8Pb0.2)1.8Sr2Rh1.6O8 and (Bi0.9Pb0.1)1.8Sr2Rh1.6O8: Pb replaces Bi inside the rock-salt block, the carrier-doping route in every Bi-based misfit oxide, leaving the RhO2 sheet alone.

basis: The single composition Bi4O4S3 is the parent of the BiS2-based superconductor family reported in 2012, which is exactly what the one paper is on. Its structure is Bi2O2 fluorite-like layers alternating with BiS2 bilayers in I4/mmm, with a partially occupied SO4 layer between them supplying the carriers, so it belongs with the layered BiS2 compounds and nowhere else in the taxonomy. Confidence is medium because the seed entry is written around REO1-xFxBiS2 in P4/nmm and this is the sulfate-interlayer member at a different symmetry and a different doping mechanism. I disagree with the reference completely: every MP candidate offered is a bismuth sulfate or oxysulfide at an unrelated stoichiometry -- Bi2SO7, Bi2(SO4)3, Bi2SO2, Bi2S2O9, even a cobalt-bearing sulfate -- and none of them is Bi4O4S3. That is the 2019 snapshot lacking the compound rather than these being alternatives to it.

Every composition is ZrCxNy with x plus y running from 0.79 to 0.96, and the single paper is a review of ZrC, ZrN and ZrCN ceramics. ZrC and ZrN are both rocksalt and completely miscible, so the carbonitride is one Fm-3m phase with C and N sharing the anion site at random and the shortfall from unity being anion vacancies, which is the non-stoichiometry this prototype is written for. I disagree with the reference: the three MP candidates offered, Zr2CN, Zr4C3N and Zr4CN3, are all R-3m and all without ICSD backing -- computed ordered C/N arrangements on the same rocksalt lattice. They are a statement about which orderings are low in energy, not about what a sintered carbonitride is, and the material measured here is the disordered solid solution.

The compositions are C@PbTe and PbTeCx for x from 0.28 to 2.8, the curator records PbTe-graphene nanocomposites for five samples, and two of the three papers are titled for PbTe-graphene nanocomposites. The host is rocksalt PbTe with carbon as a separate phase -- graphene sheets or a carbon shell at the grain boundaries -- not a ternary compound. I reject the detected C/(C+Pb) solid-solution axis and leave solid_solution_axis null: C and Pb are both group 14, but carbon does not enter the PbTe cation site at any level, and PbTeC2.8 reads as 74 at.% carbon only because a two-phase nanocomposite was written as one formula. This is the composite-additive failure mode the README warns about, so the carbon is recorded as a second phase and does not relabel the host.

dopant_roles.basis: The third paper is on n-type PbTe, and iodine on the Te site is the standard n-type donor for it. Carbon is the other minor species by the 5 at.% test but it is a second phase rather than a lattice species, so it is described in the basis instead of being given a dopant role.

basis: Every composition is Pr1-xCaxFe1-yMyO3 with x from 0.3 to 0.7 and M = Ni, W or Co -- an ABO3 ferrite with Pr and Ca sharing the A site and Fe holding the octahedral B site. Two of the four papers name Pr0.5Ca0.5Fe0.9W0.1O3 and Pr0.6Ca0.4Fe0.8Co0.2O3 as perovskites directly. Confidence is medium because the third paper is on a Co-free perovskite/brownmillerite nanocomposite: at these Ca levels the oxygen deficiency can order into brownmillerite layers, which is a different prototype at a composition the parser cannot distinguish, since the delta in ABO3-delta is not written out. MP offers only CaPr3(FeO3)4 Pm mp-1227161 with no ICSD backing, a computed A-site ordering rather than a measured phase.

dopant_roles.basis: Pr1-xCaxFe0.8Ni0.2O3 across five compositions: Ni on the octahedral B site.
Pr0.5Ca0.5Fe0.9W0.1O3: hexavalent W on the B site, a donor that compensates the Ca acceptor.
Pr0.6Ca0.4Fe0.8Co0.2O3 from the third paper: B-site substitution.

basis: Every composition is Yb14-xCaxMnSb11 with x from 2 to 8, plus the Mn-free Yb14Ca2Sb11, and the first paper is titled Enhanced High-Temperature Thermoelectric Performance of Yb14-xCaxMnSb11. This is the Ca14AlSb11 structure type in I41/acd: isolated Sb anions, Sb3 linear trimers and an MnSb4 tetrahedron, with the divalent cations on the Yb sites. Ca-for-Yb is isovalent size substitution on those cation sites, which is how the paper tunes the lattice thermal conductivity without changing the carrier count. No reference entry is offered for the ternary.

dopant_roles.basis: Mn is not a dopant here at all: it is a stoichiometric host species holding the MnSb4 tetrahedral site of the A14MnSb11 structure, and it falls under the 5 at.% cut only because the formula unit has 26 atoms. The role vocabulary has no value for a host constituent that lands below the threshold, so alloying_component is used to carry the one thing stage 3 needs -- that no doping level should be computed from this fraction. The genuine variable is whether the Mn site is occupied at all, which is what separates Yb14Ca2Sb11 from the rest.

basis: The compositions are Ge1-xCdxTe with x from 0.10 to 0.15; the doubled Cd terms, as in Ge0.88Cd0.08Cd0.04Te, are the paper writing two Cd contributions and not two species. The single paper is on CdxBiyGe1-x-yTe alloys, so the host is GeTe with Cd on the Ge site: the ferroelectric rhombohedral R3m distortion of rocksalt at room temperature. The measured window runs to 803 K and the taxonomy puts the R3m to Fm-3m conversion at about 700 K, so these curves cross it and both phases are recorded. The transition temperature is a taxonomy default and is composition-dependent in both directions here -- Cd alloying and the Ge vacancy concentration both move it -- so the 700 K figure should not be read as this material own. No reference entry is offered, so the mp_ids stay null.

Every composition is Ce(In1-xSnx)3 with x from 0.1 to 0.7 and the single paper is on the thermoelectric power and resistivity of that series. CeIn3 and CeSn3 are both AuCu3 (L12) cubic Pm-3m -- Ce at the cell corner, the p-block element on the three face centres -- and they form a continuous solid solution, so every point here is one L12 phase. In and Sn are adjacent groups rather than isovalent, so this is not an isoelectronic axis and none is recorded: Sn-for-In adds an electron per substitution and that band filling is what drives CeIn3 from a Kondo antiferromagnet towards the CeSn3 mixed-valence state, which is the experiment. I disagree with the reference: Ce2(InSn)3 Pmmm mp-1227310, primary on no ICSD backing at all, is a computed ordered supercell of the same L12 solid solution rather than a separate phase.

The compositions are (Ce,Nd)Pd3 with Ce/(Ce+Nd) from 0.30 to 0.60, plus two points where Th replaces part of the rare earth, and the paper is on modifying the thermoelectric properties of CePd3 by substitution. CePd3 and NdPd3 are both AuCu3 (L12) cubic Pm-3m with the rare earth at the corner and Pd on the three face centres, fully miscible, so the whole series is one L12 phase. No reference entry is offered.

dopant_roles.basis: Th0.05(Nd0.6Ce0.4)0.95Pd3 and Th0.1(Nd0.6Ce0.4)0.9Pd3: tetravalent Th on the trivalent rare-earth corner site, which both dilutes the Ce sublattice and adds an electron -- the substitution the paper title is about.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: the rare-earth corner site of the AuCu3 cell
solid_solution_axis.note: Ce/(Ce+Nd) 0.30-0.60 over all nine compositions. Both are trivalent rare earths on one site, but this is not an inert isoelectronic swap in the way an anion substitution would be: CePd3 is a mixed-valence Kondo lattice and diluting its Ce sublattice with magnetic Nd changes the ground state, so the axis is the subject of the paper rather than alloying convenience.

basis: Six of the nine samples are (Sr,Eu)2CoO4 -- SrEuCoO4, EuSrCoO4, Eu0.75Sr1.25CoO4 and Eu1.25Sr0.75CoO4 -- the n = 1 Ruddlesden-Popper member, K2NiF4 type in I4/mmm, a single layer of corner-sharing CoO6 octahedra between rock-salt (Sr,Eu)O layers. The other three are Eu2SrCo1.5Fe0.5O7, the n = 2 member with a double octahedral layer, which the third paper introduces as a new material. Both are the same prototype at different n, so the host does not need splitting between prototypes, but stage 2 must resolve n per composition because the mp_id differs. MP offers SrEuCoO4 I4mm (107) mp-1218291 at hull 0.041 with no ICSD backing; I4mm is a polar variant of the same layering and I would expect the centrosymmetric I4/mmm, so I do not adopt that entry here.

dopant_roles.basis: Eu2SrCo1.5Fe0.5O7: Fe shares the octahedral B site with Co at a quarter of it, written into the target formula rather than added to it.

basis: The single paper is titled for eco-friendly beta-FeSi2 and the curator composition details unpack every composition as (((Fe0.95Co0.05)xSi1-x)1-yGey)Cu,P -- FeSi2 with Co on the Fe site, Ge on the Si site, and Cu and P added on top. Beta-FeSi2 is the semiconducting orthorhombic Cmce phase, which is the only reason this chemistry appears in a thermoelectric dataset; the metallic alpha and B20 epsilon forms are not what is being measured to 1073 K for a power factor. Co at 6.3 at.% and Ge at 6 at.% both clear the 5 per cent cut and so are carried as host elements, but their roles are the familiar ones: Co on the Fe site is the standard n-type donor for beta-FeSi2 and Ge on the Si site is isoelectronic alloying for lattice thermal conductivity. No reference entry is offered for the quaternary.

dopant_roles.basis: P from 0.03 to 0.05 per formula across every composition: a group-15 donor on the Si site, the n-type dopant the paper scans.

Cu at 0.007 to 0.014 per formula, written outside the FeSi2 bracket in the curator formula. Cu is added to beta-FeSi2 both as a dopant on the metal site and as an aid to the alpha-to-beta conversion during sintering, and some of it ends up at grain boundaries rather than in the lattice, so the site assignment is a candidate.
Sb at 0.01 to 0.02 in the two co-doped compositions: another group-15 donor on the Si site, added alongside P.

basis: Two families share this chemistry. La2CoFeO6, La1.8Sr0.2CoFeO6 and La1.6Sr0.4CoFeO6 are written as the B-site ordered double perovskite, and the first paper is titled for enhancing the power factor by inducing octahedral order, so the ordering is its whole point. La0.9Sr0.1Co0.5Fe0.5O3, La0.8Sr0.2Co0.3Fe0.7O3 and La0.8Sr0.2Co0.7Fe0.3O3 are the disordered ABO3 perovskite, and the 1994 paper covers La1-xSrxCo1-yFeyO3 as a family. At y = 0.5 the ordered and disordered forms are the same composition written two ways, so composition cannot separate them and only the paper can -- exactly the mixed host the review queue exists for. I take the disordered perovskite as primary because it spans the wider Co:Fe range and both Sr-doped series, with the double perovskite as the alternative. MP offers La2FeCoO6 P2_1/c mp-1223373 and La4Fe(CoO4)3 P-1 mp-1223109, both without ICSD backing: computed orderings, which is evidence that ordered arrangements are low in energy but not that these samples are ordered.

dopant_roles.basis: Sr from 0.1 to 0.4 per formula on the A site in eight of nine compositions: divalent Sr for trivalent La is the hole-doping knob of every lanthanum cobaltite-ferrite, and the third paper is titled for its effect.

basis: Every composition is LayFe4-xCoxSb12 -- LaFe3CoSb12, La0.9FeCo3Sb12, La0.85Fe2.7Co1.3Sb12 -- and the papers are on La-filled skutterudites, one of them titled LaxFeCo3Sb12. Fe plus Co totals 4 and Sb 12 in every case, which is the CoSb3 framework count exactly, with La in the icosahedral void. Fe-for-Co on the framework creates the charge deficit that the trivalent La filler compensates, so the Fe:Co ratio and the filling fraction move together rather than independently; that coupling is the p-type design of this family and means the La content is not a free doping level. The Yb0 written into Yb0La0.85Fe2.7Co1.3Sb12 is a zero-content term carried over from a double-filled YbxLayFe2.7Co1.3Sb12 series and contains no Yb, which is why it does not appear as a dopant candidate. No reference entry is offered.

Six of the nine samples are La0.3Sr0.7Ti0.4Co0.6O3 and two more are the same series at Co = 0.3 and 0.45, the subject of the second paper, La0.3Sr0.7Ti1-xCoxO3: a disordered ABO3 perovskite with La and Sr on the A site and Ti and Co sharing the octahedral B site. The ninth, Sr1.2La0.8CoTiO6, is the same chemistry written as an ordered double perovskite, (Sr0.6La0.4)2CoTiO6, and the first paper is titled for double perovskites. As in the Co-Fe-La-O host, the ordered and disordered forms are indistinguishable by composition -- Sr1.2La0.8CoTiO6 is La0.4Sr0.6Ti0.5Co0.5O3 rearranged -- so this is mixed and only the papers can settle which sample is which. The MP candidate SrLa3Ti2(CoO6)2 P-4m2 mp-1218234 sits at hull 0.085 with no ICSD backing and is a computed B-site ordering, so it does not decide the question either.

Every composition is Y(Co1-xNix)2 across the full x range and the single paper is on the electrical properties and spin fluctuations of that series. YCo2 and YNi2 are both cubic C15 MgCu2-type Laves phases in Fd-3m and form a continuous solid solution, so the whole host is one phase; the stray Y(Co0.4Ni0.6) without the subscript 2 is a transcription slip, not a 1:1 compound. Ni-for-Co fills the d band and suppresses the itinerant-electron metamagnetism of YCo2, which is the experiment, but it is not an isoelectronic swap and no axis is recorded. I disagree with the reference across the board: all five MP candidates -- Y2(CoNi)5, Y2CoNi5, Y6CoNi, YCo3Ni2, YCoNi -- carry no ICSD backing and sit at stoichiometries none of these samples approach. They describe what else the Y-Co-Ni system computes as, not what was measured.

Every composition is (Ti,Zr)CoSb1-xSnx and all four papers say so, two of them naming half-Heusler alloys in their titles. The 1:1:1 count holds throughout: (Ti+Zr) : Co : (Sb+Sn) is 1:1:1, which is the MgAgSb-ordered F-43m half-Heusler with one of the two tetrahedral voids empty. Sn clears 5 at.% and is carried as a host element, but its role is the p-type acceptor on the Sb site that every one of these papers is scanning. No reference entry is offered for the quinary.

dopant_roles.basis: Ti0.65Zr0.5Hf0.15CoSb0.35Sn0.65 in the third paper, which is on phase-separated half-Heuslers: Hf is a third group-4 cation on the same site as Ti and Zr, isovalent with both, added for mass contrast and phase separation rather than to change the carrier count.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: the group-4 cation site of the half-Heusler cell
solid_solution_axis.note: Ti/(Ti+Zr) runs 0.20-0.80 with median 0.50 over eight compositions, so this is a genuine alloy across its whole range rather than a dilute substitution, and no single parent compound covers the host. Hf joins the same site in one composition, making it ternary on that sublattice.

basis: This host holds two silicide families and the split is clean on the Si ratio. Cr0.6Mn0.4Si, Cr0.4Mn0.6Si, Cr0.8Mn0.2Si and Cr0.1Mn0.9Si are monosilicides at Si:TM = 1, and the third paper is on transition-metal monosilicides; CrSi and MnSi are both B20 FeSi-type in P2_13 and are mutually soluble, so those are one B20 phase across the series. Mn0.75Cr0.15Ru0.1Si1.74 and (Mn0.8Cr0.2)Si1.758 are at Si:TM near 1.75, which is the higher manganese silicide, and the second paper is titled for chimney-ladder compounds. Those are different structures at different stoichiometries, so the host is mixed and splits by composition. I take B20 as primary on composition count, with the chimney ladder as the alternative. I disagree with the reference: Mn2CrSi Fm-3m mp-1185616 is the full-Heusler ordering, with no ICSD backing and at a stoichiometry no sample here has, and Mn2CrSi Immm at hull 2.994 is not a real phase at all.

dopant_roles.basis: Mn0.75Cr0.15Ru0.1Si1.74, from the paper on the simultaneous substitution of Cr and Ru: Ru takes the transition-metal site of the chimney-ladder structure alongside Mn and Cr. Note that this composition belongs to the chimney-ladder half of the host, not the B20 half.

basis: Every composition is a chromium sulfo-selenide at Cr:chalcogen near 2:3 -- Cr2S2.4Se0.6, Cr2S1.5Se1.5, Cr2S0.6Se2.4 -- with one point at Cr3(S,Se)4, and the papers are on chromium sulfo-selenides and on Cr2Se3. Cr2X3 and Cr3X4 are both NiAs-derived: the anions keep the hexagonal close packing and the metal occupies two thirds or three quarters of the octahedral sites, with the vacancies ordering into alternate layers to give the trigonal and monoclinic superstructures. The seed nias entry anticipates exactly this and says so in its own note, that the Cr-Se host holds Cr2Se3 defect variants, which is why I use it rather than proposing something. Confidence is medium because the prototype is written for the 1:1 parent at P63/mmc and the real space group here is one of the ordered-vacancy superstructures, which stage 2 has to pick. The MP candidates, Cr2SeS P-6m2 at hull 0.151 and Cr4(SeS)3 R3, both carry no ICSD backing and are computed S/Se orderings rather than measured phases.

dopant_roles.basis: Mn0.04Cr1.96Se2.7S0.3, from the paper on codoped Cr2Se3: Mn on the octahedral Cr site.

solid_solution_axis.note: S/(S+Se) runs 0.10-0.87 over all nine compositions, which is nearly the full join, so this host is a sulfo-selenide series and not a doped binary. The vacancy ordering that sets the actual space group can itself change across the join, so the parent must be assigned per composition.

basis: Cs8Na16Ge136 is the type-II clathrate outright, and the first paper says so in its title. The Ge136 framework is the defining count of the type-II structure in Fd-3m: 16 small Ge20 cages, which take Na, and 8 large Ge28 cages, which take Cs. MP confirms it as CsNa2Ge17 Fd-3m mp-640321 at hull 0.000 with 6 ICSD references, which is Cs8Na16Ge136 divided by eight -- the same compound in its primitive formula.

dopant_roles.basis: Cs8Na9.94Tl6.06Ge136: the Ge count stays at 136 and Na plus Tl stays at 16, so Tl takes guest positions in the small cages rather than entering the framework. That is what the paper title, Cs8Na16-xTlxGe136, encodes.

Cs8Na16Cu5Ge131: here Cu5 plus Ge131 is 136, so the substitution is inside the framework, and the paper is titled for framework-substituted Cs8Na16Cu5Ge131. Cu on the covalent network sets the electron count, which is the clathrate doping mechanism the README singles out.

basis: Every composition is CuxTi2S4 with x from 0.375 to 1, and the first paper is titled Thermoelectric Properties and Electronic Structures of CuTi2S4 Thiospinel. That is the normal spinel in Fd-3m with Cu on the tetrahedral A site and Ti on the octahedral B site, and MP backs it as Ti2CuS4 Fd-3m mp-3951 at hull 0.000 with 5 ICSD references, the best-attested entry for the formula. I record a disagreement with ref 1, which the project ranks above MP: TEDesignLab offers Ti(CuS)4 I-42m mp-29091, but that is TiCu4S4 -- four coppers per titanium, the inverse of the measured ratio -- so it is a different compound in the same chemistry rather than a competing polymorph, and preferring it here would be wrong. The Cu deficiency in Cu0.375Ti2.25S4 and Cu0.5Ti2.25S4 is vacancy formation on the tetrahedral site, the carrier-concentration knob of this material, not a second phase.

Five of the nine samples are ErNiSb itself and the rest are ErNiSn1-xSbx at x above 0.95; the third paper is titled for the high-temperature power factor of half-Heusler phases RENiSb. MP gives ErNiSb F-43m (216) mp-21272 at hull 0.000 with 3 ICSD references, which is the half-Heusler ordering directly. The off-stoichiometric points ErNiSb1.05, ErNi1.02Sb and ErNi1.02Sb1.05 are small excesses used to control secondary phases and vacancy content rather than different compounds.

dopant_roles.basis: ErNiSn0.01Sb0.99 through ErNiSn0.05Sb0.95, and two papers titled for the effect of Sn doping on ErNiSb: group-14 Sn on the group-15 Sb site is an acceptor, the p-type knob of this material.

basis: Two related but distinct structures share this host. Five compositions are EuNi2(Si1-xGex)2, the ThCr2Si2 type in I4/mmm, and the first paper is on the thermoelectric power of exactly that series. Four samples are EuNi(Si0.8Ge0.2)3, an RTX3 compound and not a 122 at all: that is the BaNiSn3 type in I4mm, the non-centrosymmetric ordering of the same BaAl4 parent, and the second paper is on EuNi(Si1-xGex)3 under pressure. So the host is mixed and splits cleanly on the Ni:X ratio, 1:2:2 against 1:1:3. The MP entry EuSiNi2Ge I4mm (107) mp-1225155 is worth reading carefully rather than adopting: its formula is the 122 stoichiometry, EuNi2SiGe, but its space group is I4mm, because ordering Si and Ge onto the two distinct X positions of a 122 lowers the symmetry to exactly the BaNiSn3 setting. It carries no ICSD backing, so it is a computed Si/Ge ordering of the 122 and not evidence for the 113 phase.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: the main-group X site of the BaAl4-derived framework
solid_solution_axis.note: Ge/(Ge+Si) runs 0.20-0.82 with median 0.75 over six compositions. Si and Ge are isovalent, so the substitution acts through chemical pressure rather than carrier count, which is why EuNi2(Si1-xGex)2 is scanned across it -- the Eu valence transition moves with the cell volume. The axis spans both structure types in this host, so it must be applied within each rather than across them.

basis: All three compositions are Sr1-xEuxTiO3, at x = 0.25, 0.5 and 0.75, and the papers are on Eu substitution in SrTi0.8Nb0.2O3 and on the oxygen content of these titanates. SrTiO3 and EuTiO3 are both cubic Pm-3m perovskites with nearly identical cells, divalent Eu sitting on the Sr A site, so the join is one perovskite phase throughout. No reference entry is offered. Two things are worth noting without changing the label: SrTiO3 has an antiferrodistortive Pm-3m to I4/mcm rotation near 105 K, which the 12 K measurement start does reach, but it is an octahedral tilt within the same prototype rather than a change of structure; and one sample is an epitaxial film, where strain can hold a tilted or polar variant that bulk ceramics do not show.

dopant_roles.basis: (Sr0.5Eu0.5)Ti0.8Nb0.2O3: pentavalent Nb on the tetravalent Ti site is the standard n-type donor for SrTiO3, and it is written into the parent formula of the first paper rather than added as a trace.

basis: Three samples are Fe4N outright and the second paper is on pseudo-single-crystal gamma-prime Fe4N. That is the antiperovskite: nitrogen at the body centre of an fcc iron cell, Pm-3m, which is the M3XY inverse perovskite this prototype is written for, and MP lists Fe4N Pm-3m mp-535 with 3 ICSD references. The rest are ion-beam-deposited films at falling nitrogen content. Fe0.81N0.19 is still essentially Fe4N, but Fe0.92N0.08 and Fe0.93N0.07 are far leaner than any line compound in this system and sit where nitrogen is a supersaturated interstitial in body-centred iron, that is nitrogen-bearing martensitic alpha-Fe and the ordered alpha-double-prime Fe16N2 that grows out of it. MP has that ordered end as Fe8N I4/mmm mp-555 at hull 0.003 with 8 ICSD references, which is Fe16N2 in its primitive formula, so the phase is real and well attested -- but composition alone cannot tell me whether these films are the ordered nitride or simply supersaturated alpha-Fe, and a sputtered film is exactly where both appear together. I therefore leave those compositions against unresolved_crystalline rather than proposing a prototype I cannot place them in, mark the host mixed, and set confidence low for the host as a whole even though the Fe4N half is solid. Fe3N P6_322 mp-1804, the best-attested entry in the MP list with 9 ICSD references, is the epsilon nitride at higher nitrogen than anything measured here and is not a candidate for these samples.

Every composition is Fe(V,Nb)1-xTixSb and all three papers are on FeNbSb-based half-Heuslers, one titled Are Solid Solutions Better in FeNbSb-Based Thermoelectrics. The 1:1:1 count holds: Fe : (V+Nb+Ti) : Sb is 1:1:1, the F-43m half-Heusler with one tetrahedral void left empty. Ti clears the 5 at.% cut at 0.16 to 0.24 of three atoms and so is carried as a host element, but its role is the group-4-for-group-5 acceptor that sets the hole concentration in every one of these papers. No reference entry is offered for the quinary.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: the group-5 site of the half-Heusler cell
solid_solution_axis.note: Nb/(Nb+V) runs 0.30-0.75 with median 0.40 over all nine compositions. V and Nb are isovalent, so the substitution works through mass and size contrast on the lattice thermal conductivity and through band convergence, not through carrier count -- the carrier count is set separately by Ti. Both end members, FeVSb and FeNbSb, are real half-Heuslers, so the parent is genuinely composition-dependent.

basis: The host is elemental gallium with three dilute In alloys, and the papers are on the thermoelectric power of pure gallium and on liquid Ga alloys. The solid is alpha-Ga, the orthorhombic A11 structure in Cmce with a covalent Ga-Ga dimer, and MP confirms it as Ga Cmce mp-142 at hull 0.000 with 9 ICSD references. The taxonomy has no entry for it -- solid_solution_alloy is the elemental-metal bucket but is defined as the Cu, W and Mg packings, which alpha-Ga is not -- so I propose alpha_ga_a11. The thing that actually matters for this host is temperature: gallium melts at 303 K and the measured window starts at 302 K and runs to 773 K, or 1053 K on the full span, so almost every curve here is liquid gallium and only the very start of the low-temperature paper is on the crystal. I record that as a phase sequence rather than hiding it behind a crystal label, with the melt as the second phase, which is why confidence is medium for the crystalline assignment.

other_polymorphs.note: beta-Ga Cmcm at hull 0.010 with 2 ICSD references against 9 for alpha: it forms on undercooling the melt, not on heating the solid, so it is not in the sequence.
Ga I4/mmm at hull 0.026 with 2 ICSD references, a pressure-stabilised form.

dopant_roles.basis: Ga0.9999In0.0001 through Ga0.999In0.001, that is 100 to 1000 ppm. At these levels indium is a dilute impurity used to study residual scattering rather than an alloying addition. The site language is strictly right only below 303 K; above the melting point there is no lattice site and In is simply a solute in the melt.

basis: All nine compositions are Ga1-xZnx from x = 0.1 to 0.8 and the single paper is titled Electronic transport properties of liquid Ga-Zn alloys. The measured window is 561-1077 K; gallium melts at 303 K, zinc at 693 K, and the Ga-Zn liquidus lies below the top of this window across the whole composition range, so what is reported is the transport of a melt and there is no crystal structure to assign. Ga and Zn are also almost completely immiscible as solids: the system is a simple eutectic at 3.9 at.% Zn and 298 K with no intermetallic at all, so even frozen this would be a two-phase mixture of alpha-Ga and hexagonal Zn rather than a solid solution. I propose liquid_metal for cases like this rather than forcing amorphous, which means a quenched glass, or solid_solution_alloy, which asserts a crystalline solution that this system does not form. I disagree with the reference: ZnGa3 Pm-3m mp-971720 at hull 0.074 with no ICSD backing is a computed cubic compound that the Ga-Zn phase diagram does not contain.

Eight of the nine samples are Lu3Ir4Ge13 and the ninth is (Yb0.3Lu0.7)3Ir4Ge13. The 3-4-13 stoichiometry is the Remeika phase signature, and MP gives Lu3Ge13Ir4 Pm-3n (223) mp-1197864 at hull 0.005 with an ICSD reference, which is the Yb3Rh4Sn13 structure type directly -- a cubic cage of Ge around the rare earth. The paper, on low carrier density and fragile magnetism in a Kondo lattice system, is the usual physics of these compounds.
