The taxonomy has no 3-4-13 entry in the seed, so this uses the prototype proposed from chunk 009; that entry was written around the stannides and this is the germanide analogue at the same structure, which is worth noting when it is reviewed for v4. The other MP candidates -- Lu3Ge3Ir2, Lu5(Ge5Ir2)2, LuGeIr -- are real Lu-Ir-Ge compounds at stoichiometries none of these samples approach.

dopant_roles.basis: (Yb0.3Lu0.7)3Ir4Ge13: Yb on the rare-earth site of the cage. In a Kondo lattice paper this is not inert doping -- Yb is the magnetic ion being introduced into a non-magnetic Lu host.

basis: Every composition is Zr0.5Hf0.5Ni1-xPdxSn0.99Sb0.01 and all three papers are on that exact material, one of them titled for half-Heusler Zr0.5Hf0.5Ni0.8Pd0.2Sn structure and thermoelectric properties. The count is 1:1:1 with (Zr,Hf) on the group-4 site, (Ni,Pd) on the transition-metal site and (Sn,Sb) on the main-group site: the MgAgSb-ordered F-43m half-Heusler. Zr and Hf are fixed at 0.5 each in every composition, so there is no solid-solution axis to record even though the site is shared. No reference entry is offered for the quinary.

dopant_roles.basis: Sn0.99Sb0.01 in every composition: group-15 Sb on the group-14 Sn site is the n-type donor, held fixed here while Pd is varied.

Oxygen appears only in the two compositions written as (half-Heusler)92.9(HfO2)7.1 and (half-Heusler)97.03(HfO2)2.97, and the curator records 3, 6 and 9 vol per cent ZrO2 nanoinclusions. This is a deliberately added oxide second phase for phonon scattering, not oxygen in the half-Heusler lattice and not pressing residue either.

basis: Six of the nine samples are Ho2SbO2 and MP gives Ho2SbO2 I4/mmm (139) mp-1067935 at hull 0.000 with an ICSD reference. That is the anti-ThCr2Si2 layering: fluorite-like [Ho2O2] slabs alternating with flat square nets of Sb, which is the same construction as Bi2O2Se -- [Bi2O2] slabs alternating with square Se nets, also I4/mmm. So the seed entry fits structurally even though it is named and written for a single compound; it should be generalised to A2O2X in v4, and that naming gap is why I record medium rather than high. The host is mixed beyond that: Ho3SbO3 is monoclinic C2/m at mp-1104812 and Ho8Sb3O8 is another member again, and the third paper is a review of the (RE,Ca)mPnnOm rare-earth pnictide oxide series, which is precisely a homologous family rather than one structure. Those two compositions need their own assignment.

dopant_roles.basis: Ho2Sb0.8Bi0.2O3: Bi and Sb are both group 15 and the review paper covers Pn = Sb and Bi as one family, so Bi takes the pnictide square net without changing the electron count. Note the composition is written O3 rather than O2, so its oxygen content does not match Ho2SbO2 and it may belong with the other members rather than with the 2-1-2.

basis: Five of the nine samples are HoPdSb and the third paper is titled Antimonides with the half-Heusler structure: New thermoelectric materials. HoPdSb is the 1:1:1 F-43m half-Heusler. One sample is HoPd2Sb, the 1:2:1 full Heusler in Fm-3m -- the same structure with the second tetrahedral void filled -- and the first two papers cover both, being on rare-earth-based Heusler phases REPdZ and REPd2Z. That is a real split between two prototypes rather than an ambiguity, and it separates cleanly on the Pd:Ho ratio, so the host is mixed. MP has the full Heusler as HoSbPd2 Fm-3m mp-977574 at hull 0.000 but does not list HoPdSb itself; the other candidates, Ho5Sb2Pd and Ho5SbPd2, are Ho-rich binaries-plus at stoichiometries no sample here approaches. The remaining compositions, HoPd1.02Sb1.05 and HoPdSb1.05, are small excesses for phase control rather than different compounds.
reference_disagreement: assigned sg [216], ICSD-backed references for this host report [62]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: Four samples are Zn5Sb4In1.85 and the curator records Zn5Sb4In2-x; two of the three papers are on that compound, one titled Zn5Sb4In2-delta - a Ternary Derivative of Thermoelectric Zinc Antimonides. No seed prototype describes it -- it is an ordered orthorhombic ternary with its own In site, not the rhombohedral beta-Zn4Sb3 with disordered interstitials -- so I propose zn5sb4in2_ternary. The other five samples are (ZnSb)1-x(InSb)x from 10 to 50 per cent InSb, and the paper calls them binary systems: ZnSb is orthorhombic CdSb-type and InSb is zincblende, with essentially no mutual solubility, so those are two-phase composites of two different prototypes rather than the ternary. The host is therefore mixed and splits by composition. MP offers Zn9(InSb3)2 P2_12_12_1 (19) mp-1202823 at hull 0.046 with 2 ICSD references; the orthorhombic ternary family and space group are right, but Zn9In2Sb6 is Zn:In = 4.5 against 2.5 for Zn5Sb4In2, so I record it as a candidate in the proposal and do not adopt the mp_id here.

Seven of the nine samples are IrO2 and two are Ir0.9Sn0.1O2. MP gives IrO2 P4_2/mnm (136) mp-2723 at hull 0.000 with 7 ICSD references, the rutile structure, and the papers are the classic transport studies of IrO2 and RuO2 -- both rutile metals -- plus a recent one on electron correlation and suppressed thermal conductivity. Nothing here suggests anything but rutile: it is the only form of IrO2 obtained at ambient pressure.

other_polymorphs.note: IrO2 Pa-3 at hull 0.094 with 1 ICSD reference against 7 for rutile: the pyrite-type form, reached under pressure rather than on heating.
IrO2 I4_1/amd at hull 0.258 with no ICSD backing.

dopant_roles.basis: Ir0.9Sn0.1O2: tetravalent Sn on the tetravalent Ir site, and SnO2 is itself rutile, so this is an isostructural dilution of the Ir sublattice. It does not change the formal charge but it does dilute the correlated Ir 5d network, which is what the third paper is about.

basis: All five compositions are La1-xSrxVO3 with x from 0.25 to 0.6, and the papers are on the Mott transition in this series. LaVO3 is the orthorhombic Pbnm perovskite and SrVO3 the cubic Pm-3m one, and the join is a single perovskite phase throughout with V holding the octahedral B site; Sr-for-La drives V from d2 towards d1 and that band filling is the metal-insulator transition being studied. Sr exceeds 5 at.% everywhere, so there are no dopant candidates even though Sr is doing the doping. I disagree with the reference: all three MP candidates are SrLaVO4 and Sr3LaV3O12, which are vanadates with V in a higher oxidation state at stoichiometries none of these samples have, and none carries ICSD backing.

Six of the nine samples are TiN and the rest are TiN0.72 to TiN0.9. MP gives TiN Fm-3m (225) mp-492 at hull 0.000 with 34 ICSD references, by far the best-attested entry in the chunk, and the papers are on titanium carbonitride cermets and on nitrides prepared by spark plasma sintering. Rocksalt TiN tolerates a wide nitrogen deficiency without changing structure, so TiN0.72 is the same Fm-3m phase with vacancies on the anion site -- the non-stoichiometry this prototype is written for rather than an impurity or a second phase. Ti2N P4_2/mnm mp-8282 is a real compound but at half the nitrogen of anything measured here.

Seven of the nine samples are Nd2Zr2O7 and MP gives Nd2Zr2O7 Fd-3m (227) mp-5977 at hull 0.000 with 8 ICSD references. That is the pyrochlore: an ordered, oxygen-deficient superstructure of fluorite with Nd on the eight-coordinate A site, Zr octahedral, and one eighth of the anion sites vacant and ordered. The papers are on rare-earth A2Zr2O7 zirconates for thermal-barrier coatings, which is the low thermal conductivity this ordering produces. One caveat is recorded rather than hidden: the curator notes Phases present : Pyrochlore + Fluorite for one sample, and Nd2Zr2O7 sits close to the radius-ratio boundary of the pyrochlore field, so the same composition can come out as the disordered defect fluorite depending on how it was fired. That is a genuine order-disorder alternative for this host, not a different chemistry, so it is recorded as the alternative prototype rather than as a mixed host.

dopant_roles.basis: (Nd0.8Yb0.2)2Zr2O7, and the second paper is titled for the effect of Yb3+ doping on phase structure and thermal conductivity: isovalent Yb on the A site, added for mass contrast, though the smaller radius also pushes the structure towards the defect fluorite.
(Nd0.8Ce0.2)2Zr2O7.2: the excess oxygen written into the formula says Ce is entering as Ce4+ rather than Ce3+, which is charge compensation on the A site rather than simple isovalent substitution.

basis: The compositions and the papers do not agree here and I record the conflict rather than resolving it quietly. The compositions read ZnNiSn and Zn27-30Ni37-40Sn32-33, but both papers are on Zr-Ni-Sn: one on amorphous Zr-Ni-Sn thin films and one on preparing ZrNiSn half-Heusler compounds with crystalline alignment, and the curator details -- short-duration microgravity, solidified in normal gravity at 1-g -- match the ZrNiSn solidification study directly. ZrNiSn is the canonical n-type half-Heusler. ZnNiSn is not one and could not be: Zn is not a group-4 element and the 18-electron count that makes the half-Heusler semiconducting does not work with it. The likeliest reading by a wide margin is that Zr was transcribed as Zn in the composition strings, so I assign half_heusler but at low confidence, because if the compositions are right then this assignment is wrong and a single character decides which. The host is also mixed on its own terms: four samples are films from the amorphous-films paper, so an amorphous phase is present alongside whatever the crystalline material is. No reference entry is offered, which is itself consistent with a composition string that does not correspond to a real compound.

The single composition is ReO3 and both papers are on conductive ReO3 thin films. This is the compound the prototype is named for: corner-sharing ReO6 octahedra with the perovskite A site empty, cubic Pm-3m, and metallic. The reference needs reading rather than following. MP ranks ReO3 Im-3 (204) mp-20741 as the primary on 18 ICSD references, but Im-3 is the octahedrally tilted variant of the same framework, not the ambient structure; ReO3 has a soft rotational mode that a relaxed calculation readily tilts into, so 18 ICSD references sitting on that entry most likely belong to cubic ReO3 and have been attached to a tilted relaxed structure. It makes no difference to the prototype, which covers the framework and its distortions, but the space group should not be taken from that entry for a 31-296 K ambient measurement. The other candidates -- ReO2 Pbcn, Re2O7, Re2O9, ReO5 -- are separate rhenium oxides, not polymorphs of ReO3. The README warning attached to this prototype applies in reverse here: the distortion series belongs to WO3, and ReO3 genuinely is the cubic aristotype, so no sequence should be applied to this host.

Every composition is Tl2-xRu2O7-y, with one Mn-substituted point, and MP gives Tl2Ru2O7 Fd-3m (227) mp-22094 at hull 0.000 with 2 ICSD references -- the pyrochlore, two interpenetrating networks of corner-sharing RuO6 octahedra and of Tl2O tetrahedra. The papers are on Tl2Mn2O7 pyrochlore magnetoresistance and on the metal-semiconductor transition in high-pressure-synthesised Tl2Ru2O7, so the family is stated. The deficits written into Tl1.7Ru2O6.55 and Tl2Ru2O6.5 are vacancies on the Tl and O sites of that same structure, which is the carrier-concentration knob of these ruthenate pyrochlores rather than a different compound. Worth noting without changing the label: Tl2Ru2O7 has a metal-insulator transition near 120 K accompanied by a symmetry-lowering distortion, and the 10-290 K window sits across it, but that is a distortion within the pyrochlore prototype rather than a change of prototype, so it is not recorded as a phase sequence.

dopant_roles.basis: Tl2Mn0.3Ru1.7O7: Mn on the octahedral B site. Tl2Mn2O7 is itself a pyrochlore and the first paper is on it, so this composition sits on the Tl2(Ru,Mn)2O7 join between two members of the same structure rather than being dilute doping of one.

basis: The compositions are tantalum suboxides spread continuously across the range -- TaO, TaO1.3, TaO1.5, Ta0.53O0.47, Ta0.49O0.51, Ta0.47O0.53 -- and both papers are on sputtered films: one on conductive filaments in resistive-switching devices, one titled Tantalum Suboxide Films with Tunable Composition and Electrical Resistivity. A continuously tunable composition and resistivity is what an amorphous film does; a crystalline system would step between line compounds instead. So I assign amorphous rather than pick a crystal prototype the films probably do not have. The reference supports this rather than contradicting it: MP puts rocksalt TaO Fm-3m mp-1895 at hull 1.105 and Ta2O I-43m at 1.769, which are not bulk phases at all despite carrying ICSD references, and the only entries near the hull are TaO2 P4_2/mnm at 0.071 and Ta2O5 C2/c at 0.008 -- the crystalline end members these films sit between without reaching. Confidence is medium because no paper was read: an annealed or crystallised film would be rutile TaO2 or Ta2O5 instead.

The host is two different compounds in a clean 5:4 split. Five samples are Yb2O3, the cubic C-type rare-earth sesquioxide in Ia-3, which MP gives as mp-2814 with 26 ICSD references; four are YbO, which MP gives as Fm-3m mp-1216 with 2 ICSD references, and the third paper is titled for high electron mobility in rock-salt YbO, so the rocksalt monoxide is stated outright. Divalent YbO and trivalent Yb2O3 are genuinely different compounds, not polymorphs, so the host is mixed and splits on the O:Yb ratio alone. This host is also a clean illustration of why the chunk ranks by ICSD count rather than hull distance: Yb2O3 sits at hull 0.199 while YbO sits at 0.000, which would rank the sesquioxide below a monoxide it is in no way less stable than -- the 26 references against 2 tell the true story.

The whole host is one paper, on Re6GaxSeyTe15-y, and every composition is Re6(Se,Te)15 with or without gallium. That stoichiometry is a Re6 octahedral cluster chalcogenide: a Re6Ch8 cluster core of the kind that runs through this chemistry, with the remaining chalcogen in bridging units between clusters. No seed prototype covers it -- chevrel is the Mo6X8 rhombohedral cluster with intercalated cations, which is a different cluster, a different symmetry and a much lower chalcogen count -- so I propose re6ch15_cluster. MP supports the outline with Re6Te7Se8 Pbca (61) mp-667286 at hull 0.000, but on a single ICSD reference. Confidence is low and deliberately so: the Re6 core is well established, but the arrangement of the chalcogen beyond it, and therefore the space group, rests on one reference and on family behaviour rather than on a structure report for these compositions. The proposal says the same and should be reviewed before v4.

dopant_roles.basis: Re6GaxSeyTe15-y with x from 0.5 to 1: the Re6 and the chalcogen totals both stay fixed as Ga is added, so gallium is not replacing either. It most plausibly sits as a cation in the space between cluster units, which is the interstitial role, but this is inference from the formula and not from a structure determination, so it is medium at best and the proposal flags it for confirmation.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: the chalcogen positions of the Re6 cluster unit
solid_solution_axis.note: Se/(Se+Te) runs 0.16-0.50 with median 0.30 over all nine compositions, so the host is a Se-Te join rather than a doped binary. Se and Te are isovalent, but they need not be equivalent within a cluster compound: the core and bridging chalcogen positions are crystallographically distinct and may not accept the two elements equally, so the single axis figure should not be read as a uniform site occupancy.

basis: Both compositions are (ZnSb)x(SnTe)1-x at 73:27 and 67:33, and the single paper is titled High thermoelectric performance in ZnSb-SnTe pseudo-binary materials. ZnSb and SnTe are not mutually soluble in any meaningful amount and are not even the same kind of structure: ZnSb is the orthorhombic CdSb type in Pbca with Sb-Sb dimers, and SnTe is cubic rocksalt. A pseudo-binary of the two is a designed two-phase composite, so this host genuinely holds two prototypes and must be split by composition; ZnSb is the majority phase in both compositions and takes the primary label. Confidence is medium rather than high because with no reference entry and only two compositions, the possibility that one component partly dissolves in the other, or that an interfacial ternary forms, rests on nothing but the phase diagram.

Nine sputter-deposited SncSi1-c films spanning Si fractions 0.30 to 0.72, from one paper on the electrical evolution of that series. Silicon and tin are essentially immiscible in the solid state -- the equilibrium diagram is a simple eutectic with mutual solubility below 0.1 at.% and no compound -- so a homogeneous crystalline Sn0.34Si0.66 does not exist. What sputtering at these compositions produces is an amorphous or nanocrystalline film, usually amorphous Si with Sn clusters, which is why the paper follows the electrical properties as a function of composition and of annealing rather than reporting a structure. I therefore disagree with [ref 1]: the TEDesignLab entry SiSn F-43m mp-1009813 sits 0.150 eV above the hull on a single ICSD reference and is a metastable diamond-like phase reachable only by epitaxy, not the phase of these films, and the Materials Project entries Si18Sn Cm at hull 0.920 and SiSn3 Pm-3m at hull 0.321 are computed cells rather than observed compounds. Confidence is low because no structural measurement is reported at host level and the answer may differ film by film.

other_polymorphs.note: The zincblende SiSn of [ref 1], hull 0.150 on one ICSD reference. Diamond-structured Si-Sn alloys have been grown epitaxially, so the entry is not fictitious, but it is not an equilibrium phase and a magnetron-sputtered film is not how it is made.

solid_solution_axis.note: The detector reports this as an isoelectronic series because Si and Sn are both group 14, and at the level of the composition table that is what it looks like. It is not a substitutional series: there is no shared crystallographic site, because there is no single phase for the two elements to share. The axis is a deposition parameter, and near the ends the minority element is a second phase rather than a dilute substituent.

basis: Seven of the nine samples are elemental Ti, which is hcp alpha-Ti (A3, P6_3/mmc) at room temperature, matching mp-46 with 31 ICSD references. Ti97Al3 and Li(Ti0.99V0.01)24 are dilute solutions in the same lattice. This follows the treatment already given to the other elemental metal hosts in the ledger (Ag, Al, Cu, Fe, Ni, Nb, Cr, W), all of which are filed under solid_solution_alloy for the A1/A2/A3 close-packed metals. The papers are about hydrides, silicide quantum-dot superlattices and Ti-SiC or Ti-TiB2 composites, so the Ti here is a matrix rather than the object of study, but the matrix structure is not in doubt.

other_polymorphs.note: beta-Ti, bcc Im-3m, is the equilibrium phase above about 1155 K. The measured range reaches 1063 K, so no curve here crosses it, but a hotter measurement in this host would and the transition is strongly depressed by beta stabilisers such as the V present in one composition.

dopant_roles.basis: Ti97Al3: Al is the classic alpha stabiliser and dissolves substitutionally in hcp Ti well beyond 3 at.%.
Li(Ti0.99V0.01)24: V is a beta stabiliser and substitutes on the Ti site; at 1 at.% it stays in solution.

The formula Li(Ti0.99V0.01)24 is one Li to 24 Ti and does not correspond to any Li-Ti compound; Li is practically insoluble in Ti. It is most likely a transcription of a layer or additive rather than a solute, and the curator detail for this host reads only QDSL. Left unknown rather than guessed.

basis: Four samples are elemental Zn, hcp A3 in P6_3/mmc with its large c/a, matching mp-79 with 30 ICSD references, and four more are Zn0.978Al0.02Ga0.002 from a paper on Al-Zn solid solutions -- the same lattice with dilute solutes. The ninth sample, YbCoNiZn20, is not that at all: it is a 1-2-20 cage compound of the CeCr2Al20 type, the same family as the YbCo2Zn20 of the Co-Zn host at rank 794 in this chunk, and the Materials Project line for this host already shows the isostructural ZrZn22 and HfZn22 in Fd-3m. So the host is mixed and the single sample must be split off by composition.

dopant_roles.basis: Zn0.978Al0.02Ga0.002 comes from a study of Al-Zn solid solutions; Al dissolves substitutionally in hcp Zn at this level.
0.2 at.% Ga in the same samples. One of the papers concerns liquid Ga-Zn alloys, where the question does not arise; in the solid films it is a dilute substitutional solute.
In YbCoNiZn20 the Yb occupies the large CN16 cage of the 1-2-20 framework. It falls below 5 at.% only because the formula has 23 atoms, so it is a stoichiometric constituent and not a dopant.
Stoichiometric occupant of the transition-metal site of YbT2Zn20, shared here with Ni. Below the 5 at.% cut for the same arithmetic reason as Yb.
YbCoNiZn20 is the half-substituted member of YbCo2-xNixZn20; Ni takes the Co site.

basis: All eight samples are CaZn1-xAg1-ySb from one paper on defect modulation in that system, with Zn plus Ag summing to between 0.6 and 0.75 rather than to 2. The vacancy content is not incidental, it is what makes the phase valence-precise: Ca2+ plus (1-x)Zn2+ plus (1-y)Ag+ balances Sb3- only when 2(1-x) plus (1-y) equals 1, which CaZn0.4Ag0.2Sb and CaZn0.35Ag0.3Sb both satisfy to within the digitised precision. That is the signature of an ABX Zintl phase with a mixed-occupancy honeycomb site, i.e. the ZrBeSi ordered AlB2 type that CaAgSb, CaAgAs and CaAgP adopt. The same prototype was proposed from the Ag-Ca-Ce-Sb host in chunk 010, which is the identical chemistry with Ce on the Ca site, so this is the second host to need it. Confidence is medium because the chunk file offers NO reference line for this host at all -- neither TEDesignLab nor Materials Project -- so the space group rests on the structure literature for the isostructural silver pnictides rather than on any entry here.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: honeycomb B site shared with Sb
solid_solution_axis.note: Zn and Ag share the honeycomb site but are NOT isoelectronic -- Zn2+ against Ag+ -- so moving along this axis changes the electron count and forces the vacancy concentration to follow. That is exactly what the paper calls defect modulation, and it is the carrier-concentration knob rather than a neutral alloying axis. The detector did not flag this host because the two elements are not in the same group; the axis is recorded here because it is nonetheless the variable the samples scan. x is Zn/(Zn+Ag) computed from the listed compositions.

basis: All four compositions are Ba8Ga16-xAlxSn30 with x from 4 to 10, and both papers name the phase in their titles as type-VIII clathrate. The Ba-Ga-Sn clathrate is the textbook case where type VIII rather than type I is the stable form -- beta-Ba8Ga16Sn30 -- and the project README records that the v0.2 lineage corrected exactly this error in v2, where Ba-Ga-Sn had been filed under type I. Al substitutes for Ga in the framework and does not change the cage topology. No reference line is offered for this host, so the assignment rests on the compositions and the paper titles.

other_polymorphs.note: alpha-Ba8Ga16Sn30 is the type I form of the same composition and is obtained by a different growth route, not by heating the type VIII phase. Both are studied as thermoelectrics and they have different transport, so a sample of this host must not be assumed to be type VIII without the paper saying so -- here both papers do say so.

dopant_roles.basis: Ba8Ga16-xAlxSn30: Al is trivalent like Ga and takes framework sites, so the electron count is unchanged and the effect is on the lattice thermal conductivity and the band structure. It is a stoichiometric constituent at x from 4 to 10, not a dopant.

solid_solution_axis.note: Al and Ga are isoelectronic and share the tetrahedral framework sites, so this is a genuine substitutional series and the guest-framework electron count is fixed along it. The Sn framework sites are not involved.

basis: The whole host is single-crystal UCoAl, measured from 10 to 50 K for the metamagnetic transition. UCoAl is the standard example of an equiatomic UTX compound in the hexagonal ZrNiAl (ordered Fe2P) structure, and [ref 2] agrees directly: UAlCo P-62m mp-1079367 with 3 ICSD references, the best attested entry for this element set. The metamagnetic transition the paper probes is an electronic and magnetic one at a few tesla, not a structural transformation, so no phase sequence is recorded. The prototype comes from the chunk 009 proposal made for La-Rh-Sn and Ce-Cu-In; this is its third host.

Every composition is Fe2V1-xTaxAl, and one paper is titled for the thermoelectric properties of Heusler-type Fe2VTaxAl1-x alloys. Fe2VAl is the canonical L2_1 full Heusler pseudogap semimetal; Ta is a heavy isoelectronic substituent for V used to scatter phonons, and Fe2VTa1.12Al0.88 is the same lattice with Ta spilling onto the Al site. Nothing in the compositions suggests a second phase, and the 16 to 796 K window holds no structural transition for this family.

dopant_roles.basis: Fe2(V0.7Ta0.2Ti0.1)Al: Ti sits on the V site of the L2_1 cell. It has one electron fewer than V, so unlike Ta it shifts the Fermi level as well as the phonon spectrum -- this is p-type doping of Fe2VAl.

basis: The host holds two unrelated intermetallics. Five samples are Ni2VAl1.08, the off-stoichiometric full Heusler studied in the Phys. Rev. B paper on off-stoichiometric effects, and [ref 2] gives AlVNi2 Fm-3m mp-10899 for it. The other three, Ni75V18Al7 and its siblings, are from a paper on Ni3V-Ni3Al pseudo-binary alloys: at 75 at.% Ni these are A3B orderings of the fcc lattice, Ni3V in the tetragonal D0_22 type and Ni3Al in the cubic L1_2 type, with a two-phase field between them. A single label would be wrong, so the host is mixed and splits cleanly on the Ni fraction -- 50 at.% Ni for the Heusler against 75 at.% for the pseudo-binary. Confidence is medium for the minority group because the exact D0_22/L1_2 balance at Ni75V18Al7 depends on the V:Al ratio and on annealing.

Every composition is written as (Al2O3)a(ZrO2)b across the whole range from 8 to 77 mol% alumina, and the single paper is titled for the thermal conductivity of Al2O3-ZrO2 COMPOSITE ceramics. Alumina and zirconia are mutually insoluble to a first approximation and this is the classic two-phase toughened ceramic, so the samples are corundum grains and zirconia grains, not a solid solution. [ref 2] offers only Zr10Al6O suboxides, which are metallic Zr-Al phases with dissolved oxygen and have nothing to do with a sintered oxide composite; I am not following them. Which zirconia polymorph is present -- monoclinic baddeleyite, or the tetragonal or cubic form if a stabiliser was used -- is not determinable from these compositions, and no stabiliser appears in them.

Three different intermetallics share this host and none dominates. Al3V and its Ti-substituted variants Al3V0.95Ti0.05 and Al3V0.9Ti0.1 are the tetragonal D0_22 Al3Ti type, which [ref 2] confirms as the best attested entry here (Al3V I4/mmm mp-2554, hull 0.000, 5 ICSD references) and which the paper on the lattice thermal conductivity of pseudogap intermetallic compounds is about. PrV2Al20 and LaV2Al20 are 1-2-20 cage compounds, matching Pr(Al10V)2 and La(Al10V)2 in Fd-3m. V3Al is the A15 Cr3Si type, mp-1387 in Pm-3n, appearing here as the vanadium-rich end of the (Fe1-xVx)3Al series studied as a Heusler-type thermoelectric -- despite that framing it is not a Heusler. D0_22 takes the primary label on composition count, but the host must be split three ways.

dopant_roles.basis: Al3V0.9Ti0.1: Ti takes the V site of the D0_22 cell, and since Al3Ti is the type compound itself the substitution is complete rather than dilute in principle.

PrV2Al20: Pr occupies the CN16 Frank-Kasper cage of the 1-2-20 framework and is a stoichiometric constituent, below 5 at.% only because the formula has 23 atoms. The paper is about its non-Kramers doublet ground state, which is a property of that cage site.
LaV2Al20, the non-magnetic reference compound for the Pr member; same site.
The same 1-2-20 A site; SmV2Al20 is not among the listed compositions but Sm appears in the candidate list for this host.

basis: Seven of the eight samples are FeAs2 or Fe(As1-xSex)2, and FeAs2 is orthorhombic marcasite in Pnnm -- mp-2008 at hull 0.000 with 10 ICSD references. This is the narrow-gap semiconductor with the colossal thermopower that all three papers are about, compared there against its sister marcasite FeSb2 and against RuSb2. The eighth sample is FeAs itself, which is not a marcasite but the MnP type, an orthorhombic distortion of NiAs in Pnma with metal zigzag chains (mp-427, 16 ICSD references), and is a metallic antiferromagnet rather than a semiconductor. The two are separated by the As:Fe ratio alone, so the split is clean.

dopant_roles.basis: Fe(As0.95Se0.05)2 and its two more dilute siblings: Se has one electron more than As and sits on the pnictogen site of the marcasite, so it is the n-type doping variable for FeAs2.

basis: All eight compositions are KxSr1-xFe2As2 with x from 0.27 to 0.72, from one paper mapping the phase diagram of that series. This is the 122 iron arsenide, the ThCr2Si2 body-centred tetragonal structure with FeAs layers separated by the alkali or alkaline-earth layer, and it is the same family as the Ba1-xKxFe2As2 already named in the taxonomy notes as the case where K-for-Ba substitution IS the doping variable. The quantum criticality the paper reports is electronic. Note that the structural transition these materials undergo -- tetragonal I4/mmm to orthorhombic Fmmm below roughly 200 K in the undoped parent -- is a small orthorhombic distortion within the same prototype, and it is suppressed by the K content at which these samples sit, so no phase sequence is recorded.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: A site between the FeAs layers
solid_solution_axis.note: K and Sr share the A site but are NOT isoelectronic -- K+ against Sr2+ -- so x is the hole count per formula unit and this axis is the doping variable, not a neutral alloying axis. The automatic detector did not flag it for that reason; it is recorded here because it is the only variable the paper scans.

basis: Every composition is written as (TiB2)a(SiC)b with an explicit free-carbon term in four of them, and both papers are about spark-plasma-sintered TiB2-SiC ceramics with graphene nanoplatelet or graphite additions. TiB2 and SiC do not form a solid solution or a ternary compound at these conditions, so the samples are a two- or three-phase ceramic: AlB2-type TiB2, a SiC polytype, and residual graphite. No reference line is offered for this host, and none is needed -- the composition strings are already written as a mixture.

Six of eight samples are LaB6 and the other two are Ce1-xLaxB6, all from low-temperature studies of the LaB6 and CeB6 Kondo systems. LaB6 is the textbook CaB6-type cubic hexaboride, a Pm-3m framework of B6 octahedra with the rare earth in the cube centre, and [ref 2] confirms it decisively: mp-2680 at hull 0.000 with 20 ICSD references. Four of the samples are single crystals, which is how this family is normally studied.

dopant_roles.basis: Ce0.25La0.75B6 and Ce0.05La0.95B6: Ce takes the cube-centre site of the B6 framework. CeB6 and LaB6 are a continuous series, and dilution of the Ce sublattice is the experimental variable -- the single-ion Kondo limit at one end, the dense Kondo lattice at the other -- so this is a tuning axis rather than doping in the carrier sense.

basis: Both compositions are HgBa2Ca2Cu3O8, the n equals 3 member of the mercury cuprate series and the highest-Tc superconductor at ambient pressure, one of them with Re on the Hg site. The structure is three CuO2 planes separated by Ca, capped by BaO layers, with a SINGLE Hg-O sheet of partial oxygen occupancy as the charge reservoir -- primitive P4/mmm, not the body-centred double-reservoir stacking of BSCCO. [ref 2] supports the family through the n equals 2 member Ba2CaCu2HgO6 in P4/mmm, mp-6879 with 6 ICSD references; the measured composition is the next term of the same homologous series and has no entry of its own in the dump. The taxonomy had no mercury or thallium cuprate entry, so one is proposed. The 87 to 302 K window crosses Tc, which is an electronic transition and not a structural one.

dopant_roles.basis: Hg0.82Re0.18Ba2Ca2Cu3O8: Re takes the Hg site of the reservoir layer, where it is octahedrally coordinated rather than dumbbell coordinated -- the second paper of this host is titled for the distortion of that ReO6 octahedron. Its purpose is to stabilise the phase against the volatility of Hg, and it changes the reservoir oxygen content as a side effect.

basis: The host holds both thallium cuprate families and they differ in the charge reservoir, not in the CuO2 stacking. Five samples are Tl2Ba2Ca2Cu3O10 and Tl2Ba2CaCu2O8, which have a rock-salt Tl-O DOUBLE layer and a body-centred I4/mmm cell -- [ref 2] gives Ba2CaTl2(CuO4)2 mp-6885 with 3 ICSD references for the 2212 member. Three samples are TlBa2Ca2Cu3O9, with a SINGLE Tl-O sheet and a primitive P4/mmm cell, isostructural with the HgBa2Ca2Cu3O8 of the neighbouring host at rank 765; [ref 2] carries it as Ba6Ca6Tl5Cu9O29 mp-680433, an off-stoichiometric cell of that single-layer family. Tl-2223 and Tl-1223 carry the same three CuO2 planes and differ only in the reservoir, which is precisely why the pair must be split rather than merged. The double-layer group takes the primary label on sample count.

Five of the eight samples are ErBa2Cu4O8 and three are ErBa2Cu3O7, so the host is not simply a rare-earth-substituted 123. The 124 phase has a PAIR of edge-sharing CuO chains in place of the single chain of 123, is oxygen stoichiometric rather than carrying the variable 6+d, and does not lose oxygen on heating -- which is why it is measured at all. [ref 2] separates the two cleanly: Ba2Er(CuO2)4 in Cmmm, mp-6583 at hull 0.004 with 6 ICSD references for the 124, and Ba2ErCu3O7 in Pmmm, mp-622110 with 2 references for the 123. Ten hosts already in the ledger are filed under ybco_cuprate; this is the first that needs the 124 entry, and the split is by the Cu:Ba ratio alone.

Every composition is Ba1-xSrxTiO3 with x from 0.30 to 0.67, with La or Y added as donors and one paper adding Mn. Barium titanate and strontium titanate form a complete perovskite solid solution, and the series is the standard PTCR and dielectric material; the measured 223 to 865 K window is where its ferroelectric behaviour lives. I am not following [ref 2] here: its entries are computed Ba-Sr-Ti-O supercells and Mn-containing cells such as Ba2Sr2CaTi5O15 in Pm and Ba2Sr6Ti7MnO24, none of which is the simple ABO3 perovskite these samples are, and none carries an ICSD count. The chunk file itself warns that the references describe a chemistry rather than a sample, and this is that case.

dopant_roles.basis: Ba0.5Sr0.4La0.1TiO3: La3+ on the divalent A site is a donor, adding one electron per La and making the material n-type. At 10% of the A site it is a heavy but still substitutional doping.

(Y2O3)0.0024(Ba0.7Sr0.3TiO3)0.9976: Y3+ is the usual donor in PTCR barium titanate ceramics and sits on the A site at these very dilute levels. The paper titles are about Y doping and temperature-dependent resistivity, which is the PTCR effect.

solid_solution_axis.note: Ba2+ and Sr2+ are isovalent and share the twelve-coordinate A site, so this is a genuine isoelectronic series: it changes the tolerance factor and therefore the ferroelectric transition temperature, sliding it from about 400 K in BaTiO3 down through room temperature, without changing the carrier count. The transition temperature therefore shifts with x across this host and cannot be given a single value.

basis: The host mixes two ways of putting In into Bi2Te3. Bi1.7In0.3Sb0.2Te3 is ordinary substitution on the cation site of the tetradymite lattice, and the dual-doped n-type sample with Ga is the same. The (Bi2Te3)32.5(In2Te3)7.5 and Bi33.5In7.5Te59 compositions are not: both papers of that group describe a lamellar TWO-PHASE microstructure obtained by directional solidification and annealing, in which In2Te3 separates from the Bi2Te3 matrix. In2Te3 is a vacancy-ordered defect zincblende, one third of its cation sites empty, and is not a tetradymite at all. Tetradymite takes the primary label because it is the matrix in every sample, but the In2Te3 lamellae are a real second structure and the host has to be split.

dopant_roles.basis: Bi1.7In0.3Sb0.2Te3: Sb is isovalent with Bi and shares the cation site across the whole Bi2Te3-Sb2Te3 join, so it tunes the band structure and the lattice thermal conductivity without adding carriers.

The dual-doped film composition (Bi)26.46(In)8.13(Ga)3.77(Te)61.64: Ga is the second trivalent substituent on the cation site alongside In, and the paper is titled for the ultralow thermal conductivity it produces. Whether it stays in solution or precipitates as Ga2Te3 is not settled by the composition.

basis: Five of the eight samples are sillenites: Bi24CoO37 (twice, once as a composite with Bi0.9La0.1FeO3), Bi25FeO39 and Bi12PbO19 are all the cubic Bi12MO20-d framework of distorted BiO5 polyhedra around an isolated MO4 tetrahedron, written on different oxygen normalisations. [ref 2] supports the family strongly even though it lists no measured composition: Bi12SiO20 at mp-23492 with 14 ICSD references and Bi12GeO20 at mp-23352 are the same structure with a different guest. Three samples are plain Bi2O3, which is monoclinic alpha-Bi2O3 (mp-23262, 10 ICSD references) and a different structure entirely, and two samples additionally contain BiFeO3 perovskite as a deliberate second phase. So the host holds three prototypes and splits on the Bi:M ratio. Confidence is medium because the sillenite guest content is variable and because the composite samples are two-phase by design.

other_polymorphs.note: delta-Bi2O3, the defect-fluorite fast oxide-ion conductor, is the equilibrium form of Bi2O3 above about 1002 K. The measured range here reaches 930 K, so no curve crosses it, but it is close enough that a slightly hotter measurement in this host would and the Bi2O3 samples would then need a two-phase sequence.

dopant_roles.basis: Bi24CoO37: Co is the guest cation in the MO4 tetrahedron at the centre of the sillenite framework, a stoichiometric constituent without which the structure does not form. It falls below the 5 at.% cut only because the formula carries 24 Bi and 37 O.

Bi25FeO39 is the classic iron sillenite, Fe on the same tetrahedral guest site. In the two composite samples Fe is additionally the B cation of the BiFeO3 second phase, so its role differs between the phases of one sample.
Bi12PbO19: Pb as the sillenite guest cation. The paper of that sample is about mixed Bi2O3-PbO systems, so a separate PbO phase is also possible.

(Bi0.9La0.1)FeO3 within the composite samples: La on the perovskite A site of BiFeO3, the standard substitution for suppressing its leakage and modifying its magnetic order. It is not in the sillenite phase.

basis: Three samples are Bi4Ti3O12 and five are Na0.5Bi4.5Ti4O15 with Er substitution. Both are Aurivillius phases -- Bi2O2 layers alternating with perovskite blocks -- at m equals 3 and m equals 4 respectively, and one paper says so directly in its title, on the anisotropic thermal conductivity of the Aurivillius phase bismuth titanate. [ref 2] agrees through Ti3(BiO3)4 in Aea2, mp-23427 at hull 0.000 with 7 ICSD references, which is Bi4Ti3O12 in its ferroelectric orthorhombic setting. The two members differ only in the thickness of the perovskite block, so they are one prototype rather than a mixed host.

dopant_roles.basis: Na0.5Bi4.5Ti4O15 is a stoichiometric compound, not a doped one: Na+ and Bi3+ together fill the A sites of the four-layer perovskite block so that the block is charge balanced against the Bi2O2 layers. Na falls below the 5 at.% cut only because the formula has 24 atoms.

Na0.5Bi4.5-yEryTi4O15 with y up to 0.025: Er3+ replaces Bi3+ on the perovskite A site, isovalent, and the paper reports it improving thermal stability and electrical properties. It is too dilute to affect the layer stacking.

basis: All eight compositions are (Bi,Sb)2Te2S, and the second paper names the family in its title -- the tetradymite-type Bi2Te2S-Sb2Te2S solid solution. Tetradymite is literally Bi2Te2S, so this host is the type compound of the prototype rather than a relative of it: quintuple layers in R-3m with sulphur ordered onto the central anion site and Te on the outer two. Bi and Sb share the cation site across the full range measured here. No reference line is offered for this host, and none is needed given the paper titles.

dopant_roles.basis: Bi1.0Sb0.9Sn0.1Te2S: Sn2+ on a trivalent cation site is an acceptor, the standard p-type dopant in this chemistry.
Cl on the chalcogen site is a donor and the usual n-type dopant for tetradymites. It appears in one composition of this host.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: cation site of the quintuple layer
solid_solution_axis.note: Bi and Sb are isovalent and share the cation site, and the samples scan the middle of the join rather than sitting near an end member, so no single parent compound can be named at host level. The sulphur stays ordered on the central anion site throughout and is not part of this axis.

basis: Three samples are SnBi4Se7, a mixed-layer compound of the (SnSe)m(Bi2Se3)n series -- the selenide analogue of GeBi4Te7 and PbBi4Te7, built by inserting a rocksalt-like SnSe layer between Bi2Se3 quintuple layers -- and two papers are devoted to it. One sample is written as the eutectic (SnSe2)0.67(BiSe2)0.33 and its paper calls it a eutectic SnSe2-Bi2Se3 ALLOY, so that one is a two-phase mixture of 1T SnSe2 and tetradymite Bi2Se3. The remaining four, Bi0.9Sn0.1Se and Bi0.8Sn0.2Se, I cannot resolve from composition: a 1:1 metal-to-selenium ratio is neither Bi2Se3 nor SnBi4Se7, and BiSe itself is a mixed-layer (Bi2)(Bi2Se3) compound, so these could be Sn-substituted BiSe or a different member of the same homologous series. [ref 2] offers only Sn4Bi2Se7 in C2/m with no ICSD count, which matches none of the measured compositions. Confidence is low and this host needs a paper read before stage 2 uses it.

Every composition is 85 to 91 at.% carbon with copper and a little titanium, and both papers are about carbon/copper composites -- one on the effect of titanium impregnation on their thermal conductivity, the other on the microstructure of titanium-added carbon/copper. Carbon and copper are mutually insoluble and form no carbide, which is the whole reason titanium is added: it wets the carbon and forms an interfacial TiC layer. So the samples are graphite plus fcc copper plus a thin carbide at the interface. [ref 2] offers only CuC6 at hull 1.354, a computed intercalation cell that is not a real phase here.

dopant_roles.basis: Ti at 0.29 to 0.46 at.% is not dissolved in either phase; it is impregnated deliberately to form a TiC layer at the carbon-copper interface, which is what both papers measure. It is a third phase rather than a dopant.

basis: All eight compositions are ThCxNy with x plus y between 0.85 and 1.23, from one paper on the electrical properties of thorium carbonitrides. ThC and ThN are both rocksalt (B1) and form a continuous solid solution on the anion site, with vacancies taking up the shortfall -- which is exactly what this prototype is defined for, MX 1:1 and often substoichiometric. I am not following [ref 2], which offers ThCN in C2/m and Th2CN in R-3m: those are ordered ternary cells with one ICSD reference or none, whereas a carbonitride prepared across a continuous composition range is the disordered rocksalt.
reference_disagreement: assigned sg [225], ICSD-backed references for this host report [12]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: Five samples are written TiO2@TiCO, the at sign denoting a coating, and one paper is titled for the effect of coated TiO2 nanoparticles on the thermoelectric performance of TiC. Two more are (TiO2)5TiC and its Nb-substituted form, again a mixture written explicitly. TiC is rocksalt and TiO2 is rutile or anatase; they are separate phases with an oxycarbide interlayer where they meet, which is what the TiCO in the composition string is naming. The last sample, (TiO2)13.07C86.93, is a graphene-oxide and TiO2 mixture from the metal-to-insulator paper, again two phases. [ref 2] offers only Ti2C2O9 at hull 0.540, which is not any of these.

dopant_roles.basis: (Ti0.96Nb0.04O2)5TiC: Nb5+ on the Ti4+ site of TiO2 is a donor, the standard n-type dopant for titania and for SrTiO3-like oxides. It is in the oxide phase, not the carbide.

basis: All three compositions are written as a Ti and SiC mixture at 8 to 17 at.% SiC, and both papers are about titanium reinforced with SiC particles -- one specifically on the effect of the interfacial REACTION on thermal properties. So the samples are an hcp titanium matrix with SiC particles, plus the interfacial TiC and Ti5Si3 that reaction forms. [ref 2] lists the MAX phase Ti3SiC2 in P6_3/mmc with 16 ICSD references as the best attested compound of this element set, and it is a plausible interfacial product, but at 92 at.% Ti the bulk cannot be Ti3SiC2 and the papers describe a particulate composite, so I am not taking it as the host structure.

Seven of eight samples are ZrC and the eighth is ZrC0.99N0.03. Zirconium carbide is rocksalt B1 with a wide carbon-vacancy range, written ZrC1-x, and the papers are about sintered ZrC ceramics and a review of ZrC, ZrN and ZrCN -- all the same structure. I disagree with [ref 1] here and the disagreement is worth recording: TEDesignLab gives ZrC in F-43m mp-1009894 at hull 0.614 on a single ICSD reference, which is a zincblende cell, not the ambient phase. [ref 2] is unambiguous the other way -- ZrC Fm-3m mp-2795 at hull 0.000 with 43 ICSD references -- and the project precedence puts TEDesignLab first only as evidence, not as the decision. The rocksalt entry is right.

other_polymorphs.note: The TEDesignLab F-43m entry for ZrC, hull 0.614. Zincblende ZrC is not a phase these ceramics pass through; it is recorded here only so the disagreement with [ref 1] is visible rather than silently dropped.

dopant_roles.basis: ZrC0.99N0.03: N on the carbon site of the same rocksalt lattice. ZrC and ZrN are fully miscible, so this is the dilute end of the ZrCN join rather than an impurity, and one of the papers reviews that whole join. Note separately that the carbon content itself is substoichiometric in these ceramics, which is a vacancy effect on the same site.

basis: All eight compositions are Nd1-xCaxTiO3 with x from 0.5 to 0.7, plus one series with (Al0.5Nb0.5) co-substituted onto the Ti site. NdTiO3 and CaTiO3 are both GdFeO3-distorted orthorhombic perovskites and form a continuous solid solution; the first paper is about the band-filling dependence of transport in Nd1-xAxTiO3, which is the Ti3+ to Ti4+ count set by x and only makes sense within a single perovskite lattice. No reference line is offered for this host, so the call rests on the compositions and on the titanate chemistry.

dopant_roles.basis: Ca0.61Nd0.26Ti1-z(Al0.5Nb0.5)zO3: Al3+ and Nb5+ enter the B site as a charge-compensating PAIR, so the pair is isovalent with the 2Ti4+ it replaces and the carrier count is unchanged. The purpose is dielectric and microstructural, which is what the second paper measures.
The other half of the same (Al0.5Nb0.5) B-site pair. On its own Nb5+ would be a donor in a titanate; here it is balanced by the Al3+ and is not.

basis: Six of the eight compositions are A14MSb11 phases: Ca14MgSb11, named in its paper title as a new Mg-containing Zintl compound alongside Yb14MgSb11, and the quaternary series Ca13REMnSb11 with RE equal to La, Ce, Pr, Nd, Sm and Gd, whose paper title gives the formula explicitly. That is the 14-1-11 structure, I4_1/acd, with its MSb4 tetrahedron, Sb3 linear trimer and isolated Sb anions. The seventh composition, Ca16Sb11, is not a 14-1-11 and has no counterpart in [ref 2], which for this element set offers only the simpler binaries Ca5Sb3, Ca2Sb, Ca11Sb10 and CaSb2 -- none of which is a measured composition. Confidence is medium because of that one unresolved composition and because no reference entry covers the 14-1-11 itself.

dopant_roles.basis: In Ca13REMnSb11 the Mn is the M of A14MX11: it sits at the centre of the MnSb4 tetrahedron and is a stoichiometric constituent of the prototype, not a dopant. It falls below 5 at.% because the formula has 26 atoms. The role vocabulary has no term for a stoichiometric minority site, so alloying_component is the least wrong of the available options.
Ca14MgSb11: Mg occupies the same tetrahedral M site as Mn does, which is what makes it a new member of the family rather than a doped Ca-Sb binary.

Ca13LaMnSb11: the rare earth replaces one of the fourteen Ca cations, and being trivalent rather than divalent it adds one electron per formula unit. That is the point of the quaternary series -- it converts the p-type 14-1-11 towards n-type.
Ca13CeMnSb11, same A site and same electron count argument as La.
Ca13PrMnSb11, same A site.
Ca13NdMnSb11, same A site.
The Gd member of the same Ca13REMnSb11 series.
The Sm member of the same Ca13REMnSb11 series.

basis: Every composition is (Mg1-xCdx)3Sb2 with x from 0.1 to 0.3, and one paper is titled for enhancing the thermoelectric performance of p-type Mg3Sb2 by codoping. Alpha-Mg3Sb2 is the CaAl2Si2 type, P-3m1, with Mg on both the octahedral interlayer site and the tetrahedral site of the (Mg2Sb2) slab; Cd2+ is isovalent with Mg2+ and substitutes on the tetrahedral site, giving a continuous alloy toward Cd3Sb2. [ref 2] offers only Mg14CdSb and Mg6CdSb computed cells, which are Mg-rich intermetallics at nothing like this stoichiometry, so I am not using them. The alpha to beta transition of Mg3Sb2 lies near 1200 K, far above the 779 K upper end of the measured window.

dopant_roles.basis: Mg2.39Li0.01Cd0.8Sb2: Li+ on the divalent Mg site is an acceptor and is the p-type dopant in the codoping paper.
(Mg0.7Cd0.25Ag0.05)3Sb2: Ag+ is the second acceptor on the Mg site, used alongside Cd alloying in the same study.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: tetrahedral cation site of the Mg2Sb2 slab
solid_solution_axis.note: Mg and Cd are isovalent and share the tetrahedral site, so this changes the band structure and the lattice thermal conductivity without adding carriers -- the Cd content and the Li or Ag doping are two separate knobs in these papers. The interlayer octahedral Mg site is not thought to accept Cd, so the sublattice fraction is roughly twice the formula fraction.

basis: Six of the eight samples are plain CdS and two are Co-substituted. Bulk CdS is hexagonal greenockite, the wurtzite type, and [ref 1] ranks it first on evidence: CdS P6_3mc mp-672 at hull 0.000 with 23 ICSD references, against 14 for the zincblende form. The reason confidence is medium rather than high is the synthesis: one paper is on chemical-bath-deposited CdS films, and chemical bath deposition routinely yields the cubic zincblende phase or a mixture of the two, since the layers differ only in stacking sequence and their energies are within a few meV per atom. So the host is wurtzite unless the paper says otherwise, and a film sample may well not be.

other_polymorphs.note: Cubic CdS, hull 0.001 with 14 ICSD references. Only 1 meV per atom above the wurtzite form, so it is not metastable in any strong sense; it is selected by the growth route rather than by temperature, and chemical bath deposition tends to select it. Heating does not convert one into the other in the measured 100 to 438 K window.
CdS at hull 0.134 with 8 ICSD references; the rocksalt form appears above roughly 3 GPa and has nothing to do with these samples.

dopant_roles.basis: Co0.05Cd0.95S: Co2+ is isovalent with Cd2+ and substitutes on the tetrahedral cation site, which is the standard dilute magnetic semiconductor substitution in this chemistry rather than a carrier dopant.

basis: The whole host is the single composition CeCo2Ga8, from one paper on heavy-fermion behaviour in the quasi-one-dimensional Kondo lattice CeCo2Ga8. The 1-2-8 stoichiometry is the CaCo2Al8 or YbCo2Al8 type, orthorhombic Pbam, in which the rare earth sits in channels of the transition-metal and main-group framework -- the chains that make the compound quasi-one-dimensional and that the paper is about. [ref 2] contains it: Ce(Ga4Co)2 in Pbam, mp-1196595 at hull 0.000, though on a single ICSD reference. It ranks CeGaCo in C2/m higher on ICSD count, but that equiatomic compound is not a composition of this host, so the ranking describes the chemistry rather than these samples. The taxonomy had 1-2-10 and 1-2-20 cage entries but nothing at 1-2-8, so one is proposed.

The whole host is CeCoIn5, the most studied of the 115 heavy-fermion superconductors, measured as single crystals from 10 to 300 K. The HoCoGa5 structure is primitive tetragonal P4/mmm, alternating a CeIn3 layer with a CoIn2 layer, and [ref 2] gives it directly: CeIn5Co P4/mmm mp-19961 at hull 0.000, with the related Ce2In8Co listed alongside. The 115 prototype was proposed from the Ce-In-Ir-Rh host in chunk 010; this is the host it was named for. The transitions the papers study -- superconductivity at 2.3 K and field-tuned quantum criticality -- are electronic.

All eight compositions are La1-xCexFePO with x from 0.2 to 0.8, from one paper on spin-glass, single-ion and dense Kondo effects in that series. LaFePO is the oxypnictide 1111 structure -- alternating (La2O2) and (Fe2P2) layers in P4/nmm, the ZrCuSiAs type -- and is the parent of the iron-based superconductors, discovered before the fluorine-doped arsenide. Ce substitutes for La on the rare-earth site of the oxide layer throughout. No reference line is offered for this host, so the call rests on the composition and the family.

solid_solution_axis.note: La3+ and Ce3+ share the same site and the same formal valence, so the detector reads this as an isoelectronic series and structurally it is one. Electronically it is not: Ce carries a 4f electron and La does not, and the entire point of the series is to dilute the Ce sublattice between the single-ion Kondo limit and the dense Kondo lattice. The label isoelectronic should not be read as electronically inert here.

basis: Three different stoichiometries share this host. Three samples are Ce2Ni2Ga, the 2-2-1 Mo2FeB2 type (an ordered U3Si2 derivative, tetragonal P4/mbm) and the largest single composition; the isostructural U2AlCo2 appears in the Al-Co-U reference line of this same chunk. Two are CeNiGa, equiatomic, which [ref 2] places in P-62m at mp-31492 with 2 ICSD references -- the ZrNiAl ordered Fe2P type. Three more are CeNi5-based: CeNi4Ga, Ce(Ni0.9Ga0.1)5 and Ce(Ni0.865Ga0.135)5, which are the CaCu5 type with Ga substituting for Ni, and one paper is titled for the dependence of the CeNi5 thermopower on 4f instability. Three prototypes, separated by the Ni:Ce ratio, so the host must be split. [ref 2] ranks CeGa2Ni in Cmmm highest, but no composition here is 1-2-1.

All eight compositions are CeNi2(Ge1-xSix)2 across the full range from x equal to 0.13 to 0.80. CeNi2Ge2 and CeNi2Si2 are both ThCr2Si2-type, body-centred tetragonal I4/mmm, and form a continuous solid solution; the series is a classic route for tuning a Ce compound between magnetic order and intermediate valence by chemical pressure, which is what both papers measure. Ge and Si share the X site throughout. No reference line is offered for this host.

solid_solution_axis.note: Ge and Si are isovalent and share the X site, so this axis acts as chemical pressure: the cell contracts as Si increases, which is the variable both papers scan. No end member can be named at host level.

basis: Every composition is CeS1.34 to CeS1.43, which is precisely the gamma-Ce3-xS4 range: Ce3S4 is CeS1.333 and Ce2S3 is CeS1.5, and the gamma phase spans between them as a single Th3P4-type cubic structure (I-43d) with cerium vacancies taking up the difference. That vacancy concentration is the carrier-concentration knob, exactly as the taxonomy notes record for La3-xTe4, and it is what the two papers on cerium sulphide thermoelectrics are varying. [ref 2] ranks CeS Fm-3m first on 15 ICSD references, but no sample here is the 1:1 monosulphide, and it does list Ce3S4 in I-43d at mp-1382; the ranking describes the chemistry rather than these compositions, so I am not following it.

dopant_roles.basis: CeS1.41(SrS)0.07: SrS is added to the melt and Sr2+ enters the cation site of the Th3P4 framework. Being divalent rather than trivalent it removes electrons, so it works alongside the cation vacancies as a carrier-concentration control rather than as an inert filler.
The same cation site; the second paper is on ternary rare-earth sulphides, where divalent Eu plays the same role as Sr.

basis: The host holds three related but distinct layer stackings. Three samples are Gd0.7Sr0.3CoO3, a simple ABO3 perovskite cobaltite whose spin-state transition the third paper studies. Three are SrGdCoO4, which is the n equals 1 Ruddlesden-Popper K2NiF4 structure -- single CoO2 layers between rocksalt blocks -- and [ref 2] carries SrGdCoO4 cells at mp-1218232 and mp-1218280. Two are Sr3GdCo4O10.5, the so-called 314 cobaltite, an oxygen-vacancy-ordered perovskite superstructure in which the vacancy ordering alternates CoO6 octahedra with CoO4 tetrahedra; it is filed under perovskite here because that is what it derives from, but it deserves its own entry and stage 2 should not treat it as a simple ABO3. The split is by the Co:Sr ratio.

dopant_roles.basis: Sr3GdCo3.9Ga0.1O10.5: Ga3+ on the Co site of the 314 phase. Ga has no accessible spin states, so substituting it for Co dilutes the magnetic and spin-state behaviour while holding the framework; it also tends to prefer the tetrahedral site of the vacancy-ordered structure.

basis: Every composition is CoSi1-xGex with x from 0.1 to 0.5, two of them with 2% boron. CoSi is the B20 FeSi structure, cubic P2_13, a chiral non-centrosymmetric arrangement that is not a rocksalt or a CsCl type despite the 1:1 stoichiometry, and it is the high-power-factor alloy all three papers are about -- the first is titled for the high thermoelectric power factor in alloys based on CoSi. Ge substitutes for Si on the metalloid site of the same structure. [ref 2] offers only computed Co2SiGe and Co3SiGe2 cells with no ICSD backing, neither of which matches the measured 1:1 metal-to-metalloid ratio.

dopant_roles.basis: CoSi0.88Ge0.1B0.02: boron is written in the metalloid position and has one electron fewer than Si, so it acts as an acceptor on that site. It is small enough that an interstitial fraction cannot be excluded from the composition alone, which is why this is medium rather than high.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: metalloid site of the B20 cell
solid_solution_axis.note: Ge and Si are isovalent on the metalloid site, so the alloying suppresses the lattice thermal conductivity by mass and strain contrast without changing the carrier count -- the point of the paper on how isovalent substitutes play in different ways. The boron doping is a separate and independent knob.

basis: Every composition is La1-xSrx(Mn,Co)O3 with the B site split roughly evenly between Mn and Co, one of them also carrying Ni. These are the manganite-cobaltite perovskites: La0.7Sr0.3MnO3 with Co substituted onto the B site, rhombohedral R-3c at these Sr levels, studied here for magnetotransport and as SOFC cathodes. Mn and Co are disordered on the B site at a 1:1 ratio in a mixed-valent oxide, so this is a simple perovskite and not a B-site ordered double perovskite -- ordering of that kind needs a large charge or size difference, which Mn3+/4+ and Co3+/4+ do not provide. [ref 2] offers Sr2LaMnCoO7 (a Ruddlesden-Popper cell) and SrLaMnCoO6 in F-43m, neither of which matches the measured A:B ratio of 1:1.

dopant_roles.basis: La0.6Sr0.4Co0.5Ni0.2Mn0.3O3: Ni is the third B-site cation, taking part of the Mn share. In an SOFC cathode composition it is there for catalytic activity and conductivity rather than as a dilute dopant.

basis: Six of the eight samples are CoSb3-xSnx with x from 0.2 to 0.5, tin substituting into the Sb4 rings of the skutterudite framework, and the first paper is titled for Sn-doped CoSb3. The other two are filled: Sn1.75Co8Sb24, which is SnzCo4Sb12 with tin in the icosahedral void and has its own paper, and Pr0.5Co4Sb10Sn2, which is filled AND framework-substituted at once. [ref 2] confirms the filled variant directly with Co4SnSb12 in Im-3 at mp-15868. Framework and filled skutterudite are the same cubic Im-3 framework differing by occupancy of the void, so the host splits on whether the void is occupied, exactly as the Co-Sb host at rank 1 does.

dopant_roles.basis: Pr0.5Co4Sb10Sn2: Pr occupies the icosahedral void of the skutterudite framework, where it rattles and scatters phonons. It is a filler, not a substituent, and the tin in the same formula is doing something different -- sitting in the framework and compensating the charge the filler adds.
Ce appears as a candidate in two compositions of this host and plays the same void-filling role as Pr in the PrFe4-xTMxSb12 family the third paper is about.

basis: All five compositions are TiCoSb1-xSnx with x of 0.2 or 0.25, and the first paper is titled for the high-temperature thermoelectric properties of CoTiSb half-Heusler compounds. TiCoSb is the 18-electron half-Heusler, cubic F-43m, with one of the two tetrahedral sites of the full Heusler left vacant; Sn substitutes on the Sb site and is the p-type dopant that makes the compound useful. Two compositions carry excess Co (TiCo1.03Sb0.8Sn0.2, TiCo1.05Sb0.8Sn0.2), which goes into that vacant site and pushes very slightly toward the full Heusler -- a well-known effect in this system and the reason one paper is about phase-separated half-Heuslers -- but at 3 to 5% it does not change the prototype. No reference line is offered for this host.

dopant_roles.basis: CoTi0.8Nb0.1Ta0.1Sb0.8Sn0.2: Nb sits on the Ti site. It is isoelectronic with Ta and one electron richer than Ti, and in this quintuple-substituted composition its purpose is mass-contrast phonon scattering alongside the (Ti/Zr/Hf) alloying the third paper studies.
The other half of the same Nb and Ta pair on the Ti site, in the same composition.

basis: Every composition is RT2Zn20: YbCo2Zn20, YCo2Zn20 and the Ni-substituted series YbCo2-xNixZn20. This is the 1-2-20 CeCr2Al20 cage structure, cubic Fd-3m, with the rare earth inside a CN16 Frank-Kasper cage of zinc -- the very dilute rare-earth sublattice that gives YbCo2Zn20 its enormous Sommerfeld coefficient, which is what the first two papers are about. [ref 2] supports it with the isostructural Gd(Zn10Co)2, U(Zn10Co)2 and Zr(Zn10Co)2, all in Fd-3m at hull 0.000. The same prototype is needed for the single YbCoNiZn20 sample sitting in the elemental Zn host at rank 753.

dopant_roles.basis: Yb is the guest in the CN16 cage and a stoichiometric constituent of RT2Zn20; it falls below the 5 at.% cut only because the formula has 23 atoms. Its 4f instability is the physics of the compound, so calling it a dopant would be backwards.
YCo2Zn20 is the non-magnetic reference compound with Y on the same cage site, used to subtract the lattice contribution from the Yb member.
YbCo2-xNixZn20 with x from 0.1 to 0.5: Ni takes the transition-metal site and adds one electron per substitution, which is how the third paper tunes the thermoelectric properties.

basis: All eight compositions are Cu1+xCr2Te4 with x from 0 to 0.5, from one paper on stuffed compositions of a ferromagnetic chalcogenide. CuCr2Te4 is a normal spinel, Fd-3m, with Cu on the tetrahedral A site and Cr on the octahedral B site, and [ref 2] gives it directly: Cr2CuTe4 Fd-3m mp-22625 at hull 0.000 with 3 ICSD references. The word stuffed in the paper title is the key: the excess copper beyond x equal to 0 goes into the normally empty interstitial sites of the spinel framework rather than forming a second phase, which is why the series stays single phase to Cu1.5Cr2Te4.

All six compositions are the same material written two ways: YMn0.5Cr0.5O3 and Y2MnCrO6 are identical stoichiometries, and three of the papers call it the double perovskite Y2MnCrO6. [ref 2] supports B-site ordering with Y2MnCrO6 in P2_1/c, mp-1189214 at hull 0.016 with 2 ICSD references, the monoclinic cell that an ordered rock-salt arrangement of Mn and Cr produces. But Mn3+ and Cr3+ are the same charge and nearly the same size, which is the condition under which B-site order is usually POOR, and the degree of order depends on the synthesis rather than on the composition -- a disordered sample is simply orthorhombic YMn0.5Cr0.5O3 in Pnma. That is a sample-level question, not a composition-level one, so both prototypes are recorded. Note also that YMnO3 itself is hexagonal, not a perovskite at all; half substitution by Cr is what brings this composition into the perovskite family.

dopant_roles.basis: Y2-yLayMnCrO6 with y from 0.1 to 0.3: La3+ on the A site is isovalent with Y3+ but much larger, so it raises the tolerance factor and straightens the octahedral tilts. The paper measures its effect on the ferrimagnetism, which is a consequence of that bond-angle change rather than of doping.

basis: The host is four samples of Cr2S3 and four of Cr3S4, which are not two unrelated structures but two members of the Cr1-xS defect NiAs series: both are the hexagonal NiAs framework with ordered vacancies in alternate metal layers, Cr3S4 with a quarter of the metal sites empty in every second layer (monoclinic) and Cr2S3 with a third (trigonal). [ref 1] ranks CrS P6_3/mmc first with 6 ICSD references, which is the ideal undistorted parent, and lists Cr3S4 alongside; [ref 2] gives Cr3S4 at mp-849071 and Cr2S3 R3 at mp-849081, both at hull 0.000. Confidence is medium because the vacancy superstructure differs between the two compositions even though the parent framework does not, so stage 2 must pick the right cell per composition rather than the NiAs aristotype.

Every composition is TiFe1-yCuxSb, and the two paper titles say what it is: half-Heusler-LIKE TiFeCuSb, and vacancy-filling Heusler design. TiFeSb on its own is a 17-electron half-Heusler and therefore unstable; copper entering the vacant tetrahedral site of the MgAgAs cell carries the electron count toward 18 and stabilises it. So these sit on the continuum between half and full Heusler, with the interstitial site partly filled at x of 0.2 to 0.33 rather than empty or full. Half-Heusler takes the label because the framework and the vacancy are what the structure is built on; the alternative full Heusler is the x equal to 1 limit these samples do not reach. No reference line is offered for this host, which is why confidence is medium.

All four compositions are YSr2Cu3-zMzO7 with M equal to Cr or Ga, two of them additionally Ca-substituted on the Y site. This is the 123 structure with strontium in place of barium: YSr2Cu3O7 does not form on its own under ambient pressure, and the small Cr or Ga substitution on the CuO chain site is precisely the trick used to stabilise it, the substituting cation taking tetrahedral coordination in the chain layer. The single paper compares carrier concentrations determined structurally and electrically, which presumes the 123 framework. [ref 2] carries Sr2YCu3O7 in Pmmm at mp-985569, the right structure, though at hull 0.021 with no ICSD count -- consistent with the phase needing a stabiliser to exist at all. Confidence is medium for that reason.

dopant_roles.basis: YSr1.5Cu2.8Cr0.2O7: Cr sits on the CuO chain site, where it takes a higher oxygen coordination and stabilises the Sr-substituted 123 phase. It also fixes extra oxygen in the chain layer, so it changes the hole count as a side effect rather than being a neutral spectator.
Y0.8Ca0.2Sr1.6Ba0.4Cu2.7Ga0.3O7: Ga plays the same chain-site stabilising role as Cr, taking tetrahedral coordination there.
Y1-xCaxSr1.5Cu2.8Cr0.2O7 with x of 0.2 and 0.3: Ca2+ on the trivalent Y site adds holes to the CuO2 planes and is the deliberate doping variable in a paper about carrier concentration.

One composition is Sr1.6Ba0.4 rather than Sr2: Ba and Sr are isovalent on the same site and the ratio controls the cell size, which is what makes the 123 phase stable without or with less chain-site substitution.

basis: Four samples are DyMnO3 and four are Dy1-xAxMnO3 with A equal to Eu, K or Bi. DyMnO3 is the orthorhombic GdFeO3-distorted perovskite in Pnma -- the strongly tilted, orbitally ordered manganite whose spiral magnetic order makes it a textbook multiferroic, which is what all three papers are measuring. I disagree with [ref 2] here. It ranks DyMnO3 P6_3cm mp-636982 PRIMARY at hull 0.000 and puts the orthorhombic mp-25019 second at hull 0.023, both on 2 ICSD references. Dy is the last rare earth in the series that gives the perovskite by ordinary ceramic synthesis; the hexagonal form, with MnO5 trigonal bipyramids and no octahedra at all, is reached by thin-film growth or soft chemistry and is not what a polycrystalline sample measured for magnetotransport will be. The ICSD-count ranking cannot separate them at 2 references each, so the judgement decides.

other_polymorphs.note: Hexagonal DyMnO3, which Materials Project ranks first for this formula. It is a genuine phase -- Dy sits right on the orthorhombic-to-hexagonal boundary of the RMnO3 series -- but it is obtained by film growth or low-temperature routes, not by heating the orthorhombic form, so it is not in any thermal sequence these samples pass through.

dopant_roles.basis: Dy0.9K0.1MnO3 and Dy0.8K0.2MnO3: K+ on the trivalent A site is a strong acceptor, driving Mn3+ toward Mn4+ and introducing double-exchange hole carriers. The paper calls it Dy sublattice dilution.

Dy0.9Eu0.1MnO3: Eu3+ is isovalent with Dy3+ but larger and essentially non-magnetic in its ground state, so it dilutes the rare-earth magnetism and slightly relaxes the octahedral tilt without changing the carrier count.

Dy0.9Bi0.1MnO3: Bi3+ is isovalent on the A site but carries a stereochemically active 6s lone pair, which distorts its coordination and is the reason the paper studies it separately from the rare earths.

basis: Every composition is an ABO3 perovskite of the (La,Sr)(Mn,Fe)O3 series. SrLaFeMnO6, Sr1.4La0.6FeMnO6 and Sr1.2La0.8FeMnO6 are that series written over two formula units, La0.5Sr0.5Mn0.5Fe0.5O3 is the same thing written over one, and the leading entry (La0.7Sr0.3MnO3)(La0.7Sr0.3FeO3) is a bilayer of the manganite and the ferrite grown along (111), so it is again the same chemistry. Mn3+ and Fe3+ carry the same charge and nearly the same radius, so there is no driving force for long-range B-site order and the ceramic product is a B-site disordered perovskite. I disagree with [ref 2] on that point: every entry it ranks is a large computed cell with an ordered Mn/Fe arrangement -- SrLaMnFeO6 Pc mp-1218252 and P2/c mp-705491, and the P1 Sr3La7 supercells -- which is how a calculation has to represent a disordered site, not evidence that the ordering is real.

other_polymorphs.note: The rock-salt-ordered Mn/Fe double perovskite that Materials Project ranks for SrLaMnFeO6. Ordering of that kind is real for pairs with a large charge and size difference (Sr2FeMoO6, the subject of one of the linked papers), but not for Mn3+/Fe3+, and no ICSD-backed ordered cell is offered here.

basis: All six compositions reduce to lithium ferrite, Li0.5Fe2.5O4, with part of the cation content replaced: Li0.45Zn0.1La0.04Fe2.41O4, Li0.4Cd0.2Fe2.4O4 and Li0.4Zn0.2Fe2.4O4 all sit on the Li0.5-0.5xMxFe2.5-0.5xO4 line that the curator strings spell out explicitly. [ref 2] ranks exactly that compound first, LiFe5O8 P4_332 mp-31768 on 13 ICSD references, LiFe5O8 being Li0.5Fe2.5O4 doubled. P4_332 is the 1:3 Li/Fe ordering on the octahedral site of the Fd-3m spinel, so this is spinel with cation order rather than a separate type. Nothing in the host resembles the other ranked entries, LiFeO2 or Li5FeO4.

dopant_roles.basis: Li0.4Zn0.2Fe2.4O4 and Li0.45Zn0.1La0.04Fe2.41O4. Zn2+ has a strong tetrahedral site preference, so it takes the A site and pushes Fe3+ onto the octahedral B site, which is the standard way the magnetisation of a Li ferrite is tuned.
Li0.45Mg0.1Fe2.45O4 and Mg0.1Al0.2Li0.45Fe2.25O4: divalent Mg on the spinel cation sublattice, distributed between both sites.
Li0.4Cd0.2Fe2.4O4, and the curator gives the series as Li0.5-x/2CdxFe2.5-x/2O4. Cd2+ is large and, like Zn2+, takes the tetrahedral A site.
Mg0.1Al0.2Li0.45Fe2.25O4: trivalent Al on the octahedral Fe site, a non-magnetic diluent.

The curator gives (Li0.5Fe0.5)1-xCuxFe2O4, so Cu2+ replaces the Li0.5Fe0.5 block on the octahedral site; Jahn-Teller Cu2+ is also what drives the tetragonal distortion seen in copper-rich ferrite spinels.
Li0.6Ge0.2Fe2.2O4: Ge4+ on a spinel cation site, charge-compensated by the raised Li content, which is why this composition carries more Li than the others.

Li0.45Zn0.1La0.04Fe2.41O4 at y = 0.04 per the curator string. La3+ is far too large for either spinel site, so although the paper writes it as substitutional, part of it is likely to segregate as an orthoferrite or to grain boundaries; recorded as substitutional at medium confidence.

reference_disagreement: assigned sg [227], ICSD-backed references for this host report [212, 141, 166, 61]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: The host is one compound, FePS3, in all 8 samples, from a single paper on the metal-insulator transition of this Mott insulator. FePS3 is Fe2P2S6: a CdI2-like sheet in which two thirds of the octahedral sites hold Fe2+ in a honeycomb and the remaining third holds a P-P dimer standing perpendicular to the layer, the layers stacked by van der Waals contact in C2/m. [ref 2] agrees, ranking FePS3 C2/m mp-5864 first on 6 ICSD references; its hull value of 0.134 is the usual Materials Project penalty for a layered sulfide and is not evidence against the phase, and the alternatives it lists carry one reference each. The taxonomy had no M2P2X6 entry, so mps3_thiophosphate is proposed for it.

All six compositions are TiFe1+ySb with y between 0 and 0.46, and two of the three papers name the half-Heusler system in their titles. The half-Heusler TiFeSb is the C1b structure, F-43m, which [ref 2] carries at mp-10755 on hull 0.000: three interpenetrating fcc sublattices with the fourth tetrahedral site empty. The excess Fe of TiFe1.33Sb goes into that empty site, so these samples sit part-way along the C1b to L21 line towards the full Heusler TiFe2Sb (mp-998970). Partial filling does not make them full Heuslers -- at y = 0.33 two thirds of the site is still vacant and the transport is that of a gapped half-Heusler -- so the host is filed as half_heusler with the full Heusler as the alternative end point.

dopant_roles.basis: TiFeCu0.10Sb and TiFeCu0.15Sb, from a paper on half-Heusler-like TiFeCuxSb. With the Fe content held at 1 the Cu has nowhere to substitute, so it enters the vacant tetrahedral 4d site of the C1b cell -- the same site the excess Fe of TiFe1.33Sb occupies -- and adds electrons there.

TiFe1.0Ni0.1Sb, from a paper on TiFe1.1-xNixSb: Ni replaces Fe on the 4c site, and each substitution adds one valence electron, moving the composition towards the 18-electron count of the semiconducting half-Heusler.

basis: This host is not one structure. Its eight samples are eight different uranium silicides at one sample each -- UFe2Si2, U2Fe3Si5, U2FeSi3, U3Fe2Si7, UFe5Si3 and U1.2Fe4Si9.7 -- from papers that survey the whole U-Fe-Si ternary system for thermoelectric and magnetic behaviour. UFe2Si2 is the one that maps cleanly onto the taxonomy: the ThCr2Si2 body-centred tetragonal 122, which [ref 2] confirms at U(FeSi)2 I4/mmm mp-20924 on 3 ICSD references. U2FeSi3 is an AlB2-derived hexagonal phase with Fe and Si sharing the honeycomb net. U2Fe3Si5 is the Sc2Fe3Si5 family, which [ref 2] places in the monoclinic C2/c U2Co3Si5 setting at mp-1105639, and U3Fe2Si7, UFe5Si3 and the Si-rich U1.2Fe4Si9.7 are further distinct types with no taxonomy entry. A single host-level prototype cannot be right here; the label is recorded at low confidence and flagged mixed so stage 2 splits it composition by composition.

dopant_roles.basis: [ref 2] ranks U6Fe16Si7C Fm-3m mp-642273 alongside the carbon-free U6Fe16Si7 mp-642279, and one of the linked papers reports new U6Fe16Si7-type compounds. In that Th6Mn23-derived cell the carbon fills an octahedral void and stabilises the phase, so it is recorded as interstitial rather than as milling residue; at one sample the alternative reading, adventitious carbon from processing, cannot be excluded.

basis: All three compositions are K8GaxSn46-x with x between 6 and 8, and two of the three papers name sintered type-I clathrates in their titles. That is the 46-atom cubic Pm-3n framework of Ga and Sn tetrahedra enclosing two small and six large cages, with the eight K atoms as guests. The composition confirms the electron count: eight K+ donating eight electrons to eight Ga- framework sites is exactly charge-balanced at K8Ga8Sn38, which is the composition of 6 of the 8 samples, and the Ga-poorer K8Ga6Sn40 and K8Ga7Sn39 are the metallic, electron-excess side of the same framework. Neither reference covers the host, so mp_id is left null.

The parent is Ru2NbGa and the rest of the host is off-stoichiometry around it, Ru2-xNb1+xGa with x from -0.05 to 0.10, from one paper on chemically substituted Heusler-type Ru2NbGa. That is the L21 full Heusler, the ordered cubic Fm-3m arrangement in which Ru fills both tetrahedral sublattices and Nb and Ga alternate on the octahedral ones. [ref 2] offers exactly one entry for the host and it is that structure, NbGaRu2 Fm-3m mp-977401 at hull 0.000, though with no ICSD count attached.

dopant_roles.basis: Ru2NbGa0.95In0.05: In is the group-13 neighbour of Ga and takes the same main-group site, so it expands the lattice and scatters phonons without changing the valence electron count.
Ru2NbGa0.90Sn0.10: Sn on the Ga site adds one valence electron per substitution and is the n-type knob for a Heusler sitting in a pseudogap.
Same role as Sn -- a group-14 element on the group-13 site, adding one electron each -- for the Ge-substituted member of the same substitution study.

basis: All five compositions are Gd5Si2-xGe2+x, four of them at the 5-2-2 composition itself and the fifth written Gd5(Si0.45Ge0.55)4, which is the same thing. This is the R5T4 slab structure: blocks of Gd-T-Gd joined by T-T dimers, where breaking half of those dimers shears the cell between the monoclinic P2_1/a form and the orthorhombic Gd5Si4 O(I) form.
