That shear is the magnetostructural martensitic transition behind the giant magnetocaloric effect, it sits near 276 K for Gd5Si2Ge2, and the third paper measures thermopower and resistivity across exactly it -- so the 11-321 K window crosses it and both settings are recorded as phases. The taxonomy has no 5-4 entry, so gd5si4_type is proposed. Neither reference covers the host, so the space groups are from materials knowledge and both mp_ids are null.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: the tetrel sublattice -- both the T-T dimer sites and the T sites inside the slabs
solid_solution_axis.note: Ge/(Ge+Si) spans 0.42-0.58 over 5 compositions, so every member sits in the middle of the series and is a genuine alloy rather than a doped end member. The Si:Ge ratio is also what sets the transition temperature and which of the three settings is stable at room temperature, so the axis has to be carried into stage 3 rather than collapsed to one parent.

basis: Every composition is GdMnO3 with either Sr on the Gd site or Cr on the Mn site. GdMnO3 is the orthorhombic GdFeO3-distorted perovskite in Pnma, the strongly tilted and orbitally ordered manganite whose cycloidal magnetic order makes it a standard multiferroic, and Gd is well inside the large-rare-earth range that gives the perovskite rather than the hexagonal RMnO3 form. [ref 2] agrees, ranking GdMnO3 Pnma mp-1189827 first on 4 ICSD references; its hull value of 0.323 is the familiar Materials Project error for Mn oxides and carries no weight against 4 references. The only competing entry, GdMn2O5, is a different stoichiometry that no composition here approaches. The misspelt GdMn0.8Cr.2O3 is the same composition as GdMn0.8Cr0.2O3.

dopant_roles.basis: GdMn0.9Cr0.1O3 and GdMn0.8Cr0.2O3, from a paper on Cr-substituted GdMnO3. Cr3+ is isovalent with Mn3+ on the octahedral B site but has no Jahn-Teller distortion and a half-filled t2g shell, so it dilutes the orbital order and changes the magnetic exchange without adding carriers.
Gd0.8Sr0.2MnO3, from a paper on Gd1-xSrxMnO3. Sr2+ on the trivalent A site converts Mn3+ to Mn4+ and is the hole-doping variable that drives the double-exchange transport these measurements probe.

basis: Six of the eight samples are PrPt4Ge12 or a substituted version of it. That compound is the filled-skutterudite structure type, Im-3, in which the corner-shared Pt4Ge12 framework of tilted octahedra encloses an icosahedral Ge12 cage with Pr at its centre -- the same topology as RFe4Sb12, with a platinum-germanium framework instead. [ref 2] carries it as Pr(Ge3Pt)4 Im-3 mp-1105939, which is PrPt4Ge12 reduced, at hull 0.022 with 1 ICSD reference. The remaining sample, Pr3Pt4Ge6, is a different compound -- an intergrowth of PrPt2Ge2 and PrGe slabs, which [ref 2] places at Pr3(Ge3Pt2)2 Pnma mp-645543 -- so the host is flagged mixed for that one composition. The papers are about the superconductivity and correlated-electron behaviour of the 1-4-12 cage compound.

dopant_roles.basis: Pr0.9Ce0.1Pt4Ge12: Ce replaces Pr on the filler site inside the Ge12 cage. The paper probes the superconductivity through exactly this substitution, since Ce brings a different 4f configuration and Kondo coupling to the guest site.
Pr0.9Eu0.1Pt4Ge12: a second rare earth on the same cage-filler site, divalent rather than trivalent, so it changes both the local moment and the electron count donated to the framework.

PrPt4Ge11.7Sb0.3: Sb replaces Ge in the Pt4Ge12 framework itself, adding one electron per substitution and shifting the Fermi level in the pnictogen-substituted analogue the first paper studies. Not a cage filler -- the cage is already occupied by Pr.

basis: The compositions are not inorganic formulas at all: P3HT, PDPP4T and PDTPT are the acronyms of conjugated organic semiconductors -- poly(3-hexylthiophene), a diketopyrrolopyrrole-quaterthiophene copolymer, and a thiophene-pyrrole donor-acceptor polymer -- and the parser has read the letters as phosphorus and hydrogen. The papers confirm it: soluble polymers with low ionization potentials, FeCl3-doped P3HT films, and unipolar performance in a bipolar polymer. I therefore reject [ref 2] entirely; PH3 mp-696588 and P3H mp-1186360 are phosphine and a computed hydride and have nothing to do with these samples. The real structural description is a semicrystalline polymer with lamellar side-chain stacking and pi-stacked backbones, which is what the organic_polymer entry covers, and the host key itself should be treated as a parsing artefact in any later cleanup.

Every composition is IrSn1.5Te1.5, that is Ir2Sn3Te3, with small In, Pd or Ru substitutions, from two papers on the synthesis, crystal structure and transport of that one compound. Sn and Te together supply the anion sublattice and pair into Sn-Te dumbbells around octahedrally coordinated Ir, which is the pyrite motif; ordering the two anion species along one body diagonal lowers cubic Pa-3 to rhombohedral R-3, and that is precisely the cell [ref 2] gives, Sn3Te3Ir2 R-3 mp-5142 at hull 0.000 on 2 ICSD references. The prototype is therefore recorded as pyrite in its ordered ternary variant. Confidence is medium rather than high because the taxonomy has no entry for the ordered variant and the assignment rests on reading the R-3 cell as a pyrite subgroup rather than on a published type assignment.

dopant_roles.basis: Ir(Sn1.5-xInx)Te1.5 at x from 0.025 to 0.1, the main doping series of the host. Trivalent In on the tetravalent Sn site removes one electron per substitution and is the p-type knob in a compound the first paper treats as a narrow-gap semiconductor.
(Ir0.975Pd0.025)Sn1.5Te1.5: Pd on the octahedral cation site, one electron fewer than Ir, so it dopes from the cation sublattice instead of the anion one.
The Ru-substituted member of the same cation-site series; Ru sits one group to the left of Ir and acts as a stronger acceptor.

basis: All four compositions are K0.3MoO3 with Tl on the alkali site or W on the Mo site, and the papers name the molybdenum blue bronze and the thallium blue bronze directly. The structure is the monoclinic C2/m bronze: slabs ten MoO6 octahedra wide sharing edges within the slab and corners between them, with the alkali layer in between, conducting along one direction only. [ref 2] supports this once the formula is reduced -- K3(MoO3)10 C2/m mp-615973 on 3 ICSD references is K0.3MoO3 -- while [ref 1] offers only K2Mo3O10, a molybdate of a different stoichiometry. The prototype was proposed from the Mo-O-Rb host in chunk 011 and applies unchanged here. The charge-density-wave transition near 180 K that the 24-299 K window crosses is a Peierls superlattice, not a change of structure type, so it is not recorded as a phase.

dopant_roles.basis: K0.24Tl0.06MoO3 and Tl0.06K0.24MoO3, which are the same composition written two ways. Tl+ replaces K+ in the alkali layer between the slabs; the paper studies it as an impurity effect on the charge-density-wave thermopower, so it perturbs pinning rather than the band filling.
K0.3Mo0.96W0.04O3: isovalent W6+ on the Mo site inside the octahedral slab, a standard way of pinning or suppressing the density wave without changing the electron count.

basis: The host is KTaO3 with parts-per-thousand to two-percent Ba on the K site. KTaO3 is the textbook cubic perovskite, Pm-3m, a quantum paraelectric whose incipient ferroelectricity is never completed, so it stays cubic all the way to 0 K and no transition is crossed in the 10-374 K window. [ref 2] ranks exactly that, KTaO3 Pm-3m mp-3614 at hull 0.000 on 7 ICSD references, well ahead of the tantalate alternatives. The first paper, on electron-doped KTaO3, is measuring transport in that cubic lattice.

dopant_roles.basis: K1-xBaxTaO3 at x from 0.0001 to 0.02. Ba2+ on the monovalent K site donates one electron per substitution, which is the electron doping named in the paper title; the extremely dilute levels are what make this a doped quantum paraelectric rather than an alloy.

basis: Five of the eight samples are La2Mo2O9 or its Sm/W co-substituted variants, and the second paper is explicitly about the alpha-beta phase transformation of that compound. La2Mo2O9 is LAMOX, the beta-SnWO4-derived framework with an intrinsically deficient and partly disordered oxygen sublattice -- cubic P2_13 above about 853 K, monoclinic P2_1 below -- and the 14-1273 K window crosses that transition, so both settings are recorded as phases. The other three samples are La2Mo2O7, a quasi-one-dimensional bronze-like compound of a different stoichiometry (the third paper is about it, and [ref 2] gives Pnnm mp-32061 on 1 ICSD reference), so the host is flagged mixed and La2Mo2O7 is parked in unresolved_crystalline rather than forced into the LAMOX entry. Neither reference carries La2Mo2O9 at all -- [ref 1] offers La2MoO6 and [ref 2] ranks La2MoO6 I4_1/acd mp-19300 first -- so mp_id stays null.

dopant_roles.basis: La2-xSmxMo2-xWxO9 at x from 0.05 to 0.20. Sm3+ is isovalent with La3+ but smaller, and the point of the co-doping paper is that it suppresses the monoclinic alpha form and holds the cubic beta phase down to room temperature -- so on these compositions the transition recorded in phases may not be crossed at all.
The other half of the same co-substitution: isovalent W6+ on the Mo site, which stabilises the cubic phase by the same mechanism and is the classic LAMOX stabiliser.

basis: All four compositions are LixTi1.03S2 with x from 0.26 to 0.97, from two papers measuring thermoelectric power as a function of lithium content in an intercalation electrode. TiS2 is the 1T CdI2-type layered sulfide, P-3m1, and lithium enters the octahedral sites of the van der Waals gap without breaking the TiS2 sheets, so the host structure is the intercalated CdI2 layer throughout the series. [ref 2] agrees, giving LiTiS2 P-3m1 mp-9615 and Li(TiS2)3 P-3m1 mp-19755 at hull 0.000 on 2 ICSD references each -- two intercalation stages of one framework, not two different structures. The Ti1.03 excess is the familiar self-intercalation of a little extra Ti into the same gap.

Both papers name chimney-ladder compounds in their titles, and the compositions say the same thing: Ru1-xMnxSiy with y tracking the valence electron count from 1.65 down towards 1.5 as Mn replaces Ru. These are Nowotny chimney-ladder phases, in which a beta-Sn-like transition-metal chimney encloses a coupled helix of silicon atoms and the Si:M ratio adjusts itself to keep 14 valence electrons per metal. I disagree with [ref 2] here: it offers only Heusler-type entries, Mn2SiRu F-43m mp-999576 and MnSiRu2 Fm-3m mp-864966, at 1:1 and 2:1 metal-to-silicon ratios that no composition in this host approaches, and the incommensurate chimney-ladder phases are simply absent from the snapshot. Stage 2 will only find approximants for this prototype, as its taxonomy note warns.

Five of the eight samples are Yb9Mn4.2Sb9 or its Zn-substituted member Yb9Mn1.2ZnSb9, which is the Ca9Zn4.5Sb9 structure type: chains of corner-shared MnSb4 tetrahedra and Sb dimers separated by Yb2+, with a partially occupied fifth metal site that is why the formula reads 4.2 rather than 4. The remaining three are YbMn2Sb2, a different Zintl phase entirely -- the CaAl2Si2 type, trigonal P-3m1, with Mn2Sb2 slabs between Yb layers -- which [ref 2] carries as Yb(MnSb)2 P-3m1 mp-4836 on 8 ICSD references. Two real structures in one host, so it is flagged mixed and splits cleanly on the Yb:Mn ratio. The papers cover both: the glass-like thermal conductivity of the 9-4-9 phase and the Zn substitution series through it.

dopant_roles.basis: Yb9Mn1.2ZnSb9 is a member of the Yb9Mn4.2-xZnxSb9 solid solution the third paper is about, and at one Zn per formula unit it is an end-member fraction rather than dilute doping; Zn2+ and Mn2+ are isovalent on the tetrahedral framework site, so it tunes the lattice thermal conductivity rather than the carrier count. It falls under 5 at.% only because the denominator is the whole 22-atom formula.

reference_disagreement: assigned sg [55], ICSD-backed references for this host report [164]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: Six of the eight samples are Nd1.6Sr1.4NiO4 with Cu on the Ni site -- the n = 1 Ruddlesden-Popper nickelate, the K2NiF4 structure of single NiO2 planes alternating with rock-salt (Nd,Sr)O bilayers -- and [ref 2] ranks tetragonal and orthorhombic SrNdNiO4 cells for the host, mp-1217981 and mp-1218010, which are that structure. The other two are Nd0.7Sr0.3NiO3, the n = infinity member: an ordinary ABO3 perovskite nickelate. One formula has a 3:4 cation-to-oxygen ratio and the other 2:3, so the two separate cleanly on composition and the host is flagged mixed. The third paper, on infinite-layer nickelates, is about a reduced form of the same family.

dopant_roles.basis: Nd1.6Sr1.4Ni1-yCuyO4 at y from 0.02 to 0.3, the substitution series of the first paper. Cu2+ replaces Ni on the square-planar-derived B site of the NiO2 plane; it is isovalent, so it changes the orbital character and the oxygen non-stoichiometry rather than the nominal carrier count.

basis: This host is deliberately two-phase. Four of the eight compositions are written as explicit composites, ((Zn0.97Ni0.03)O)x((Ni0.6Zn0.4)O)1-x, which names both constituents: lightly Ni-doped ZnO, which is wurtzite, and Zn-rich NiO, which is rocksalt. Of the rest, (Ni0.6Zn0.4)O is rocksalt and Zn0.7Ni0.3O and Zn0.837Ni0.163O sit far above the few-percent solubility limit of Ni in wurtzite ZnO, so they too will contain both phases. Rocksalt is recorded as the primary label because it is the majority constituent in every composite here, with wurtzite and composite_multiphase as the alternatives and the host flagged mixed. [ref 2] is no help: every entry it ranks is a computed Zn-Ni-O ordering at hull 0.04-0.20 with no ICSD reference, and none of them is either binary oxide.

Every composition is ZrNiPb1-zSnzBi0.02, and both papers are explicitly about n-type ZrNiPb-based half-Heuslers. ZrNiSn is the archetypal 18-electron half-Heusler, F-43m, with Zr and the main-group element on the rock-salt sublattices, Ni on one set of tetrahedral sites and the other set empty; ZrNiPb is its isostructural heavier analogue and the two form a continuous pseudobinary. The ZrNi1.01 and ZrNi1.03 compositions are the familiar excess nickel that partly fills the vacant tetrahedral site of this exact prototype and is the usual explanation for its in-gap states. Neither reference covers the host, so mp_id is null.

dopant_roles.basis: Held at 0.02 across every composition, so it is the fixed n-type dopant of the study rather than a variable: Bi on the group-14 main-group site donates one electron each and is the standard donor for ZrNiSn-type half-Heuslers.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: the main-group site of the half-Heusler, shared with the Bi dopant
solid_solution_axis.note: Pb/(Pb+Sn) spans 0.18-0.80 over 7 compositions, so this is a genuine ZrNiSn-ZrNiPb alloy series measured across its middle rather than a doped end member. The prototype is the same at both ends, so the axis matters for stage 3 and for lattice thermal conductivity, not for the structure assignment.

basis: All four compositions are PbTi1-xNbxO3 with x from 0.04 to 0.12, from one paper on the coexistence of polar distortion and metallicity. PbTiO3 is the tetragonal ferroelectric perovskite, P4mm, with a large c/a ratio driven by the Pb 6s lone pair, and [ref 1] ranks exactly that first: TiPbO3 P4mm mp-20459 at hull 0.000 on 30 ICSD references, against 10 for the cubic Pm-3m aristotype mp-19845. The cubic form is the phase above the Curie point near 763 K, well outside the 77-423 K measurement window, so no transition is crossed and the tetragonal setting holds throughout. I disregard the [ref 2] rankings for this host: they are Hf-, Te- and W-bearing computed supercells that have nothing to do with these samples.

other_polymorphs.note: The cubic Pm-3m aristotype of the same prototype, reached above the ferroelectric Curie point near 763 K. It is a real thermal phase of PbTiO3, but it lies above the 77-423 K window these samples were measured in, so it is recorded here rather than in phases.

dopant_roles.basis: PbTi1-xNbxO3 at x from 0.04 to 0.12. Nb5+ on the tetravalent Ti site of the octahedron donates one electron per substitution, and it is that electron doping that makes the sample metallic while the polar distortion survives, which is the point of the paper.

basis: The host holds three different things and cannot carry one label. PbSb2Te4 is a genuine homologous tetradymite, a (PbTe)(Sb2Te3) member built from a seven-layer block, and [ref 2] carries it as Sb2Te4Pb R-3m mp-31507; the anisotropy paper on layered PbSb2Te4 is about that structure. Pb2Sb6Te11 is not a compound at all -- the curator records it as mixed to the nominal eutectic composition of the PbTe-Sb2Te3 system, so those four samples are a two-phase eutectic of rocksalt PbTe and tetradymite Sb2Te3, which is also what the annealing paper studies. Pb0.9Sb0.1Te is simply Sb-doped rocksalt PbTe. The homologous member is recorded as the primary label since it is the only single-phase structure here, with rocksalt, tetradymite and composite_multiphase as alternatives, and the host flagged mixed. Note that [ref 2] gives both of its entries at hull 0.74-0.85, which for these layered tellurides is a hull artefact rather than a verdict.

dopant_roles.basis: PbSb2Te4.1I0.0006, which the curator writes as PbSb2Te4 with SbI3 and Te added. The iodine enters on the tellurium site as a donor -- SbI3 is the usual carrier source for these tellurides -- and at six parts in ten thousand it is a dopant, not a component.

basis: All eight samples are Ru1-xRexSiy from a single paper on ternary and Al-containing quaternary Ru1-xRexSiy, and the silicon content tracks the substitution exactly as a chimney-ladder phase requires: y falls from 1.67 at x = 0.73 to 1.565 at x = 0.14, holding the valence electron count near 14 per metal atom. These are Nowotny chimney ladders, a beta-Sn-like metal chimney enclosing a coupled silicon helix, the same family as the Ru2Si3 and higher manganese silicide end members. Neither reference covers the host, and as the prototype note warns, only approximants of an incommensurate structure will be found in stage 2.

dopant_roles.basis: The Al-containing quaternary of the paper title. Al takes silicon sites in the ladder, and having one valence electron fewer than Si it lowers the electron count per metal atom, which in a chimney-ladder phase shifts the Fermi level and the commensurate Si:M ratio rather than acting as a simple impurity.

basis: Six of the eight samples are SmSb, which is the rocksalt monoantimonide, Fm-3m -- [ref 2] gives SmSb mp-2281 at hull 0.000 on 10 ICSD references, the best-attested entry in the chemistry -- and the third paper, on quantum oscillations and Berry phase, is about that cubic semimetal. The other two are Sm4Sb3, a different structure entirely: the anti-Th3P4 type, I-43d, which [ref 2] carries at mp-367 on 3 ICSD references and which the first two papers reach through the Yb4-xSmxSb3 series. The two separate on the Sm:Sb ratio, so the host is flagged mixed rather than forced to one label.

Five of the eight samples are ZnSnSb2, the II-IV-V2 analogue of InSb, and [ref 1] gives it in the chalcopyrite setting, I-42d mp-4756, at hull 0.000 on 3 ICSD references. The first paper is titled on sphalerite-chalcopyrite polymorphism in this very compound, so the cation-disordered sphalerite form is a real alternative for part of the set rather than a database artefact -- chalcopyrite is the cation-ordered superstructure of sphalerite and the two differ only in whether Zn and Sn order. The other three compositions, Zn9Sb3Sn, Zn7Sb3Sn and Zn11Sb3Sn, come from the second paper, on single-crystalline beta-Zn4Sb3 grown from a tin flux: they are the Zn13Sb10 phase with flux tin, a wholly different structure, so the host is flagged mixed.

other_polymorphs.note: The cation-disordered form of ZnSnSb2, which the first paper reports alongside the ordered one. Whether it appears depends on the cooling rate rather than on temperature alone, so it is not a thermal phase; [ref 2] lists it at hull 0.013 with no ICSD reference.

basis: The host is one compound, TaSb2, in all 8 samples, from the paper on the constitution of the V, Nb and Ta antimonide systems. TaSb2 is the monoclinic OsGe2 type, C2/m, with pairs of edge-sharing TaSb6 octahedra and Sb-Sb bonding -- the same structure as NbSb2, for which this prototype was proposed in chunk 014 and which already names TaSb2 among its representative materials. [ref 2] agrees: TaSb2 C2/m mp-11697 at hull 0.000 on 2 ICSD references, and it lists no marcasite or other MX2 polymorph for the formula.

Both compositions are VSb2 with a slight vanadium deficiency, V0.96-0.97Sb2, from the same survey of the V, Nb and Ta antimonide systems as the Sb-Ta host. VSb2 is the CuAl2 C16 type, tetragonal I4/mcm, and [ref 2] carries exactly that at mp-2851 on 3 ICSD references -- a different structure from the OsGe2-type TaSb2 and NbSb2 at the same MX2 stoichiometry, which is the interesting result of that paper. Its hull value of 0.033 sits against 3 ICSD references and does not displace it. The vanadium deficiency is non-stoichiometry on the host metal site, not a foreign species.

All seven samples are (GeTe)1-x(AgBiTe2)x pseudobinaries with x from 0.2 to 0.5, from one paper on n-type hierarchical structures. AgBiTe2 is a rocksalt in which Ag and Bi share the cation site, and GeTe is the rhombohedrally distorted rocksalt, so the alloy is one rocksalt lattice throughout; what changes with x is whether the R3m distortion survives. At these alloying levels the cubic form is the expected average structure, and the conversion to n-type also points away from the vacancy-rich rhombohedral GeTe. The Ge-rich end, x = 0.2, may still be rhombohedral, so the host is flagged mixed with gete_rhombohedral as the alternative and left for stage 2 to split on x. [ref 2] offers only a computed ordering, AgGeBiTe3 Imm2 mp-1229030 at hull 0.147 with no ICSD reference, which is how a calculation represents a disordered cation site rather than a structure these samples adopt.

The host is one composition, Co20Ag80, measured as a film in all seven samples, and both papers describe granular Co-Ag solids and their giant magnetothermopower. Cobalt and silver are mutually insoluble in the solid state, so this is not an alloy phase at all but nanometre-scale fcc Co particles embedded in an fcc Ag matrix -- the granular structure is the reason the samples show giant magnetoresistance and magnetothermal effects in the first place. Neither reference covers the host, and none should: there is no ternary or binary compound to find. Recorded as a two-phase composite rather than as a solid solution, which the phase diagram rules out.

All four compositions are AgCrSe2 with a little silver deficiency, Ag0.90-1.0CrSe2, from two papers revisiting it as a thermoelectric and attributing its ultralow thermal conductivity to localised Ag vibrations. The structure is the CuCrS2 type: CrSe2 sheets of edge-sharing octahedra with Ag between them in tetrahedral coordination, all Ag on one side of the gap so the stacking is polar, R3m. [ref 1] gives exactly that, CrAgSe2 R3m mp-3532 at hull 0.000 on 5 ICSD references. Near 450 K the Ag sublattice disorders over both tetrahedral sets and the symmetry becomes centrosymmetric R-3m, which the 11-824 K window crosses; since the CrSe2 framework is untouched and only the guest ordering changes, both settings are recorded under the same prototype rather than as two types. That order-disorder step is also the origin of the ultralow lattice thermal conductivity the second paper measures.

All five compositions are AgIn1-xSnxO2, and the second paper names delafossite-type layered oxides AgIn1-xSnxO2 in its title. The delafossite structure puts linearly two-coordinated Ag+ dumbbells between layers of edge-sharing InO6 octahedra. [ref 2] supports it and shows only the polytype ambiguity: InAgO2 P6_3/mmc mp-20329 and R-3m mp-22660 sit at hull 0.000 and 0.001 with one ICSD reference each, which are the 2H and 3R stackings of the same delafossite layers, not different structures. Stage 2 will have to pick a polytype; the prototype does not depend on which.

dopant_roles.basis: AgIn1-xSnxO2 at x from 0.03 to 0.1, the doping series the paper is built on. Sn4+ on the trivalent In site of the octahedral layer donates one electron per substitution and is what turns an insulating delafossite into a measurable conductor.

basis: Six of the seven samples are AgxSn1-x films spanning x = 0.2 to 0.68 with no preferred stoichiometry, from a paper on quench-condensed films -- metal vapour deposited onto a cryogenic substrate, which is the standard route to a structurally disordered metal film and is why the measurements stop at 180 K. A continuous composition range with no plateau at Ag3Sn, the only stable intermetallic that [ref 2] attests (Pmmn mp-611, 3 ICSD references), is the signature of a disordered rather than a crystalline set. Confidence is low because the chunk file carries no diffraction evidence either way: if these films crystallised on warming they would be a two-phase mixture of Ag3Sn and beta-Sn, so composite_multiphase is kept as the alternative. The seventh sample belongs to a paper on BSCCO tape, where Ag and Sn are the sheath and solder rather than a sample, and is a routing artefact of this host key.

Every composition is A5Al2Sb6 with A a mixture of Ca and Yb -- Ca1.5Yb3.5Al2Sb6 and the Pr- or Sm-bearing Ca3.2-3.5Yb1.35-1.65 members -- which is the Ca5Al2Sb6 Zintl phase: infinite chains of corner-shared AlSb4 tetrahedra with Sb-Sb bonds, charge-balanced by the divalent cations and semiconducting as a result. Ca and Yb are interchangeable on that cation site, and Yb2+ is the standard substitution for Ca2+ in this family. Confidence is medium, not high, for a reason worth flagging: both papers report a thermally activated crystal-to-crystal structural transition in this system, one of them calling it a bypass transition that converts the material from p-type to n-type, and the measured window is 302-872 K, so the samples very likely pass through it. The chunk file printed no transition line and neither reference covers the host, so the product structure cannot be named from what is here; it is recorded as an unresolved polymorph and this host should go to the review queue.

other_polymorphs.note: Both linked papers report a thermally activated solid-state crystal-to-crystal transition in (Ca,Yb)5Al2Sb6 within the measured range, with a p-type to n-type conversion attached to it. The product structure is not identifiable from the chunk file, so it is recorded here rather than guessed into phases; spans_transition is left false only because no phase sequence can be written, not because the transition is doubted.

dopant_roles.basis: Ca3.30Yb1.50Sm0.20Al2Sb6. A trivalent rare earth on the divalent cation site of a charge-balanced Zintl phase donates one electron per substitution, so it is the n-type knob rather than an isovalent diluent.
Ca3.20Yb1.65Pr0.15Al2Sb6 and Ca3.46Yb1.35Pr0.19Al2Sb6: the same trivalent-on-divalent electron donation as Sm, from the same pair of papers.

basis: Six of the seven samples are CeAl2Ga2 with La or Y on the Ce site, from two papers on Kondo-lattice and antiferromagnetic behaviour in Ce1-xLaxAl2Ga2 and Ce1-yYyAl2Ga2. CeAl2Ga2 is the ThCr2Si2 body-centred tetragonal 122, I4/mmm, with Al and Ga sharing the covalently bonded X2 layers between Ce planes, and [ref 2] gives exactly that at Ce(AlGa)2 mp-3303, hull 0.000 on 3 ICSD references. The seventh composition, Ce(Ga0.9Al0.1)2, is a different stoichiometry -- CeX2, not CeX4 -- and is the AlB2-type CeGa2 with a little Al, so the host is flagged mixed and splits on the Ce:(Al+Ga) ratio.

dopant_roles.basis: Ce1-xLaxAl2Ga2 at x from 0.05 to 0.2. La3+ is trivalent like Ce3+ but has no 4f electron, so it dilutes the Kondo lattice without changing the carrier count -- that dilution is the experiment.
Ce0.95Y0.05Al2Ga2: the same non-magnetic trivalent dilution as La but with a smaller ion, so it applies chemical pressure as well, which is why the paper studies both series side by side.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: the X site of the X2 layers in the 122 framework
solid_solution_axis.note: Al/(Al+Ga) is 0.50 for the six CeAl2Ga2 samples, which is an ordered 1:1 occupancy of the X layers rather than a variable alloy composition; the 0.10 end of the range comes from the single CeGa2-type sample, which is a different structure. So the spread here is an artefact of two compounds sharing a host key, not a genuine solid-solution series, and stage 3 should treat it per composition.

basis: All four compositions are Fe2(Ti1-xCrx)Al with x from 0.3 to 0.5, and the first paper is titled on the thermoelectric properties of Fe2TiAl Heusler alloys. Fe2TiAl is the L21 full Heusler, Fm-3m: Fe on both tetrahedral sublattices, Ti and Al alternating on the octahedral ones. Cr substitutes on the Ti sublattice and stays within that ordered cubic framework -- it is the electron-count knob for the pseudogap at the Fermi level that makes these alloys thermoelectric, not a structural change. Neither reference covers the host. Fe1.99Ti0.66Cr0.45Al0.90 is the same phase written with the small off-stoichiometry a real crystal-growth run produces.

The host is Fe2TiAl and its off-stoichiometric neighbours. Fe2.18Ti0.73Al1.09 and the doubly written Fe2Ti0.86Ti0.22Al0.92 are that compound directly, and the (Fe1-xTix)3Al series at x = 0.15 to 0.30 reduces to Fe2.55Ti0.45Al through Fe2.10Ti0.90Al, which brackets it. [ref 2] confirms the structure at TiAlFe2 Fm-3m mp-31187, hull 0.000. The Ti-poor end of the series approaches D03 Fe3Al, but D03 and L21 are the same bcc superlattice -- L21 is what D03 becomes when one of its two distinct iron sublattices is replaced by titanium -- so the whole series sits inside this prototype rather than straddling two. The papers, on off-stoichiometry and Ti doping and on flat-band effects, are about tuning the pseudogap within that one framework.

other_polymorphs.note: [ref 2] ranks Ti2AlFe F-43m mp-999069 first on 2 ICSD references, but at hull 0.178 and at a 2:1:1 titanium-rich stoichiometry that no composition in this host approaches. It is recorded here rather than allowed to override the L21 assignment.

basis: All six compositions are Sr8Al6-8Ga8-11Ge28-30, that is Sr8(Al,Ga)16Ge30, and the single paper is titled on the synthesis and thermoelectric properties of type-VIII germanium clathrates. Type VIII is the I-43m clathrate: one kind of distorted dodecahedral cage rather than the two cage types of type I, with every guest in an equivalent site. The composition is exactly charge-balanced -- 8 Sr2+ donating 16 electrons to 16 trivalent framework sites -- which is what both clathrate types demand, so the composition alone cannot separate them; the paper does. Sr8Ga16Ge30 alone is normally the type-I form, and the aluminium is what carries this set into type VIII, which is why the host is filed here with clathrate_i as the alternative. Neither reference covers the host, so mp_id is null.

The host is one composition, LaAlO3, in all seven samples, three of them thin films and the rest substrates or targets in papers about other oxides grown on them. LaAlO3 is a perovskite, and the only question is the setting. I disagree with the [ref 1] ranking: it puts LaAlO3 Pm-3m mp-5304 first on 69 ICSD references, but the cubic aristotype is the phase above about 813 K, and at every temperature in the 10-356 K window the compound is the rhombohedral R-3c form with antiphase-tilted AlO6 octahedra, which is mp-2920 at hull 0.000 on 33 references. The large cubic reference count reflects how often the idealised setting is quoted, not what is present at room temperature. The prototype is the same either way, so this changes the space group stage 2 should take, not the assignment.

other_polymorphs.note: The cubic Pm-3m form of the same prototype, reached above about 813 K. A real thermal phase, but far above the measured window here, so it is kept out of phases. It is also the setting [ref 1] ranks first, which is why the disagreement is recorded explicitly.

basis: All seven compositions are YMn4+xAl8-x, the series named in the single paper, running from YMn2Al10 to YMn6.5Al5.5. Every one of them sums to twelve framework atoms per yttrium, which is the defining count of the ThMn12 type: body-centred tetragonal I4/mmm with the transition metal and aluminium distributed over the three crystallographically distinct 8f, 8i and 8j sites, and the rare earth alone on the 2a site. [ref 2] agrees, ranking Y(MnAl2)4 I4/mmm mp-10896 first at hull 0.000 on 2 ICSD references; reduced, that formula is YMn4Al8, the centre of the series. The prototype was proposed from the Al-Ce-Cu host in chunk 011 and this is the recurrence it predicted.

Every composition is CeNi2(As1-xPx)2 with x from 0.2 to 0.8, from one paper on heavy-fermion quantum criticality in CeNi2-d(As,P)2. Both end members, CeNi2As2 and CeNi2P2, are ThCr2Si2-type: body-centred tetragonal I4/mmm, with NiPn4 tetrahedral layers separated by cerium planes and a pnictogen-pnictogen bond across the layer whose length collapses as the cell contracts. That collapse is precisely why the series is studied -- substituting the smaller phosphorus for arsenic applies chemical pressure and tunes the Kondo coupling -- and the prototype is the same at both ends. Neither reference covers the host, so mp_id is null. The nickel deficiency in the paper title is a carrier-count knob on the transition-metal site, not a second phase.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: the pnictogen site of the NiPn4 tetrahedral layer, including the interlayer Pn-Pn bond
solid_solution_axis.note: As/(As+P) spans 0.20-0.80 over all 7 compositions, every one of them a genuine alloy in the middle of the series rather than a doped end member. Both ends are the same prototype, so the axis is a chemical-pressure variable for stage 3 rather than a structure question.

basis: Every composition is La1-xSrxMnAsO with x from 0 to 0.1, from papers on the insulator-to-metal transition in that compound and on impurity doping in the La-1111 system. LaMnAsO is the ZrCuSiAs 1111 structure, tetragonal P4/nmm: alternating La2O2 fluorite-like sheets and edge-sharing MnAs4 tetrahedral layers, the same framework as LaFeAsO and LaZnAsO. Neither reference covers the host, so mp_id is left null; the assignment rests on the composition and on the 1111 naming in the second paper title.

dopant_roles.basis: La1-xSrxMnAsO at x from 0.02 to 0.1. Sr2+ on the trivalent La site of the La2O2 layer donates holes into the MnAs layer, and it is that hole doping which drives the insulator-to-metal transition and the large thermoelectric effect the first paper reports.

The impurity-doping study of the second paper substitutes on the transition-metal site of the tetrahedral layer; Fe is isovalent with Mn2+ there, so it perturbs the magnetism rather than the carrier count.

basis: The host is one compound, CeAu2Si2, in all seven single-crystal samples, from a paper on the scaling of its temperature-dependent thermopower. CeAu2Si2 is a ThCr2Si2-type 122, body-centred tetragonal I4/mmm, with AuSi4 tetrahedral layers between cerium planes -- a standard Kondo-lattice member of that family. [ref 2] confirms it: Ce(SiAu)2 I4/mmm mp-5173 at hull 0.000 on 5 ICSD references, well ahead of the two alternatives it lists.

Every composition is written as a mixture and the paper is about the effect of SiC and graphene additions on the mechanical properties and oxidation of NbB2 ceramics: (NbB2)75(SiC)25 and its carbon-bearing variants are hot-pressed two- and three-phase ceramics, not a quaternary compound. The constituents are individually well defined -- NbB2 is the AlB2 type, P6/mmm, with graphite-like boron nets between niobium layers, and SiC is a tetrahedral polytype, with free carbon as the third phase where the composition lists it separately -- so the host is recorded as a composite with both constituent prototypes as alternatives and flagged mixed. Neither reference covers the host, and a single mp_id would be wrong here in principle.

The composition is recorded as B1.6Pb0.4Sr2Ca2Cu3O10, but that is bismuth, not boron: Bi1.6Pb0.4Sr2Ca2Cu3O10 is the Pb-doped Bi-2223 cuprate, and every detail here matches it -- the exact stoichiometry, the epitaxial thick film, and a measured window of 52-114 K bracketing the 110 K transition of that phase. Boron does not form a 2223 cuprate and could not sit in the rock-salt double layer this formula requires. The structure is therefore the Bi-2223 member of the BSCCO family: two BiO rock-salt layers alternating with a three-CuO2-plane block separated by calcium. [ref 2] offers only Sr2CaCu6(BO3)6, a genuine borate, which is what a literal reading of the element list produces and is not this material. The host key should be corrected from B to Bi in any later cleanup.

dopant_roles.basis: Held at 0.4 per formula unit in the only composition of the host. Pb2+ on the Bi site of the rock-salt layer is the standard additive that stabilises the 2223 phase against the 2212 one during sintering, and it also alters the hole count in the CuO2 planes as a side effect. The element is recorded against Bi despite the host key reading B, for the reason given in the basis.

basis: Five of the seven samples are boron oxide glass or melt: three of plain B2O3, from papers on the thermal conductivity of molten B2O3 and of B2O3 glass under pressure, and two alkali borate glasses, (Li2O)10(B2O3)90 and (K2O)10(B2O3)90. B2O3 is one of the classic network glass formers and is measured here in exactly that state, so although [ref 2] ranks crystalline B2O3 P3_121 mp-306 first on 9 ICSD references, the crystal is not what these samples are -- a case where the reference describes the chemistry and not the specimen. The other two samples are B6O, boron suboxide, from a paper on hot-pressed B6O: a crystalline rhombohedral R-3m solid of B12 icosahedra with oxygen in the interstitial chain sites, the same family as boron carbide, which [ref 2] gives at mp-1346 on 6 ICSD references. Two unrelated states of matter in one host, so it is flagged mixed and splits on the B:O ratio.

dopant_roles.basis: (Li2O)10(B2O3)90: at 10 mol% Li2O this is a lithium borate glass composition, not a doped one. The alkali oxide is a network modifier -- it converts trigonal BO3 units into tetrahedral BO4 and creates non-bridging oxygens -- so it is a genuine component of the glass rather than a dilute substituent on any site.
(K2O)10(B2O3)90: the same network-modifier role as Li2O, with a larger cation, in the companion glass of the same study.

basis: Four of the seven samples are TiB2 itself, which [ref 2] attests strongly: P6/mmm mp-1145 at hull 0.000 on 16 ICSD references, the AlB2 structure of graphite-like boron sheets alternating with titanium layers. The other three are written as composites -- (Ti)93.12(TiB2)6.88 and (Ti)85.74(TiB2)14.26 are titanium-matrix particulate composites from a paper on Ti-SiC and Ti-TiB2 composites, and (TiB2)88.02(SiC)11.98 is a TiB2-SiC ceramic -- so the host is flagged mixed, with TiB2 as the label and composite_multiphase as the alternative for those three. In all of them the diboride particles themselves are the same AlB2 phase.

dopant_roles.basis: Silicon appears only through (TiB2)88.02(SiC)11.98, where it belongs to a deliberately added silicon carbide second phase. It does not enter the diboride lattice, so it is not a dopant in any structural sense.
The other half of the same SiC addition, together with the graphene nanoplatelets the third paper adds. Carbon is a separate phase here, not a substituent on the boron site.

basis: All six compositions are Bi1.8Ba2Rh1.9O8 and its substituted members, and the third paper writes the formula in the form that settles it: [Bi2Ba2O4]p(Co,Rh)O2. This is the misfit layered structure of the Bi-Sr-Co-O family with rhodium in place of cobalt -- a rock-salt-type Bi2Ba2O4 block interleaved with CdI2-type RhO2 sheets, the two subsystems having incommensurate in-plane periods, which is why the nominal cation ratios come out non-integral at 1.8 and 1.9. The prototype note already flags that such a composite has no single Materials Project entry, and indeed neither reference covers the host. The RhO2 layer rather than a CoO2 layer is a substitution within the prototype, not a different type.

dopant_roles.basis: (Bi1-xPbx)1.8Ba2Rh1.9O8 at x of 0.1 and 0.2, which the curator confirms as the series formula. Pb2+ on the trivalent Bi site of the rock-salt block dopes holes into the conducting RhO2 sheet without touching that sheet directly -- the standard way this family is doped.
Bi1.7Ba2(Co0.2Rh0.8)2O8: cobalt on the rhodium site of the CdI2-type layer, isovalent and the parent element of the family, so this composition interpolates between the cobaltite and the rhodate.

basis: The host is one compound at six oxygen contents, CaLaBaCu3Oy with y from 6.71 to 6.89, from a single paper measuring thermoelectric power across that range. Cu3O6+d with three distinct large cations is the 123 structure: the CaLaBaCu3O7 cuprate is the well-known cation-ordered variant of YBa2Cu3O7 in which La and Ba replace the two barium sites and calcium takes the yttrium site between the CuO2 planes. The oxygen content is the doping variable of the 123 family rather than a stoichiometry error, which is exactly what varying y from 6.71 to 6.89 is doing here. [ref 2] offers only computed Ba3CaLa2Cu6O13-type orderings at hull 0.03 with no ICSD references, which neither confirms nor contradicts the assignment.

Every composition is LuBaCo4O7 with a little Pb on the lutetium site, and the first paper covers the whole BaRCo4O7 series. That formula is the swedenborgite structure, hexagonal P6_3mc: alternating kagome and triangular layers of corner-sharing CoO4 tetrahedra, with Ba and the rare earth between them -- a geometrically frustrated cobaltite built from tetrahedra rather than the octahedra of a perovskite cobaltite. [ref 2] ranks exactly that first, BaLuCo4O7 P6_3mc mp-19624 on 2 ICSD references; the Pna2_1 and Cc entries it also lists at one reference each are the orthorhombic and monoclinic distortions this family undergoes on cooling below room temperature, which is well below the 306-983 K window measured here.

other_polymorphs.note: The Pna2_1 distortion of the same prototype, which [ref 2] lists at hull 0.003 on 1 ICSD reference alongside a Cc setting at mp-1193997. These are low-temperature symmetry lowerings of the hexagonal parent, below the 306-983 K window of these samples, so they are recorded here rather than in phases.

dopant_roles.basis: Lu1-xPbxBaCo4O7 at x from 0.02 to 0.1, the hole-doping series named in the second paper. Pb2+ on the trivalent Lu site oxidises the cobalt tetrahedral layers, which is how carriers are put into an otherwise poorly conducting frustrated cobaltite.

basis: K8Ba16Ga40Sn96 is the type-II clathrate formula read off exactly: 24 guest cations, K8 plus Ba16, inside a 136-atom framework, Ga40Sn96, which is the A24E136 archetype of this entry. The second paper names the type outright (off-center rattling in a type-II clathrate) and the other four compositions are the same phase with the K:Ba ratio and the Ga:Sn framework balance moved by a few percent. The alternative in the same chemistry would be the type-I phase, which reads A8E46 and is what the neighbouring Ba-Ga-Sn host holds; the 24:136 ratio here rules it out. Potassium fills the large hexakaidecahedral cages and barium the small dodecahedral ones, and Ga substitutes into the Sn framework to set the electron count. Neither reference covers this host, so the assignment rests on the stoichiometry and on the paper titles.

Six of the seven samples are BaSi2 or La-doped BaSi2, from papers on the thermoelectric properties of BaSi2 and of La-doped BaSi2. That is the orthorhombic Pnma Zintl phase of isolated (Si4)4- tetrahedra, which [ref 1] backs as the primary entry for the formula: Pnma (62) mp-1477 at hull 0.000 on 9 ICSD references, against the cubic P4_332 SrSi2-type polymorph mp-7275 at 2 references. The taxonomy had only srsi2_chiral for this chemistry, so the orthorhombic type is proposed here. The seventh sample is Ba8Ni2.6Si43.4, where 2.6 plus 43.4 makes the 46-atom framework of a type-I clathrate with eight barium guests, a genuinely different structure in the same host, so the host is flagged mixed and splits on the Si:Ba ratio.

other_polymorphs.note: The cubic P4_332 SrSi2-type polymorph of BaSi2, which [ref 1] lists at hull 0.014 on 2 ICSD references. It is obtained by high-pressure synthesis and quenching rather than by heating the orthorhombic form, so it is not part of the thermal sequence of these samples.

dopant_roles.basis: Ba1-xLaxSi2 at x of 0.02, 0.04 and 0.08, the series of the paper titled Thermoelectric Properties of La-Doped BaSi2. Trivalent La on the divalent Ba site is a donor and is how this Zintl semiconductor is made n-type.

Ba8Ni2.6Si43.4: nickel replaces silicon in the clathrate cage framework, not in the BaSi2 phase, and sets the electron count of that framework in the way Ga or Al does in Ba8Ga16Ge30. It is a host constituent of the clathrate composition rather than a dopant on the majority phase.

basis: All seven samples are TiBe12, from a paper on beryllides for fusion reactors. The MBe12 beryllides -- TiBe12, NbBe12, TaBe12, MoBe12 -- crystallise in the tetragonal ThMn12 type, I4/mmm, and [ref 2] gives exactly that cell for this composition: TiBe12 I4/mmm (139) mp-1104067 at hull 0.001. The reference ranks TiBe2 Fd-3m mp-912109 first on 6 ICSD references, but that is the cubic Laves phase of a different stoichiometry, not this compound -- an instance of the ranking describing the chemistry rather than the composition measured. The single ICSD reference behind the TiBe12 entry is weak by the chunk convention, so the assignment leans on the structure-type literature for the MBe12 family as much as on the reference.

other_polymorphs.note: TiBe2, the cubic Laves phase that [ref 2] ranks first for the Be-Ti chemistry on 6 ICSD references. It is a different compound rather than a polymorph of TiBe12 and no sample in this host has its composition; recorded here so the reference disagreement is not lost.

basis: Every composition is A Mg2Bi2 with A a mixture of Ca and Yb, and the first paper names the family: Bi-based Zintl compounds Ca1-xYbxMg2Bi2. That 1-2-2 stoichiometry with a divalent A cation is the CaAl2Si2 type, trigonal P-3m1, in which Mg and Bi build corrugated anionic MgBi4 tetrahedral layers and the A cation sits between them -- the same structure the neighbouring Bi-Mg-Yb host resolves to, where [ref 2] confirms Yb(MgBi)2 P-3m1 mp-1068042. Neither reference covers this quaternary host directly. The Bi1.98 and Bi1.99 stoichiometries are deliberate anion deficiency, the carrier-concentration knob of the second paper, not a different phase.

dopant_roles.basis: Ca0.75Yb0.25Mg1.9Zn0.1Bi1.98 and its Ca0.65Yb0.35 counterpart. Zn2+ takes the tetrahedral Mg site of the anionic layer, where it is isovalent and acts on the band structure and the lattice thermal conductivity rather than on the carrier count; the carriers in those samples come from the Bi deficiency instead.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: A cation site (the 1a position between the anionic MgBi4 layers)
solid_solution_axis.note: Recorded against the chunk file, which reports the axis as Ca/(Ca+Mg) spanning 0.13-0.28 because Ca and Mg are both group 2. That pairing is wrong structurally: in the CaAl2Si2 type Mg occupies the tetrahedral site of the anionic layer and never shares a site with Ca, whereas Yb2+ and Ca2+ have nearly the same radius and are interchangeable on the A site, which is the substitution both papers actually perform. x is Ca/(Ca+Yb) over the compositions listed, running from Ca0.3Yb0.7 to Ca0.75Yb0.25, i.e. the middle of the series where neither end member is dilute.

basis: Both compositions are Bi2Sr2(Ca,Y)Cu2O8, which is the Bi-2212 member of the BSCCO family: two BiO rock-salt layers alternating with a block of two CuO2 planes separated by the small eight-coordinate cation. The papers are the classic Bi2Sr2Ca1-xYxCu2O8+y thermopower series, measured here at x of 0.8 and 1.0, and the 30-310 K window is the low-temperature transport range that work uses. [ref 2] offers only Sr2YCu2(BiO4)2 in Cccm mp-1208863 and I4/mmm mp-1208753 at hulls of 0.089 and 0.123 with no ICSD references at all: computed orderings of the element set, not the 2212 intergrowth, so they neither confirm nor contradict the assignment and should not be used to pick a cell in stage 2.

dopant_roles.basis: Bi2Sr2Ca0.2Y0.8Cu2O8. Calcium is the parent occupant of this site in Bi-2212 and yttrium is the substituent, so the composition is better read as Y-rich Bi-2212 with a fifth of that site still calcium. The Ca:Y ratio is the hole-count variable of the family -- trivalent Y for divalent Ca removes holes from the CuO2 planes, which is what drives the thermopower changes both papers report -- so this element is the doping axis rather than an impurity.

basis: The matrix in every composition is (Bi,Sb)2Te3 at or near the Bi0.5Sb1.5Te3 workhorse ratio, so the host structure is the rhombohedral tetradymite of quintuple Te-Bi-Te-Bi-Te layers. What varies is the copper. Two compositions are written as explicit pseudobinaries, (Cu4Te3)x(Bi0.5Sb1.5Te3)1-x at x of 0.1 and 0.2, from a paper on exactly that pseudobinary, and a third paper adds Cu7Te4 nanorods: in those the copper telluride is a deliberate second phase and the sample is a composite rather than a single structure. In Cu0.4Bi0.5Sb1.1Te3 and its neighbours the copper is more plausibly taken up by the tetradymite itself, in the van der Waals gap or on the cation site. The host is therefore flagged mixed, with the tetradymite matrix as the label and composite_multiphase for the pseudobinary and nanorod samples. Neither reference covers the host.

Every composition is K2Bi8-xSbxSe13, which the second paper names as the series. K2Bi8Se13 is the exemplar of this prototype: a module-built complex bismuth chalcogenide in which NaCl-type and Bi2Te3-type blocks assemble into a large low-symmetry cell, with potassium in its own site and a mixed Bi/K position that is the source of the structural inhomogeneity the first paper studies. Antimony substitutes for bismuth across the whole range and drives the n-to-p crossover of the second paper title. Neither reference covers the host, and by the prototype note each composition is effectively its own structure, so the cell has to be resolved per composition in stage 2 rather than from a single entry.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: the trivalent pnictogen sites of the module framework
solid_solution_axis.note: Bi/(Bi+Sb) runs from 0.15 to 0.80 across the six compositions, so both end members are reached and neither is a dilute substituent. Sb3+ and Bi3+ are isovalent, but the substitution is not transport-neutral here: it moves the material from n-type to p-type, which the second paper attributes to which of the several inequivalent metal sites the antimony prefers. That makes the site distribution, not just the fraction, a stage 2 question.

basis: Four of the seven samples are YbMg2Bi2 and the rest are Sb-substituted or Bi-deficient versions of it, from papers on the Zintl phase YbMg2Bi2 and on CaMg2Bi2, EuMg2Bi2 and YbMg2Bi2 together. [ref 2] gives the structure directly: Yb(MgBi)2 P-3m1 (164) mp-1068042 at hull 0.000, which is the trigonal CaAl2Si2 type of anionic MgBi4 tetrahedral layers separated by the divalent A cation. Its two ICSD references make it a weak primary by the chunk convention, but it is the only entry offered and it agrees with the structure reported across the whole AMg2Bi2 family.

dopant_roles.basis: YbMg2Bi1.88Sb0.1 and YbMg2Bi1.78Sb0.2. Sb and Bi are both group 15 and share the anion site of the MgBi4 layers, so the substitution adds no carriers; it works on the band gap and on point-defect phonon scattering. Note that these compositions are also Bi and Sb deficient overall -- 1.98 against 2 -- so the carrier count in them comes from that vacancy, not from the antimony.

basis: The host splits between two structures of the same chemistry. Bi2Ru2O7 and Bi1.5Y0.5Ru2O7, four of the seven samples, are the cubic pyrochlore A2B2O7, which [ref 2] attests well at Fd-3m (227) mp-23445, hull 0.000, 6 ICSD references, and the third paper is explicitly about controlling oxygen vacancies in the defect pyrochlore. The other three samples are Bi3Ru3O11, an A3B3O11 compound of the KSbO3 family built from edge-sharing Ru2O10 octahedral dimers in cubic Pn-3 -- a different framework, not a pyrochlore, and metallic where the pyrochlore is at best a poor metal. No taxonomy entry existed for it, so ksbo3_bi3ru3o11 is proposed in this chunk and carried in alt_prototype_ids; the host must split on the Bi:Ru:O ratio, A2B2O7 against A3B3O11. The first paper listed for this host is about CuO-added AgSbO3 ceramics and contains no Bi or Ru, so it appears to be a linkage artefact and was not used.

dopant_roles.basis: Bi1.5Y0.5Ru2O7: yttrium on the eight-coordinate A site of the pyrochlore. Y3+ and Bi3+ are both trivalent so this adds no carriers, but replacing the 6s2 lone-pair cation with a simple trivalent one withdraws Bi 6s character from the states at the Fermi level, which is how this family is tuned between metallic and semiconducting behaviour.

basis: The three compositions are PbBi2S4, Pb3Bi2S6 and a Cl-doped member, and the third paper names the family: the PbmBi2S3+m homologous series. These are lead-bismuth sulfosalts built from NaCl-like slabs of variable width bounded by differently coordinated lead, which is exactly what this prototype covers -- its notes already list Pb5Bi6Se14 as a member and Bi-Pb-Se as an example host. [ref 1] supports both members individually: Bi2PbS4 Pnma (62) mp-641924 at hull 0.002 on 16 ICSD references, which is galenobismutite, and Bi2(PbS2)3 C2/m (12) mp-629690 at hull 0.000 for the Pb3Bi2S6 member. Those are genuinely different structures, so although one prototype id covers the host, the cell must be taken per composition in stage 2; that is the prototype convention rather than a mixed host.

dopant_roles.basis: Pb0.9Cl0.1Bi2S3. A halide on the sulfur site is the standard donor in lead and bismuth sulfides, contributing one extra electron per substitution, and the second paper is about enhancing this earth-abundant sulfide by exactly that route. It is recorded against the anion site rather than as a lead-site species despite where the parser placed it in the string.

reference_disagreement: assigned sg [11], ICSD-backed references for this host report [62, 12, 63]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: The two compositions are GeC0.12 and GeC0.06 from one paper on nanocomposite thermoelectric materials, and the curator records the composition as GeC0.06. Read as a compound this would be germanium carbide, and that is where both references point, but GeC does not exist as an equilibrium bulk phase: [ref 1] puts GeC F-43m mp-1002164 at hull 0.436 and [ref 2] puts the rocksalt and wurtzite variants at 1.271 and 0.441, which are computed zincblende-type structures several hundred meV per atom above the hull. A carbide that far above the hull is not what a hot-pressed sample contains. The physically consistent reading of six to eleven atomic percent carbon in germanium, in a paper about nanocomposites, is diamond-cubic germanium with carbon present as a dispersed second phase, since carbon is essentially insoluble in Ge. The host is therefore assigned to the germanium matrix and flagged mixed, and this is one of the cases where the references are recorded as disagreeing rather than followed.

other_polymorphs.note: Zincblende GeC, the entry [ref 1] offers for this formula, at hull 0.436 on a single ICSD reference. Recorded here rather than as the assignment: it is a computed structure far above the hull, and cubic GeC is only ever reported as a strained epitaxial or ion-beam-synthesised film, never as a bulk phase reachable by heating.

basis: This host is four unrelated molecular solids that share an element set. Four samples are guanidinium metal formates, [C(NH2)3]Cu(HCOO)3 and [C(NH2)3]Zn(HCOO)3, from the paper on anisotropic heat conduction in metal-organic framework perovskites: an ABX3 framework in which formate anions bridge the octahedral metal, topologically a perovskite with a three-atom linker in place of the oxide ion. No taxonomy entry covered that, so formate_mof_perovskite is proposed here. Two samples are Ni(C3H10N2)2NO2ClO4, the Haldane-chain compound NENP, measured along and across the spin-chain direction as the curator notes record -- a one-dimensional nickel coordination polymer, not a framework perovskite, and it is parked in unresolved_crystalline. The seventh is C6H7N(CH3COO)0.5, which the curator identifies outright as polyaniline, CAS 25233-30-1, so it belongs to organic_polymer. [ref 2] is no help at all here: it ranks urea, H4CN2O mp-23778, and other small molecular solids of the same four elements. The host must be split per composition.

dopant_roles.basis: The octahedral B-site metal of [C(NH2)3]Cu(HCOO)3, which is a host constituent and not a dopant -- it falls under 5 at.% only because hydrogen and carbon dominate the atom count in a metal-organic formula. Copper and zinc are the interchangeable B cations of this family, and the copper member is the Jahn-Teller distorted one whose anisotropic thermal conductivity the paper measures.
As Cu: the B-site metal of [C(NH2)3]Zn(HCOO)3, the undistorted member of the same pair.

The chain metal of Ni(C3H10N2)2NO2ClO4 (NENP), where it carries the S = 1 spins whose magnetic heat transport the third paper reports. Again a host constituent of its own composition rather than a dopant on any other.

Chlorine appears only as the perchlorate counter-anion of NENP, ClO4-, which balances the charge of the nickel chain and sits in the lattice between chains. It is neither a dopant nor a contaminant, and the role vocabulary has no term for a genuine host constituent that the 5 at.% cut pushed below the threshold, so it is recorded as unknown with this note rather than forced into a wrong category.

basis: Every composition is TaC with at most about one atomic percent tungsten, written in the composite notation (W)x(TaC)100-x. Tantalum carbide is the rocksalt interstitial carbide and [ref 2] attests it as strongly as anything in this chunk: TaC Fm-3m (225) mp-1086 at hull 0.000 on 37 ICSD references. The other entries it lists, Ta2C and Ta3C2 in P-3m1 and the computed Ta3C and Ta4C3, are the lower carbides of the same system at different C:Ta ratios and no sample here has their stoichiometry. The papers are on densification and on hot rolling of TaC-based solid solutions, so the tungsten is a sintering and solid-solution addition to the carbide rather than a separate phase.

dopant_roles.basis: Held between 0.21 and 1.05 percent across the five compositions. Tungsten dissolves on the metal site of the rocksalt carbide -- TaC and WC-derived carbides form extensive solid solutions -- and at this level it is a grain-growth and densification control in the first paper rather than a carrier-count dopant. The composite notation of the composition string should not be read as a second phase.

basis: All six compositions are ThCx with x from 0.787 to 0.91, and the first paper is titled Electrical Properties of Nonstoichiometric Thorium Carbides. That is monocarbide ThC with carbon vacancies, the rocksalt interstitial carbide, which [ref 2] gives as ThC Fm-3m (225) mp-1164 at hull 0.000 on 12 ICSD references. The carbon deficiency is the point of the samples rather than an impurity or a stoichiometry error: the vacancy concentration is what the resistivity and thermopower are being measured against, exactly as the prototype notes describe for TaN0.89. The dicarbide ThC2, which [ref 2] also lists at C2/c mp-7224, is a different structure but no composition here approaches its C:Th ratio.

Elemental calcium, one composition and one paper on the electrical resistivity and thermoelectric power of Ca and Sr above room temperature. Calcium is face-centred cubic at ambient conditions -- [ref 2] gives Ca Fm-3m (225) mp-45 at hull 0.000 on 12 ICSD references -- and transforms to body-centred cubic at about 716 K, which the 311-848 K measured window crosses. That is exactly what a paper measuring Ca above room temperature is looking at, so both phases are recorded rather than one label. The reference corroborates the second phase without meaning to: its Im-3m entry mp-21 carries 14 ICSD references, more than the fcc ground state, which is what a genuinely accessible high-temperature polymorph looks like in an ICSD count. Both phases fall under this prototype, whose display name already spans A1 and A2.

other_polymorphs.note: [ref 2] also lists Ca in I4/mmm (8 ICSD references), I4/mcm mp-1008498 (6) and Cmcm mp-1064227 (3). Calcium has a well-populated high-pressure sequence beyond bcc, and these cells belong to it rather than to the ambient-pressure thermal sequence, so none of them is reached in a resistivity measurement at one atmosphere. They have no taxonomy entry of their own.

basis: Five of the six compositions are written in the misfit notation by the curator directly, as [Ca2-xPrx(Co,Cu)O4][CoO2]1.60, and the second paper is on the double modulation and microstructure of the thermoelectric misfit compound. That is the Ca3Co4O9 family: a rock-salt-type [Ca2CoO3] block interleaved with CdI2-type CoO2 sheets whose in-plane periods are incommensurate, which is why the block ratio comes out at the irrational 1.60 and why the nominal formula is also writable as Ca3Co4O9. The sixth composition, Ca3Co3.2Cu0.8O9, is the same phase in the collapsed notation. Copper substitutes into the rock-salt block rather than forming a separate phase, which is the subject of the first paper. Neither reference covers the host, and by the prototype note this composite has no single Materials Project entry.

dopant_roles.basis: Ca2-xPrx at x from 0.07 to 0.30 in four compositions, with the curator confirming the bracketed formula. Trivalent Pr on the divalent Ca site of the rock-salt block donates electrons and so reduces the hole count of the conducting CoO2 sheet without entering that sheet -- the standard way this family is doped, and the enhanced electronic correlation the first paper reports.

basis: Six of the seven samples are Ca3(Co,Mn)2O6 -- Ca3CoMnO6 and Ca3Co1.25Mn0.75O6 -- from papers on Ca3Co2-xMnxO6. That A3B2O6 stoichiometry is the K4CdCl6-derived chain compound of this prototype: infinite one-dimensional chains of alternating face-sharing octahedra and trigonal prisms, with Ca between them. In the ordered Ca3CoMnO6 member the Mn takes the octahedral site and the Co the trigonal-prismatic one, which is what makes it the multiferroic Ising chain it is known as. [ref 2] agrees on the compound and gives Ca3MnCoO6 R-3c (167) mp-704674, a rhombohedral setting of that chain structure, though on a single ICSD reference at hull 0.054. The seventh sample is Ca3Mn0.9Co3.1O9, an A3B4O9 composition, which is the misfit cobaltite instead -- a different structure of the same three metals -- so the host is flagged mixed and splits on the (Co+Mn):Ca ratio, 2:3 against 4:3.

The host is the Ca3Co4O9 misfit cobaltite with strontium substituted for calcium, plus two hexagonal cobaltites that are not that structure. Ca2SrCo4O9 and (Ca0.7Sr0.3)3Co4O9 are A3Co4O9, the misfit composition, and the second paper is on the effect of substituting Sr for Ca in Ca3Co4O9; Sr1.9Ca1.2Y0.9Co4O10.5 has four large cations to four cobalt and is best read as the same misfit with a Y-substituted rock-salt block, which is what the curator formula Ca3-xSrxCo4O9+d describes. Against that, (Sr0.7Ca0.3)4Co3O9 and (Sr0.53Ca0.45)5Co4O12 sit at A:Co ratios of 1.33 and 1.25, which belong to the one-dimensional face-sharing hexagonal cobaltite series that runs through Sr6Co5O15 to Ca3Co2O6 rather than to a misfit intergrowth -- and the third paper is precisely a phase-compatibility study of the Sr-Ca-Co-O system, so several phases in one host is expected here. Both alternatives are carried and the host splits on the A:Co ratio. [ref 2] offers only computed Sr-Ca-Co-Cu-O orderings with no ICSD references and does not settle anything.

dopant_roles.basis: Sr1.9Ca1.2Y0.9Co4O10.5, two samples. Yttrium is trivalent on a divalent alkaline-earth site in the rock-salt block, so it donates electrons into the CoO2 sheet and lowers the hole count, the same role Pr plays in the Ca-Co-Cu-O host. The unusually high oxygen content of 10.5 goes with that extra cation charge rather than being an independent variable.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: the alkaline-earth site of the rock-salt block
solid_solution_axis.note: Ca/(Ca+Sr) spans 0.30-0.70 over the five compositions, so this is a genuine alloy on the A site rather than dilute substitution at either end. Ca2+ and Sr2+ are isovalent, but the substitution is not transport-neutral: the larger Sr changes the misfit ratio between the two subsystems and eventually stabilises a different structure type altogether, which is why two of the compositions here are hexagonal cobaltites rather than misfits. The transition in structure along the axis means no single parent can be named for the host.

basis: Every composition is (La,Ca)(Fe,Cr)O3 -- five of them at La0.3Ca0.7Fe0.7Cr0.3O3 with small A-site deficiencies of 0.96 to 0.99, and one at La0.75Ca0.25Cr0.75Fe0.25O3. An ABO3 oxide with two trivalent-to-divalent A cations and two octahedral B cations is the perovskite aristotype, orthorhombically distorted at these tolerance factors, and the papers confirm the use: cathodes for solid oxide fuel cells and a study of the Cr4+ content and electrical conductivity of La0.75Ca0.25Cr1-yFeyO3. Neither reference covers this five-element host. The A-site deficiency and the oxygen nonstoichiometry written as O3-d in the second paper are the carrier-count variables of the family, not evidence of another phase; the Ca content is far too high, at 0.7 of the A site, for Ca to be read as a dopant.

All seven compositions are (Sr,Ca)TiO3 with a donor on one site or the other, and the papers name it: the electron-doped perovskites Sr1-xCaxTiO3 and the (Sr1-x-yCaxNdy)TiO3 series. SrTiO3 is the cubic perovskite and CaTiO3 the orthorhombic Pnma one, so the solid solution is perovskite throughout with the octahedral tilting increasing as Ca replaces Sr; at the Ca fractions here, 0.25 to 0.67, the room-temperature structure is already tilted rather than cubic. The measured window of 16-868 K sits below the tilt transitions of both end members, so no transition is crossed. [ref 2] offers only computed Sr-Ca-Ti-O supercell orderings in P1, C2 and Pm with no ICSD references, one of them flagged ambiguous; they describe cation-ordering variants of the same perovskite and do not bear on the prototype.

dopant_roles.basis: Held at 0.1 of the A site in four compositions. Trivalent La on the divalent A site donates one electron per substitution into the Ti 3d band, which is what makes these titanates n-type conductors; it is the doping variable of the series rather than an impurity.
Sr0.75Ca0.25Ti0.97Nb0.03O3 and Sr0.6Ca0.4Ti0.97Nb0.03O3. Nb5+ on the Ti4+ octahedral site is the B-site route to the same electron doping, and the two routes are used interchangeably in this family.
The Nd of the (Sr1-x-yCaxNdy)TiO3 paper, a trivalent A-site donor like La but with a smaller ionic radius, so it also increases the octahedral tilting.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: the twelve-coordinate A site of the perovskite
solid_solution_axis.note: Ca/(Ca+Sr) spans 0.25-0.67 over seven compositions, the middle of the SrTiO3-CaTiO3 series, so neither end member is the parent and the composition decides which it is closer to. Ca2+ and Sr2+ are isovalent and share the A site, so this adds no carriers -- the carriers come from La, Nd or Nb -- but it does change the tolerance factor and hence the octahedral tilt, and with it the band width.

basis: Every composition is CaTiO3 with a substituent on one site or the other, and [ref 1] settles the structure conclusively: CaTiO3 Pnma (62) mp-4019 at hull 0.000 on 55 ICSD references, the orthorhombically tilted perovskite. The papers are on alkaline-earth titanates and on band filling in Nd1-xAxTiO3, so the samples are the electron-doped titanate rather than any of the other Ca-Ti-O phases the references list -- CaTi2O4, Ca3Ti2O7 and Ca4Ti3O10 are the Ruddlesden-Popper and related intergrowths of the same chemistry and no composition here has their Ca:Ti ratio. The 79-867 K window lies well below the Pnma to I4/mcm tilt transition near 1500 K, so no transition is crossed.

other_polymorphs.note: The I4/mcm tetragonal tilt phase of CaTiO3, which [ref 1] lists at hull 0.019 on 4 ICSD references, and above it the cubic Pm-3m aristotype mp-5827 on 12 references. Both are genuine thermal phases of this compound but they appear only above roughly 1500 K, far outside the 79-867 K measured window, so they are recorded here rather than in phases.

dopant_roles.basis: Ca0.9La0.1TiO3 and Sr0.15Ca0.75La0.1TiO3. Trivalent La on the divalent Ca site donates an electron into the Ti 3d band and is the n-type dopant of these titanates.
Nd0.1Ca0.9TiO3 and Nd0.2Ca0.8TiO3, the Nd1-xAxTiO3 band-filling series of the third paper. Same trivalent A-site donor role as La, and at x of 0.2 it is no longer dilute.

CaTi0.9Fe0.1O3 and CaTi0.8Fe0.2O3. Iron enters the octahedral B site, where as Fe3+ against Ti4+ it is an acceptor and is normally charge-compensated by oxygen vacancies rather than by holes -- the opposite sense to the A-site rare earths, and at 0.2 it is an alloying level rather than a dopant level.

Sr0.15Ca0.75La0.1TiO3, one composition. Sr2+ for Ca2+ on the A site adds no carriers; it enlarges the A cation and reduces the octahedral tilting, and it is the dilute end of the same axis that the Ca-O-Sr-Ti host covers in the middle.

basis: Two samples are CaZrO3 and five are CaMnxZr1-xO3 with x from 0.05 to 0.24, from two papers on CaMnxZr1-xO3 as an NTC thermistor ceramic. CaZrO3 is the orthorhombic perovskite and [ref 1] gives it as Pnma (62) mp-4571 at hull 0.000 on 9 ICSD references. Note the second entry on that line, CaZrO3 (221), which carries a space group but no mp_id: it is one of the TEDesignLab space groups with no Materials Project counterpart, and it names the cubic aristotype, which CaZrO3 does not adopt anywhere near the 373-1473 K window measured here -- the same failure mode the project records for the cubic ReO3 entry standing in for monoclinic WO3. The orthorhombic entry is the one to carry forward. The first paper listed for this host is on the thermophysical properties of BaUO3 and shares no element with these compositions, so it looks like a linkage artefact and was not used.

dopant_roles.basis: CaMnxZr1-xO3 at x from 0.05 to 0.24 in five compositions. Manganese occupies the octahedral Zr4+ site, where its mixed Mn3+/Mn4+ valence provides the small-polaron hopping conduction that gives the strongly temperature-dependent resistance these NTC-thermistor papers are about; the accompanying oxygen vacancies are the subject of the third paper. At the upper end, 0.24, this is a solid solution rather than doping.

basis: All five compositions are Cd2Cu3In3Te8 with the Cd:Cu ratio shifted, and the first paper covers the A2Cu3In3Te8 family for A = Cd, Zn, Mn, Mg. The cation-to-anion count is 8:8, so this is a fully occupied adamantine structure -- an ordered zincblende superstructure, not a defect or ordered-vacancy compound -- and the charge balance works out exactly with Cd2+, Cu+, In3+ and Te2-. That places it in the tetrahedral diamond-like family of the stannite entry, whose I-42m ordering is also what [ref 2] offers for the nearest formula it has, Cd2InCuTe4 mp-1227025 at hull 0.014 with no ICSD references. Confidence is medium rather than high because A2Cu3In3Te8 is a larger superstructure than the A2BCX4 archetype of this entry and its exact cation ordering has to come from the paper in stage 2; if that ordering turns out to be a distinct type, this host is where a new entry would be needed.

The host holds two Zintl antimonides at different A:Cd ratios. Four samples are (Yb,Eu)2CdSb2 -- Yb1.64Eu0.36CdSb2 and its three neighbours -- which is the 2-1-2 family with two divalent A cations per cadmium; no taxonomy entry existed for it, so zintl_2_1_2_a2cdsb2 is proposed here. Two samples are YbxEu1-xCd2Sb2, the 1-2-2 composition of the first paper, which is the trigonal CaAl2Si2 type already in the taxonomy. The two differ only by that ratio in the composition string, so the host splits on A:Cd. Neither reference covers the host at all, which is why the proposed entry leaves its space group null rather than asserting one.

solid_solution_axis.note: Eu/(Eu+Yb) spans 0.18-0.84 over all seven compositions, so both ends are reached and the parent compound depends on the composition. Eu2+ and Yb2+ are both divalent and interchangeable on the A site, and the point of the substitution in the second paper is mass and strain contrast to suppress the lattice thermal conductivity, not carrier doping. The axis runs across both structure types present in the host, so it cannot be used to separate them.

basis: Six of the seven samples are SrCeCoO4 or Sr1.05Ce0.95CoO4, from two papers on the structural, magnetic, electrical and thermal transport properties of that compound. An A2BO4 oxide with a single octahedral cation is the n = 1 Ruddlesden-Popper phase, K2NiF4 type: one perovskite layer alternating with one rock-salt layer, with the two large cations sharing the nine-coordinate A site. Charge balance puts cobalt at 2+ against Sr2+ and Ce4+, which is consistent. Confidence is held at medium because Ce4+ is a small and highly charged occupant for that A site and neither reference covers the host, so the K2NiF4 assignment rests on the stoichiometry and the family rather than on evidence. The seventh sample, Ce0.5Sr0.5Co0.8Fe0.2O3, is an ABO3 perovskite cathode material from the third paper -- a different structure of the same elements -- so the host is flagged mixed and splits on the A:B ratio, 2:1 against 1:1.

dopant_roles.basis: Ce0.5Sr0.5Co0.8Fe0.2O3, the perovskite composition of the host. Iron shares the octahedral B site with cobalt in the standard SrCoFeO3-based SOFC cathode, where the Co:Fe ratio tunes the mixed valence and the oxygen vacancy concentration. It has no bearing on the K2NiF4 phase that the other six samples are.

basis: All four compositions are DyCoO3 with a small substitution on one site or the other, and the papers are on the high-temperature thermoelectric properties of Ln(Co,Ni)O3 and on Sr doping of DyCoO3. A rare-earth cobaltite at ABO3 is the orthorhombic perovskite -- [ref 2] gives DyCoO3 Pnma (62) mp-24848 at hull 0.010 on 5 ICSD references, the only entry it offers for the host, which agrees. Dy3+ is a small A cation so the octahedral tilting is large, but the structure type is unambiguous at this stoichiometry.

dopant_roles.basis: Dy0.9Ca0.1CoO3, two samples. Divalent Ca on the trivalent Dy site is an acceptor: it oxidises cobalt towards Co4+ and makes the cobaltite p-type, which is how this family is made conducting.
Dy0.975Sr0.025CoO3, the composition of the strontium-doping paper. The same divalent acceptor role as Ca with a larger cation, so it also relieves some of the octahedral tilt.
DyCo0.95Ni0.05O3, from the Ln(Co,Ni)O3 paper. Nickel takes the octahedral B site rather than the A site, where it alters the spin state and the band width of the transition-metal d states directly.

basis: Every composition is NdzFe3CoSb12 with z from 0.85 to 1.0, and both papers name it: p-type NdzFe4-xCoxSb12 and nanostructured NdxFe3CoSb12. Sb12 with four transition metals per formula unit is the skutterudite framework of corner-linked MSb6 octahedra with Sb4 rings, and the neodymium occupies the large icosahedral void at its centre, which is the filled variant rather than the binary one. The z below unity is deliberate partial filling, the carrier-count and rattler-concentration variable of this family, and the Co-for-Fe ratio is what sets the electron count that makes the filling possible at all. Neither reference covers the host; the neighbouring Fe-Nd-Sb host in this same chunk gives Nd(FeSb3)4 Im-3 mp-15026 for the unsubstituted end, which is the filled skutterudite cell.

Every composition is Ti(Fe,Co,Ni)Sb at the 1:1:1 stoichiometry, and both papers say so outright -- an alternative approach to improving half-Heusler properties, and Ti(Fe,Co,Ni)Sb pseudo-ternary alloys. The half-Heusler MgAgAs structure is the F-43m cell with one of the two tetrahedral sites of the full Heusler left vacant, and what makes these compositions work is that mixing Fe, Co and Ni averages the d-electron count back to the 18-electron closed shell that the semiconducting half-Heusler requires: TiFe0.3Co0.2Ni0.5Sb and TiFe0.25Co0.25Ni0.5Sb both balance Fe against Ni around Co. No reference covers this five-element host, but the isoelectronic TiCoSb parent is one of the best-attested half-Heuslers there is.

dopant_roles.basis: Ti0.85Hf0.15Fe0.3Co0.2Ni0.5Sb, one composition. Hf and Ti are both group 4 and share the M site, so the substitution adds no carriers; its purpose is the large mass contrast that scatters phonons and lowers the lattice thermal conductivity, which is the standard move in this family. At 0.15 of the site it is alloying rather than dilute doping.

basis: Four compositions are Na0.71Co1-xRuxO2 with x from 0.2 to 0.5, and the fifth, NaCo2.5Ru0.5O4, is the same material in the older NaCo2O4 notation that the second paper uses in its title, NaCo2-xMxO4 -- dividing by two gives Na0.5(Co,Ru)O2. Both are the gamma-NaxCoO2 layered oxide: edge-sharing CoO2 octahedral sheets with sodium partially occupying the sites between them. The sodium content x is the compositional variable of this structure rather than a dopant, as the prototype notes record, and the first paper is on ruthenium substitution in layered sodium cobaltate NaxCoO2. Neither reference covers the host. Note that the ruthenium is not dilute -- up to half the transition-metal site -- so at the upper end this is a (Co,Ru)O2 solid solution held in the same layered framework.

Every composition is (Ta,Nb)CoSn at 1:1:1, and the second paper is titled n-type TaCoSn-based half-Heuslers as promising thermoelectric materials. TaCoSn and NbCoSn are 18-electron half-Heuslers in the MgAgAs structure, F-43m, with one tetrahedral site vacant, and the first paper studies the isoelectronic CoTiSb half-Heusler alongside. Ta and Nb are both group 5 and share the M site at a fixed 0.6:0.4 in five of the six compositions, so the substitution is a lattice-thermal-conductivity measure within one structure rather than a second phase. No reference covers this four-element host.
