dopant_roles.basis: Ta0.6Nb0.4CoSn1-ySby at y from 0.02 to 0.08, the doping series of the second paper. Antimony has one more valence electron than tin, so on the main-group site it pushes the compound past 18 electrons and dopes it n-type; this is the carrier-count knob of the host, distinct from the isovalent Ta/Nb mixing on the metal site.

basis: All seven samples are ZrNiSn with cobalt substituted for nickel, written either as ZrNi1-xCoxSn or in the atomic-percent form Zr30Ni32Co5Sn32, and the third paper is on the ordered structures and thermoelectric properties of MNiSn for M = Ti, Zr, Hf. ZrNiSn is the archetypal n-type half-Heusler: the F-43m MgAgAs cell with one of the two tetrahedral sites empty. The one composition that needs care is ZrNiCo0.4Sn, where nickel is already at full occupancy and the cobalt is extra -- and that is exactly what the first paper is about, vacancy site occupation by Co and Ir in half-Heusler ZrNiSn. At 0.4 occupancy the compound is still the half-Heusler with interstitials on the vacant site rather than the full Heusler, so the host is left unmixed and the full Heusler is carried only as the limit that route heads towards. No reference covers this four-element host.

Every composition is Yb(Rh1-xCox)2Si2, seven single crystals from one paper on the thermopower evolution across that series. YbRh2Si2 is one of the best-studied ThCr2Si2-type compounds there is: the body-centred tetragonal I4/mmm cell of Si-Rh-Si layers separated by ytterbium, and it is the canonical heavy-fermion quantum-critical system. Cobalt and rhodium are both group 9 and isostructural end members -- YbCo2Si2 is also ThCr2Si2-type -- so the whole series stays in one structure while the chemical pressure from the smaller cobalt drives the magnetic transition, which is what the measurement is for. No reference covers this four-element host.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: the transition-metal site of the TSi4 tetrahedral layer
solid_solution_axis.note: Co/(Co+Rh) spans 0.18-0.78 over the seven crystals, so neither end member is dilute. The two are isovalent and isostructural, and the substitution acts as chemical pressure -- cobalt is the smaller ion, so it contracts the lattice and moves the system across its magnetic quantum critical point. That is the variable the paper scans, not carrier concentration.

basis: Five of the seven samples are CuCrSe2, from two papers that call it a phonon-glass electron-crystal thermoelectric and a ternary chromium chalcogenide. That is the layered CuCrS2 type, rhombohedral R3m: CrSe2 octahedral sheets with copper in the tetrahedral sites between them, mobile at high temperature. The other two samples are CuCr1.64V0.22Se4 and CuCr1.79V0.08Se4, which are CuCr2Se4 spinel -- the second paper is explicitly on CuCrxVySe4 p-type spinel semiconductors -- so the host holds two structures and splits on the Se:Cu ratio, 2:1 against 4:1. The references disagree with the majority here and are recorded rather than followed: [ref 2] ranks the spinel Cr2CuSe4 Fd-3m mp-3880 first at hull 0.000 on 14 ICSD references and gives the layered CrCuSe2 R3m mp-7861 at hull 0.247 on one reference. The layered compound is real and well characterised, and it is what five of these seven samples are; this is the reference describing the chemistry rather than the specimen.

dopant_roles.basis: CuCr1.64V0.22Se4 and CuCr1.79V0.08Se4, the two spinel compositions. Vanadium takes the octahedral Cr site of the spinel; with the accompanying cation deficiency on that site it sets the hole concentration these p-type spinel semiconductors are studied for. It has no part in the layered CuCrSe2 phase.

basis: The whole host is LaCrGe3, seven samples from two papers on its heavy-fermion and Kondo-lattice behaviour and its ferromagnetic quantum critical point. [ref 2] gives it cleanly: LaCrGe3 P6_3/mmc (194) mp-1080078 at hull 0.000 on 5 ICSD references. That cell is the BaNiO3 2H structure -- infinite chains of face-sharing CrGe6 octahedra running along c with lanthanum between them -- which is the structure this entry is named for, and BaNiO3 is one of its listed representative materials. One scope note for the review: the proposed entry writes its formula archetype as ABO3 and its structural class as perovskite-derived, which is oxide-specific, whereas LaCrGe3 is an intermetallic germanide of the same 2H face-sharing topology. The archetype should be widened to ABX3 rather than a near-duplicate entry being created for the germanide.

The whole host is NiCr2S4, seven samples from one paper titled Ordered-Defect Sulfides as Thermoelectric Materials, and the title is the assignment. NiCr2S4 is the Cr3S4-type monoclinic derivative of NiAs: hexagonal sulfur layers with fully occupied metal layers alternating with half-occupied ones in which the vacancies order, lowering the symmetry to C2/m. [ref 1] gives exactly that cell, Cr2NiS4 C2/m (12) mp-27512 at hull 0.056 on 1 ICSD reference -- a weak primary by the chunk convention, so it corroborates rather than settles, and the remaining Materials Project entries are computed Cr-Ni-S orderings in P-1 and P2/m with no ICSD references at all. No taxonomy entry covered the ordered-vacancy derivative, only the NiAs parent and the spinel, so cr3s4_defect_nias is proposed here. The spinel is the alternative this formula could have taken -- FeCr2S4 is one -- but nickel in this system gives the monoclinic phase, and the ordered vacancies are what the paper attributes the low lattice thermal conductivity to.

All seven samples are Cr1-xRuxSb2 with x from 0.2 to 0.8, from one paper on the structural and electrical properties of that series. Both end members are marcasite-type diantimonides in orthorhombic Pnnm -- CrSb2 and RuSb2 are isostructural, built from edge-sharing MSb6 octahedral chains with Sb-Sb bonding between them -- so the solid solution stays in one structure across the whole range, which is what lets the paper treat it as a continuous series. Neither reference covers the host. Note that this substitution is not isoelectronic: chromium is group 6 and ruthenium group 8, so x is a band-filling variable and the series crosses from the narrow-gap correlated CrSb2 towards the semimetallic RuSb2. Both elements sit above the 5 at.% cut, so neither appears as a dopant candidate, which is correct here -- this is an alloy axis, not doping.

This host is three intermetallics of one chemistry. LaCu4In and its Ce-substituted versions, three samples, are the cubic AuBe5 (C15b) type in F-43m, the family YbAgCu4 exemplifies and which this entry covers at ABC4. LaInCu2, two samples, is the full Heusler instead -- [ref 2] gives LaInCu2 Fm-3m mp-20491 at hull 0.017 on 4 ICSD references, which is the L2_1 MnCu2Al cell, not AuBe5. The remaining LaCu5In compositions are a third thing again: [ref 2] places LaInCu5 in Pnnm (58) mp-1203883 at hull 0.000 on 1 ICSD reference, an orthorhombic phase that matches no taxonomy entry, so those compositions go to unresolved_crystalline until the cell is checked in stage 2. The host therefore splits on the Cu:In ratio, 2 against 4 against 5, and none of the three labels can stand for the others. The papers are magnetotransport and thermopower studies of the Ce-diluted heavy-fermion versions of each.

dopant_roles.basis: Ce0.1La0.9Cu4In, Ce0.2La0.8Cu4In and (Ce0.2La0.8)Cu5In. Cerium replaces lanthanum on the rare-earth site, and the point of the dilution is that Ce carries a 4f moment while La does not: these are dense-Kondo systems studied as a function of how far apart the magnetic ions are, so the substituent is the physics rather than a carrier dopant.

basis: The host is two unrelated compounds. Four samples are LaCu6 and CexLa1-xCu6, from papers on point-contact spectra of dense Kondo substances and on the heavy-fermion state in CeCu6; LaCu6 is isostructural with CeCu6, the orthorhombic Pnma phase this entry is named for, and [ref 2] gives LaCu6 Pnma mp-636256 at hull 0.006 on 3 ICSD references. Three samples are written La2Cu04, which is La2CuO4 with a transcribed zero for the oxygen -- the third paper is on evidence for superconductivity in La2CuO4 -- and that is the n = 1 Ruddlesden-Popper cuprate, K2NiF4 type, a completely different structure. The host splits on whether oxygen is present at all, and the composition-string typo should be corrected upstream so the formula parses as an oxide.

dopant_roles.basis: Ce0.094La0.906Cu6, Ce0.18La0.82Cu6 and Ce0.29La0.71Cu6. As in the Cu-In-La host, cerium on the lanthanum site is the magnetic ion being diluted in a heavy-fermion study, not a carrier dopant; LaCu6 is the non-magnetic reference lattice for CeCu6.

basis: All seven samples are Cu2MgSnSe4 and its In-substituted and Cu-excess variants, from one paper introducing it as a new wide band gap thermoelectric quaternary selenide. A2BCX4 with Cu+, Mg2+, Sn4+ and Se2- is charge balanced at a 1:1 cation-to-anion ratio, which makes it a quaternary ordered zincblende of the stannite or kesterite family, the diamond-like structure this entry covers. Confidence is medium and not high because no reference line exists for this host at all and because stannite and kesterite differ only in how the Cu and Mg order over the cation sites -- the two are hard to separate by X-ray diffraction and the choice has to come from the paper in stage 2. The Cu2.05Mg0.95 and Cu2.075Mg0.925 compositions are deliberate Cu-on-Mg antisite substitution, the p-type route for this family.

dopant_roles.basis: Cu2MgSn1-xInxSe4 at x of 0.05, 0.075 and 0.1. Trivalent In on the tetravalent Sn site is an acceptor and is the carrier-concentration knob of the paper, working in the same direction as the Cu-on-Mg excess in the other compositions.

basis: All seven samples are CuMn1+xO2 with x from 0 to 0.2, from a paper on fabricating and measuring exactly that series. CuMnO2 is crednerite, the delafossite ABO2 structure -- O-Cu-O dumbbells linking edge-sharing MnO6 octahedral sheets -- monoclinically distorted to C2/m because Jahn-Teller active Mn3+ deforms the octahedral layer. It is the same prototype as CuFeO2 and CuAlO2 with a cooperative distortion, not a different type. The references are recorded as disagreeing: [ref 2] offers no CuMnO2 entry at all, ranking instead Mn3Cu3O8 P4_332 mp-652534 on 1 ICSD reference, Mn(Cu3O4)2 Fm-3m and other cubic and low-symmetry Cu-Mn-O orderings. Those are the spinel-related copper manganites of the same chemistry, which is what a Cu-Mn-O search returns, and not the layered compound these samples are; the excess manganese of CuMn1.2O2 may well precipitate some of that spinel, which is worth checking in stage 2.
reference_disagreement: assigned sg [166], ICSD-backed references for this host report [212]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: Every composition is CuxMo6S8 with x from 2 to 4, and two of the three papers name the family outright: thermoelectric properties of Chevrel-phase sulfides MxMo6S8 and preparation of Chevrel-phase CuxMo6S8. The Mo6S8 unit is the Chevrel cluster -- an octahedron of molybdenum inside a cube of sulfur -- and the clusters pack rhombohedrally with the copper in the channels between them. The copper content is the intercalation and carrier-concentration variable of the structure, not an impurity, which is what the x series scans. [ref 2] offers only computed P1 Cu-Mo-S cluster orderings, mp-675745 and mp-675781 at hulls of 0.069 and 0.072 with no ICSD references, so the cell must come from the Chevrel literature in stage 2. The third paper, on Cu-doped MoS2 nanosheets, would be a different structure entirely, but no composition in this host has the MoS2 stoichiometry, so the host stays unmixed.

All seven samples are Cux(Dy2S3)1-x with x from 0.006 to 0.125, from one paper on the thermoelectric properties of Cu-doped dysprosium sesquisulfide, measured to 1275 K. A rare-earth sesquisulfide at that temperature, doped by adding a small amount of a monovalent metal, is the classic gamma-phase Th3P4-type situation: Ln2S3 written as Ln2.67S4 carries one third of a cation vacancy per formula unit in the cubic I-43d framework, and filling or emptying that vacancy is the carrier-concentration knob the prototype notes already describe for La3-xTe4. That is what Cu at these levels is doing. The reference points the other way and is recorded rather than followed: [ref 2] ranks Dy2S3 Pnma (62) mp-1270 at hull 0.000 on 2 ICSD references, the orthorhombic form, which is the low-temperature structure for the heavier lanthanides. Dy sits near the boundary where the cubic gamma phase stops forming, so which one a high-temperature synthesis produced is exactly the sort of question the paper itself would settle; confidence is medium and the orthorhombic alternative is kept.

other_polymorphs.note: Orthorhombic Pnma Dy2S3, the U2S3-type form, which [ref 2] gives as the primary entry for the formula on 2 ICSD references. It has no taxonomy entry of its own. It is not a metastable structure -- for the heavier rare earths it is the ambient form -- so if the paper reports it, this record should be changed to it rather than the polymorph simply being noted here.

dopant_roles.basis: Cux(Dy2S3)1-x at x from 0.006 to 0.125. In the Th3P4-type framework the natural home for a small monovalent cation is the partially vacant cation site -- one third of it is empty at the Ln2S3 stoichiometry -- so copper is recorded as filling that void rather than as replacing dysprosium. That is what makes it a carrier-count dopant. If the orthorhombic form turns out to be the right structure the role would have to be revisited, since it has no such vacancy; the confidence reflects that.

basis: Six of the seven samples are ErPdSb and the first paper is on the thermoelectric and thermophysical properties of ErPdX half-Heuslers for X = Sb and Bi. [ref 2] gives ErSbPd F-43m (216) mp-11836 at hull 0.000, which is the MgAgAs half-Heusler cell with one tetrahedral site vacant. The seventh sample is ErPd2Sb, which fills that site and is the full Heusler -- the second paper covers both, REPdZ and REPd2Z, in one study -- so the host holds two prototypes and splits cleanly on the Pd:Er ratio, 1 against 2. The Er3(SbPd2)4 Fm-3m entry mp-1193806 that [ref 2] ranks first is a third stoichiometry again, Er3Pd8Sb4, which no sample here matches.

One composition, MgF2, seven samples from a paper on the reproducibility of its physical properties. Magnesium fluoride is the textbook rutile-structure fluoride, tetragonal P4_2/nmm in the setting [ref 2] prints as P4_2/mnm (136) mp-1249 at hull 0.000 on 23 ICSD references -- the strongest attestation for anything in this host by a wide margin. The other MgF2 entries it lists, Pa-3 with 6 references and Pnnm with 3, are the cubic and alpha-PbO2-type high-pressure polymorphs, and MgF3 at hull 0.481 is not a real compound; none of them is reached in the 318-1108 K ambient-pressure window measured here. Note that this is an insulator being characterised as a reference material rather than a thermoelectric.

other_polymorphs.note: The Pa-3 polymorph of MgF2 at hull 0.067 on 6 ICSD references, and the Pnnm alpha-PbO2-type form mp-1072956 at hull 0.037 on 3. Both are pressure-induced denser packings of the same formula rather than thermal phases, so neither is crossed on heating at one atmosphere; the taxonomy has no entry for either.

basis: Every composition is (Ti,Hf)(Fe,Ni)Sb at the 1:1:1 stoichiometry, and the papers name the design: high-performance disordered half-Heusler materials and p-type double half-Heusler Ti2FeNiSb2. The double half-Heusler is the important detail: TiFe0.5Ni0.5Sb, written here as Ti1.6Hf0.4FeNiSb1.7Sn0.3 and its neighbours, averages the valence electron count of an 17-electron FeSb and a 19-electron NiSb half-Heusler back to the semiconducting 18, giving a compound that is still the MgAgAs F-43m structure but with two species ordered or disordered over its single tetrahedral site. So the whole host is one prototype, and what varies is the site occupancy rather than the structure type. No reference covers this five-element host.

dopant_roles.basis: Sb1.7Sn0.3 in three of the compositions, from the double half-Heusler paper. Tin has one fewer valence electron than antimony, so on the main-group site it takes the compound below 18 electrons and dopes it p-type; this is the carrier-count knob of those samples.

Ti0.8Hf0.2Fe0.5Co0.15Ni0.35Sb, one composition from the Ti(Fe,Co,Ni)Sb paper. Cobalt sits between iron and nickel in electron count on the same tetrahedral site, so replacing part of the nickel with it is a finer adjustment of the same 18-electron balance rather than a separate dopant mechanism.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: the group 4 M site of the half-Heusler
solid_solution_axis.note: Hf/(Hf+Ti) spans 0.20-0.50 over the seven compositions. Hf and Ti are isovalent group 4 elements on the same site, so the substitution adds no carriers; it is there for the mass and strain contrast that scatters phonons, and it is the standard lattice-thermal-conductivity measure in this family. At these fractions it is alloying throughout, with no dilute end.

basis: All three compositions are FeVSb with hafnium and titanium substituted onto the vanadium site -- Fe(V0.8Hf0.2)0.8Ti0.2Sb, FeV0.64Hf0.16Ti0.2Sb and the Nb-containing member -- and the first paper is titled Optimizing the thermoelectric performance of FeVSb half-Heusler compounds. FeVSb is an 18-electron half-Heusler in the MgAgAs F-43m structure, and the group 4 substituents Hf and Ti each remove one electron from the group 5 vanadium site, which is what makes this series p-type. So the substitution is simultaneously the carrier-count knob and the phonon-scattering mechanism, and all of it happens within one structure type. No reference covers this five-element host.

dopant_roles.basis: FeV0.49Nb0.15Hf0.16Ti0.2Sb, the composition of the third paper on Nb-doped FeV0.64Hf0.16Ti0.2Sb. Niobium is group 5 like vanadium and shares that site, so unlike the Hf and Ti already there it adds no holes; it is the heavier homologue and acts through mass contrast on the lattice thermal conductivity.

basis: Every composition is NdzFe4-xCoxSb12, and [ref 2] gives the structure directly: Nd(FeSb3)4 Im-3 (204) mp-15026 at hull 0.000, which is NdFe4Sb12 -- the body-centred cubic filled skutterudite, an Sb12 framework of corner-linked FeSb6 octahedra with Sb4 rings and the neodymium in the large icosahedral void at the cell centre. The papers are on fully filled skutterudite unicouples and on NdzFe4-xCoxSb12, so the filling is the point. NdFe4Sb12 needs the filler for charge balance in a way binary CoSb3 does not, which is why z sits at or just below 1 rather than at the few per cent typical of Yb-filled CoSb3, and the Nd0.9Fe3Sb12 composition is framework-deficient rather than a different phase.

dopant_roles.basis: NdFe3.5Co0.5Sb12 and Nd0.9Fe3.5Co0.5Sb12. Cobalt has one more d electron than iron and takes the same framework octahedral site, so the Co:Fe ratio sets the electron count of the framework and with it how much filler the void will accept -- this is framework substitution in the skutterudite sense, not a dilute impurity, and it works together with z rather than independently of it.

basis: All seven single crystals are TlIn1-xGaxTe2 with x from 0.2 to 0.8, from one paper on the X-ray diffraction characterisation and electrical properties of that series. TlInTe2 is the TlSe structure type, tetragonal I4/mcm: chains of edge-sharing In3+Te4 tetrahedra running along c with monovalent thallium in eightfold sites between them, which is the chain family this entry covers together with InTe. Gallium replaces indium on the trivalent chain site across the whole range and both TlGaTe2 and TlInTe2 are the same type, so the series stays in one structure. [ref 2] offers only TlIn2GaTe4 I222 (23) mp-1216591 at hull 0.024 with no ICSD references, which is a computed cation ordering of one composition rather than evidence about the structure type, so it is noted and not used to pick the cell.

solid_solution_axis.shared_site: the trivalent tetrahedral site of the chain
solid_solution_axis.note: Ga/(Ga+In) spans 0.20-0.80 over the seven crystals, so both end members are reached and the parent compound depends on the composition. Ga3+ and In3+ are isovalent on the chain site, so the substitution adds no carriers; it widens the band gap continuously from TlInTe2 to TlGaTe2, which is what the paper measures. Note that the thallium here is monovalent and on a different site entirely -- it is not part of this axis.

basis: Three unrelated structures share this host. Four of the six compositions are La0.85Sr0.15Ga0.8Mg0.2O2.825, the LSGM oxide-ion conductor, on its own and as composites with 1.3 to 9.4 parts of Sm-doped ceria; LSGM is the LaGaO3 perovskite with acceptor substitution on both sites, and [ref 1] attests the parent at LaGaO3 R-3c (167) mp-3336 on 24 ICSD references with the Pnma setting mp-5837 on 18 more. La3Ga5.5Ta0.5O14 is langatate and La2Ga5SiO14 is langasite -- almost certainly La3Ga5SiO14 with a transcription slip, since langasite requires three lanthanum -- and the first paper is on the thermal and piezoelectric properties of fresnoite and langasite-family crystals, which confirms that reading. Both already have their own taxonomy entries. The ceria in the composite samples is a separate fluorite phase, so those compositions are composites rather than single structures. The host must be split per composition, and the perovskite is recorded as the label only because it is the majority.

dopant_roles.basis: Ga0.8Mg0.2 in the five LSGM compositions. Divalent Mg on the trivalent octahedral Ga site is an acceptor, and it is charge-compensated by oxygen vacancies rather than by holes -- which is the whole design of the material, since those vacancies are what carry the ionic current. The O2.825 stoichiometry is that compensation written out.
La0.85Sr0.15, the A-site half of the same acceptor doping, generating oxygen vacancies by the same mechanism as the Mg on the B site.

Cerium appears only inside the (Ce0.85Sm0.15O1.925) term of the three composite compositions. That is Sm-doped ceria, a fluorite-structure second phase deliberately mixed with the LSGM, not a substituent in the perovskite lattice -- the point of those samples is the two-phase composite.
The acceptor inside that same ceria phase, where it sits on the Ce site. It belongs to the second phase rather than to the host, so at host level it is recorded the same way as the cerium.

La3Ga5.5Ta0.5O14. Tantalum is a host constituent of langatate, not a dopant: it occupies one specific octahedral site of the langasite framework and its presence is what distinguishes langatate from langasite. It falls below 5 at.% only because the formula has fourteen oxygens.
La2Ga5SiO14. As with Ta, silicon is a framework constituent of langasite occupying the small tetrahedral site, not a dopant on anything.

basis: The host key is a parsing artefact and the material is not a Mg-Ga intermetallic. Every composition reads (Mg2)y(Si0.3Sn0.7)0.05Ga0.95, which puts gallium at 95 per cent of the non-Mg part and silicon and tin at 5 -- the reverse of the real material. The paper is titled Enhanced hole concentration through Ga doping and excess of Mg, so the compound is Mg2Si0.3Sn0.7 with a few per cent of gallium, i.e. the antifluorite Mg2(Si,Sn) thermoelectric, and the two subscripts have been transposed in the composition string. The y multiplier on Mg2, 0.95 to 1.12, is the excess-Mg variable of the same paper. The same misparse was already recorded in the Mg host at rank 280, where these compositions fell through to a bare Mg key; here they land on Ga-Mg instead, so the string should be fixed upstream rather than in stage 2. [ref 2] returns Mg-Ga binaries -- MgGa2, Mg5Ga2, Mg2Ga5, Mg2Ga -- which is what the element list literally implies and is not this material; that disagreement is the consequence of the parse, not evidence about the structure.

dopant_roles.basis: Silicon is a host element of Mg2Si0.3Sn0.7, not a minor element: it appears below the cut only because the bracketed (Si0.3Sn0.7) group was given the dopant multiplier that belongs to the gallium. Recorded the same way as in the Mg host at rank 280, for consistency.

As Si -- the majority anion-site element of the real Mg2(Si,Sn) composition, misplaced by the same transposition. On the corrected formula Si and Sn form an isoelectronic solid solution on the anion site at roughly 30:70.

Gallium is the actual dopant of these samples despite the parse placing it at 95 per cent. It is recorded on the anion site rather than the Mg site: the paper reports an enhanced hole concentration, and trivalent Ga replacing tetravalent Si or Sn is an acceptor, whereas Ga on the divalent Mg site would be a donor and give electrons. This differs from the Mg host record at rank 280, which assigned Ga to the Mg site; the p-type result is the reason for placing it on the anion site here, and the paper would settle it.

reference_disagreement: assigned sg [225], ICSD-backed references for this host report [72, 194, 139, 190]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: The three compositions are Gd2S3, GdS1.48 and GdS1.43, i.e. sulfur-to-gadolinium ratios of 1.43 to 1.50, which is the Gd(3-x)S4 cation-vacancy range of the Th3P4 type: Gd3S4 is the filled x = 0 end at GdS1.333 and Gd2S3 is the fully vacant x = 0.333 end at GdS1.5. The non-integer subscripts are exactly how that vacancy variable gets written, and the lead paper is titled Thermoelectric properties of Th3P4-type rare-earth sulfides Ln2S3, with a corrigendum to the same work as a third reference. I disagree with [ref 2] for these samples: it ranks Gd2S3 Pnma (62) mp-608146 first on 5 ICSD references, but Pnma is the alpha (orthorhombic) polymorph of Gd2S3 and the gamma Th3P4-type polymorph is what these papers make and measure. MP does carry the cubic member, Gd3S4 I-43d (220) mp-20036 at hull 0.012 with 2 ICSD references, which is the structure the whole GdS(1.33-1.5) range belongs to.

other_polymorphs.note: alpha-Gd2S3, orthorhombic Pnma, 5 ICSD references and the MP primary for this formula. It is a real ambient polymorph of Gd2S3, not a metastable artefact, but it is not the Th3P4-type phase these papers report; the taxonomy has no entry for the alpha rare-earth sesquisulfide structure.

basis: Every composition is LaPt4Ge(12-x)Sb(x) with x between 4 and 5.3 -- LaPt4Ge7Sb5, LaPt4Ge8Sb4, LaPt4Ge6.7Sb5.3 -- so each formula unit has one La guest inside a framework of exactly twelve p-block atoms bonded to four Pt. That is the LnT4X12 filled-skutterudite stoichiometry, and the paper is titled From Superconductivity Towards Thermoelectricity: Ge-Based Skutterudites. LaPt4Ge12 is the germanide member of that family, superconducting near 8 K; antimony replacing germanium on the four-membered framework rings is how the valence electron count is tuned away from the superconducting composition towards a thermoelectric one. Neither reference covers this chemistry at all, so no mp_id is recorded. Antimony is a framework constituent here rather than a dopant, which is why it sits above the 5 per cent cut and appears in the host key.

All seven compositions are Ge0.72-0.76Pb0.1Sb0.1Te with 0 to 4 per cent Al, i.e. GeTe with a tenth of the germanium site taken by lead and a tenth by antimony. The papers are a lone-pair engineering study and the Science high-entropy GeTe work, both of which are about the rhombohedral GeTe host. GeTe is the rhombohedral R3m ferroelectric distortion of rocksalt below its Curie temperature and converts to cubic Fm-3m above it, and the 297-801 K measured window straddles that, so both phases are recorded. The transition sits near 700 K in pure GeTe but cation alloying of this size pulls it down, so 700 K is an upper estimate rather than a value for these compositions. Neither reference covers this quaternary, so mp_id is null on both phases.

dopant_roles.basis: Al0.01 to Al0.04 replacing germanium in Ge0.76-xAlxPb0.1Sb0.1Te. Trivalent Al on the divalent Ge site is a donor, so it compensates part of the very high intrinsic hole concentration that germanium vacancies give GeTe, which is the usual reason aluminium is added to this system.

basis: All seven samples are URu(1-x)Pd(x)Ge for x = 0.2 to 0.7, and the paper is titled Thermoelectric Power of the URu1-xPdxGe System. These are equiatomic actinide UTX germanides: URuGe and UPdGe both crystallise in the orthorhombic TiNiSi type (ordered Co2Si, Pnma), which is the standard structure for UTX compounds with a late transition metal and a p-block partner, so the whole substitution series stays in one prototype and Ru and Pd form a complete solid solution on the T site rather than acting as dopants. The taxonomy entry is written around rare-earth RTX exemplars such as CePdGa and CeNiSn; U here plays the same role as the rare earth, which is why the confidence is medium rather than high. Neither reference covers this chemistry, so mp_id is null. The measured window is 12-301 K, the magnetic and heavy-fermion regime of the paper, with no structural transition involved.

Four of the seven samples are stoichiometric HfPtSn and the rest are HfPtSn with half a per cent to one per cent of Ir or Co on the Pt site. Two of the three papers say so in their titles -- Thermoelectric properties of p-type half-Heusler compound HfPtSn -- and the third is the MNiSn ordered-structures survey. [ref 2] agrees on the structure: HfSnPt F-43m (216) mp-20889 with 2 ICSD references, and F-43m is the C1b half-Heusler setting. Its hull value of 0.493 eV/atom is not credible for a compound with two ICSD entries and repeated published syntheses; it is a 2019-dump artefact and the space group is the part of that line worth using. HfPtSn is an 18-electron half-Heusler like HfNiSn, so the semiconducting count holds.

dopant_roles.basis: Hf(Pt0.995Ir0.005)Sn and Hf(Pt0.99Ir0.01)Sn. Iridium has one d electron fewer than platinum, so substituting it removes one electron per site from the 18-electron count and dopes the compound p-type, which matches the p-type half-Heusler of the paper titles.

Hf(Pt0.99Co0.01)Sn. Cobalt takes the same transition-metal site as the isoelectronic-with-Ir case but from the 3d row, again one electron short of the closed-shell count, so it is the same p-type knob.

basis: Every composition is Hg3In2Se6 with a per cent or two of Fe or Mn, and the paper title gives the compound as (HgSe)3(In2Se3), i.e. a point on the HgSe-In2Se3 join. Compounds on that join are the classic ordered-vacancy tetrahedral compounds: In2Se3 supplies a third of its cation sites as vacancies, and the resulting adamantane framework with ordered cation vacancies is what the taxonomy calls defect chalcopyrite. [ref 1] supports the join rather than the exact composition -- it gives In2HgSe4 I-4 (82) mp-20731 at hull 0.000, which is the defect-stannite member one step further along the same line -- so the structure type is corroborated but the stoichiometry is not, and no mp_id is carried at host level. Confidence is medium for that reason: the cation-vacancy ordering scheme of the 3:2:6 member is not fixed by either reference. The samples are single crystals measured at 75-304 K.

dopant_roles.basis: Hg3In2Se6Fe0.02 and Fe0.03. The paper is about electron scattering mechanisms in single crystals, so iron here is a dilute magnetic and scattering centre on a tetrahedral cation site; mercury is the site it most plausibly takes, but an ordered-vacancy lattice also offers empty tetrahedral sites, so this is not settled without the paper.
Hg3In2Se6Mn0.03, the same role as Fe -- divalent Mn on the divalent Hg site is the standard dilute magnetic substitution in II-VI derived tetrahedral semiconductors.

M0+ is not an element. Two compositions read Hg3In2Se6M0.01 and M0.02, where M is the generic metal placeholder of the paper standing for the Fe or Mn of the other samples; the parser took the letter M literally.

basis: Three samples are plain HgSe single crystals and four are (Hg3Se)0.9(Al2Se3)0.1 with a trace of Mn. HgSe at ambient pressure is the zincblende semimetal, and [ref 2] is unambiguous about it: HgSe F-43m (216) mp-820 at hull 0.000 with 12 ICSD references. I do not follow [ref 1] here -- TEDesignLab gives HgSe P3_221 (154) mp-1018722 with a single ICSD reference at hull 0.037, which is the cinnabar-type structure that HgSe adopts only above about 0.7 GPa, and nothing in these papers (electrical and optical properties of melt-grown crystals, 78-478 K) involves pressure. The rocksalt Fm-3m entry mp-957 at hull 0.160 is the next high-pressure phase above that, so both non-zincblende entries go in other_polymorphs.

other_polymorphs.note: Cinnabar-type HgSe, the TEDesignLab primary, with 1 ICSD reference. It forms above roughly 0.7 GPa and is not reached by heating at ambient pressure. Filed under trigonal_te as the nearest available id for a trigonal helical-chain structure; it is not a perfect match and stage 2 should not treat it as one.
The next phase up the pressure sequence, 4 ICSD references at hull 0.160. Not accessible in an ambient-pressure transport measurement.

dopant_roles.basis: Aluminium enters only as the Al2Se3 half of (Hg3Se)0.9(Al2Se3)0.1, a ten per cent pseudo-binary addition rather than dilute doping. Al2Se3 is itself a defect-zincblende selenide, so it alloys into the same tetrahedral anion framework and brings ordered cation vacancies with it.
Mn0.0001 to Mn0.002, i.e. parts in ten thousand -- the manganese-doped part of the paper title. Divalent Mn on the divalent Hg tetrahedral site is the standard dilute magnetic substitution here.

basis: Every composition is PbTe with iodine and a little chromium: three are written as atomic percentages near Pb47Te47I5 and two as Pb1.045-1.09Cr0.009Te1I0.11-0.2. Both papers name PbTe explicitly, one of them as PbTe:Cr co-doped. PbTe is rocksalt Fm-3m throughout the 147-599 K window with no structural transition. Neither reference returns a line for this ternary, so mp_id is null; nothing about a few per cent of iodine on the tellurium sublattice changes the prototype. Note that iodine sits in the host key only because the 5 at.% split is taken on the whole formula -- at 5 at.% of PbTe it is 10 per cent of the anion sublattice, which is high for a dopant but is still doping and not an end member, since there is no rocksalt PbI2 to alloy with.

dopant_roles.basis: Cr0.009 per formula unit in the two co-doped compositions. Chromium on the lead site of PbTe is the well-known resonant-level donor that the first paper is about (dramatic enhancement of thermoelectric power factor in PbTe:Cr), so it is a cation-site substituent rather than a scatterer or a second phase.

Iodine is above the 5 at.% cut and therefore in the host key, but it is acting as a dopant: a halogen on the tellurium site donates one electron each and is the standard n-type dopant for PbTe. Recorded here so the role is not lost just because the split put it on the host side of the line.

basis: Six of the seven samples are In3Ni2, and [ref 2] gives In3Ni2 P-3m1 (164) mp-21385 at hull 0.000 with 5 ICSD references, which is the Al3Ni2 type -- the ordered-vacancy derivative of the NiAs/Ni2In pair, with a third of the metal layer sites empty and the vacancies ordered. The taxonomy has nias but no A3B2 ordered-vacancy entry, so al3ni2_trigonal is proposed in prototypes_proposed.jsonl before use. The seventh sample, In46Ni54, comes from the paper on electrical resistivity and absolute thermoelectric power of liquid indium alloys and is responsible for the 1379 K top of the measured range, far above any solidus in this binary -- that sample is a melt and belongs to liquid_metal, so the host is flagged mixed and splits by paper rather than by stoichiometry. The InNi P6/mmm mp-19876 entry that MP ranks first on 9 ICSD references is the equiatomic CsCl-related phase, a different compound in the same binary, and is not what the composition strings here say.

The five compositions are Ir(1-x)Sn(x)O2 for x = 0.2 to 0.6, from a single paper on Sn-doped IrO2 for spintronics. Both end members are rutile -- IrO2 and SnO2 are among the most standard P4_2/mnm rutile oxides -- so the whole cation solid solution is one prototype and no split is needed anywhere along it. Neither reference returns a line for the ternary, so mp_id is null. The measurement is 10-302 K with no structural transition in range. Note that Ir and Sn are not isoelectronic (group 9 against group 14), so this is a genuine cation solid solution with a carrier-count gradient, not an isoelectronic alloy axis; both are above the 5 per cent cut throughout, so neither is recorded as a dopant.

All five compositions are La(1-x)K(x)MnO3 with x = 0.25 to 0.35, the hole-doped manganite: potassium is monovalent on the trivalent La site, so each substitution creates one Mn(IV) and drives the ferromagnetic metallic state the magnetotransport papers are measuring. The ABO3 stoichiometry with a rare earth and an alkali sharing the A site and manganese alone on the B site is the perovskite archetype. Neither reference returns a line for this quaternary, so mp_id is null. The 10-402 K window crosses the Curie temperature and the associated metal-insulator transition, which is a magnetic and electronic transition, not a change of prototype -- the lattice stays a distorted perovskite (rhombohedral R-3c or orthorhombic Pnma depending on x) throughout, so no phases array is recorded.

dopant_roles.basis: One composition is La0.7Na0.05K0.25MnO3, from the paper on La0.7Na0.3-xKx. Sodium plays exactly the same part as potassium -- a monovalent A-site cation replacing trivalent La -- so it is a co-substituent on the A site, differing only in ionic radius and therefore in tolerance factor.

basis: The single composition, repeated across all seven samples, is (K0.5Na0.5)NbO3 -- KNN, the lead-free piezoelectric, here made oxygen-deficient for thermoelectric use, which is what the paper title says. KNN is the 50:50 solid solution of two ABO3 perovskites, KNbO3 and NaNbO3, with K and Na sharing the twelve-coordinate A site and Nb alone on the octahedral B site. I disagree with [ref 2]: it returns only tetragonal-tungsten-bronze-type and related entries (K2NaNb3O9 Pm, K4NaNb5O15 Pm, K5Na3Nb8O20 P1), which are different stoichiometries in the same K2O-Na2O-Nb2O5 phase field and carry no ICSD references at all, so none of them describes a 1:1 K:Na niobate perovskite. Two ferroelectric transitions fall inside the 321-1006 K window, orthorhombic to tetragonal near 470 K and tetragonal to cubic near 690 K, but both are displacive distortions of the same perovskite aristotype rather than a change of prototype, and the chunk file prints no transition line, so they are noted here instead of being recorded as phases. Oxygen deficiency is the carrier-doping variable of this paper and is a host-element non-stoichiometry, not an added dopant.

Six of seven samples are La0.54Pr0.36Te0.1MnO3 or La0.36Pr0.54Te0.1MnO3 and the seventh is (La0.7Pb0.3)0.5(Pr0.63Ca0.37)0.5MnO3 -- in every case the A-site subscripts sum to one and manganese alone occupies the B site, which is the ABO3 perovskite manganite. The two papers are on Pr-doped La manganites and on ferro-antiferromagnetic coupling in mixed manganites, both squarely in this family. [ref 2] agrees on chemistry but not on formula: its La3PrMn4O12 Pm and LaPrMn2O6 Pmc2_1 entries are ordered A-site supercells with no ICSD references, computational orderings of what is experimentally a disordered A-site solid solution, so no mp_id is carried. The 12-379 K window crosses the magnetic ordering and metal-insulator transitions these papers measure; those are not prototype changes and the perovskite distortion pattern is unchanged, so no phases array is recorded.

dopant_roles.basis: Te0.1 in La0.54Pr0.36Te0.1MnO3, where the three A-site subscripts sum to exactly 1.00, so tellurium is being put on the A site rather than on the oxygen sublattice. Tellurium doping of manganites is done for electron doping -- a higher-valent A cation reduces Mn(IV), the opposite of the usual divalent substitution -- which is consistent with the transport the paper reports.
The (Pr0.63Ca0.37) half of the composite composition. Divalent Ca on the trivalent rare-earth A site is the standard hole-doping substitution in manganites.

The (La0.7Pb0.3) half of the same composition. Divalent Pb on the A site is again hole doping, and Pb is used in these ferro-antiferromagnetic coupling studies because it makes a ferromagnetic metallic block against the Pr-Ca charge-ordered one.

basis: All five compositions are Tl(10-x)La(x)Te6 with x between 0.9 and 1.15, essentially Tl9LaTe6, and the papers are titled Crystal structures and thermoelectric properties of the series Tl10-xLnxTe6 and Thermoelectric properties of hot-pressed Tl9LnTe6. That series is the rare-earth-substituted Tl5Te3 structure: Tl10Te6 is Tl5Te3 doubled, and the lanthanide takes one specific thallium site, which is why the composition sits so tightly at x = 1. [ref 2] agrees and supplies the structure directly -- La(Tl3Te2)3 I4/m (87) mp-1223306 at hull 0.000 is LaTl9Te6 written as a multiple, and I4/m is the Tl5Te3 space group. The second MP entry, La5TlTe8 I-4 mp-35907, is a different stoichiometry in the same ternary and not what these compositions say.

All six compositions are Li(x)NbO2 with x from 0.6 to 1.0. The O:Nb ratio of 2 settles the compound: this is LiNbO2, not the ferroelectric LiNbO3, and the papers are on evidence of superconductivity in Li(x)NbO2 and on phonon scattering in the same deintercalated series. [ref 2] does list it -- LiNbO2 P6_3/mmc (194) mp-3924 at hull 0.000 with 6 ICSD references -- but ranks LiNbO3 R3c (161) mp-3731 first on 32 references; I disagree with taking that primary, because it is a different compound of the same binary and the stoichiometry here is unambiguous. The structure is layers of trigonal-prismatically coordinated NbO2 with lithium in octahedral interlayer sites, which is the inverse of the gamma-NaxCoO2 arrangement and has no entry in the taxonomy, so linbo2_layered is proposed before use. Lithium content is a compositional and doping variable of the same kind as x in NaxCoO2, not an impurity level, so it is described here and left to stage 3 rather than recorded as a dopant.

This host holds two different Zintl phases that share all four elements. Five samples are YbZn(2-x)Mn(x)Sb2 with x = 0.25 to 0.4, which is the trigonal CaAl2Si2-type 1-2-2 Zintl phase -- the papers are titled Improved thermoelectric performance in the Zintl phase compounds YbZn2Sb2 and Thermoelectric Properties of Zintl Compound YbZn2Sb2 with Mn Substitution. The other two are Yb9Mn(1.2-2.2)Zn(2-3)Sb9, the 9-4-9 Zintl structure of the third paper, Thermoelectric properties of the Yb9Mn4.2-xZnxSb9 solid solutions, which is a different framework entirely. The two separate cleanly on the Yb:Sb ratio (1:2 against 1:1), so the host is flagged mixed for a stoichiometric split in stage 2. Neither reference returns a line for either compound, so no mp_id is recorded. Manganese and zinc are both above the cut in every composition and are framework constituents of the polyanion, not dopants.

The six compositions are Mn(3.1-3.51)Sn(0.49-0.9), i.e. Mn3+xSn1-x, which the first paper names in its title: Kondo physics in antiferromagnetic Weyl semimetal Mn3+xSn1-x films. Mn3Sn is the hexagonal D0_19 ordered-hcp AB3 structure, P6_3/mmc, whose manganese kagome layers carry the non-collinear antiferromagnetism and the large anomalous Nernst and Hall signals these papers measure, and excess manganese simply takes tin sites, which is why the two subscripts move in opposite directions and always sum to about 4. [ref 2] lists Mn3Sn P6_3/mmc mp-1095178 with 3 ICSD references; its hull value of 0.173 is a DFT artefact for a frustrated magnet whose true magnetic ground state is not the collinear one the calculation assumes, and the MP primary MnSn2 I4/mcm is a different compound of the binary at a tin-rich composition that appears nowhere here.

dopant_roles.basis: Indium appears below the cut in a single composition. On the D0_19 lattice the only site it can plausibly take is the tin site, where trivalent In against tetravalent Sn removes an electron, so it would act as a band-filling knob of the kind the second paper (balancing band convergence and resonant levels) is after. One composition and no direct evidence, so this is the weakest call in the record.

basis: Four compositions are Mo(1-x)Nb(x)Te2 for x = 0.2 to 0.8 and two more read Mo(0.78-0.88)Nb(0.12-0.22)Te, which is the same series with the tellurium subscript mis-transcribed as 1 instead of 2. The papers are titled Rich structural phase diagram and thermoelectric properties of layered [dichalcogenides] and Critical enhancement of thermopower in a chemically tuned polar semimetal -- that polar semimetal is Td MoTe2 (Pmn2_1), and the chemical tuning is exactly this niobium substitution, which stabilises the distorted-octahedral phase at room temperature. NbTe2 itself is the distorted-octahedral C2/m structure, so the niobium-rich half of this series is unambiguously 1T-prime-type, while the x = 0.2 end may still be 2H, which is why the host is flagged mixed with mos2_2h as the alternative and splits on x. The taxonomy had no distorted-octahedral entry -- the chunk-007 Mo-Te record had to park 1T-prime MoTe2 in unresolved_crystalline for exactly this reason -- so mote2_1t_prime is proposed before use. Neither reference returns a line for the ternary, so mp_id is null. The 10-301 K window crosses the 1T-prime to Td stacking change near 250 K, which is a change of setting within this prototype rather than a change of prototype, so it is noted here rather than recorded as a phase.

Every composition is Sr2TiMoO6 with small La or Ba substitution on the strontium site, and the papers say so outright: Environmental friendly Sr2TiMoO6 double perovskite for high temperature thermoelectrics. The A2BB(prime)O6 stoichiometry with two different B cations of different size and charge is the rock-salt B-site ordered double perovskite, and [ref 2] confirms it -- Sr2TiMoO6 I4/m (87) mp-1078580 at hull 0.003 with an ICSD reference, I4/m being the tetragonally distorted ordered double perovskite, with the cubic Fm-3m entry mp-1218376 as the undistorted aristotype. The measured window is 332-1235 K; any tetragonal-to-cubic straightening within it is a distortion of the same ordered aristotype rather than a prototype change, and the chunk file prints no transition line, so no phases sequence is recorded.

dopant_roles.basis: La0.15 to La0.3 in La(x)Sr(2-x)TiMoO6, which is the third paper (metal-like electrical conductivity in LaxSr2-xTiMoO6). Trivalent La on the divalent Sr A site donates one electron per substitution into the Mo 4d band, which is the electron-doping knob that makes the series metallic.

Ba0.1Sr1.9TiMoO6, from the paper on the effect of Ba doping. Barium is isovalent with strontium, so it adds no carriers; it enlarges the A cation and raises the tolerance factor, tuning the octahedral tilt and the lattice thermal conductivity rather than the carrier count.

basis: The compositions are written as mole fractions of two oxides -- (MoO3)3(TeO2)7, (MoO3)0.1(TeO2)0.1 and so on -- not as a crystalline formula, and the second paper is titled Low-temperature metallic behaviour of amorphous MoO3-TeO2 thin films. TeO2 is one of the classic heavy-metal-oxide glass formers and MoO3 its usual modifier, so the MoO3-TeO2 binary is a glass-forming system and these samples are glasses or amorphous films; no crystalline prototype applies. The O/(O+Te) axis the chunk file flags with a CHECK marker resolves to no: oxygen is the network anion and tellurium a network cation here, so they do not share a site and this is not a substitution axis. [ref 2] returns crystalline Te2MoO7 P2_1/c mp-19453 and TeMo5O16 Pc, which are the crystalline compounds of the same binary and are not what an amorphous film is made of, so no mp_id is recorded.

Every composition is Ti(0.8-1.3)Mo6Se8 with up to Cu0.5, and the papers name it: Thermoelectric and structural properties of a new Chevrel phase and Thermoelectric properties of Mo6Se8-based Chevrel phase. The Mo6Se8 unit is the defining Chevrel cluster -- an octahedron of molybdenum inside a cube of selenium -- and the titanium and copper occupy the channel sites between clusters. [ref 2] supports it: Ti(Mo3Se4)2 R-3 (148) mp-1104333 is TiMo6Se8 written as a multiple, with an ICSD reference, and R-3 is the rhombohedral Chevrel setting; its hull value of 0.133 reflects that ternary Chevrels are entropy- and cluster-stabilised rather than 0 K ground states.

dopant_roles.basis: Cu0.05 to Cu0.5 in CuxTi(1.3-y)Mo6Se8, always paired with a reduction in titanium. Copper does not replace an atom of the Mo6Se8 cluster; it enters the channel sites between clusters alongside titanium and donates electrons into the cluster band. In the role vocabulary that is cage_filler rather than substitutional, and it is the same physics as a filler in a skutterudite void: an electron source plus a rattler.

basis: The single composition is NbN across all seven samples, and both papers are on NbN thin films -- transition temperatures and upper critical fields, and resistivity of polycrystalline films -- measured 10-300 K, which is the superconducting and normal-state regime of delta-NbN. Delta-NbN is the B1 rocksalt nitride, and [ref 2] agrees emphatically: NbN Fm-3m (225) mp-1580 with 22 ICSD references, far ahead of anything else in the binary. The hull value of 0.202 says only that perfectly stoichiometric cubic NbN is not a 0 K ground state -- it is stabilised by nitrogen vacancies, which is exactly the non-stoichiometry the taxonomy entry is written around -- and does not argue against the assignment. The other MP entries (Nb4N5, Nb2N, Nb5N6, Nb2N3) are different stoichiometries of the Nb-N system rather than polymorphs of NbN; the hexagonal ones are recorded as other structures reachable in this chemistry but not by these films.

other_polymorphs.note: Nb5N6 P6_3/mcm, one ICSD reference. A different stoichiometry in the Nb-N phase field rather than a polymorph of NbN; recorded so the hexagonal nitrides of this system are not mistaken for phases of the cubic film.

basis: Six of the seven samples are (U0.8Pu0.2)N, the mixed mononitride fast-reactor fuel. UN and PuN are both B1 rocksalt nitrides and are fully miscible, so the solid solution is one rocksalt phase across the whole composition range and across the 410-1975 K window, where the molecular-dynamics paper studies exactly this lattice. The seventh string, (U)81.26(PuN)18.74, comes from the U-PuO2/U-PuC/U-PuN cermet fuel paper: a cermet is metal uranium plus a ceramic nitride, two phases by construction rather than a solid solution, so the host is flagged mixed with composite_multiphase as the alternative for that sample. [ref 2] returns PuUN2 R-3m mp-1219668 and PuU4N5 I4/mmm mp-1219808 with no ICSD references; both are cation-ordered supercells of the same rocksalt lattice, a computational ordering of what is experimentally a disordered cation solid solution, so no mp_id is carried at host level.

The curator strings settle what the composition strings obscure: these are [(NbOx)n/(STNO)m] superlattice films, where STNO is SrTiNb0.2O3, i.e. Nb-doped SrTiO3. The perovskite is the transport-active component and the reason for the work (Thermoelectric Properties of Strontium Titanate Superlattices), and niobium on the titanium site is the n-type donor that makes it conduct. But a superlattice is two structures by construction, and the second one is not a perovskite: NbOx layers are the defect-rocksalt NbO structure, cubic with a quarter of both the metal and the oxygen sites vacant and ordered. So the host is flagged mixed with rocksalt_oxide as the alternative, and the split is by layer rather than by composition -- no element ratio separates them because each film contains both. [ref 2] returns only tetragonal-tungsten-bronze-type Sr-Ti-Nb-O entries (Sr3TiNb4O15 Pc, Sr4Ti3Nb2O15 R-3m, Sr2LaTi2Nb3O15 Pbam), none with ICSD references; those are different stoichiometries in the same phase field and are not what a lightly Nb-doped SrTiO3 film is, so no mp_id is recorded.

dopant_roles.basis: One composition carries lanthanum below the cut, from the second paper on (1-x)SrTiO3-(x)La-substituted bulk ceramics. Trivalent La on the divalent Sr A site is the other standard donor for strontium titanate, working in the same direction as Nb on the B site.

basis: Six of seven samples are SmNiO3 and the seventh is Sm0.8Sr0.2NiO3. SmNiO3 is a rare-earth nickelate, an ABO3 perovskite with the GdFeO3 octahedral tilt pattern, and [ref 2] is decisive: SmNiO3 Pnma (62) mp-25588 at hull 0.000 with 27 ICSD references, with the undistorted cubic Pm-3m entry mp-1099668 at hull 0.121 as the aristotype. The papers are on the electronic phase transition of rare-earth nickelates and on perovskite Sm(1-x)Sr(x)NiO3, so the perovskite reading is the papers own. The 10-483 K window crosses the nickelate metal-insulator transition near 400 K, which is accompanied by a subtle symmetry lowering from Pnma to P2_1/n as the NiO6 octahedra bond-disproportionate. That is a distortion within the perovskite prototype, not a change of prototype, and the chunk file prints no transition line, so it is noted here rather than recorded as a phase sequence.

dopant_roles.basis: Sm0.8Sr0.2NiO3, from the paper on Sm(1-x)Sr(x)NiO3. Divalent Sr on the trivalent Sm A site is hole doping, which suppresses the metal-insulator transition and is the point of the substitution.

basis: All seven samples are ZrNiPb with 0 to 2 per cent bismuth, and the paper is titled Thermoelectric Properties of n-type ZrNiPb-Based Half-Heuslers. ZrNiPb is the lead analogue of ZrNiSn, an 18-electron C1b half-Heusler (F-43m) and therefore a semiconductor, which is what makes it a thermoelectric candidate. Neither reference returns a line for this ternary -- the Zr-Ni-Pb system is not in the 2019 Materials Project dump -- so mp_id is null and stage 2 will have to resolve it by another route.

dopant_roles.basis: ZrNiPb(1-x)Bi(x) for x = 0.005 to 0.02, the whole doping series of the paper. Bismuth has one more valence electron than lead, so on the p-block site it donates one electron per substitution and pushes the 18-electron compound n-type -- which is precisely the n-type of the title.

basis: Five compositions, all TiNiSb or TiNiSb with about ten per cent of Co, Mn or Fe on one site. [ref 2] gives TiNiSb F-43m (216) mp-20952 at hull 0.000 with 3 ICSD references, F-43m being the C1b half-Heusler setting, and the papers are on TiCo(1-x)Ni(x)Sb solid solutions and on semi-Heusler phases. Worth recording that TiNiSb is a 19-electron half-Heusler (Ti 4 plus Ni 10 plus Sb 5), one electron past the 18-electron closed shell, so unlike TiNiSn it is metallic rather than semiconducting -- the prototype is the same but the transport is not, and the TiCo(1-x)Ni(x)Sb series in the first paper exists to sweep between the 18- and 19-electron counts. The second MP entry, TiNi2Sb Fm-3m mp-10261, is the full-Heusler of the same ternary; no composition here is at that 1:2:1 ratio.

dopant_roles.basis: TiCo0.1Ni0.9Sb, one point on the TiCo(1-x)Ni(x)Sb series of the first paper. Cobalt has one d electron fewer than nickel, so it moves the count from 19 towards the semiconducting 18.

NiTi0.9Mn0.1Sb. The third paper is on disordered Mn semi-Heusler phases, and manganese is large and electropositive enough to take the titanium site rather than the nickel one; it also carries a local moment, which is what that magnetic study is after.

TiFe0.1Ni1.0Sb -- note the nickel subscript stays at 1.0, so iron is added rather than exchanged in the string as written; on the C1b lattice the vacant tetrahedral site is available, but the physically ordinary reading is partial replacement of nickel by the neighbouring 3d metal. Two electrons short of nickel, so a stronger p-type push than cobalt.

basis: Five of seven samples are Sm2SbO2, a rare-earth pnictide oxide: fluorite-type [Sm2O2] slabs alternating with square nets of antimony, which is the same I4/mmm layer topology as Bi2O2Se and the closest thing the taxonomy carries. [ref 2] supports the compound -- Sm2SbO2 I4/mmm (139) mp-1219180 at hull 0.000 -- though with no ICSD references, and the review paper in the chunk (Rare-Earth Pnictide Oxides (RE,Ca)mPnnOm) is about exactly this family. The other two compositions are single samples of different members of that homologous series and are not this structure: Sm3SbO3 is monoclinic C2/m (mp-983597, one ICSD reference) and Sm8Sb3O8 has no reference entry at all. The taxonomy has no id for either, so the host is flagged mixed with unresolved_crystalline standing in for them rather than stretching the Bi2O2Se label over three different structures. Confidence is medium because the Bi2O2Se entry is being used for an antimonide analogue rather than for its own chemistry.

One composition, Sm2Zr2O7, across all seven samples, from papers on rare-earth A2Zr2O7 zirconates for thermal-barrier and thermoelectric use. [ref 2] gives Sm2Zr2O7 Fd-3m (227) mp-4408 at hull 0.000 with 3 ICSD references, the pyrochlore setting. The interesting part is the curator note on one sample: Phases present: Pyrochlore + Fluorite. Sm2Zr2O7 sits almost exactly on the pyrochlore/defect-fluorite stability boundary for A2B2O7 zirconates (the cation radius ratio is near the 1.46 threshold), so ordered pyrochlore and the disordered defect-fluorite of the same composition coexist depending on how the ceramic was fired. The host is therefore flagged mixed with fluorite_oxide as the alternative. This is a synthesis-dependent coexistence, not a transition crossed on heating -- the order-disorder transition in this system is around 2000 K, above the 293-1673 K window -- so it is not recorded in phases.

The papers are SnO2 addition to ZnO (Zn(1-x)Sn(x)O), a ZnO-SnO2 film study, and Al and Sn doped ZnO nanoparticles -- so most of these samples are tin-doped wurtzite ZnO, and the curator note x = [Sn]/[Zn] confirms that tin is being counted against a zinc oxide host. Sn0.15ZnO1.15 through Sn0.5ZnO1.5 are that series. One composition is explicitly Zn2SnO4, the spinel, which is the compound that forms once tin exceeds its solubility in ZnO, so the host is flagged mixed and splits on the Sn:Zn ratio. This is the case the chunk file warns about with Al-O-Zn: [ref 1] ranks ZnSnO3 R3c (161) mp-13334 first, and ilmenite or LiNbO3-type ZnSnO3 is a metastable phase made by high-pressure or soft-chemistry routes, not by the ceramic sintering and sputtering these papers use, so I do not follow it. [ref 2] Zn2SnO4 Fd-3m mp-1103830 is the right structure for the one spinel composition.

other_polymorphs.note: Ilmenite/LiNbO3-type ZnSnO3 R3c, the TEDesignLab primary with 2 ICSD references at hull 0.041. A metastable phase of the Zn-Sn-O system that is not produced by the sintering and sputtering routes of these papers; kept out of the assignment for the same reason the chunk file keeps ZnAl2O4 out of Al-O-Zn.

basis: Five of the seven samples are Sr(Fe0.2Ti0.2Mo0.2Nb0.2Cr0.2)O3 -- the high-entropy perovskite of the paper titled High-Entropy Perovskites: An Emergent Class of Oxide Thermoelectrics. Five different cations share the octahedral B site in equal amounts, so each is 20 per cent of that site but only 4 per cent of the whole formula, which is why they all fall below the 5 at.% cut without being dopants in any sense; this host is a clean example of the sublattice-versus-formula problem the README describes. Sr0.95La0.05Ti0.02Mn0.0126O3 is La- and Mn-substituted SrTiO3, also a perovskite. The third string, Sr20.995Ti0.005O4, is broken: the Sr2(M)O4 stoichiometry together with the spin-triplet paper identifies it as Ti-substituted Sr2RuO4, whose ruthenium has been lost in parsing -- that is a Ruddlesden-Popper n = 1 phase, a different prototype, so the host is flagged mixed and the composition string should be fixed upstream rather than split in stage 2. [ref 1] and [ref 2] both return binary strontium oxides and peroxides (SrO Fm-3m mp-2472, SrO2, SrO6, SrO10), which is what the two-element host key literally implies and is not any of these ternary and quaternary oxides.

dopant_roles.basis: One of the five equiatomic B-site cations of the high-entropy perovskite, at 20 per cent of the B site. It is a constituent of the compound, not a dilute substituent, and appears under the cut only because the cut is taken on the whole formula. Titanium also appears as the B-site host of the two SrTiO3-derived compositions.
Equiatomic B-site constituent of Sr(Fe,Ti,Mo,Nb,Cr)O3, 20 per cent of the B site.
Equiatomic B-site constituent, 20 per cent of the B site. Along with Nb it supplies the reducible high-valent cation that carries the electrons in this family.
Equiatomic B-site constituent, 20 per cent of the B site.
Equiatomic B-site constituent, 20 per cent of the B site.
Sr0.95La0.05, i.e. five per cent of the A site. Trivalent La on the divalent Sr site is the standard donor for strontium titanate.
The Mn0.0126 of the same composition, from the paper on the effects of Mn substitution. A transition metal at that level sits on the octahedral B site alongside titanium.

basis: The paper title is explicit: Thermoelectric Power Measurements of xSb-(60-x)V2O5-40TeO2 Glasses, and the curator strings are the batch compositions in mole per cent (10Sb-50V2O5-40TeO2 and so on). V2O5-TeO2 is a standard oxide glass-forming pair -- tellurite glasses modified with vanadium pentoxide, whose conduction is small-polaron hopping between V(IV) and V(V) -- so no crystalline prototype applies. The O/(O+Te) axis the chunk file flags resolves to no again: oxygen is the network anion and tellurium a network-forming cation, so they do not share a site. [ref 2] returns crystalline V-Te-O compounds (V2Te2O9 Fdd2 mp-649905, VTeO4 P2_1/c mp-32482) which are the devitrification products of this system, not the glasses measured here, so no mp_id is recorded.

dopant_roles.basis: Antimony is the x of the xSb-(60-x)V2O5-40TeO2 series, from 5 to 15 mole per cent, added at the expense of V2O5. That is a third glass component being varied across a series, not a dilute dopant in a lattice; it falls below the 5 at.% cut only because the formula is dominated by oxygen.

basis: The curator note gives the series outright: (PbSe)1+delta(TiSe2)n with 1 <= n <= 18, thin-film intergrowths. The composition strings are the n = 1 to 6 members of it -- PbTiSe3 is PbSe plus one TiSe2, PbTi2Se5 is PbSe plus two, and so on to PbTi6Se13 -- and the paper is on carrier dilution in TiSe2-based intergrowth compounds. Structurally these are rocksalt PbSe bilayers interleaved with CdI2-type TiSe2 layers, with the two subsystems incommensurate along the shared in-plane direction, which is what the 1+delta records. Stage 2 must treat this as two subsystems: there is no single Materials Project entry for a misfit compound, and neither reference returns anything for this ternary in any case. These are turbostratically disordered ferecrystals rather than classical misfit crystals, but the two-subsystem description is the same.

Every composition is Pb(1-x)Sr(x)Te with two per cent sodium, x running from 0.1 to 0.8. PbTe and SrTe are both rocksalt and the PbTe-SrTe join is one of the most worked-on band-engineering systems in thermoelectrics, which is what the record-ZT paper is about. Strontium exceeds its solubility in PbTe at a few per cent, so the high-x samples are two-phase -- rocksalt PbTe-rich matrix with rocksalt SrTe precipitates, which is the point of the non-equilibrium processing -- but both phases are the same prototype, so no split is needed and the host is not flagged mixed. Neither reference returns a line for the ternary, so mp_id is null. Strontium sits in the host key rather than in dopant_roles because it exceeds the cut in every composition; it is an alloying end member, not a dopant.

dopant_roles.basis: Na0.02 in every composition, held fixed while the Sr content is swept. Monovalent sodium on the divalent cation site of a rocksalt telluride is the standard p-type acceptor for PbTe and its alloys, and holding it constant while varying strontium is what isolates the band-offset effect the papers are measuring.

basis: Three samples are YPd3 and four are Y(1-x)U(x)Pd3 with x = 0.05 or 0.1. [ref 2] gives YPd3 Pm-3m (221) mp-559 at hull 0.000 with 8 ICSD references, which is the L1_2 Cu3Au order -- palladium on the face centres, yttrium at the corners of a cubic close-packed cell. The papers are Kondo studies that use YPd3 as a non-magnetic host into which a dilute actinide or lanthanide moment is placed (thermoelectric power of the (Ce,Y)Pd3 system; evidence for the Kondo effect in Y(1-x)U(x)Pd3), so the host structure is the fixed background of the experiment rather than the variable. The other MP entries (Y3Pd2, Y3Pd4, YPd, YPd2) are different compounds of the binary, each with a single ICSD reference, and none matches the 1:3 ratio here.

dopant_roles.basis: U0.05 and U0.1 on the yttrium corner site of the L1_2 cell -- the dilute Kondo impurity the two papers are built around. It is substitutional in the strict sense: same site, same coordination, a magnetic 5f moment replacing a non-magnetic one.

basis: The six compositions run Pr3Te4, Pr2.9Te4, Pr2.78Te4, Pr2.74Te4, Pr2.70Te4, Pr2.67Te4 -- a single cation-vacancy series from Pr3Te4 to Pr2.67Te4, which is Pr2Te3 written on a four-tellurium basis. That is the Th3P4 structure with its cation sublattice progressively emptied, and the vacancy concentration is the carrier-density knob rather than a dopant, which is why the paper (Praseodymium Telluride: A High-Temperature, High-ZT Thermoelectric Material) sweeps it so finely. [ref 2] confirms the structure: Pr3Te4 I-43d (220) mp-2127 at hull 0.009 with 2 ICSD references. I do not follow its primary, PrTe Fm-3m mp-2532 with 6 ICSD references -- that is the rocksalt monotelluride, a different compound of the same binary, and every composition here is at Pr:Te of 3:4 or below.

The compositions are TiPtSb and Ti(1-x)PtSb down to Ti0.75PtSb, and the single paper is titled A new defective 19-electron TiPtSb half-Heusler thermoelectric compound -- so both the prototype and the defect chemistry come straight from the title. TiPtSb has 19 valence electrons, one too many for the 18-electron C1b gap, and each titanium vacancy removes four electrons, so the titanium deficiency is the intrinsic carrier knob and not an impurity; that is why no element appears below the cut in this host. Neither reference returns a line for the ternary, so mp_id is null.

One composition, UPt3, across all seven samples, from three transport and thermodynamic papers on the canonical heavy-fermion superconductor. [ref 2] gives UPt3 P6_3/mmc (194) mp-30855 at hull 0.000 with 4 ICSD references, which is the D0_19 ordered-hcp AB3 structure the taxonomy carries with LaAl3 and CeAl3 as representatives -- the same MgCd3-type family, and the hexagonal layer stacking is what gives UPt3 its strongly anisotropic transport. The other MP entries (UPt5 F-43m, UPt2 Cmcm, U3Pt) are different stoichiometries of the binary. The measured range is quoted as 13-349 K on two curves with a full span to 1010 K; nothing in these papers involves a structural transition, and the transitions they do study (heavy-fermion coherence near 10 K, superconductivity near 0.5 K) are electronic.

RuSb2Te has three pnictogen-or-chalcogen atoms per ruthenium, the MX3 skutterudite ratio, with Sb and Te ordered on the four-membered framework rings; the paper is titled Thermoelectric Properties of RuSb2Te Ternary Skutterudites. Charge counting is what makes the substitution necessary: RuSb3 does not exist because ruthenium brings two electrons too few, and replacing one antimony in three by tellurium restores the same valence electron count that stabilises CoSb3. I disagree with [ref 2] here. Its two entries for this ternary are SbTeRu P2_1/c (14) mp-1102857 at hull 0.358 with 2 ICSD references and Sb2TeRu Immm (71) mp-1219496 at hull 0.381; neither is the Im-3 skutterudite framework, the first is a 1:1:1 compound rather than the 1:2:1 measured here, and hull values above 0.35 eV/atom for both suggest the ternary is poorly covered in the 2019 dump rather than that the skutterudite is wrong. No mp_id is recorded.

dopant_roles.basis: Ru0.95Fe0.05Sb2Te. Iron is the 3d member of the same group as ruthenium and takes the octahedrally coordinated metal site of the skutterudite framework; one electron short of ruthenium, so it dopes p-type.

RuSb2Sn0.1Te0.9 and Ru0.95Sn0.1Sb2Te0.9, where tin enters as tellurium is removed -- so it is going onto the framework ring site, not the metal site. Tin has two electrons fewer than tellurium there, making it the p-type framework knob.

Yb0.05RuSb2Te. Once the host is known to be a skutterudite, the only place five per cent of a large electropositive rare earth can go is the icosahedral void of the framework, exactly as Yb does in Yb(x)Co4Sb12 -- an electron donor and a rattler, not a substituent.

reference_disagreement: assigned sg [204], ICSD-backed references for this host report [14]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: TaS2 with a sulfur excess of a few thousandths (TaS2.002 to TaS2.008), a curator note giving a quantity xes in mg/cc, one paper with no recorded title, and a 12-299 K window. TaS2 has two ambient polytypes and the composition cannot separate them: 2H-TaS2 is trigonal prismatic (P6_3/mmc), with a charge-density wave near 75 K and superconductivity near 0.8 K, while 1T-TaS2 is octahedral (P-3m1, CdI2 type) and undergoes a commensurate CDW and Mott localisation near 180 K that dominates its thermopower completely. Those are different materials for transport purposes, so the host is flagged mixed and the confidence is low; 2H is recorded as the primary only because it is the more commonly grown and more commonly measured of the two. I do not follow [ref 2], which names TaS2 Fmm2 (42) mp-1411 with 8 ICSD references as primary: an orthorhombic setting is a distortion or superstructure description of a stacking polytype, not one of the two ambient forms, and it does not tell us which polytype was measured. The paper would settle this in one line.

Two samples are Sb2Se3 and five are Sb2Se3 with about one atomic per cent of tellurium, which the curator records precisely as 61.3 at% Se, 37.6 at% Sb, 1.1 at% Te. [ref 2] is unambiguous: Sb2Se3 Pnma (62) mp-2160 at hull 0.000 with 11 ICSD references and no competing polymorph -- the stibnite structure, built from quasi-one-dimensional (Sb4Se6)n ribbons held together by weak inter-ribbon bonding. That anisotropy is what the first paper exploits when it grows [010]-oriented whiskers. The third paper is on BiSbSe3, but no composition in this host carries bismuth.

dopant_roles.basis: Te0.01 per Sb2Se3, i.e. 1.1 at% by the curator count. Tellurium is group 16 like selenium and takes anion sites in the ribbon, adding no carriers; it tunes the band edges and scatters phonons through its mass and size contrast. At about 1.7 per cent of the anion sublattice it is dilute, so it is a substituent rather than a Sb2Se3-Sb2Te3 alloying end member.

basis: All seven compositions read ((SnSe)1.15)(V(1.12-1.42)Se)n for n = 1 to 6, and the paper is titled Influence of interstitial V on structure and properties of ferecrystals. These are the same kind of intergrowth as the Pb-Se-Ti host at rank 933: rocksalt SnSe bilayers interleaved with CdI2-type VSe2 layers, with 1.15 being the incommensurate ratio between the two subsystems, and turbostratic rather than epitaxial stacking between them. Neither reference returns anything for this ternary, and a misfit compound has no single Materials Project entry in any case, so stage 2 must resolve the two subsystems separately.

dopant_roles.basis: Vanadium is a host element and sits well above the cut, but its role is the subject of the paper and worth recording: the dichalcogenide block is written V1.12Se to V1.42Se rather than VSe2 stoichiometric, and the excess vanadium occupies sites in the van der Waals gap between VSe2 layers. That is interstitial self-intercalation, and it is what carries the charge between the two subsystems.

basis: This host holds at least three different things and no composition dominates. YbSi (2 samples) is the CrB-type chain compound -- [ref 2] gives YbSi Cmcm (63) mp-10651 at hull 0.000 with 2 ICSD references -- and it is the Yb heavy-fermion silicide of the high-pressure thermopower and two-band-model papers. Yb5Si3 (1 sample, with its own paper titled Thermoelectric properties of Yb5Si3) is the Mn5Si3 D8_8 structure, MP mp-1188257 P6_3/mcm with 3 ICSD references, which is a different prototype the taxonomy already carries. The remaining four compositions read YbSi5 and YbCo(0.1-0.2)Si(4.8-4.9), a 1:5 Yb:Si ratio for which no phase exists in the Yb-Si binary: the silicon-rich phases are YbSi2 and Yb3Si5, both AlB2-derived (mp-1671 P6/mmm and mp-349 P-62m, 4 ICSD references each), so those strings are either a garbled silicon-rich silicide or a transposed Yb5(Si,Co)3. The assignment is therefore low confidence and mixed, with alb2 listed because it is where the unidentified silicon-rich compositions would land if they are what they look like. This host needs the papers, not more inference.

dopant_roles.basis: Cobalt appears only in the three unidentified silicon-rich compositions (YbCo0.1Si4.9 and neighbours), so its site cannot be judged until the compound is. If those are AlB2-type YbSi(2-x) it would substitute into the silicon net; if they are a mis-transcribed Yb5(Si,Co)3 it would take a silicon site in the Mn5Si3 framework. Deliberately left unknown rather than guessed.

basis: The four compositions are Ba8Ag5Ge41, Ba8Ag6Ge40, Ba8Ag5Ga1Ge40 and Ba8Ag5Ga2Ge39 -- in every case eight barium guests inside a framework of exactly 46 tetrahedrally bonded atoms, which is the type I clathrate stoichiometry Ba8M(x)Ge(46-x) and nothing else. The papers confirm it: An exploration of noble metal substitution in germanium based clathrates, and a study of Ba8-based clathrate thermoelectrics. Silver and gallium are both framework substituents chosen to set the electron count -- five silver atoms on the 46-atom framework is close to the charge-balanced composition for eight divalent guests. [ref 2] returns only Ba(AgGe)2 I4/mmm mp-13910, a ThCr2Si2-type 1-2-2 compound of the same ternary at a completely different stoichiometry, so no mp_id is recorded.

dopant_roles.basis: Ga1 and Ga2 per 46-atom framework in two compositions. Gallium replaces germanium on the covalent cage framework and removes one electron per substitution, which together with silver is how the Zintl count for eight Ba guests is balanced. It falls below the 5 at.% cut only because the formula unit has 54 atoms; it is a framework constituent, not a dilute impurity.

reference_disagreement: assigned sg [223], ICSD-backed references for this host report [139]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: All six samples are BaAg2SnSe4, three of them stoichiometric or slightly cation-deficient and two carrying Na or In substitution, and the paper is titled Origins of ultralow thermal conductivity in 1-2-1-4 quaternary selenides. [ref 1] carries BaAg2SnSe4 as PRIMARY with space group 23 (I222) and supplies no mp_id, so this is one of the ICSD-backed TEDesignLab entries with no Materials Project counterpart in the 2019 dump. The taxonomy had no entry for the AM2M(prime)Q4 family, so ba_1214_chalcogenide is proposed before use. It is deliberately not filed under stannite_kesterite: barium is far too large for a tetrahedral site, so the structure is an AgSe4/SnSe4 tetrahedral framework with Ba in cavities rather than a diamond-like cation ordering, and the rattling of that large cavity cation is exactly what the paper credits for the ultralow thermal conductivity. Confidence is medium because the space group comes from one reference line and the family is reported in more than one setting.

dopant_roles.basis: Ba0.92Na0.08Ag2SnSe4. Monovalent sodium on the divalent barium cavity site removes one electron per substitution, so it is the p-type acceptor of this series.
BaAg2Sn0.9In0.1Se4. Trivalent indium on the tetravalent tin site of the tetrahedral framework is again an acceptor, working on the framework rather than on the cavity cation.

basis: Four of the six compositions are Ag(0.2-0.4)Bi0.5Sb(0.2-1.5)Te3 -- silver added to Bi0.5Sb1.5Te3, the workhorse p-type tetradymite alloy -- and the third paper is on quaternary Ag-Bi-Sb-Te alloys prepared by pressureless sintering. The other two are written as (Ag2Te)0.25 and (Ag2Te)0.5 of (Bi0.5Sb1.5Te3), i.e. 25 and 50 per cent silver telluride: at that level Ag2Te is a second phase and the sample is a tetradymite/Ag2Te composite, not a doped tetradymite, so the host is flagged mixed and those two split off in stage 2. Silver below its solubility takes a cation site as an acceptor; above it, it precipitates as Ag2Te, which is the whole subject of the Ag2Te doping paper. [ref 2] offers only Ag2BiSbTe4 I-4m2 mp-1229125 at hull 0.457 with no ICSD references, a computed ordered quaternary that is not the measured material, so no mp_id is recorded. The Bi/Sb ratio spans 0.25 to 0.71 across the host, so the parent tetradymite composition is per-composition work for stage 3, not a host-level label.

solid_solution_axis.note: Bi/(Bi+Sb) over six compositions, median 0.31. Bismuth and antimony are isoelectronic and share the octahedral cation site of the tetradymite layer, so this is a genuine substitution axis; the structure is tetradymite across the whole of it, but the parent end member is not the same at x = 0.25 and x = 0.71.

basis: All six compositions are Ag10Te4Br3 with partial anion substitution -- Cl for Br, S or Se for Te -- from the Nilges paper on a conceptional approach to materials for resistivity switching and thermoelectrics. It is a silver-rich telluride bromide with mobile silver in a Te/Br anion substructure, which is neither an argyrodite (no central tetrahedral cation, different anion count) nor a simple binary silver chalcogenide, so ag10te4br3_type is proposed before use. [ref 2] has no entry at this composition: Ag5Te2Br Pnma mp-1215016 is the neighbouring 5-2-1 compound of the same family (the chloride analogue of which is the next host in this chunk) and Ag9Te4Br3 P1 mp-676260 at hull 0.062 is a computed silver-deficient variant with no ICSD backing. So no mp_id is recorded and the ambient space group is not settled by the references. Silver-ion order-disorder transitions are reported in this family and the measured window is 289-524 K, so the measurement probably crosses one; no temperature is established by either reference, so none is asserted here and the paper should be read.
